the lesson.

lessons.title: Natsume Soseki and "Ten Nights of Dreams"
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{夏目|なつめ}{漱石|そうせき} is the writer most Japanese people read first and remember longest. This honors
lesson introduces him, retells the first of his 『{夢十夜|ゆめじゅうや}』 ("Ten Nights of Dreams") in modern
Japanese, and explains why one of his novels, 『こころ』, has a place in Japanese schools. The
discussion uses the concessions of lessons 1 to 4.

漱 is outside N2: you'll see {漱石|そうせき} only here, always with furigana, for recognition.

## Who was {夏目|なつめ}{漱石|そうせき}?

| | |
|---|---|
| lived | 1867–1916, born in Edo (soon to be renamed Tokyo) |
| work | English teacher, then university lecturer, then a novelist writing for the Asahi newspaper from 1907 |
| abroad | studied in London from 1900 to 1902, on a government grant: unhappy years, by his own account |
| best-known works | 『{吾輩|わがはい}は{猫|ねこ}である』 ("I Am a Cat"), 『ぼっちゃん』, 『さんしろう』, 『こころ』 |
| on money | his portrait was on the 1,000-yen note first issued in 1984; a new design with Noguchi Hideyo replaced it from 2004 |

(Both kanji of わがはい are outside N2: shown in this title only, for recognition. The titles
ぼっちゃん and さんしろう are given in kana for the same reason.) Old notes like the Sōseki
1,000-yen note have not been withdrawn, so you may still be handed one, though it's rare now.

{漱石|そうせき} was a {近代|きんだい} writer in the full sense: he wrote at the time when Japan was turning
itself into a modern state, and his characters are people caught between old ways and new ones,
often lonely, often unable to say what they feel. That's one reason his books still feel close to
readers today.

## 『{夢十夜|ゆめじゅうや}』

『{夢十夜|ゆめじゅうや}』 is a set of ten short pieces, each one a dream, published in the Asahi newspaper
in ten instalments in the summer of 1908 (25 July to 5 August). Several of them open with the same
words:

> こんな{夢|ゆめ}を{見|み}た。

("I had a dream like this.") The dreams are strange and beautiful, sometimes frightening, and
none of them is explained. The text is long out of copyright, and you can read the whole thing
free online (the course's reading list, in lesson 30, gives places). The original was printed in the spelling of
its time: older kana use (for example ゐ and ゑ, and いふ for いう) and some kanji forms that aren't
used today. Many modern editions update the spelling.

### The first night, retold

Here is the first night, retold in this course's own modern Japanese. It isn't a translation of
the original sentences, only of the story.

> {夢|ゆめ}の{中|なか}で、{私|わたし}は{一人|ひとり}の{女|おんな}のそばに{座|すわ}っていた。{女|おんな}は{静|しず}かに{横|よこ}になったまま、「もうすぐ{死|し}にます」と{言|い}う。{顔|かお}の{色|いろ}はよく、とても{死|し}にそうには{見|み}えない。それにもかかわらず、{女|おんな}ははっきりと、{自分|じぶん}は{死|し}ぬのだと{言|い}う。
>
> {女|おんな}は{最後|さいご}にこう{頼|たの}んだ。「{死|し}んだら、{大|おお}きなかいがらであなを{掘|ほ}って{埋|う}めてください。そして{空|そら}から{落|お}ちてきた{星|ほし}のかけらを、おはかの{印|しるし}に{置|お}いてください。それから、おはかのそばで{待|ま}っていてください。また{会|あ}いに{来|き}ますから。」
>
> 「いつ{来|く}るのか」と{聞|き}くと、{女|おんな}は「{百年|ひゃくねん}{待|ま}っていてください」と{答|こた}えた。そして{死|し}んだ。
>
> {私|わたし}は{言|い}われたとおりにして、おはかの{前|まえ}に{座|すわ}った。{日|ひ}が{昇|のぼ}り、{日|ひ}が{沈|しず}む。{何度|なんど}{数|かぞ}えたか、もう{分|わ}からない。{百年|ひゃくねん}はまだ{来|こ}ない。{女|おんな}にだまされたのではないか、という{気|き}がしてきた。
>
> そのとき、{石|いし}の{下|した}から{細|ほそ}いくきが{伸|の}びてきて、{白|しろ}いゆりの{花|はな}が{開|ひら}いた。{私|わたし}は{花|はな}のつゆに{口|くち}を{付|つ}けた。ふと{空|そら}を{見|み}ると、{明|あ}けの{明星|みょうじょう}が{光|ひか}っていた。「もう{百年|ひゃくねん}はたっていたのだ」と、{私|わたし}はそのとき{初|はじ}めて{気|き}がついた。

かいがら = a shell; あな = a hole; はか = a grave; くき = a stem; ゆり = a lily; つゆ = dew. These are in
kana because their kanji are outside N2, except ゆり, whose spelling {百合|ゆり} is a special reading
this course doesn't teach. {印|しるし} = a mark. {明|あ}けの{明星|みょうじょう} = the morning star; だます = to deceive.

The lily is never explained. Is the woman the flower? Has she kept her promise, or has the dreamer
simply waited long enough to believe so? Readers have argued for a century. That is part of the
pleasure: the story gives you the images, and leaves the meaning to you.

## Why do schools read 『こころ』?

『こころ』 was serialized in the Asahi newspaper in 1914. It is narrated by a student who befriends
a lonely older man he calls 「{先生|せんせい}」. The last part of the novel is a long letter from
{先生|せんせい}, his {遺書|いしょ} (a letter left before death), in which he finally tells the secret of his
past: a friendship, a love, and a betrayal.

That last part, 「{先生|せんせい}と{遺書|いしょ}」, has been a standard text in Japanese high-school textbooks
for many years, usually in the second year. Several reasons are given, and teachers differ:

- it's long enough to discuss, yet the extract can be read in a few weeks of lessons;
- the feelings in it (jealousy, guilt, loneliness, the wish to be understood) are ones teenagers
  know;
- its language is modern enough to read, yet old enough to teach how written Japanese has changed;
- it raises questions with no single answer, which suits class discussion.

Not everyone agrees it belongs there. Some say the story is too dark for teenagers, or that one
famous novel shouldn't take up so much of the syllabus; others answer that its darkness is
exactly what makes students think. Either way, so many adults have read it at school that a
mention of 「{先生|せんせい}と{遺書|いしょ}」 is enough for most Japanese readers to know what you mean.

## Discussion: concessions at work

These sentences use lessons 1 to 4. Read each and check its meaning.

{漱石|そうせき}の{小説|しょうせつ}は{百年|ひゃくねん}{以上|いじょう}{前|まえ}に{書|か}かれたものの、{今|いま}{読|よ}んでも{古|ふる}さを{感|かん}じない。 — Sōseki's novels were written over a hundred years ago, but they don't feel dated even now.
{短編|たんぺん}とはいえ、『{夢十夜|ゆめじゅうや}』を{一度|いちど}で{理解|りかい}するのは{難|むずか}しい。 — They may be short pieces, but "Ten Nights of Dreams" is hard to understand at a first reading.
{有名|ゆうめい}な{作家|さっか}だからといって、{全部|ぜんぶ}の{作品|さくひん}が{面白|おもしろ}いわけではない。 — A writer being famous doesn't make every one of their works interesting.
{女|おんな}が{花|はな}になったにしても、ならなかったにしても、この{話|はなし}の{美|うつく}しさは{変|か}わらない。 — Whether the woman became the flower or not, the beauty of the story is the same.

## The writer's words

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {小説家|しょうせつか} | novelist |
| {近代|きんだい} | the modern age (in Japan, from the Meiji era) |
| {短編|たんぺん} / {長編|ちょうへん} | short story / long work (novel) |
| れんさい | serialization (its second kanji is outside N2) |
| {語|かた}り{手|て} | narrator |
| {遺書|いしょ} | a letter left before death; a will |
| ぶんごう | a great writer, a literary giant (its second kanji is outside N2) |

## Key points

- {夏目|なつめ}{漱石|そうせき} (1867–1916): novelist of the Meiji and early Taishō years; on the 1,000-yen note
  first issued in 1984.
- 『{夢十夜|ゆめじゅうや}』 (1908): ten dream pieces, several opening こんな{夢|ゆめ}を{見|み}た. The first night: a
  woman, a promise, a hundred years, a white lily.
- 『こころ』 (1914): its last part, 「{先生|せんせい}と{遺書|いしょ}」, is a long-standing high-school text.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Before and on the occasion: に先立って, にあたって, に際して
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 1 was about concession: "although", "despite", "even if". Module 2 is about time: the
**[[temporal expressions]]** that place one event against another. N3 gave you the everyday ones
(うちに, たびに, とたん, ところ). N2 adds the formal ones you meet in speeches, notices, news
reports and letters, where a simple 〜{前|まえ}に or 〜とき would sound too plain.

This lesson starts with occasions: the moment before an important event, the start of something
new, and the formal "when".

{開会式|かいかいしき}に{先立|さきだ}って、{選手|せんしゅ}たちが{入場|にゅうじょう}した。 — Before the opening ceremony, the athletes marched in.
{新生活|しんせいかつ}を{始|はじ}めるにあたって、{家具|かぐ}をそろえた。 — Before starting my new life, I got the furniture together.
ご{利用|りよう}に{際|さい}しては、{規約|きやく}をお{読|よ}みください。 — Before using the service, please read the terms.
{試験|しけん}を{前|まえ}にして、{眠|ねむ}れない{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いている。 — With the exam coming up, I keep having sleepless nights.

The theme is events and ceremonies: holding them, giving and winning prizes, formal thanks and
apologies, and the letters that go with all of these. Several words you know in kana now get
kanji: {伺|うかが}う, {承|うけたまわ}る, {拝見|はいけん}する, {祝|いわ}う, {誘|さそ}う, {謝|あやま}る, {感謝|かんしゃ},
{依頼|いらい}.

> **Before you start: kana or kanji?** This course writes the N2 compound particles of this
> module with kanji where the brief decided so: に{先立|さきだ}って, に{際|さい}して, {次第|しだい}, {以来|いらい},
> を{通|つう}じて, を{機|き}に, {末|すえ}に, {折|おり}に. These stay in kana: にあたって, にわたって,
> にともなって, をきっかけに, につけ, つつ, あげく. Lesson 1 and the module 1 reference sheet have the
> full list.

## Before (an important event): 〜に{先立|さきだ}って

{先立|さきだ}つ means "to go first, to come before". 〜に{先立|さきだ}って says that something is done
*before an important event, as preparation for it or as its first part*. It's formal: speeches,
news, notices and business writing.

| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| noun + に{先立|さきだ}って | {開会|かいかい}に{先立|さきだ}って |
| verb (dictionary form) + に{先立|さきだ}って | {工事|こうじ}を{始|はじ}めるに{先立|さきだ}って |
| written: に{先立|さきだ}ち | {発売|はつばい}に{先立|さきだ}ち |
| before a noun: に{先立|さきだ}つ + noun | {試合|しあい}に{先立|さきだ}つ{記者会見|きしゃかいけん} |

{新製品|しんせいひん}の{発売|はつばい}に{先立|さきだ}ち、{店頭|てんとう}で{試食会|ししょくかい}が{開|ひら}かれた。 — Ahead of the new product's launch, a tasting was held in the shops.
{工事|こうじ}を{始|はじ}めるに{先立|さきだ}って、{近所|きんじょ}の{家|いえ}にあいさつに{回|まわ}った。 — Before starting the building work, we went round the neighbours to introduce ourselves.
{式|しき}に{先立|さきだ}つ{練習|れんしゅう}は、{前日|ぜんじつ}の{午後|ごご}に{行|おこな}います。 — The rehearsal for the ceremony will be held the afternoon before.

The event after に{先立|さきだ}って is big enough to need preparing for: a ceremony, a launch, an
election, building work, a performance. For an ordinary day it sounds far too grand:
{寝|ね}る{前|まえ}に{歯|は}を{磨|みが}く, not に{先立|さきだ}って.

Two other uses of {先立|さきだ}つ you'll meet:

- {親|おや}に{先立|さきだ}つ: to die before one's parents (a sad, formal phrase).
- {先立|さきだ}つもの: "the thing that comes first", that is, money: {旅行|りょこう}したいが、{先立|さきだ}つものがない
  (I'd like to travel, but I haven't got the money).

## On the occasion of a new start: 〜にあたって

〜にあたって (written: にあたり) marks *an important moment, usually a new start*, and what you do
or feel at it: preparations, resolutions, greetings, thanks. It's kana in this course. It joins
like に{先立|さきだ}って.

{開店|かいてん}{十周年|じゅっしゅうねん}にあたり、{記念|きねん}セールを{行|おこな}います。 — To mark our tenth anniversary, we're holding a commemorative sale.
{留学|りゅうがく}するにあたって、{両親|りょうしん}とよく{話|はな}し{合|あ}った。 — Before going to study abroad, I talked it through properly with my parents.
{新年|しんねん}を{迎|むか}えるにあたり、{一言|ひとこと}ごあいさつ{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。 — As we welcome the New Year, let me say a few words.

Speeches love it: {受賞|じゅしょう}にあたって (on receiving this award), {卒業|そつぎょう}にあたって (on
graduating), {入社|にゅうしゃ}にあたって. The moment is a positive or neutral turning point you
face deliberately. For an accident or a sudden bad event it doesn't fit:
{事故|じこ}の{際|さい}は (in the event of an accident), not にあたって.

### に{先立|さきだ}って or にあたって?

| | に{先立|さきだ}って | にあたって |
|---|---|---|
| core idea | before the event, in time order | at the moment of facing it |
| what follows | an action done earlier (a rehearsal, an announcement) | an attitude, a preparation, a greeting |
| typical | {開会|かいかい}に{先立|さきだ}って{国歌|こっか}を{歌|うた}う | {開会|かいかい}にあたって{一言|ひとこと}{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます |

Often both work, with a small change of focus: {工事|こうじ}を{始|はじ}めるに{先立|さきだ}って (strictly before
it starts) and {工事|こうじ}を{始|はじ}めるにあたって (as we get ready to start it) are both natural.

## On the occasion, when (formal): 〜に{際|さい}して, 〜{際|さい}(は)

〜に{際|さい}して (written: に{際|さい}し; before a noun: に{際|さい}しての) means "on the occasion of,
when": the event is special (a move, a wedding, an emergency, signing a contract). N3 lesson 29
taught 〜{際|さい}は in notices; に{際|さい}して is its more formal, more "special occasion" partner.

{結婚|けっこん}に{際|さい}して、{多|おお}くの{方|かた}からお{祝|いわ}いをいただきました。 — On our marriage we received gifts from many people.
{契約|けいやく}に{際|さい}しては、{身分|みぶん}{証明書|しょうめいしょ}が{必要|ひつよう}です。 — When signing the contract, you'll need ID.
{離陸|りりく}に{際|さい}して、シートベルトをご{着用|ちゃくよう}ください。 — Please wear your seat belt for take-off.

〜{際|さい}(は) / 〜の{際|さい}(に) is the everyday formal "when", common in notices and in staff
announcements. It suits routine events too, which に{際|さい}して doesn't:

お{帰|かえ}りの{際|さい}は、お{忘|わす}れ{物|もの}のないようご{注意|ちゅうい}ください。 — When you leave, please take care not to leave anything behind.
{次回|じかい}ご{来店|らいてん}の{際|さい}に、このカードをお{持|も}ちください。 — Please bring this card on your next visit.

| Form | Example | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| 〜{際|さい}(は) / 〜の{際|さい}(に) | お{帰|かえ}りの{際|さい}は | formal "when"; notices, staff |
| 〜に{際|さい}して(は) / に{際|さい}し | ご{入学|にゅうがく}に{際|さい}して | a special occasion; very formal |
| 〜にあたって / にあたり | ご{入学|にゅうがく}にあたって | facing a new start; speeches |

に{際|さい}して and にあたって overlap a lot, and many sentences take either. A rough guide: にあたって
looks ahead to what the new start needs ({準備|じゅんび}, {決意|けつい}); に{際|さい}して points at the
moment itself and what is done then. If you're unsure in a notice, 〜の{際|さい}は is the safe choice.

## With … ahead: 〜を{前|まえ}に(して)

〜を{前|まえ}に(して) is less formal: "with … coming up, just before". It often describes feelings
or a situation, and can also be literal ("in front of").

{卒業|そつぎょう}を{前|まえ}に、{友|とも}だちと{寄|よ}せ{書|が}きを{作|つく}った。 — With graduation coming up, my friends and I made a card everyone signed.
{大勢|おおぜい}の{人|ひと}を{前|まえ}にして{話|はな}すのは、{今|いま}でも{緊張|きんちょう}する。 — Speaking in front of a lot of people still makes me nervous.

It doesn't need an "important" event: {旅行|りょこう}を{前|まえ}に{新|あたら}しい{靴|くつ}を{買|か}った (I bought new shoes
just before my trip) is ordinary speech.

## On the occasion (letters): 〜{折|おり}(に)

{折|おり} is an old word for "time, occasion". 〜{折|おり}(に) / 〜{折|おり}には is "when (there's a
chance)", polite and mostly written: letters, emails to clients, speeches. Recognize it; you'll
rarely need to produce it.

お{近|ちか}くにお{越|こ}しの{折|おり}には、ぜひお{立|た}ち{寄|よ}りください。 — If you're ever in the area, please do drop in.
{先日|せんじつ}お{会|あ}いした{折|おり}に{伺|うかが}ったお{話|はなし}を、{今|いま}もよく{思|おも}い{出|だ}します。 — I often think of what you told me when we met the other day.

In seasonal greetings it means "this time of year": {寒|さむ}さの{厳|きび}しい{折|おり}、どうぞお{体|からだ}を
{大切|たいせつ}になさってください (in this harsh cold, please take care of yourself). You'll also see the old
form {寒|さむ}さ{厳|きび}しき{折|おり}.

## Who uses which

| Pattern | Speeches | Notices | Letters | News | Conversation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| に{先立|さきだ}って / に{先立|さきだ}ち | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ | rare |
| にあたって / にあたり | ✓ (very common) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | formal talk |
| に{際|さい}して / に{際|さい}し | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | rare |
| 〜{際|さい}は / 〜の{際|さい}に | | ✓ (very common) | ✓ | | staff to customers |
| を{前|まえ}に(して) | ✓ | | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| {折|おり}に / {折|おり}には | ✓ | | ✓ (very common) | | rare |

In casual speech, all of these turn back into {前|まえ}に and とき: {結婚|けっこん}するとき、みんなにお{祝|いわ}いを
もらった.

## Events, prizes and thanks

| Topic | Words |
|---|---|
| holding events | {開催|かいさい}する, {主催|しゅさい}する, {主催者|しゅさいしゃ}, {催|もよお}し, {催|もよお}す, イベント, セレモニー, {例年|れいねん} |
| ceremonies | {開会式|かいかいしき}, {閉会式|へいかいしき}, {式次第|しきしだい}, {参列|さんれつ}する, しかい, {祝辞|しゅくじ}, {謝辞|しゃじ}, {晴|は}れ{着|ぎ}, {礼服|れいふく}, {晴|は}れ{舞台|ぶたい}, {門出|かどで} |
| invitations | {招|まね}き, {招待券|しょうたいけん}, {案内状|あんないじょう}, {出欠|しゅっけつ}, {誘導|ゆうどう}する |
| prizes | {賞|しょう}, {大賞|たいしょう}, {賞金|しょうきん}, {賞品|しょうひん}, {賞状|しょうじょう}, {景品|けいひん}, トロフィー, {受賞|じゅしょう}する, {受賞者|じゅしょうしゃ}, {授賞式|じゅしょうしき}, {入賞|にゅうしょう}する, {授与|じゅよ}する, ひょうしょうする, {候補|こうほ} |
| thanks and apology | {謝罪|しゃざい}する, {謝礼|しゃれい}, {感謝状|かんしゃじょう}, {礼状|れいじょう}, {光栄|こうえい}, {心|こころ}より, {何卒|なにとぞ}, {拝借|はいしゃく}する, {了承|りょうしょう}する |
| gifts | {贈|おく}り{物|もの}, {寄贈|きぞう}する, {寄付|きふ}する, {花束|はなたば}, {寄|よ}せ{書|が}き, {贈答品|ぞうとうひん}, {内祝|うちいわ}い, {水引|みずひき}, ギフト |

Notes:

- {受賞|じゅしょう} (receiving a prize) and {授賞|じゅしょう} (giving one) sound the same. The winner
  {受賞|じゅしょう}する; the ceremony is the {授賞式|じゅしょうしき}.
- {謝罪|しゃざい}する is public and formal (a company, a minister); people simply {謝|あやま}る.
- {参列|さんれつ}する is for ceremonies, weddings and funerals; for a class or a meeting you
  {出席|しゅっせき}する.
- {贈|おく}る is "to give (a gift, a prize, words)"; {送|おく}る is "to send". They're the same word
  おくる with two kanji: {花束|はなたば}を{贈|おく}る, {荷物|にもつ}を{送|おく}る.
- {賞品|しょうひん} (a prize you win) and {商品|しょうひん} (goods for sale) are homophones.

## Formal letters

A formal Japanese letter has a fixed shape. You don't need to write one at N2, but you need to
read one, and the reading below is one.

| Part | What it does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| opening word | "Dear …" | はいけい (its second kanji is outside N2); {前略|ぜんりゃく} for a short letter that skips the next part |
| seasonal greeting ({時候|じこう}のあいさつ) | a line on the season | {春|はる}らしい{暖|あたた}かな{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いております。 |
| asking after the reader | wishing them well | {皆様|みなさま}にはお{元気|げんき}でお{過|す}ごしのことと{存|ぞん}じます。 |
| main text | starts with さて | さて、このたびは… |
| closing greeting | a wish for the reader's health | どうぞお{体|からだ}を{大切|たいせつ}になさってください。 |
| closing word | "Yours sincerely" | {敬具|けいぐ} (after はいけい), {草々|そうそう} (after {前略|ぜんりゃく}) |

The closing greeting is often a wish for the reader's health, such as
{寒|さむ}さの{厳|きび}しい{折|おり}、どうぞご{自愛|じあい}ください (in this cold season, please look after yourself).
{自愛|じあい} is "taking care of oneself", a letter word. {追伸|ついしん} (P.S.) comes after the closing word.

Some seasonal openings, in this course's wording (real letters vary a great deal):

| Season | Opening line |
|---|---|
| spring | さくらの{便|たよ}りが{聞|き}かれるころとなりました。 (さくら: its kanji is outside N2) |
| summer | {暑|あつ}い{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いておりますが… ({暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}い season) |
| autumn | {秋|あき}も{深|ふか}まってまいりました。 |
| winter | {寒|さむ}さが{一段|いちだん}と{厳|きび}しくなってまいりました。 ({寒中見舞|かんちゅうみま}い after New Year) |

{四季|しき} (the four seasons) is the theme of these lines; {季|き} is lesson 6's kanji, but
きせつ (season) stays in kana because its second kanji isn't on the list.

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji: holding events, prizes and gifts, thanks, and the humble verbs of letters.

### Events and celebrations

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 催 | hold (an event); urge | サイ | もよお(す) | 13 | {開催|かいさい}, {主催|しゅさい}, {催|もよお}し, {催|もよお}す |
| 祝 | celebrate | シュク | いわ(う) | 9 | {祝|いわ}う, お{祝|いわ}い, {祝日|しゅくじつ}, {祝辞|しゅくじ}, {祝電|しゅくでん}, {祝福|しゅくふく}, {内祝|うちいわ}い |
| 季 | season | キ | — | 8 | {四季|しき}, {季語|きご} |

- {祝|いわ}う (N3), お{祝|いわ}い (N4) and {祝日|しゅくじつ} (N5) are now written with kanji.
- {季語|きご} (a season word in a haiku, N3) gets its kanji. きせつ (season) stays in kana: its
  second kanji is outside N2.
- 催 also means "urge": さいそくする (to press for a reply) has 催 and an off-list kanji, so it's in
  kana.

### Prizes and gifts

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 賞 | prize, praise | ショウ | — | 15 | {賞|しょう}, {賞金|しょうきん}, {賞品|しょうひん}, {受賞|じゅしょう}, {大賞|たいしょう}, {賞状|しょうじょう} |
| 贈 | give (a gift) | ゾウ | おく(る) | 18 | {贈|おく}る, {贈|おく}り{物|もの}, {寄贈|きぞう}, {贈答品|ぞうとうひん} |

- 賞 and 贈 both contain the "shell" (貝, money), like N3's 財 and 資: valuable things. It sits at the bottom of 賞 and on the left of 贈.
- 贈 has 18 strokes, the most in this lesson.

### Thanks, introductions and requests

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 謝 | thank; apologize | シャ | あやま(る) | 17 | {謝|あやま}る, {感謝|かんしゃ}, {謝罪|しゃざい}, {謝礼|しゃれい}, {謝辞|しゃじ}, {感謝状|かんしゃじょう} |
| 紹 | introduce | ショウ | — | 11 | {紹介|しょうかい}, {紹介状|しょうかいじょう} |
| 介 | between; help | カイ | — | 4 | {紹介|しょうかい}; {介護|かいご} (care, lesson 26) |
| 依 | depend on; request | イ | — | 8 | {依頼|いらい}, {依頼状|いらいじょう} |
| 誘 | invite; lead | ユウ | さそ(う) | 14 | {誘|さそ}う, {誘|さそ}い, {誘導|ゆうどう} |

- {謝|あやま}る (N4), {感謝|かんしゃ} (N3), {依頼|いらい}する (N3), {誘|さそ}う and {誘|さそ}い (N3) are now written
  with kanji.
- 謝 covers both thanking and apologizing: {感謝|かんしゃ} is thanks, {謝罪|しゃざい} is apology. Both are
  ways of "acknowledging what you owe".
- 紹 and 介 almost always appear together, in {紹介|しょうかい}.

### Humble verbs

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 伺 | visit, ask (humble) | — | うかが(う) | 7 | {伺|うかが}う |
| 承 | accept, hear (humble) | ショウ | うけたまわ(る) | 8 | {承|うけたまわ}る, {承知|しょうち}, {了承|りょうしょう} |
| 拝 | worship; humble prefix | ハイ | おが(む) | 8 | {拝見|はいけん}, {拝借|はいしゃく}, {参拝|さんぱい}, {拝|おが}む |

- {伺|うかが}う (N4), {承|うけたまわ}る and {承知|しょうち}する (N3), {拝見|はいけん}する (N4) and {拝|おが}む (N3) are
  now written with kanji. 伺 is almost only used in {伺|うかが}う; learn it by its kun'yomi.
- 拝 before a verb makes it humble: {拝見|はいけん}する (see), {拝借|はいしゃく}する (borrow). はいけい
  (Dear…) has 拝 and an off-list kanji, so it's written in kana.
- うけたまわ(る) is the longest kun'yomi in this lesson: five kana before the okurigana.

Memory notes:

- 催 is a person (亻) beside a mountain (山) with a bird (隹) under it: someone calling people
  together on a hilltop, holding an event.
- 祝 is the altar (礻) and a kneeling person with a big mouth (兄): praying out loud to celebrate.
- 賞 has a roof with rays of light over the shell (貝, money): something valuable shown off, a prize.
- 贈 is the shell (貝, money and goods) next to a shape like a stacked steamer: goods piled up to give.
- 謝 is words (言), a body (身) and a hand (寸): bowing your body and saying "thank you" or "sorry".
- 紹 is thread (糸) beside a sword over a mouth (口): a thread and a call that draw people together.
- 介 is a person standing between two lines: someone in the middle, a go-between.
- 依 is a person (亻) and clothes (衣): relying on someone as on your clothes.
- 誘 is words (言) and a grain plant (禾) over a bent shape: tempting words that lead someone along.
- 伺 is a person (亻) beside an official's mouth (口) under a roof: calling on someone important, humbly.
- 承 is hands raised to receive something from above: accepting humbly.
- 拝 is a hand (扌) beside two crossed stalks: hands together in prayer.
- 季 is grain (禾) over a child (子): the young crop of each season.

```trace
催祝賞贈謝紹介依誘伺承拝季
```

## Dialogue: getting ready for the award ceremony

みずき works at a city cultural centre. Tomorrow is the award ceremony of the city's photo contest,
and her colleague けんた is checking the arrangements with her. (Polite workplace speech, with a
little casual Japanese between colleagues.)

```dialogue
# The day before the ceremony
けんた: {明日|あした}の{授賞式|じゅしょうしき}、{準備|じゅんび}はどうですか。
= How are the preparations for tomorrow's award ceremony?
みずき: だいたい{終|お}わりました。{式|しき}に{先立|さきだ}って、{十時|じゅうじ}から{会場|かいじょう}で{最後|さいご}の{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせがあります。
= Mostly done. Before the ceremony, there's a final meeting at the venue from ten.
けんた: {受賞者|じゅしょうしゃ}の{方|かた}には{連絡|れんらく}しましたか。
= Have you contacted the prizewinners?
みずき: ええ。{全員|ぜんいん}から{出欠|しゅっけつ}のお{返事|へんじ}をいただきました。{大賞|たいしょう}の{方|かた}は、ご{家族|かぞく}といらっしゃるそうです。
= Yes. Everyone's let us know whether they're coming. The grand-prize winner is coming with their family.
けんた: それはよかった。{会場|かいじょう}に{入|はい}る{際|さい}の{誘導|ゆうどう}は？
= That's good. What about guiding people when they come in?
みずき: {入口|いりぐち}で{受付|うけつけ}をしたら、{係|かかり}の{人|ひと}が{席|せき}までご{案内|あんない}します。
= Once they've checked in at the entrance, staff will show them to their seats.
けんた: しかいは{田中|たなか}さんでしたっけ。
= The MC is Tanaka, isn't it?
みずき: はい。{開会|かいかい}にあたって{市長|しちょう}があいさつをして、そのあと{賞状|しょうじょう}と{賞品|しょうひん}の{授与|じゅよ}です。
= Yes. The mayor gives a speech to open the event, and then the certificates and prizes are presented.
けんた: {賞品|しょうひん}って{何|なん}でしたっけ。
= What were the prizes again?
みずき: {大賞|たいしょう}はカメラと{賞金|しょうきん}{十万円|じゅうまんえん}、{入賞|にゅうしょう}した{方|かた}には{商品券|しょうひんけん}です。
= For the grand prize, a camera and 100,000 yen; for the other winners, gift vouchers.
けんた: なるほど。あ、{式次第|しきしだい}、{一部|いちぶ}もらえますか。{受賞者|じゅしょうしゃ}のお{名前|なまえ}を{確認|かくにん}しておきたいので。
= I see. Oh, could I have a copy of the programme? I'd like to check the winners' names.
みずき: どうぞ。{読|よ}み{方|かた}が{難|むずか}しいお{名前|なまえ}には、ふりがなを{付|つ}けておきました。
= Here you are. I've put readings next to the names that are hard to read.
けんた: さすがですね。じゃあ、{本番|ほんばん}を{前|まえ}に、{今日|きょう}は{早|はや}めに{帰|かえ}りましょう。
= Impressive. Well then, with the big day coming, let's go home early today.
みずき: そうですね。{式|しき}が{終|お}わったら、{皆|みな}さんにお{礼状|れいじょう}も{書|か}かなきゃ。
= Yes. And once the ceremony's over, I'll have to write thank-you letters to everyone.
```

{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせ = a planning meeting (N3); {係|かかり} = the staff in charge; 〜でしたっけ = "was it…?"
(checking something you half remember). Count the occasions: {式|しき}に{先立|さきだ}って (before),
{入|はい}る{際|さい}の (when), {開会|かいかい}にあたって (on opening), {本番|ほんばん}を{前|まえ}に (with the big
day ahead).

## Reading: a letter of thanks

A prizewinner writes to the organizer of a photo contest after the ceremony. (Formal letter,
です/ます.)

> はいけい
>
> {新緑|しんりょく}の{美|うつく}しいきせつとなりました。{皆様|みなさま}にはますますお{元気|げんき}でお{過|す}ごしのことと{存|ぞん}じます。
>
> さて、{先日|せんじつ}の{授賞式|じゅしょうしき}では{大変|たいへん}お{世話|せわ}になりました。このたびは{思|おも}いがけず{大賞|たいしょう}をいただき、{心|こころ}より{感謝|かんしゃ}{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。{式|しき}に{先立|さきだ}って{会場|かいじょう}の{皆様|みなさま}が{温|あたた}かく{迎|むか}えてくださったおかげで、{緊張|きんちょう}していた{私|わたし}も{落|お}ち{着|つ}いてステージに{上|あ}がることができました。また、{家族|かぞく}の{席|せき}までご{用意|ようい}いただき、{母|はは}も{大変|たいへん}{喜|よろこ}んでおりました。
>
> {写真|しゃしん}を{始|はじ}めて{三十年|さんじゅうねん}になりますが、{賞|しょう}をいただいたのは{初|はじ}めてです。{受賞|じゅしょう}にあたって、これまで{撮|と}ってきた{写真|しゃしん}を{見直|みなお}してみました。{昔|むかし}の{写真|しゃしん}には、{今|いま}はもうない{店|みせ}や{橋|はし}が{写|うつ}っていて、{町|まち}の{歴史|れきし}を{改|あらた}めて{感|かん}じました。いただいた{賞金|しょうきん}の{一部|いちぶ}は、{市|し}の{図書館|としょかん}に{写真集|しゃしんしゅう}を{寄贈|きぞう}する{費用|ひよう}に{使|つか}わせていただきたいと{考|かんが}えております。
>
> {授賞式|じゅしょうしき}で{選考|せんこう}{委員|いいん}の{先生|せんせい}がおっしゃった「{写真|しゃしん}は{町|まち}の{記録|きろく}でもある」というお{言葉|ことば}は、{今|いま}も{心|こころ}に{残|のこ}っております。これからは{町|まち}の{小|ちい}さな{変化|へんか}も{記録|きろく}するつもりで、カメラを{持|も}って{歩|ある}きたいと{思|おも}います。
>
> {来年|らいねん}の{展示会|てんじかい}の{際|さい}には、ぜひお{手伝|てつだ}いさせてください。お{近|ちか}くにお{越|こ}しの{折|おり}には、{私|わたし}の{小|ちい}さな{写真|しゃしん}{教室|きょうしつ}にもお{立|た}ち{寄|よ}りいただければ{幸|さいわ}いです。
>
> きせつの{変|か}わり{目|め}ですので、どうぞお{体|からだ}を{大切|たいせつ}になさってください。まずは{書中|しょちゅう}にてお{礼|れい}{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
>
> {敬具|けいぐ}

{新緑|しんりょく} = fresh green leaves (early summer); {写真集|しゃしんしゅう} = a photo book; {書中|しょちゅう}にて =
by letter (formal); きせつの{変|か}わり{目|め} = the turn of the seasons. Real letters write きせつ with
kanji; this course keeps it in kana because its second kanji is outside N2.

1. Why does the writer say they could go up on stage calmly?
2. What did the writer do on receiving the prize, and what did they notice?
3. What will part of the prize money be used for?
4. What does the writer offer to do next year?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Because before the ceremony the staff welcomed them warmly ({式|しき}に{先立|さきだ}って…{温|あたた}かく{迎|むか}えてくださったおかげで).
2. They looked back through the photos they'd taken over the years ({受賞|じゅしょう}にあたって…{見直|みなお}してみました) and
   felt the town's history again: the old photos show shops and a bridge that no longer exist.
3. To pay for donating photo books to the city library.
4. To help at next year's exhibition ({展示会|てんじかい}の{際|さい}には…お{手伝|てつだ}いさせてください).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Dear …,

The season of beautiful fresh green has come. I trust you are all keeping well.

Thank you very much for all you did at the award ceremony the other day. I was quite unexpectedly
given the grand prize, and I'm sincerely grateful. Thanks to everyone at the venue welcoming me so
warmly before the ceremony, even I, nervous as I was, could go up on stage calmly. You also kindly
arranged seats for my family, and my mother was delighted.

I've been taking photographs for thirty years, but this is the first time I've won a prize. On
receiving it, I looked back through the photos I've taken. The old ones show shops and a bridge
that are gone now, and I felt the history of the town anew. I would like to use part of the prize
money to pay for donating photo books to the city library.

What one of the judges said at the ceremony, "a photograph is also a record of the town", has
stayed with me. From now on I'd like to walk about with my camera, meaning to record
even the small changes in the town.

When the exhibition is held next year, please let me help. And if you're ever in the area, I'd be
glad if you dropped in at my small photography class.

The seasons are changing, so please take good care of yourselves. For now, let me thank you by
letter.

Yours sincerely,

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{開会|かいかい}に{先立|さきだ}ちまして、{主催者|しゅさいしゃ}よりごあいさつ{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
= Before we begin, a few words from the organizers.
{受賞|じゅしょう}にあたり、{一言|ひとこと}お{礼|れい}を{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
= On receiving this award, let me say a few words of thanks.
ご{利用|りよう}の{際|さい}は、{係員|かかりいん}にお{声|こえ}がけください。
= When you use it, please speak to a member of staff.
お{近|ちか}くにお{越|こ}しの{折|おり}には、ぜひお{立|た}ち{寄|よ}りください。
= If you're ever in the area, please drop in.
{本日|ほんじつ}はお{招|まね}きいただき、ありがとうございます。
= Thank you for inviting me today.
```

{先立|さきだ}ちまして is the polite ます form inside the sentence, common in speeches.

## Common mistakes

- に{先立|さきだ}って for everyday "before": ×{朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}に{先立|さきだ}って{顔|かお}を{洗|あら}う sounds
  absurdly grand. Use 〜{前|まえ}に.
- にあたって with a bad, unplanned event: ×{地震|じしん}にあたって. Use 〜の{際|さい}は
  ({地震|じしん}の{際|さい}は、{机|つくえ}の{下|した}に{入|はい}ってください).
- Forgetting の before {際|さい} after a noun: ×ご{利用|りよう}{際|さい}は → ご{利用|りよう}の{際|さい}は. After a verb, no
  の: お{帰|かえ}りになる{際|さい}は.
- Mixing up {受賞|じゅしょう} (receive) and {授賞|じゅしょう} (award): the winner {受賞|じゅしょう}する; the
  organizers hold a {授賞式|じゅしょうしき}.
- {参列|さんれつ}する for a meeting: you {出席|しゅっせき}する at a meeting; {参列|さんれつ} is for ceremonies.
- Writing {送|おく}り{物|もの} for a gift: the gift is {贈|おく}り{物|もの}.

## Key points

- 〜に{先立|さきだ}って / に{先立|さきだ}ち / に{先立|さきだ}つ + noun: before an important event (formal).
- 〜にあたって / にあたり: at an important moment, usually a new start; speeches and greetings.
- 〜に{際|さい}して / に{際|さい}し: on a special occasion; 〜(の){際|さい}は: the formal "when" of notices.
- 〜を{前|まえ}に(して): with … ahead, or in front of; everyday as well as formal.
- 〜{折|おり}(に): on the occasion (letters); {寒|さむ}さの{厳|きび}しい{折|おり} in seasonal greetings.
- Formal letters: はいけい … {敬具|けいぐ}, {前略|ぜんりゃく} … {草々|そうそう}, a seasonal greeting first.
- New kanji: 催 祝 賞 贈 謝 紹 介 依 誘 伺 承 拝 季. Write {伺|うかが}う, {承|うけたまわ}る, {拝見|はいけん}する,
  {祝|いわ}う, {誘|さそ}う, {謝|あやま}る, {感謝|かんしゃ}, {依頼|いらい} with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: As soon as and depending on: 次第, た上で, 末に, あげく
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 6 placed an action before or at an important occasion. This lesson is about what comes
after: "as soon as", "only after checking", "after long effort, finally" and "after all that,
in the end (sadly)". Along the way, one small word, {次第|しだい}, also gives you "it depends on".

{書類|しょるい}が{届|とど}き{次第|しだい}、{手続|てつづ}きを{始|はじ}めます。 — We'll start the procedure as soon as the documents arrive.
{内容|ないよう}を{確認|かくにん}した{上|うえ}で、{署名|しょめい}してください。 — Please sign after you've checked the contents.
{悩|なや}んだ{末|すえ}に、{契約|けいやく}を{更新|こうしん}しないことにした。 — After a lot of agonizing, I decided not to renew the contract.
{迷|まよ}ったあげく、{結局|けっきょく}{何|なに}も{買|か}わなかった。 — After all that dithering, I ended up buying nothing.

The theme is contracts, certificates and official documents: signing and stamping, registering,
proving who you are, copies and originals, savings, tickets. N4 and N3 gave you the forms and the
counter ({申込書|もうしこみしょ}, {記入|きにゅう}, {窓口|まどぐち}); this lesson gives you the paper itself.
{契約|けいやく}, {届|とど}く, {届|とど}ける, {提出|ていしゅつ}, {条件|じょうけん}, {簡単|かんたん}, {記録|きろく}, {登録|とうろく},
{預|あず}ける and {預|あず}かる are now written with kanji.

## As soon as: ます stem + {次第|しだい}

ます stem + {次第|しだい} means "as soon as A happens, (I'll) do B". It's formal: shops, offices,
business emails and announcements.

{商品|しょうひん}が{入荷|にゅうか}し{次第|しだい}、ご{連絡|れんらく}いたします。 — We'll contact you as soon as the item comes in.
{会議|かいぎ}が{終|お}わり{次第|しだい}、{議事録|ぎじろく}をお{送|おく}りします。 — I'll send you the minutes as soon as the meeting is over.
{準備|じゅんび}ができ{次第|しだい}、{出発|しゅっぱつ}しましょう。 — Let's leave as soon as we're ready.

Nouns of action can take it directly: {到着|とうちゃく}{次第|しだい} (as soon as it arrives), {決定|けってい}{次第|しだい}
(as soon as it's decided).

Two limits, both because 〜{次第|しだい} looks ahead to something someone will *do*:

- B is an intention, a request or a plan: ご{連絡|れんらく}します, お{知|し}らせください, {出発|しゅっぱつ}しましょう.
  For a past fact, use 〜とすぐ(に) or 〜たとたん: {駅|えき}に{着|つ}くとすぐ、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}した.
- A is something expected to happen. For the unexpected, use N3's 〜たとたん.

〜たらすぐ is the everyday equivalent: {届|とど}いたらすぐ{連絡|れんらく}するね.

## It depends on: noun + {次第|しだい}

After a noun, {次第|しだい} means "depends on": the noun decides the outcome.

| Form | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| N + {次第|しだい}だ / です | {結果|けっか}はあなた{次第|しだい}です。 | The result is up to you. |
| N + {次第|しだい}で | {天気|てんき}{次第|しだい}で、{予定|よてい}を{変|か}えます。 | We'll change the plan depending on the weather. |
| N + {次第|しだい}では | {条件|じょうけん}{次第|しだい}では、{契約|けいやく}を{見直|みなお}すこともある。 | Depending on the terms, we may review the contract. |

{次第|しだい}では adds "in some cases": a possibility, often an unwelcome one.
It works for good outcomes too: {努力|どりょく}{次第|しだい}で、だれでも{上手|じょうず}になれる (with effort, anyone can get good at it).

〜によって (N3) overlaps: {天気|てんき}によって{予定|よてい}を{変|か}える. {次第|しだい} stresses that this one thing
decides everything; によって simply says the outcome varies with it.

## That's how it is (formal): 〜{次第|しだい}です

In formal letters and emails, 〜{次第|しだい}です after the plain form explains the circumstances: "that's
why…", "hence…". It often ends the explanation of why you're writing.

{先日|せんじつ}{提出|ていしゅつ}した{書類|しょるい}に{誤|あやま}りがありましたので、ご{連絡|れんらく}した{次第|しだい}です。 — I found a mistake in the documents I submitted the other day, which is why I'm contacting you.
こういう{次第|しだい}で、{契約|けいやく}を{解約|かいやく}させていただきたいと{存|ぞん}じます。 — This being so, I would like to cancel the contract.

Also: {事|こと}の{次第|しだい} (how things came about), {式次第|しきしだい} (a ceremony's programme, lesson 6), and
N3's adverb {次第|しだい}に (gradually).

| Use | Form | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| as soon as | ます stem / action noun + {次第|しだい} | {届|とど}き{次第|しだい} |
| depends on | noun + {次第|しだい}だ / {次第|しだい}で(は) | {天気|てんき}{次第|しだい}で |
| that's how it is | plain form + {次第|しだい}です | ご{連絡|れんらく}した{次第|しだい}です |
| gradually | {次第|しだい}に (N3) | {次第|しだい}に{寒|さむ}くなる |

## After doing it properly: 〜た{上|うえ}で

> **Review (N3 lesson 28).** 〜{上|うえ}で with the dictionary form or a noun means "in doing, for the
> purpose of": {生活|せいかつ}する{上|うえ}で{大切|たいせつ}なこと (what matters in daily life).

With the た form (or noun + の), 〜た{上|うえ}で means "after doing A (properly), then B": A is a
necessary step before B. Notices and contracts use it constantly.

{内容|ないよう}をよく{読|よ}んだ{上|うえ}で、{署名|しょめい}してください。 — Read the contents carefully, then sign.
{家族|かぞく}と{相談|そうだん}した{上|うえ}で、お{返事|へんじ}します。 — I'll answer once I've talked it over with my family.
{面接|めんせつ}の{上|うえ}で、{採用|さいよう}を{決|き}めます。 — We'll decide on hiring after an interview.

〜てから is the plain "after"; 〜た{上|うえ}で says A is done on purpose so that B can be done
properly. For a simple sequence of events, use てから: {家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}ってから{食事|しょくじ}をした, not
た{上|うえ}で.

〜た{上|うえ}での + noun: {十分|じゅうぶん}{考|かんが}えた{上|うえ}での{結論|けつろん} (a conclusion reached after careful
thought).

## In terms of: noun + {上|じょう}

{上|じょう} after a noun means "in terms of, from the point of view of". It's a suffix, like N3's 〜{的|てき},
and very common in writing.

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {契約上|けいやくじょう} | under the contract |
| {法律上|ほうりつじょう} | legally |
| {健康上|けんこうじょう}の{理由|りゆう} | health reasons |
| {仕事上|しごとじょう}の{付|つ}き{合|あ}い | business relationships |
| {歴史上|れきしじょう} | in history |
| {書類上|しょるいじょう}は | on paper |
| インターネット{上|じょう}で | on the internet |

{契約上|けいやくじょう}、{途中|とちゅう}で{解約|かいやく}すると{違約金|いやくきん}がかかる。 — Under the contract, if you cancel partway through there's a fee.
{書類上|しょるいじょう}は{問題|もんだい}ないが、{実際|じっさい}にはだれも{住|す}んでいない。 — On paper there's no problem, but in fact nobody lives there.

Careful with the reading: {上|じょう} here, {上|うえ} in た{上|うえ}で. A listening question can turn on it.

## After long effort, finally: 〜た{末|すえ}(に)

{末|すえ} is "the end (of a period)": {今月|こんげつ}の{末|すえ}, {年末|ねんまつ}. 〜た{末|すえ}(に) / N の{末|すえ}(に) means
"after a long process (of effort, thought, discussion), finally": the result can be good or bad,
but it was reached the hard way. Written and formal.

{何度|なんど}も{話|はな}し{合|あ}った{末|すえ}に、{両社|りょうしゃ}は{契約|けいやく}を{交|か}わした。 — After many rounds of talks, the two companies signed a contract.
{長|なが}い{話|はな}し{合|あ}いの{末|すえ}、{家賃|やちん}を{下|さ}げてもらえた。 — After long talks, I got them to lower the rent.
{悩|なや}みに{悩|なや}んだ{末|すえ}、{大学院|だいがくいん}に{進|すす}むことにした。 — After agonizing over it for ages, I decided to go on to graduate school.

〜の{末|すえ} also takes nouns of effort:
{努力|どりょく}の{末|すえ}, {苦労|くろう}の{末|すえ}, {検討|けんとう}の{末|すえ}.

## After all that (sadly): 〜たあげく

〜たあげく(に) / N のあげく also means "after a long process", but the process was tiring or
troublesome, and the result is *bad, disappointing or annoying*. It's kana in this course.

{二時間|にじかん}も{迷|まよ}ったあげく、{何|なに}も{買|か}わずに{帰|かえ}った。 — After two hours of dithering, I went home without buying anything.
{店員|てんいん}と{言|い}い{争|あらそ}ったあげく、{返品|へんぴん}を{断|ことわ}られた。 — After a long argument with the shop assistant, my return was refused.
{何度|なんど}も{書類|しょるい}を{出|だ}し{直|なお}したあげく、{結局|けっきょく}しんせいは{通|とお}らなかった。 — After resubmitting the papers again and again, the application still didn't go through. (しんせい: its second kanji is outside N2.)

あげくの{果|は}てに ("and to cap it all") piles one more bad thing on top: recognize it.

### {末|すえ}に or あげく?

| | 〜た{末|すえ}(に) | 〜たあげく |
|---|---|---|
| process | long effort, thought or talks | long, tiring or troublesome |
| result | good or bad; reached at last | bad or disappointing |
| register | written, formal | written and spoken |
| example | {努力|どりょく}した{末|すえ}に{合格|ごうかく}した (passed, after real effort) | {迷|まよ}ったあげく{買|か}わなかった (didn't buy, after all that) |

With a good result, あげく sounds wrong: ×{努力|どりょく}したあげく、{合格|ごうかく}した. With a bad result,
{末|すえ}に is possible in writing ({検討|けんとう}の{末|すえ}、{計画|けいかく}は{中止|ちゅうし}された: after review, the plan was
dropped), but あげく adds the speaker's frustration.

## Not until: 〜てからでないと (review)

> **Review (N3 lesson 2).** 〜てからでないと / 〜てからでなければ: "not until A (can B)". The second half
> is negative or difficult: {契約書|けいやくしょ}を{読|よ}んでからでないと、{署名|しょめい}できません (I can't sign until I've
> read the contract).

〜た{上|うえ}で and 〜てからでないと often describe the same rule from two sides:
{確認|かくにん}した{上|うえ}で{署名|しょめい}してください (check, then sign) and
{確認|かくにん}してからでないと{署名|しょめい}できません (you can't sign before you've checked).

Notes:

- Japan still uses personal seals: N5's はんこ. A {実印|じついん} is registered at the city office for
  big contracts; an everyday one is a {認|みと}め{印|いん}. Forms say ご{署名|しょめい}またはご{押印|おういん} (sign or
  stamp).
- {届|とど}け / {届|とど}け{出|で} is any form you hand in to an office: {出生届|しゅっしょうとどけ} (a birth),

- {戸籍|こせき} is the family register: Japanese citizens' births, marriages and deaths are recorded in
  it. {籍|せき}を{入|い}れる is to register a marriage.
- {解約|かいやく} ends a contract or an account; to cancel a booking you キャンセルする.
- 〜{券|けん} is a ticket or voucher; the everyday train ticket is still きっぷ.
- {証人|しょうにん} (a witness) is [しょうにん:0]; lesson 8's {商人|しょうにん} (a merchant) is [しょうにん:1].

Memory notes:

- 契 is a cut mark (the top part, notches on a tally) over a big person (大): a pledge cut into
  wood, a contract.
- 条 is a branch (木) with a walking foot on top: a long line, an item in a list.
- 証 is words (言) and 正 (correct, N4): words that show something is right, proof.
- 提 is a hand (扌) and a sun (日) over a walking foot: holding something up in the light to show it.
- 印 is a hand pressing down on a kneeling person: pressing a seal.
- 届 is a body (尸) with 由 (reason) under it: a message that reaches someone.
- 預 is 予 (in advance, N3) and a head (頁): putting something in someone's charge ahead of time.
- 籍 is bamboo (竹, the top: old records were bamboo strips) over a plough shape and a sun (日):
  the names of the farmers written on bamboo, a register.
- 録 is metal (金) and a shape like water dripping: carving a record into metal.
- 券 has a sword shape at the bottom: a ticket cut along the line.
- 複 is clothes (衤) and a doubled shape: clothes in layers, more than one.
- 略 is a field (田) and 各 (each): marking out each field roughly, in outline.
- 簡 is bamboo (竹) over 間 (between, N5): bamboo strips with gaps, a short note.

## Dialogue: signing a lease

ゆい is renting her first flat. At the estate agent's, しゅうへい goes through the contract with her.
(The agent speaks polite business Japanese; ゆい answers politely.)

```dialogue
# At the estate agent's
しゅうへい: では、{契約書|けいやくしょ}の{内容|ないよう}をご{説明|せつめい}いたします。ご{確認|かくにん}いただいた{上|うえ}で、こちらにご{署名|しょめい}とご{押印|おういん}をお{願|ねが}いします。
= Now, let me explain the contract. Once you've checked it, please sign and stamp here.
ゆい: はい。はんこは{持|も}ってきました。
= Right. I've brought my seal.
しゅうへい: ありがとうございます。{契約期間|けいやくきかん}は{二年|にねん}で、その{後|あと}は{更新|こうしん}できます。
= Thank you. The contract runs for two years, and after that it can be renewed.
ゆい: {途中|とちゅう}で{解約|かいやく}する{場合|ばあい}は、どうなりますか。
= What happens if I cancel partway through?
しゅうへい: {一|いっ}か{月|げつ}{前|まえ}までにご{連絡|れんらく}いただければ、{違約金|いやくきん}はかかりません。{契約上|けいやくじょう}、それより{遅|おそ}いと{一|いっ}か{月分|げつぶん}の{家賃|やちん}がかかります。
= If you tell us at least a month in advance, there's no cancellation fee. Under the contract, any later than that and it's one month's rent.
ゆい: {分|わ}かりました。{保証人|ほしょうにん}は{父|ちち}でもだいじょうぶですか。
= I see. Is it all right if my father is the guarantor?
しゅうへい: はい。お{父|とう}{様|さま}の{収入|しゅうにゅう}を{証明|しょうめい}する{書類|しょるい}を{一部|いちぶ}お{願|ねが}いします。コピーで{結構|けっこう}です。
= Yes. We'll need one document proving your father's income. A copy is fine.
ゆい: {父|ちち}に{頼|たの}んで、{届|とど}き{次第|しだい}お{送|おく}りします。
= I'll ask him and send it as soon as it arrives.
しゅうへい: お{願|ねが}いします。それから、{家賃|やちん}は{毎月|まいつき}{二十七日|にじゅうしちにち}に{口座|こうざ}から{引|ひ}き{落|お}としになります。
= Thank you. Also, the rent will be taken from your account on the 27th of every month.
ゆい: はい。……あの、ここの「{入居|にゅうきょ}{日|び}はしんさ{次第|しだい}」というのは？
= Right. …Um, what does this mean, "move-in date depends on the screening"?
しゅうへい: {保証|ほしょう}{会社|がいしゃ}のしんさ{次第|しだい}で、{入居|にゅうきょ}できる{日|ひ}が{決|き}まるということです。{通常|つうじょう}は{一週間|いっしゅうかん}ほどです。
= It means the day you can move in depends on the guarantee company's check. It usually takes about a week.
ゆい: そうですか。いろいろ{見|み}て{迷|まよ}った{末|すえ}に{決|き}めた{部屋|へや}なので、{早|はや}く{住|す}みたいです。
= I see. I chose this flat after looking at lots of places and agonizing, so I'd like to move in soon.
しゅうへい: {結果|けっか}が{出|で}{次第|しだい}、すぐにお{電話|でんわ}いたします。
= I'll call you as soon as we have the result.
```

{入居|にゅうきょ} = moving in (to a flat); しんさ = screening (its first kanji is outside N2);
{通常|つうじょう} = usually (formal).
{結構|けっこう}です here means "that's fine". Note {契約上|けいやくじょう} (in terms of the contract) and
{確認|かくにん}いただいた{上|うえ}で (after you've checked).

## Reading: before you sign

An explanatory column from a city's newsletter for new residents (だ/である style).

> {新生活|しんせいかつ}を{始|はじ}めると、{部屋|へや}を{借|か}りる、スマホを{買|か}う、{口座|こうざ}を{作|つく}るなど、{契約|けいやく}の{機会|きかい}が{一度|いちど}に{増|ふ}える。どれも{店|みせ}の{人|ひと}が{説明|せつめい}してくれるが、{説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}いた{上|うえ}で{署名|しょめい}したからといって、{内容|ないよう}を{理解|りかい}したとは{限|かぎ}らない。
>
> {市|し}の{消費|しょうひ}{生活|せいかつ}センターには、「{契約書|けいやくしょ}をよく{読|よ}まずにサインした」という{相談|そうだん}が{毎年|まいとし}{多|おお}く{寄|よ}せられる。たとえば、ある{大学生|だいがくせい}は{店員|てんいん}の{言|い}うまま{複数|ふくすう}のサービスに{加入|かにゅう}し、{二か月後|にかげつご}に{解約|かいやく}しようとしたところ、{違約金|いやくきん}が{必要|ひつよう}だと{言|い}われた。{店|みせ}に{何度|なんど}も{電話|でんわ}したあげく、{結局|けっきょく}{全額|ぜんがく}を{支払|しはら}うことになったという。{中|なか}には、{使|つか}っていないサービスの{料金|りょうきん}を{一年|いちねん}{以上|いじょう}{払|はら}い{続|つづ}けていた{人|ひと}もいる。
>
> {契約上|けいやくじょう}の{問題|もんだい}を{避|さ}けるには、まず{規約|きやく}の「{解約|かいやく}」と「{料金|りょうきん}」の{部分|ぶぶん}を{確認|かくにん}することだ。{契約期間|けいやくきかん}と{更新|こうしん}の{条件|じょうけん}も、{料金|りょうきん}と{同|おな}じくらい{大切|たいせつ}だ。{分|わ}からない{言葉|ことば}や{略語|りゃくご}があれば、その{場|ば}で{質問|しつもん}すればいい。{説明|せつめい}が{複雑|ふくざつ}すぎる{場合|ばあい}は、「{家族|かぞく}と{相談|そうだん}した{上|うえ}で{決|き}めます」と{言|い}って、{一度|いちど}{帰|かえ}るのも{一|ひと}つの{方法|ほうほう}である。
>
> また、{契約書|けいやくしょ}の{写|うつ}しは{必|かなら}ずもらっておくこと。{契約|けいやく}{内容|ないよう}は{店|みせ}{次第|しだい}で{大|おお}きく{違|ちが}うので、{後|あと}で{問題|もんだい}が{起|お}きたとき、{証明|しょうめい}になるのは{手元|てもと}の{書類|しょるい}だけだ。{困|こま}ったことがあれば、{一人|ひとり}で{悩|なや}まず、センターに{連絡|れんらく}してほしい。{相談|そうだん}は{無料|むりょう}で、{内容|ないよう}を{確認|かくにん}し{次第|しだい}、{担当者|たんとうしゃ}から{返事|へんじ}をする。

{消費|しょうひ}{生活|せいかつ}センター = a consumer advice centre; {言|い}うまま = just as (someone) says;
{加入|かにゅう} = joining, signing up; {手元|てもと} = at hand; {担当者|たんとうしゃ} = the person in charge.
〜からといって〜とは{限|かぎ}らない is lesson 1's.

1. What does the writer say about signing after hearing an explanation?
2. What happened to the university student?
3. What two parts of the terms should you check first?
4. Why should you keep a copy of the contract?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Signing after hearing the explanation doesn't necessarily mean you've understood the contents.
2. The student joined several services just as a shop assistant suggested, tried to cancel
   two months later, was told there was a cancellation fee, phoned the shop many times, and in
   the end had to pay it all (〜たあげく、{結局|けっきょく}…).
3. The parts about cancellation ({解約|かいやく}) and charges ({料金|りょうきん}).
4. Contracts differ a lot from shop to shop, and if there's a problem later, the only proof you
   have is the paperwork in your hands.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

When you start a new life, the chances to sign contracts multiply all at once: renting a room,
buying a smartphone, opening a bank account. In each case the shop staff explain it, but just
because you sign after hearing the explanation doesn't mean you've understood what it says.

Every year the city's consumer advice centre receives many enquiries along the lines of "I signed
without reading the contract properly". For example, one university student signed up to several
services just as a shop assistant suggested, and when they tried to cancel two months later
they were told they'd have to pay a cancellation fee. After phoning the shop again and again, in
the end they had to pay the whole amount. Some people have even kept paying for a service they
weren't using for over a year.

To avoid problems under a contract, the first thing to do is to check the parts of the terms on
cancellation and on charges. The contract period and the conditions for renewal matter just as
much as the charges. If there are words or abbreviations you don't understand, just ask
on the spot. If the explanation is too complicated, one way is to say "I'll decide after talking
it over with my family" and go home for now.

Also, be sure to get a copy of the contract. What contracts say differs greatly from shop to shop,
so if a problem comes up later, the only proof you have is the paperwork in your hands. If you
run into trouble, don't worry about it alone: please contact the centre. Advice is free, and the
person in charge will reply as soon as they've looked into it.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{確認|かくにん}し{次第|しだい}、ご{連絡|れんらく}いたします。
= I'll contact you as soon as I've checked.
{天気|てんき}{次第|しだい}で、{中止|ちゅうし}になる{場合|ばあい}もあります。
= Depending on the weather, it may be cancelled.
{内容|ないよう}をご{確認|かくにん}の{上|うえ}、ご{署名|しょめい}ください。
= Please check the contents, then sign.
{検討|けんとう}の{末|すえ}、{今回|こんかい}は{見送|みおく}ることになりました。
= After consideration, we've decided to pass on it this time.
{迷|まよ}ったあげく、{何|なに}も{買|か}いませんでした。
= After all that dithering, I didn't buy anything.
```

ご{確認|かくにん}の{上|うえ} is the noun form of 〜た{上|うえ}で, the standard wording on forms.

## Common mistakes

- 〜{次第|しだい} with a past fact: ×{家|いえ}に{着|つ}き{次第|しだい}、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきた. 〜{次第|しだい} is for
  what someone will do next: {着|つ}き{次第|しだい}、お{電話|でんわ}します. For the past, 〜とすぐに.
- The wrong form before {次第|しだい}: ×{届|とど}く{次第|しだい}, ×{届|とど}いた{次第|しだい}. It's the ます stem:
  {届|とど}き{次第|しだい}.
- 〜た{上|うえ}で for a plain sequence: ×{起|お}きた{上|うえ}で{顔|かお}を{洗|あら}った. Use 〜てから. た{上|うえ}で is for a
  step done so that the next can be done properly.
- あげく with a good result: ×{頑張|がんば}ったあげく、{合格|ごうかく}した. Use 〜た{末|すえ}に.
- Reading {上|じょう} as うえ in {契約上|けいやくじょう} and {法律上|ほうりつじょう}.
- {解約|かいやく} for a booking: a reservation is キャンセル or {取|と}り{消|け}し.

## Key points

- ます stem + {次第|しだい}: as soon as (then I'll / please …); formal.
- noun + {次第|しだい}だ / {次第|しだい}で(は): it depends on; 〜{次第|しだい}です: that's why (formal letters).
- 〜た{上|うえ}で / ご〜の{上|うえ}: after doing A properly, B.
- noun + {上|じょう}: in terms of ({契約上|けいやくじょう}, {法律上|ほうりつじょう}, {書類上|しょるいじょう}).
- 〜た{末|すえ}(に): after long effort, finally (any result); 〜たあげく: after all that, a bad end.
- 〜てからでないと: not until (review).
- New kanji: 契 条 証 提 印 届 預 籍 録 券 複 略 簡. Write {契約|けいやく}, {届|とど}く, {届|とど}ける,
  {提出|ていしゅつ}, {条件|じょうけん}, {簡単|かんたん}, {記録|きろく}, {登録|とうろく}, {預|あず}ける with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Since and throughout: 以来, てからというもの, にわたって
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lessons 6 and 7 were about single moments: before, at, as soon as, after. This lesson is about
stretches of time: "ever since", "since that day, everything changed", "over three hundred
years", "all through the year". These are the patterns of history writing, of news reports and
of telling your own story.

{城|しろ}が{完成|かんせい}して{以来|いらい}、この{町|まち}は{城下町|じょうかまち}として{栄|さか}えてきた。 — Ever since the castle was completed, this town has flourished as a castle town.
{祖母|そぼ}が{亡|な}くなってからというもの、{祖父|そふ}はすっかり{元気|げんき}をなくしてしまった。 — Ever since my grandmother died, my grandfather has lost all his spirit.
{戦|たたか}いは{百年|ひゃくねん}にわたって{続|つづ}いた。 — The fighting went on for a hundred years.
もう{少|すこ}しで{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れるところだった。 — I very nearly missed the train.

The theme is history: periods and eras, war and rebellion, rulers and samurai, castles, ruins,
heritage and treasures. N3 gave you {時代|じだい}, {歴史|れきし}, {武士|ぶし}, {伝統|でんとう}; now
{城|しろ} (N4), {仏|ほとけ} and {仏教|ぶっきょう} (N3), {画像|がぞう} (N3) and {将来|しょうらい} (N4) get their
kanji, and you'll meet the words of a museum, a castle tour and a history programme.

## Ever since: 〜て{以来|いらい}, noun + {以来|いらい}

〜て{以来|いらい} / noun + {以来|いらい} means "ever since (a point in the past), and still now". The
second half is a state, a habit or a change that has continued from that point.

| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| て form + {以来|いらい} | {日本|にほん}に{来|き}て{以来|いらい} |
| noun + {以来|いらい} | {入学|にゅうがく}{以来|いらい}, {明治|めいじ}{以来|いらい}, {去年|きょねん}の{夏|なつ}{以来|いらい} |
| それ{以来|いらい} / あれ{以来|いらい} | since then |
| {以来|いらい}の + noun | {記録|きろく}{開始|かいし}{以来|いらい}の{大雪|おおゆき} (the heaviest snow since records began) |

{大学|だいがく}を{卒業|そつぎょう}して{以来|いらい}、{彼|かれ}とは{一度|いちど}も{会|あ}っていない。 — I haven't seen him once since we graduated.
この{寺|てら}は、{建|た}てられて{以来|いらい}{一度|いちど}も{火事|かじ}にあっていない。 — This temple has never had a fire since it was built.
{去年|きょねん}{転|ころ}んで{怪我|けが}をした。それ{以来|いらい}、{階段|かいだん}を{下|お}りるのが{怖|こわ}い。 — I fell and hurt myself last year. Since then I've been scared of going down stairs.

〜てから is the plain "after": {卒業|そつぎょう}してから{留学|りゅうがく}した (I studied abroad after
graduating). 〜て{以来|いらい} needs the continuing part: you can't use it for a single later event.
×{卒業|そつぎょう}して{以来|いらい}、{留学|りゅうがく}した. And it looks back from now, so not for the future:
×{来月|らいげつ}{以来|いらい} (for "from next month on", {来月|らいげつ}から or {来月|らいげつ}{以降|いこう}, N3).

## Since that day, everything changed: 〜てからというもの

〜てからというもの means "ever since A, (there has been) a big change". It's stronger and more
emotional than て{以来|いらい}: the speaker or writer is struck by how much changed. It lives in
writing and in storytelling.

{子供|こども}が{生|う}まれてからというもの、{夜|よる}ゆっくり{寝|ね}たことがない。 — Ever since the baby was born, I haven't had a good night's sleep.
{世界遺産|せかいいさん}に{登録|とうろく}されてからというもの、{静|しず}かだった{村|むら}に{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{押|お}し{寄|よ}せるようになった。 — Ever since it was registered as a World Heritage Site, tourists have poured into the once quiet village.

{押|お}し{寄|よ}せる = to surge in (a gloss). Limits:

- The first half is a single event that triggered the change.
- The second half is the changed state that has continued, usually with 〜ようになった, 〜ばかりだ,
  〜ない, ずっと.
- It isn't for requests or plans, and it isn't used for small, ordinary things:
  ×{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べてからというもの、{眠|ねむ}い sounds absurd.

| | 〜て{以来|いらい} | 〜てからというもの |
|---|---|---|
| meaning | ever since (a fact) | ever since (look how things changed) |
| second half | a continuing state or habit | a striking change that has continued |
| feel | neutral, written or formal speech | emotional, written and narrative |
| example | {入社|にゅうしゃ}{以来|いらい}、{同|おな}じ{部署|ぶしょ}にいる | {入社|にゅうしゃ}してからというもの、{毎日|まいにち}が{忙|いそが}しい |

## Over a span: 〜にわたって

〜にわたって (written: にわたり; before a noun: にわたる / にわたった) follows a span of time, a
space, or a number of things, and says something covers *all of it*. It's kana in this course.

| Span | Example |
|---|---|
| time | {三日間|みっかかん}にわたって, {三百年|さんびゃくねん}にわたる{歴史|れきし} |
| space | {全国|ぜんこく}にわたって, {関東|かんとう}から{九州|きゅうしゅう}にわたる{地域|ちいき} |
| number of things | {十回|じゅっかい}にわたって, {五|いつ}つの{分野|ぶんや}にわたる{研究|けんきゅう} |

{発掘|はっくつ}は{二十年|にじゅうねん}にわたって{行|おこな}われた。 — The excavation went on for twenty years.
{委員会|いいんかい}は{三時間|さんじかん}にわたり、{城|しろ}の{修理|しゅうり}について{話|はな}し{合|あ}った。 — The committee spent three hours discussing the castle repairs.
{大雨|おおあめ}で、{関東|かんとう}から{九州|きゅうしゅう}にわたる{広|ひろ}い{地域|ちいき}に{被害|ひがい}が{出|で}た。 — The heavy rain caused damage over a wide area, from Kantō to Kyūshū.

The noun before にわたって names a whole stretch, so it needs a length or a range: a point in
time doesn't work. ×{三時|さんじ}にわたって. For "from A to B", から〜にかけて (N3) is the everyday
choice: {午後|ごご}から{夜|よる}にかけて{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}る. にわたって is more formal and stresses the
whole span.

## All through: 〜を{通|つう}じて (review and more)

> **Review (N3 lesson 14).** 〜を{通|とお}して / 〜を{通|つう}じて: "through, by means of":
> {友|とも}だちを{通|とお}して{知|し}り{合|あ}った (we met through a friend).

With a period of time, 〜を{通|つう}じて means "all through, throughout": {一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて (all year
round), {一生|いっしょう}を{通|つう}じて (all one's life). を{通|つう}じて is the more written of the two; with time,
both are heard.

この{島|しま}は{一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて{暖|あたた}かい。 — This island is warm all year round.
えど{時代|じだい}を{通|つう}じて、{日本|にほん}では{大|おお}きな{戦争|せんそう}はほとんどなかった。 — All through the Edo period, there was hardly any major war in Japan.

What's the difference from にわたって? を{通|つう}じて says something holds *at every point* of the
period (it was warm the whole time); にわたって says an activity *filled* the span (the
excavation took twenty years).

## Right down to: 〜にいたるまで (to recognize)

〜にいたるまで means "right down to, even": it names the last, most surprising member of a range.
It's written and in kana here (its kanji is outside N2). Often 〜から〜にいたるまで.

{子供|こども}からお{年寄|としよ}りにいたるまで、{町|まち}の{人|ひと}はみんなこの{祭|まつ}りを{楽|たの}しみにしている。 — Everyone in town, from children to the elderly, looks forward to this festival.
{城|しろ}の{修理|しゅうり}は、{屋根|やね}から{小|ちい}さなくぎにいたるまで、{昔|むかし}の{方法|ほうほう}で{行|おこな}われた。 — The castle was repaired the old way, right down to the smallest nails.

Lesson 26 comes back to にいたる in written Japanese.

## Nearly: 〜ところだった

> **Review (N3 lesson 3).** ところ marks a stage of an action: {食|た}べるところ (about to eat),
> {食|た}べているところ, {食|た}べたところ.

Dictionary form + ところだった means "nearly happened (but didn't)": a close call. It often comes with
もう{少|すこ}しで or {危|あや}うく.

もう{少|すこ}しで{大事|だいじ}な{書類|しょるい}を{捨|す}てるところだった。 — I very nearly threw away an important document.
{危|あや}うく{事故|じこ}を{起|お}こすところだった。 — I came close to causing an accident.
{君|きみ}が{教|おし}えてくれなかったら、{約束|やくそく}を{忘|わす}れるところだったよ。 — If you hadn't told me, I'd have forgotten the appointment.

With the ない form, 〜ないところだった is "nearly didn't": {間|ま}に{合|あ}わないところだった (I nearly
didn't make it). Compare N3's 〜ところだった meaning "was just about to": {出|で}かけるところだった
(I was just about to go out, when…). Context tells them apart; もう{少|すこ}しで and {危|あや}うく mark the
close-call meaning.

## The words of history

| Topic | Words |
|---|---|
| war and rebellion | {軍|ぐん}, {軍人|ぐんじん}, {海軍|かいぐん}, {陸軍|りくぐん}, {武器|ぶき}, {武力|ぶりょく}, {反乱|はんらん}, {戦乱|せんらん}, 〜の{乱|らん}, {乱|みだ}れる, {乱|みだ}す, {戦場|せんじょう}, {敗北|はいぼく}, {占領|せんりょう}する, {植民地|しょくみんち}, {終戦|しゅうせん}, {戦前|せんぜん}, {戦後|せんご} |
| change | {革命|かくめい}, {改革|かいかく}, {開国|かいこく}, {統一|とういつ}する |
| rulers and samurai | {将軍|しょうぐん}, {武将|ぶしょう}, {大名|だいみょう}, {家来|けらい}, {主君|しゅくん}, {支配|しはい}する, {支配者|しはいしゃ}, {天下|てんか}, {領地|りょうち}, {城主|じょうしゅ}, {武道|ぶどう} |
| society | {身分|みぶん}, {農民|のうみん}, {商人|しょうにん}, {先祖|せんぞ}, {子孫|しそん} |
| castles | {城下町|じょうかまち}, {城跡|しろあと}, {天守|てんしゅ}, {落城|らくじょう} |
| ruins and heritage | {遺跡|いせき}, {遺産|いさん}, {世界遺産|せかいいさん}, {遺品|いひん}, {遺族|いぞく}, {跡|あと}, {跡地|あとち}, {史跡|しせき}, {発掘|はっくつ}, {出土|しゅつど}する, {土器|どき}, {復元|ふくげん}する |
| treasures | {宝|たから}, {宝物|たからもの}, {国宝|こくほう}, {宝石|ほうせき}, {宝|たから}くじ |
| Buddhism and images | {仏像|ぶつぞう}, {大仏|だいぶつ}, {像|ぞう}, {想像|そうぞう}する, {映像|えいぞう} |
| periods | {中世|ちゅうせい}, {近代|きんだい}, {年号|ねんごう}, {元号|げんごう}, {平安時代|へいあんじだい}, {戦国時代|せんごくじだい}, {年表|ねんぴょう} |
| time words | {永遠|えいえん}, {永住|えいじゅう}する, {旧|きゅう}〜, {旧友|きゅうゆう}, {栄|さか}える |
| telling history | {言|い}い{伝|つた}え, {時代劇|じだいげき}, {考古学|こうこがく} |

Notes:

- Japanese periods are named after where power sat, or after era names: {平安|へいあん} (Kyoto's old
  name), えど (the old name of Tokyo: its first kanji is outside N2), {明治|めいじ}. Since 1868 each
  emperor has had one era name, {元号|げんごう}; everyday speech says {年号|ねんごう}.
- {戦後|せんご} (postwar) and {終戦|しゅうせん} (the end of the war) usually mean 1945 in Japan. The
  {後|ご} of {戦後|せんご} is ゴ; compare {後|あと} and {後|のち}.
- {遺産|いさん} is both an inheritance and a heritage; {世界遺産|せかいいさん} is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
- {先祖|せんぞ} is usually one's own family's ancestors; N3's {祖先|そせん} is wider (the ancestors of
  people, or of a species).
- {革|かわ} (leather), {皮|かわ} (skin, lesson 5) and {川|かわ} (river) are all かわ with the same pitch:
  only context and kanji tell them apart.
- {商人|しょうにん} (merchant) is [しょうにん:1]; lesson 7's {証人|しょうにん} (witness) is
  [しょうにん:0].

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji: war and rule, castles and samurai, ruins and treasures.

### War, rule and change

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 軍 | army | グン | — | 9 | {軍|ぐん}, {軍人|ぐんじん}, {海軍|かいぐん}, {陸軍|りくぐん}, {将軍|しょうぐん} |
| 武 | military, martial | ブ | — | 8 | {武士|ぶし}, {武器|ぶき}, {武力|ぶりょく}, {武将|ぶしょう}, {武道|ぶどう} |
| 将 | general; future | ショウ | — | 10 | {将軍|しょうぐん}, {武将|ぶしょう}, {将来|しょうらい} |
| 乱 | disorder | ラン | みだ(れる), みだ(す) | 7 | {反乱|はんらん}, {戦乱|せんらん}, {乱|みだ}れる, {乱|みだ}す, {混乱|こんらん} (lesson 29) |
| 革 | leather; reform | カク | かわ | 9 | {革命|かくめい}, {改革|かいかく}, {革|かわ} |
| 旧 | old, former | キュウ | — | 5 | {旧|きゅう}〜, {旧友|きゅうゆう}, {復旧|ふっきゅう} (lesson 29) |

- {武士|ぶし} (N3's ぶし) and {将来|しょうらい} (N4's しょうらい) are now written with kanji.
- 将 in {将来|しょうらい} means "about to": what's about to come, the future.
- 革 is a stretched hide: leather, and figuratively changing the skin of something, reform.

### Castles and Buddhism

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 城 | castle | ジョウ | しろ | 9 | {城|しろ}, {城下町|じょうかまち}, {城跡|しろあと}, {城主|じょうしゅ}, {落城|らくじょう} |
| 仏 | Buddha | ブツ | ほとけ | 4 | {仏|ほとけ}, {仏教|ぶっきょう}, {仏像|ぶつぞう}, {大仏|だいぶつ} |
| 像 | image, statue | ゾウ | — | 14 | {像|ぞう}, {仏像|ぶつぞう}, {画像|がぞう}, {想像|そうぞう}, {映像|えいぞう} |

- {城|しろ} (N4), {仏|ほとけ} and {仏教|ぶっきょう} (N3: ブツ becomes ブッ before キョウ) and {画像|がぞう} (N3)
  are now written with kanji.
- 城 is しろ alone and in {城跡|しろあと}, ジョウ in {城下町|じょうかまち} and {城主|じょうしゅ}; names of
  castles take ジョウ: 〜{城|じょう}.

### Ruins, heritage and treasures

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 跡 | trace, ruins | セキ | あと | 13 | {跡|あと}, {跡地|あとち}, {遺跡|いせき}, {史跡|しせき}, {足跡|あしあと} |
| 遺 | leave behind | イ | — | 15 | {遺跡|いせき}, {遺産|いさん}, {遺品|いひん}, {遺族|いぞく} |
| 宝 | treasure | ホウ | たから | 8 | {宝|たから}, {宝物|たからもの}, {国宝|こくほう}, {宝石|ほうせき} |
| 永 | eternal, long | エイ | — | 5 | {永遠|えいえん}, {永住|えいじゅう}, {永久|えいきゅう} (lesson 27) |

- {足跡|あしあと} (N3's あしあと) is now written with kanji.
- 遺 is イ in the words here; in ゆいごん (a will) it's read ユイ.
- {跡|あと} (a trace) and {後|あと} (after) are different words: {車|くるま}の{跡|あと} (tyre tracks),
  {食事|しょくじ}の{後|あと} (after the meal).

Memory notes:

- 軍 is a cover (冖) over a cart (車, N5): carts under cover, an army on the march.
- 武 is a spear shape and a foot (止, stop): walking with weapons, military.
- 将 is a half-tree shape, a hand and 寸: a hand that holds command, a general.
- 乱 is tangled thread on the left with a hook on the right: tangled up, disorder.
- 革 is an animal skin stretched out flat, head at the top: leather.
- 旧 is a line beside the sun (日): a day that has gone by, old.
- 城 is earth (土) and 成 (become, N3): earth built up into walls, a castle.
- 仏 is a person (亻) and ム: a person with something private inside, the Buddha.
- 像 is a person (亻) and 象 (elephant, lesson 13's kanji): a figure of a person, an image.
- 跡 is a foot (⻊) beside a figure with arms spread: footprints, a trace left behind.
- 遺 is the road (辶) and a basket over a shell (貝, money): valuables dropped by the roadside,
  left behind.
- 宝 is a roof (宀) over a jewel (玉, lesson 25's kanji): a treasure kept in the house.
- 永 is water (水) with an extra stroke at the top: a river that flows on and on, eternal.

```trace
軍武将乱革旧城仏像跡遺宝永
```

## Dialogue: at the castle museum

あやか and たくみ, university friends, are visiting the museum in an old castle town.
(Casual speech.)

```dialogue
# In the castle museum
あやか: ねえ、{見|み}て。この{城|しろ}、{四百年|よんひゃくねん}{以上|いじょう}{前|まえ}に{建|た}てられたんだって。
= Hey, look. It says this castle was built over four hundred years ago.
たくみ: へえ。{建|た}てられて{以来|いらい}、ずっと{同|おな}じ{家|いえ}が{城主|じょうしゅ}だったの？
= Huh. Has the same family been lord of the castle ever since it was built?
あやか: ううん。{戦国時代|せんごくじだい}には{何度|なんど}も{城主|じょうしゅ}が{変|か}わったみたい。{反乱|はんらん}もあったって。
= No. Apparently the lord changed many times in the Warring States period. There was a rebellion too.
たくみ: そっか。で、こっちの{年表|ねんぴょう}によると、えど{時代|じだい}を{通|つう}じて{町|まち}が{栄|さか}えたんだね。
= I see. And according to this timeline, the town flourished all through the Edo period.
あやか: そうそう。{城下町|じょうかまち}として{商人|しょうにん}がたくさん{集|あつ}まったらしいよ。
= That's right. Lots of merchants gathered here, as it was a castle town.
たくみ: あ、このかたな、{国宝|こくほう}だって。{初|はじ}めて{本物|ほんもの}{見|み}た。
= Oh, this sword is a national treasure, it says. First time I've seen a real one.
あやか: たくみ、{時代劇|じだいげき}{見|み}るようになってからというもの、かたなの{話|はなし}ばっかりだよね。
= Ever since you started watching period dramas, all you talk about is swords.
たくみ: だってかっこいいじゃん。……あれ、{天守|てんしゅ}は{明治|めいじ}に{一度|いちど}{取|と}り{払|はら}われたって{書|か}いてある。
= Well, they're cool. …Oh, it says the keep was pulled down once in the Meiji era.
あやか: {今|いま}のは{戦後|せんご}に{復元|ふくげん}されたものなんだって。{昔|むかし}の{写真|しゃしん}をもとに。
= Apparently the one standing now was rebuilt after the war, based on old photos.
たくみ: へえ、{全然|ぜんぜん}{分|わ}からなかった。{三年|さんねん}にわたって{工事|こうじ}したらしいよ。
= Wow, I couldn't tell at all. Apparently the work took three years.
あやか: あ、もうすぐ{四時|よじ}だ。{天守|てんしゅ}、{四時半|よじはん}で{閉|し}まるんだって。
= Oh, it's nearly four. The keep closes at half past four, they say.
たくみ: え、{危|あぶ}な！ もう{少|すこ}しで{上|のぼ}らずに{帰|かえ}るところだった。{急|いそ}ごう！
= What, that was close! We nearly went home without going up. Let's hurry!
```

かたな = sword (its kanji is outside N2); {本物|ほんもの} = the real thing; {取|と}り{払|はら}う = to pull
down, clear away. {危|あぶ}な is a casual exclamation, "close call!".

## Reading: a festival four hundred years old

A newspaper's local page (だ/である style). The town, {青原|あおはら}, is invented.

> {城下町|じょうかまち}として{知|し}られる{青原|あおはら}{市|し}で、{今年|ことし}も「{武者|むしゃ}{行列|ぎょうれつ}」が{行|おこな}われた。{城|しろ}の{完成|かんせい}を{祝|いわ}って{始|はじ}まったとされるこの{祭|まつ}りは、{四百年|よんひゃくねん}{以上|いじょう}にわたって{続|つづ}いている。
>
> {祭|まつ}りの{中心|ちゅうしん}は、{武将|ぶしょう}や{家来|けらい}の{姿|すがた}をした{市民|しみん}{約|やく}{三百人|さんびゃくにん}が、{城跡|しろあと}から{駅|えき}までの{二|に}キロにわたって{歩|ある}く{行列|ぎょうれつ}だ。{子供|こども}からお{年寄|としよ}りにいたるまで、{参加者|さんかしゃ}は{自分|じぶん}で{衣装|いしょう}を{用意|ようい}する。{古|ふる}い{家|いえ}では、{先祖|せんぞ}から{伝|つた}わる{革|かわ}の{道具|どうぐ}を{今|いま}も{使|つか}っているという。{行列|ぎょうれつ}の{最後|さいご}には、{城主|じょうしゅ}の{役|やく}の{市長|しちょう}が{馬|うま}に{乗|の}って{登場|とうじょう}し、{見物客|けんぶつきゃく}を{喜|よろこ}ばせる。
>
> もっとも、{祭|まつ}りは{一度|いちど}も{止|と}まらなかったわけではない。{戦争|せんそう}の{間|あいだ}は{中止|ちゅうし}され、{戦後|せんご}もしばらくは{行列|ぎょうれつ}を{出|だ}せる{状態|じょうたい}ではなかった。{再開|さいかい}されたのは{戦後|せんご}{十年|じゅうねん}ほどたってからで、それ{以来|いらい}、{毎年|まいとし}{秋|あき}に{行|おこな}われている。{当時|とうじ}を{知|し}る{人|ひと}によると、{再開|さいかい}の{年|とし}には{衣装|いしょう}が{足|た}りず、{家族|かぞく}の{古|ふる}い{着物|きもの}を{直|なお}して{使|つか}ったそうだ。
>
> {十年前|じゅうねんまえ}に{城跡|しろあと}が{国|くに}の{史跡|しせき}に{指定|してい}されてからというもの、{祭|まつ}りを{見|み}に{来|く}る{観光客|かんこうきゃく}は{増|ふ}える{一方|いっぽう}だ。{一方|いっぽう}で、{市|し}の{人口|じんこう}は{減|へ}りつつあり、{行列|ぎょうれつ}に{参加|さんか}する{若者|わかもの}も{少|すく}なくなった。{保存会|ほぞんかい}の{会長|かいちょう}は「もう{少|すこ}しで{祭|まつ}りが{続|つづ}けられなくなるところだったが、{最近|さいきん}は{市外|しがい}から{参加|さんか}してくれる{人|ひと}もいる。{一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて{準備|じゅんび}は{大変|たいへん}だが、この{祭|まつ}りを{子孫|しそん}に{残|のこ}したい」と{話|はな}している。

{武者|むしゃ}{行列|ぎょうれつ} = a procession of people dressed as samurai; {衣装|いしょう} = costume (lesson 24);
{見物客|けんぶつきゃく} = spectators; {保存会|ほぞんかい} = a preservation society. 〜つつ(ある) is lesson 9's.

1. How long has the festival been going on, and how did it start, according to the article?
2. Who takes part in the procession, and what do they prepare themselves?
3. Has the festival been held every year without a break? Explain.
4. What has changed since the castle ruins became a historic site, and what worries the
   society?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. For over four hundred years ({四百年|よんひゃくねん}{以上|いじょう}にわたって). It's said to have begun as a
   celebration of the castle's completion.
2. About three hundred citizens, from children to elderly people, dressed as warlords and
   retainers. They prepare their own costumes.
3. No. It was stopped during the war, and for a while after the war it couldn't be held. It was
   restarted about ten years after the war and has been held every autumn since then.
4. The number of tourists has kept rising; but the town's population is shrinking and fewer young
   people take part. The festival nearly couldn't continue, though now some people from outside
   the town join in.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

In the castle town of Aohara, the samurai procession took place again this year. Said to
have begun as a celebration of the castle's completion, the festival has continued for over four
hundred years.

At its heart is a procession of about three hundred citizens, dressed as warlords and their
retainers, who walk the two kilometres from the castle ruins to the station. Everyone taking
part, from children to the elderly, prepares their own costume. In some old families, leather
gear handed down from their ancestors is still used. At the end of the procession, the mayor,
playing the lord of the castle, appears on horseback to the delight of the spectators.

That said, the festival hasn't gone on without a single break. It was stopped during the war, and
for some time after it the town was in no state to put on a procession. It was restarted about
ten years after the war, and since then it has been held every autumn. According to people who
remember those days, in the year it restarted there weren't enough costumes, so families altered
old kimonos to use.

Ever since the castle ruins were designated a national historic site ten years ago, the number
of tourists coming to see the festival has kept rising. At the same time, the town's population
is shrinking, and fewer young people take part in the procession. The chair of the preservation
society says: "We very nearly couldn't keep the festival going, but recently some people come
from outside the town to take part. Preparing for it is hard work all year round, but we want to
leave this festival to our descendants."

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{日本|にほん}に{来|き}て{以来|いらい}、ずっとこの{町|まち}に{住|す}んでいます。
= I've lived in this town ever since I came to Japan.
{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}してからというもの、{毎日|まいにち}が{楽|たの}しくてしかたがない。
= Ever since I moved, every day has been a joy.
{工事|こうじ}は{三年|さんねん}にわたって{行|おこな}われました。
= The work was carried out over three years.
この{地方|ちほう}は{一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて{雨|あめ}が{多|おお}い。
= It rains a lot in this region all year round.
もう{少|すこ}しで{忘|わす}れるところでした。
= I very nearly forgot.
```

## Common mistakes

- 〜て{以来|いらい} for a single later event: ×{日本|にほん}に{来|き}て{以来|いらい}、{京都|きょうと}に{行|い}った. Say
  {日本|にほん}に{来|き}てから or use a continuing state: {日本|にほん}に{来|き}て{以来|いらい}、{毎年|まいとし}{京都|きょうと}に{行|い}っている.
- 〜て{以来|いらい} or てからというもの about the future: ×{来年|らいねん}{卒業|そつぎょう}して{以来|いらい}. Both look back
  from now.
- にわたって after a point in time: ×{三時|さんじ}にわたって, ×{今日|きょう}にわたって. It needs a span
  ({三時間|さんじかん}, {一週間|いっしゅうかん}, {全国|ぜんこく}).
- Reading {戦後|せんご} as せんあと, or {城跡|しろあと} as じょうあと.
- 〜ところだった with the た form: ×{忘|わす}れたところだった. The close call takes the dictionary form:
  {忘|わす}れるところだった.
- Writing {後|あと} for a trace: {雪|ゆき}の{上|うえ}の{跡|あと} (tracks in the snow).

## Key points

- 〜て{以来|いらい} / noun + {以来|いらい} / それ{以来|いらい}: ever since, with a continuing state.
- 〜てからというもの: ever since, look how things changed (emotional, written).
- 〜にわたって / にわたり / にわたる: over a whole span of time, space or number.
- 〜を{通|つう}じて with a period: all through ({一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて).
- 〜にいたるまで: right down to (to recognize).
- dictionary form + ところだった: nearly happened (もう{少|すこ}しで, {危|あや}うく).
- New kanji: 軍 武 将 乱 革 旧 城 仏 像 跡 遺 宝 永. Write {城|しろ}, {仏|ほとけ}, {仏教|ぶっきょう},
  {武士|ぶし}, {将来|しょうらい}, {画像|がぞう}, {足跡|あしあと} with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: While and in progress: つつ, つつある, にともなって
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 8 measured spans of time. This lesson is about processes: doing two things at once, a
change that is under way, and one change that drags another along with it. These are the
patterns of the economy pages and of reports on industry, which talk constantly about things
"increasing", "being lost" and "changing along with" something else.

{景色|けしき}を{楽|たの}しみつつ、ゆっくり{歩|ある}いた。 — I walked slowly, enjoying the scenery.
{町|まち}の{工場|こうじょう}は{減|へ}りつつある。 — The town's factories are dwindling.
{技術|ぎじゅつ}の{進歩|しんぽ}にともなって、{働|はたら}き{方|かた}も{変|か}わってきた。 — As technology has advanced, the way people work has changed too.
{農家|のうか}の{数|かず}は{減|へ}るばかりだ。 — The number of farming households just keeps falling.

The theme is industry and trade: factories and products, technology, farming, imports and
exports, freight. {機械|きかい} and {材料|ざいりょう} (N4), {取材|しゅざい}, {設定|せってい} and {競技|きょうぎ}
(N3) are now written with kanji.

This lesson owns two terms: **[[simultaneous action]]** (つつ) and **[[progressive aspect]]** (つつある).

## While (written): ます stem + つつ

ます stem + つつ means "while doing A, (also) B": two actions at the same time, by **the same
person**. It's a written, slightly literary version of N4's ながら.

{父|ちち}は{新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}みつつ、コーヒーを{飲|の}んでいた。 — My father was drinking coffee as he read the paper.
{工場|こうじょう}の{見学|けんがく}では、{説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}きつつ{製造|せいぞう}の{工程|こうてい}を{見|み}て{回|まわ}った。 — On the factory tour, we went round looking at the production process as we listened to the explanations.

That's the basic idea of simultaneous action: one subject, two actions. Where つつ really
shines is with thinking and feeling verbs, which ながら handles less elegantly in writing:

{将来|しょうらい}のことを{考|かんが}えつつ、{仕事|しごと}を{探|さが}している。 — I'm looking for a job, thinking about my future.
{伝統|でんとう}を{守|まも}りつつ、{新|あたら}しい{技術|ぎじゅつ}も{取|と}り{入|い}れている。 — They keep up tradition while also bringing in new technology.

| | 〜ながら | 〜つつ |
|---|---|---|
| register | everyday, spoken and written | written, formal speeches |
| subject | the same person | the same person |
| typical verbs | any action: {歌|うた}いながら, {歩|ある}きながら | thought and attitude: {考|かんが}えつつ, {感|かん}じつつ, {守|まも}りつつ |
| "although" | ながらも ({知|し}っていながら) | つつも ({知|し}りつつも) |

Like ながら, つつ needs one subject: for "while A does X, B does Y", use 〜{間|あいだ}(に) or
〜ている{間|あいだ} (N4/N3).

> **Review (lesson 2).** 〜つつ(も) also means "although": {悪|わる}いと{知|し}りつつ(も)…:
> {体|からだ}に{悪|わる}いと{知|し}りつつ、ついお{菓子|かし}を{食|た}べてしまった (I knew it was bad for me, but I
> ate the sweets anyway). The two uses share a form; the second half tells you which: a contrast
> means "although", a second action at the same time means "while".

## In progress: ます stem + つつある

ます stem + つつある means "is in the process of …-ing": a change that is happening now, step by
step. This is the progressive aspect of written Japanese, used constantly in news reports,
reports and essays.

{世界|せかい}の{人口|じんこう}は{今|いま}も{増|ふ}えつつある。 — The world's population is still growing.
{手作|てづく}りの{技|わざ}が{失|うしな}われつつある。 — Handmade skills are being lost.
{景気|けいき}は{少|すこ}しずつ{回復|かいふく}しつつある。 — The economy is gradually recovering.

It goes with verbs of change: {増|ふ}える, {減|へ}る, {変|か}わる, {進|すす}む, {回復|かいふく}する, {広|ひろ}がる,
{消|き}える, {失|うしな}われる, {近|ちか}づく. Compare 〜ている:

| Sentence | What it says |
|---|---|
| {工場|こうじょう}が{減|へ}っている。 | Factories have decreased / are decreasing (the state now, or the trend). |
| {工場|こうじょう}が{減|へ}りつつある。 | Factories are decreasing, and the process is still going on. |

〜ている with a change verb can mean the result ({窓|まど}が{開|あ}いている: it's open); 〜つつある always
means the change is under way. For ordinary actions such as {読|よ}む or {食|た}べる, use 〜ている:
{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいる, not ×{読|よ}みつつある. In speech, 〜てきている is the natural equivalent:
{工場|こうじょう}が{減|へ}ってきている.

## Along with: 〜にともなって

〜にともなって (written: にともない; before a noun: にともなう) means "as A happens (or changes), B
happens too": B comes along with A. It's formal, common in news and business. Its kanji is
outside N2, so it's kana here.

| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| noun + にともなって | {人口|じんこう}の{増加|ぞうか}にともなって |
| verb (dictionary form) + のにともなって | {工場|こうじょう}が{移転|いてん}するのにともなって |
| にともない (written) | {台風|たいふう}の{接近|せっきん}にともない |
| にともなう + noun | {開発|かいはつ}にともなう{問題|もんだい} (problems that come with development) |

{工業化|こうぎょうか}にともなって、{都市|とし}に{人|ひと}が{集|あつ}まった。 — With industrialization, people gathered in the cities.
{新工場|しんこうじょう}の{完成|かんせい}にともない、{百人|ひゃくにん}を{新|あら}たに{採用|さいよう}する。 — With the completion of the new factory, a hundred people will be newly hired.
{円安|えんやす}にともなう{輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}の{値上|ねあ}がりが{続|つづ}いている。 — Imported goods keep going up in price as the yen weakens.

A is usually a change or an event (a noun of change: {増加|ぞうか}, {移転|いてん}, {完成|かんせい},
{発展|はってん}); B is what changes with it. It's about things in the world, not about what one
person does: for "as I got older, I…", につれて is more natural.

## As (review): 〜とともに, 〜につれて

> **Review (N3 lesson 4).** 〜につれて / 〜にしたがって: as A changes gradually, B changes in
> proportion ({年|とし}をとるにつれて{涙|なみだ}もろくなった). 〜とともに: together with; at the same time
> as; as ({社会|しゃかい}の{変化|へんか}とともに、{家族|かぞく}の{形|かたち}も{変|か}わる).

| Pattern | Core idea | Typical A | Register |
|---|---|---|---|
| 〜につれて | B changes step by step with A | a gradual change | spoken and written |
| 〜とともに | A and B together (also "with a person") | a change, an event, a person | written |
| 〜にともなって | B comes along with A | a change or an event (often a noun) | formal, news |

Many sentences take any of the three: {技術|ぎじゅつ}の{進歩|しんぽ}につれて / とともに / にともなって、
{生活|せいかつ}が{便利|べんり}になった. Only とともに works with people: {家族|かぞく}とともに{暮|く}らす (to live
with one's family), not にともなって.

## Only getting worse: 〜{一方|いっぽう}だ and 〜ばかりだ

> **Review (N3 lesson 4).** Dictionary form + {一方|いっぽう}だ: it keeps going one way.
> {物価|ぶっか}は{上|あ}がる{一方|いっぽう}だ (prices just keep going up).

Dictionary form + ばかりだ says much the same, but it's almost always about a change for the
worse, and it sounds more like a complaint:

{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}らないので、{野菜|やさい}の{値段|ねだん}は{上|あ}がるばかりだ。 — With no rain, vegetable prices just keep going up.
{若|わか}い{人|ひと}が{町|まち}を{出|で}ていき、{商店|しょうてん}は{減|へ}るばかりだ。 — Young people are leaving town, and the shops just keep disappearing.

| | 〜{一方|いっぽう}だ | 〜ばかりだ |
|---|---|---|
| direction | one way only | one way only |
| good or bad | usually bad, sometimes neutral or good | almost always bad |
| feel | a description of a trend | a complaint or a worry |

Don't confuse it with N3's other ばかり: た form + ばかり (just did), noun + ばかり (nothing but).
ばかりだ after the dictionary form is the trend one.

## Dialogue: a factory visit

The engineering student りく visits a small factory that makes kitchen goods. The manager, はるみ,
shows him round. (Polite speech.)

```dialogue

= This is the production line. Everything from processing the materials to packing into boxes is done here.
りく: {思|おも}ったより{人|ひと}が{少|すく}ないですね。
= There are fewer people than I expected.
はるみ: ええ。{十年|じゅうねん}ほど{前|まえ}から{自動化|じどうか}を{進|すす}めてきました。{機械|きかい}の{導入|どうにゅう}にともなって、{作業|さぎょう}の{効率|こうりつ}がずいぶん{上|あ}がったんです。

= Did the jobs for people disappear?
はるみ: なくなったというより、{変|か}わりつつありますね。{今|いま}は{機械|きかい}を{管理|かんり}する{技術者|ぎじゅつしゃ}が{必要|ひつよう}なんです。

= Yes, about thirty per cent of sales are exports. But the price of raw materials just keeps going up…
```
