## Common mistakes

- からには for a plain cause and its result: "The train was late, so I was late" is
  {電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れたので、{遅刻|ちこく}した. からには needs a second half that someone is committed
  to (a duty, a resolve, advice).
- Forgetting である after a noun: {学生|がくせい}であるからには, {学生|がくせい}である{以上|いじょう}. ×{学生|がくせい}からには
  is wrong.
- Reading the "since" {以上|いじょう} as "more than". If {以上|いじょう} follows a clause ({契約|けいやく}した{以上|いじょう}), it's
  "since"; after a number ({三人|さんにん}{以上|いじょう}) it's "or more".
- じょう in place of うえ: in 〜た{上|うえ}は the reading is うえ. 〜{上|じょう} (in terms of) follows a noun:
  {法律上|ほうりつじょう}.
- ことだし for a heavy reason: {法律|ほうりつ}で{禁止|きんし}されていることだし、やめるべきだ sounds
  oddly light. ことだし goes with relaxed suggestions; from a rule, use {以上|いじょう} or からには.
- {否定|ひてい} and {否認|ひにん}: you {否認|ひにん}する a charge; you {否定|ひてい}する a claim or a rumour.

## Key points

- 〜からには (plain form; noun or な-adjective + である): now that, since… so (you must, I will,
  you should). Spoken and written.
- 〜{以上|いじょう}(は): since, given that; more formal and logical; common in rules and contracts, and
  after negatives (as long as… not).
- 〜{上|うえ}は (mostly after た): since, now that; very formal; recognize it (こうなった{上|うえ}は).
- 〜のだから (review): a shared reason pushing advice or a complaint; 〜ことだし: a light, casual
  reason before a suggestion.
- New kanji: 権 義 律 則 令 裁 弁 士 被 否 禁 厳 処. Write {法律|ほうりつ}, {規則|きそく}, {権利|けんり},
  {裁判|さいばん}, {禁止|きんし}, {被害|ひがい}, {弁当|べんとう} with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Just because, precisely because: ばかりに, だけに, だけあって
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 11's reasons committed someone to something. This lesson's reasons colour the result:

- 〜ばかりに: just because of one thing, something bad happened;
- 〜だけに: precisely because of it, the result is what you'd expect, or all the stronger;
- 〜だけあって: as you'd expect of it (praise);
- 〜ものだから: the reason, offered as an excuse or a personal explanation.

{値段|ねだん}だけで{選|えら}んだばかりに、すぐにこわれてしまった。 — Just because I chose on price alone, it broke almost at once.
{期待|きたい}していただけに、がっかりした。 — I'd expected so much that I was all the more disappointed.
{有名|ゆうめい}な{店|みせ}だけあって、{味|あじ}はさすがだ。 — As you'd expect of a famous shop, the food really is good.
{安|やす}かったものだから、つい{買|か}いすぎてしまって。 — It was so cheap, you see, I ended up buying too much.

The theme is buying and selling: prices, sales and advertising, shops and consumers, and the
arithmetic and big numbers that go with them. Household money and banks were N3's (lesson 7);
companies and markets are lesson 17's. Carried words that now take kanji: {物価|ぶっか},
{新鮮|しんせん}, {普通|ふつう}, {一般的|いっぱんてき}, {平均|へいきん}, {予算|よさん}.

## 〜ばかりに: just because (with a bad result)

〜ばかりに says that one cause, often a small one, was enough to bring about a result nobody
wanted. There's usually regret or frustration in it.

| Before ばかりに | Example |
|---|---|
| verb, plain form | {言|い}ったばかりに / {知|し}らないばかりに |
| い-adjective | {安|やす}いばかりに |
| な-adjective + な or である | {正直|しょうじき}なばかりに |
| noun + である | {初心者|しょしんしゃ}であるばかりに |

{私|わたし}が{余計|よけい}なことを{言|い}ったばかりに、{話|はなし}がまとまらなかった。 — Just because I said something unnecessary, we couldn't reach an agreement.
{説明書|せつめいしょ}を{読|よ}まなかったばかりに、{保証|ほしょう}が{受|う}けられなくなった。 — Just because I didn't read the instructions, I lost the warranty.
{英語|えいご}ができないばかりに、いい{仕事|しごと}を{逃|のが}してしまった。 — Just because I couldn't speak English, I missed out on a good job.

The result is something bad or unwanted. For a good result, use おかげで:
{安|やす}かったおかげで、たくさん{売|う}れた (it sold well thanks to the low price). ばかりに there would
sound as if selling well were a misfortune.

### 〜たいばかりに: just because (someone) wanted

With the たい form it means "just because (someone) wanted…", and the second half is something
they went to great lengths to do. Here the result needn't be bad; the point is how far the wish
drove them.

{限定品|げんていひん}を{手|て}に{入|い}れたいばかりに、{朝|あさ}{四時|よじ}から{並|なら}んだ。 — Just because I wanted to get the limited edition, I queued from four in the morning.
{子供|こども}に{会|あ}いたいばかりに、{父|ちち}は{毎週|まいしゅう}{三時間|さんじかん}かけてやってくる。 — Just to see the children, my father travels three hours every week.

### ばかりに and せいで

Both give the cause of a bad result, and often either works. せいで (N3) simply blames a cause and
is common in speech; ばかりに stresses that this one thing was enough, sounds more regretful, and
is more at home in writing and careful speech.

{雨|あめ}のせいで、お{客|きゃく}さんが{少|すく}なかった。 — Because of the rain, there were few customers. (a plain cause: ばかりに would be odd after a bare noun)
{一言|ひとこと}{謝|あやま}らなかったばかりに、{客|きゃく}を{失|うしな}った。 — Just because we didn't say sorry, we lost the customer.

## 〜だけに: precisely because

〜だけに takes a fact and says the result follows from it, more than usual. It goes two ways.

1. *As you'd expect from it.*

   {人気|にんき}の{店|みせ}だけに、{平日|へいじつ}でも{混|こ}んでいる。 — Being such a popular shop, it's crowded even on weekdays.
   {駅前|えきまえ}だけに、{家賃|やちん}が{高|たか}い。 — Being right by the station, the rent is high.

2. *All the more (often against the hope).* The fact makes the feeling stronger.

   {期待|きたい}していただけに、がっかりした。 — I'd expected so much that I was all the more disappointed.
   {高|たか}かっただけに、こわれたときはショックだった。 — Because it had been expensive, it was all the more of a shock when it broke.

| Before だけに | Example |
|---|---|
| verb, plain form | {期待|きたい}していただけに |
| い-adjective | {高|たか}いだけに |
| な-adjective + な | {有名|ゆうめい}なだけに |
| noun (+ である) | {人気|にんき}の{店|みせ}だけに, {専門家|せんもんか}であるだけに |

だけに can colour a good result or a bad one; the speaker just says "of course, given that…".

## 〜だけあって, 〜だけのことはある: as you'd expect (praise)

〜だけあって praises something for living up to what it is: its price, its name, its training. The
second half is a good point.

{高|たか}いだけあって、{品質|ひんしつ}がいい。 — It's expensive, but then the quality is good, as you'd expect.
{有名|ゆうめい}なブランドだけあって、{長|なが}く{使|つか}える。 — As you'd expect of a famous brand, it lasts a long time.
さすがプロだけあって、{説明|せつめい}が{分|わ}かりやすい。 — As you'd expect of a professional, the explanation is easy to follow.

At the end of a sentence it's 〜だけのことはある (or だけある): "it's worth it, it lives up to it".

このかばんは{十年|じゅうねん}{使|つか}ってもこわれない。{高|たか}かっただけのことはある。 — I've used this bag for ten years and it hasn't fallen apart. It was worth the price.

So: だけあって is almost always praise; だけに can go either way. "Being a famous restaurant, it was
all the more disappointing" needs だけに: {有名|ゆうめい}な{店|みせ}だけに、がっかりした.
さすが often comes before both: さすが{有名店|ゆうめいてん}だけあって.

## 〜ものだから, 〜もので: excuses and explanations

〜ものだから gives a reason as a personal explanation: "you see", "it's just that". It's very common
when apologizing or explaining why you did something. In speech it's often 〜もんだから; 〜もので is a
little more formal and suits apologies.

{道|みち}が{混|こ}んでいたもので、{遅|おく}れてしまいました。 — The roads were busy, you see, so I'm afraid I'm late.
{安|やす}かったものだから、つい{三|みっ}つも{買|か}っちゃった。 — It was so cheap, I ended up buying three.
{初|はじ}めてだったものですから、{使|つか}い{方|かた}が{分|わ}からなくて…。 — It was my first time, so I didn't know how to use it…

Two habits of these patterns:

- The second half is usually what happened or a state, not an order or an invitation. For "it's
  cheap, so buy it" use から: {安|やす}いから{買|か}いなさい.
- They soften: the speaker presents the reason as something that couldn't be helped. That's why
  they're polite in apologies, and why they can sound like excuses.

## Reminder: おかげで, せいで, あまり

> **Review (N3 6 and 15).** おかげで: a good result, "thanks to" ({割引券|わりびきけん}のおかげで{安|やす}く
> {買|か}えた). せいで: a bad result, blame ({値上|ねあ}げのせいで{客|きゃく}が{減|へ}った). 〜あまり(に):
> "so much that" ({心配|しんぱい}のあまり、{眠|ねむ}れなかった; {驚|おどろ}いたあまり、{声|こえ}が{出|で}なかった).

## Which one?

| Pattern | Result | Feeling | Register |
|---|---|---|---|
| おかげで | good | thanks | neutral |
| せいで | bad | blame | neutral, spoken |
| ばかりに | bad (or extreme effort after たい) | regret: just this one thing | written, careful speech |
| だけに | as expected, or all the stronger | "naturally, given that" | neutral |
| だけあって / だけのことはある | good | praise: lives up to it | neutral |
| ものだから / もので | what happened | excuse, explanation | spoken; もので in apologies |
| あまり(に) | extreme | too much feeling or effort | neutral, written |

## Buying, selling and counting

| Topic | Words |
|---|---|
| prices | {価格|かかく}, {定価|ていか}, {物価|ぶっか}, {単価|たんか}, {原価|げんか}, {安価|あんか}, {価値|かち}, {割高|わりだか}, {割安|わりやす}, {値札|ねふだ} |
| amounts | {金額|きんがく}, {額|がく}, {全額|ぜんがく}, {半額|はんがく}, {総額|そうがく}, {差額|さがく}, {多額|たがく}, {高額|こうがく}, {定額|ていがく}, {代金|だいきん} |
| selling | {販売|はんばい}, {販売店|はんばいてん}, {販売員|はんばいいん}, {通販|つうはん}, {市販|しはん}, {自動販売機|じどうはんばいき}, {小売|こう}り, {業者|ぎょうしゃ}, {売買|ばいばい}, {売|う}り{手|て}, {買|か}い{手|て} |
| sales | {売|う}り{上|あ}げ, {売|う}れ{行|ゆ}き, {売|う}り{切|き}れ, {値引|ねび}き, {安売|やすう}り, お{買|か}い{得|どく}, {割引券|わりびきけん}, クーポン, {価格競争|かかくきょうそう} |
| advertising | {宣伝|せんでん}, {宣言|せんげん}, チラシ, キャンペーン, ブランド, {新商品|しんしょうひん}, {店頭|てんとう} |
| shoppers | {消費者|しょうひしゃ}, {買|か}い{物|もの}{客|きゃく}, {客層|きゃくそう}, {一般|いっぱん}, {普段|ふだん} |
| goods | {普及品|ふきゅうひん}, {珍品|ちんぴん}, {珍味|ちんみ}, {生鮮食品|せいせんしょくひん}, {鮮度|せんど}, {保証|ほしょう}, {数量|すうりょう}, {枚数|まいすう}, コスト |
| counting | {計算|けいさん}, {暗算|あんざん}, {足|た}し{算|ざん}, {引|ひ}き{算|ざん}, {掛|か}け{算|ざん}, {割|わ}り{算|ざん}, {換算|かんさん}, {決算|けっさん}, {採算|さいさん}, {倍率|ばいりつ}, {均一|きんいつ}, {均等|きんとう} |

Notes:

- {価格|かかく} is the formal and written word for {値段|ねだん}; {定価|ていか} is the list price, before any
  discount. {物価|ぶっか} is prices in general (the cost of living).
- {宣伝|せんでん} is the activity (advertising, publicity); {広告|こうこく} (N3) is the advertisement itself.
- {割高|わりだか} and {割安|わりやす} compare value, not price: a big pack can cost more and still be
  {割安|わりやす}.
- Discounts are counted in tenths: {三割引|さんわりびき} is 30% off. {半額|はんがく} is half price.
- {百円|ひゃくえん}{均一|きんいつ}: everything at 100 yen. {均一|きんいつ} is "all the same"; {均等|きんとう} is
  "in equal shares".
- {一般|いっぱん}の{人|ひと} is a member of the public; {一般的|いっぱんてき} (N3) is "general, common".

### Big numbers

Japanese counts in groups of four digits: {万|まん} (10,000), {億|おく} (100,000,000), then ちょう
(a trillion; its kanji is outside N2).

| Number | Japanese | English |
|---|---|---|
| 10,000 | {一万|いちまん} | ten thousand |
| 1,000,000 | {百万|ひゃくまん} | a million |
| 100,000,000 | {一億|いちおく} | a hundred million |
| 1,000,000,000 | {十億|じゅうおく} | a billion |
| 100,000,000,000 | {千億|せんおく} | a hundred billion |
| 1,000,000,000,000 | {一|いっ}ちょう | a trillion |

So "a billion yen" is {十億円|じゅうおくえん}, and a company with sales of 3.5 billion yen has
{売|う}り{上|あ}げ{三十五億円|さんじゅうごおくえん}. Times: {二倍|にばい} (twice), {三倍|さんばい}, {十倍|じゅうばい};
{倍|ばい} alone is "double".

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji: selling and prices, quality, and numbers.

### Selling and prices

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 販 | sell | ハン | — | 11 | {販売|はんばい}, {販売店|はんばいてん}, {通販|つうはん}, {市販|しはん}, {自動販売機|じどうはんばいき} |
| 価 | price, value | カ | — | 8 | {価格|かかく}, {価値|かち}, {定価|ていか}, {物価|ぶっか}, {単価|たんか}, {原価|げんか} |
| 額 | amount; frame; forehead | ガク | ひたい | 18 | {金額|きんがく}, {額|がく}, {半額|はんがく}, {全額|ぜんがく}, {総額|そうがく}, {額|ひたい} (forehead) |
| 宣 | proclaim | セン | — | 9 | {宣伝|せんでん}, {宣言|せんげん} |
| 算 | calculate | サン | — | 14 | {計算|けいさん}, {予算|よさん}, {算数|さんすう}, {暗算|あんざん}, {決算|けっさん}, {足|た}し{算|ざん} |

- {物価|ぶっか} (N3), {予算|よさん} (N3) and {算数|さんすう} (arithmetic at primary school) are now written
  with kanji.
- 算 becomes ザン after a verb stem: {足|た}し{算|ざん}, {引|ひ}き{算|ざん}, {掛|か}け{算|ざん}, {割|わ}り{算|ざん}.
- 販 has the "shell" (money) on the left, like many money kanji: 販, 財, 資, 貯.

### Fresh, rare and ordinary

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 鮮 | fresh; vivid | セン | あざ(やか) | 17 | {新鮮|しんせん}, {鮮度|せんど}, {生鮮食品|せいせんしょくひん}, {鮮|あざ}やか |
| 珍 | rare | チン | めずら(しい) | 9 | {珍|めずら}しい, {珍品|ちんぴん}, {珍味|ちんみ} |
| 普 | general, wide | フ | — | 12 | {普通|ふつう}, {普段|ふだん}, {普及品|ふきゅうひん}, {普及|ふきゅう} (lesson 17) |
| 般 | general; sort | ハン | — | 10 | {一般|いっぱん}, {一般的|いっぱんてき}, {全般|ぜんぱん} |
| 均 | even, level | キン | — | 7 | {平均|へいきん}, {均一|きんいつ}, {均等|きんとう} |

- {新鮮|しんせん}, {普通|ふつう}, {一般的|いっぱんてき} and {平均|へいきん} (N3 and earlier) are now written with
  kanji.
- 般 is ハン, which becomes パン in {一般|いっぱん} and {全般|ぜんぱん}.
- 鮮 is a fish (魚) beside a sheep: two things best eaten fresh. With 額 (18 strokes), 鮮 (17) is
  one of this lesson's two longest kanji.

### Numbers and counting

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 枚 | counter for flat things | マイ | — | 8 | 〜{枚|まい}, {一枚|いちまい}, {枚数|まいすう} |
| 億 | hundred million | オク | — | 15 | {億|おく}, {一億|いちおく}, {十億|じゅうおく}, {億万長者|おくまんちょうじゃ} |
| 倍 | times, double | バイ | — | 10 | {倍|ばい}, {二倍|にばい}, {倍率|ばいりつ} |

- The counters 〜{枚|まい} and 〜{倍|ばい} (N4 and N3) are now written with kanji: チケット{二枚|にまい},
  {三倍|さんばい}.
- 億 and 倍 both have the person radical (亻) on the left.

Memory notes:

- 販: money (the shell) going back (反) and forth: selling.
- 価: a person (亻) beside 西 (west) over a little table: a person setting out goods and naming a price.
- 額: 客 (guest) beside the "head" shape on the right: the forehead a guest bows, the frame above
  the face.
- 宣: a roof (宀) over a sun between two lines: news spread through the whole house: to proclaim.
- 算: bamboo (竹, lesson 3) over 目 and two hands: counting with bamboo sticks.
- 鮮: 魚 (fish) and a sheep: things that must be fresh.
- 珍: 王 (here, a jewel) beside fine slanting strokes like hair: a precious, rare jewel.
- 普: 並 (lined up, lesson 27) over 日 (sun): the sun shining on everything in a row: general.
- 般: a boat on the left and a hand holding a tool on the right: all sorts of things carried by
  boat.
- 均: earth (土) beside a shape divided evenly: earth smoothed flat.
- 枚: a tree (木) and a hand (攵): planks counted one by one.
- 億: a person (亻) and 意 (mind): a number only the mind can hold.
- 倍: a person (亻) beside a shape split open: one turned into two, double.

```trace
販価額宣算鮮珍普般均枚億倍
```

## Dialogue: the cheap vacuum cleaner

Two friends, Haruka and Sōta, meet at a café. (Casual speech.)

```dialogue
# A bargain that wasn't
はるか: そうた、なんか{元気|げんき}ないね。どうしたの？
= Sōta, you look a bit down. What's wrong?
そうた: {聞|き}いてよ。{先月|せんげつ}{通販|つうはん}で{掃除機|そうじき}を{買|か}ったんだけど、もうこわれちゃって。
= Listen to this. I bought a vacuum cleaner online last month, and it's already broken.
はるか: え、もう？
= What, already?
そうた: {値段|ねだん}だけで{選|えら}んだばかりに、こうなったんだよ。{半額|はんがく}だったものだから、つい。
= This is what I get for choosing on price alone. It was half price, you see, so I just went for it.
はるか: {保証|ほしょう}は？
= What about the warranty?
そうた: それがさ、{説明書|せつめいしょ}を{捨|す}てちゃったんだ。
= That's the thing. I threw the instructions away.
はるか: あーあ。{安|やす}かっただけに、{残念|ざんねん}だね。
= Oh no. And it being such a bargain makes it all the more annoying.
そうた: うん。はるかのは{何|なん}だっけ。
= Yeah. What's yours, again?
はるか: うちのはドイツのブランド。{定価|ていか}で{買|か}ったから{高|たか}かったけど、{十年|じゅうねん}{使|つか}っても{全然|ぜんぜん}{問題|もんだい}ないよ。
= Mine's a German brand. I paid the list price, so it was expensive, but it's been fine for ten years.
そうた: さすが、{有名|ゆうめい}なブランドだけあるね。
= Well, that famous brand lives up to its name.
はるか: うん、{高|たか}かっただけのことはあったよ。{次|つぎ}は{店頭|てんとう}で{見|み}てから{買|か}えば？{販売員|はんばいいん}さんに{質問|しつもん}もできるし。
= Yeah, it was worth the money. Next time why not look in a shop before you buy? You can ask the staff questions, too.
そうた: そうする。でも{店|みせ}に{行|い}くと、{販売員|はんばいいん}さんの{説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}いて、つい{高|たか}いのを{買|か}っちゃいそう。
= I will. But if I go to a shop, I'll probably listen to the salesperson and end up buying an expensive one.
はるか: それなら{予算|よさん}を{決|き}めてから{行|い}けばいいじゃない。
= Then just set a budget before you go.
そうた: そうだね。{今度|こんど}こそ{失敗|しっぱい}しないぞ。
= You're right. This time I'm not going to mess it up.
```

{説明書|せつめいしょ} = instructions. Sōta's ばかりに comes
with regret, his ものだから is an excuse, Haruka's だけに makes the annoyance stronger, and
だけある / だけのことはあった praise the expensive machine.

## Reading: the cheapest supermarket in town

A newspaper-style article (だ/である style).

> {駅|えき}の{東口|ひがしぐち}に{大型|おおがた}スーパーが{開店|かいてん}してから{半年|はんとし}。{周辺|しゅうへん}の{店|みせ}の{間|あいだ}で、{激|はげ}しい{価格競争|かかくきょうそう}が{続|つづ}いている。
>
> {新|あたら}しい{店|みせ}は、{野菜|やさい}や{肉|にく}などの{生鮮食品|せいせんしょくひん}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に、{近所|きんじょ}の{店|みせ}より{一割|いちわり}から{二割|にわり}{安|やす}い{価格|かかく}で{販売|はんばい}している。{開店|かいてん}の{日|ひ}にはチラシの{効果|こうか}もあって、{朝|あさ}から{千人|せんにん}{以上|いじょう}の{買|か}い{物|もの}{客|きゃく}が{並|なら}んだ。{近所|きんじょ}に{住|す}む{会社員|かいしゃいん}の{男性|だんせい}は「{食費|しょくひ}が{月|つき}に{五千円|ごせんえん}ほど{減|へ}った。{物価|ぶっか}が{上|あ}がっているだけに、{本当|ほんとう}に{助|たす}かる」と{喜|よろこ}ぶ。
>
> {困|こま}っているのは{昔|むかし}からのしょうてんがいだ。{四十年|よんじゅうねん}{続|つづ}く{八百屋|やおや}の{主人|しゅじん}は「{安|やす}さだけで{勝負|しょうぶ}すると、{大|おお}きな{店|みせ}にはかなわない。{値下|ねさ}げを{続|つづ}けたばかりに{店|みせ}を{閉|し}めた{仲間|なかま}もいる」と{話|はな}す。この{店|みせ}の{客|きゃく}も、{以前|いぜん}の{三分|さんぶん}の{二|に}ほどに{減|へ}ったという。
>
> {一方|いっぽう}で、{安|やす}さ{以外|いがい}で{客|きゃく}を{集|あつ}める{店|みせ}もある。ある{魚屋|さかなや}は、{毎朝|まいあさ}{市場|いちば}で{選|えら}んだ{魚|さかな}の{鮮度|せんど}と、{調理法|ちょうりほう}を{教|おし}えてくれるサービスで{人気|にんき}だ。{値段|ねだん}は{少|すこ}し{高|たか}いが、「さすが{専門店|せんもんてん}だけあって、{味|あじ}が{違|ちが}う」という{声|こえ}が{多|おお}い。{店主|てんしゅ}は「{値段|ねだん}で{勝|か}てない{以上|いじょう}、{品質|ひんしつ}で{勝負|しょうぶ}するしかない」と{言|い}う。
>
> {消費者|しょうひしゃ}にとって、{安|やす}く{買|か}えるのはありがたいことだ。だが、{近所|きんじょ}の{店|みせ}がなくなれば、{車|くるま}を{持|も}たないお{年寄|としよ}りは{困|こま}るだろう。{便利|べんり}な{店|みせ}ができただけに、{町|まち}の{店|みせ}の{役割|やくわり}をもう{一度|いちど}{考|かんが}える{必要|ひつよう}がありそうだ。{安|やす}さを{求|もと}めるあまり、{大切|たいせつ}なものを{失|うしな}ってはいないだろうか。

{大型|おおがた} = large (model); {周辺|しゅうへん} = the surrounding area (lesson 27's word);
しょうてんがい = shopping street (its last kanji is outside N2); {八百屋|やおや} = greengrocer; {勝負|しょうぶ}する =
to compete; かなわない = can't match; {調理法|ちょうりほう} = cooking method.

1. What has happened since the large supermarket opened?
2. Why does the greengrocer say some shopkeepers closed down?
3. How does the fishmonger attract customers?
4. What does the writer think should be done now?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Fierce price competition among the shops around it; it sells fresh food 10–20% cheaper.
2. Because they kept cutting prices ({値下|ねさ}げを{続|つづ}けたばかりに): competing on price alone, a small shop can't beat a big one.
3. With the freshness of fish chosen at the market every morning and a service that explains how to cook them; customers say the taste is different, as you'd expect of a specialist.
4. Precisely because a convenient shop has opened, the town should think again about what local shops do (for example for older people without cars).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

It's six months since a large supermarket opened at the east exit of the station. Fierce price
competition continues among the shops around it.

The new shop sells fresh food such as vegetables and meat, above all, at prices 10 to 20 per
cent lower than nearby shops. On opening day, with help from its flyers, more than a thousand
shoppers queued from the morning. A man who works for a company and lives nearby is delighted:
"My food bill has gone down by about 5,000 yen a month. With prices rising, it really helps."

The ones in trouble are the old shopping streets. The owner of a greengrocer's that has been
going for forty years says, "If you compete on cheapness alone, you can't beat the big shops. I
have friends who closed down just because they kept cutting their prices." His own shop is said to have lost about a third of
its customers.

On the other hand, some shops attract customers with something other than low prices. One
fishmonger is popular for the freshness of the fish chosen at the market every morning and for
a service that tells you how to cook them. The prices are a little higher, but many say, "As
you'd expect of a specialist shop, the taste is different." The owner says, "Since we can't win
on price, we have to compete on quality."

For consumers, being able to buy cheaply is welcome. But if the local shops disappear, older
people without cars will struggle. Precisely because a convenient shop has opened, it seems we
need to think again about the role of the town's shops. In our eagerness for low prices, aren't
we losing something important?

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{安|やす}さだけで{選|えら}んだばかりに、{失敗|しっぱい}しました。
= Just because I chose on price alone, it went wrong.
{期待|きたい}していただけに、{残念|ざんねん}です。
= I'd expected a lot, so it's all the more disappointing.
さすがプロだけあって、{上手|じょうず}ですね。
= As you'd expect of a professional, you're very good.
{道|みち}が{混|こ}んでいたもので、{遅|おく}くなりました。
= The roads were busy, so I'm late.
{一億円|いちおくえん}あったら、{何|なに}に{使|つか}いますか。
= What would you spend a hundred million yen on?
```

## Common mistakes

- ばかりに with a good result: "Thanks to the low price, it sold well" is
  {安|やす}かったおかげで、よく{売|う}れた.
- だけあって for a disappointment: "Being a famous restaurant, it was all the more
  disappointing" needs だけに; だけあって praises.
- ものだから before a command: {安|やす}いものだから、{買|か}いなさい sounds odd; give the advice with から.
- Grouping big numbers in threes, as in English: Japanese groups them in fours, so 10,000,000 is
  {千万|せんまん} and 1,000,000,000 is {十億|じゅうおく}.
- {価格|かかく} in casual chat: {値段|ねだん} is the everyday word; {価格|かかく} sounds like a notice or a report.
- {宣伝|せんでん} for the advert itself: a poster or a TV advert is {広告|こうこく} or a CM (シーエム).

## Key points

- 〜ばかりに: just because (of this one thing), with a bad result and regret; 〜たいばかりに: just
  because (someone) wanted, so they went to great lengths.
- 〜だけに: precisely because; as you'd expect, or all the more.
- 〜だけあって / 〜だけのことはある: praise; it lives up to what it is.
- 〜ものだから / 〜もので: a personal reason or excuse; not before orders or invitations.
- Review: おかげで (good), せいで (bad), あまり (too much).
- Big numbers: {万|まん}, {億|おく}, ちょう; 1 billion = {十億|じゅうおく}.
- New kanji: 販 価 額 宣 算 鮮 珍 普 般 均 枚 億 倍. Write {物価|ぶっか}, {新鮮|しんせん}, {普通|ふつう},
  {一般的|いっぱんてき}, {平均|へいきん}, {予算|よさん}, 〜{枚|まい}, 〜{倍|ばい} with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Based on and in line with: にもとづいて, をもとに, にそって, におうじて
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lessons 11 and 12 gave reasons. This lesson gives the **[[basis]]** of an action: what a decision
rests on, what something was made from, what it follows and what it varies with. These are the
phrases of reports, research, news and official explanations.

{調査|ちょうさ}の{結果|けっか}に{基|もと}づいて、{計画|けいかく}を{見直|みなお}した。 — We reviewed the plan on the basis of the survey results.
{祖母|そぼ}の{話|はなし}をもとに、{小説|しょうせつ}を{書|か}いた。 — I wrote a novel based on my grandmother's stories.
マニュアルにそって{作業|さぎょう}を{進|すす}めてください。 — Please carry out the work following the manual.
{年齢|ねんれい}に{応|おう}じて、{料金|りょうきん}が{変|か}わります。 — The fee varies according to age.

The theme is research, data and statistics: surveys, measurement, probability and ratios,
samples and standards. University life and papers were N3's (lesson 12), and so were society's
percentages ({割合|わりあい}, {変化|へんか}); science and space are lesson 18's. Carried words that now
take kanji: {調査|ちょうさ}, {検査|けんさ}, {対象|たいしょう}, {傾向|けいこう}, {目標|もくひょう}, {伝統|でんとう}.

## 〜に{基|もと}づいて: based on

〜に{基|もと}づいて says what an action or a judgement rests on: facts, data, a law, a rule, an
experience. The basis stays as it is; you measure against it or follow it. It's formal and very
common in writing.

| Form | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜に{基|もと}づいて / 〜に{基|もと}づき | before a verb (〜{基|もと}づき is written) | {事実|じじつ}に{基|もと}づいて{書|か}く |
| 〜に{基|もと}づく + noun | before a noun | {法律|ほうりつ}に{基|もと}づく{処分|しょぶん} |
| 〜に{基|もと}づいた + noun | before a noun | {経験|けいけん}に{基|もと}づいた{意見|いけん} |

{裁判官|さいばんかん}は{法律|ほうりつ}に{基|もと}づいて{判断|はんだん}する。 — Judges decide on the basis of the law.
これは{実際|じっさい}の{事件|じけん}に{基|もと}づいた{映画|えいが}だ。 — This is a film based on a real case.
{国|くに}の{基準|きじゅん}に{基|もと}づき、{水|みず}の{安全性|あんぜんせい}を{検査|けんさ}しました。 — Following national standards, we tested the water's safety.

The verb itself is {基|もと}づく (to be based on), and it's nearly always used in these forms:
この{計画|けいかく}はデータに{基|もと}づいている (this plan is based on data).

## 〜をもとに(して): using as a source

〜をもとに(して) says what you used as material to make something new: a story turned into a film,
answers turned into a product, a sketch turned into a design. The source is changed or built on.
もと is written in kana in this course (in print you'll also see it with kanji).

{祖母|そぼ}の{話|はなし}をもとに、{小説|しょうせつ}を{書|か}いた。 — I wrote a novel based on my grandmother's stories.
アンケートの{回答|かいとう}をもとにして、{新商品|しんしょうひん}を{開発|かいはつ}した。 — We developed a new product using the questionnaire answers.
{古|ふる}い{写真|しゃしん}をもとにした{町|まち}の{地図|ちず}が{完成|かんせい}した。 — A map of the town drawn from old photographs has been finished.

### に{基|もと}づいて or をもとに?

Often either works: データに{基|もと}づいて / データをもとに{予測|よそく}する (forecast from data). The
difference is in what the first noun is.

| | に{基|もと}づいて | をもとに |
|---|---|---|
| the noun is | grounds, a standard, a rule | material, a source |
| what happens to it | you follow it or check against it | you build something new from it |
| typical nouns | {法律|ほうりつ}, {規則|きそく}, {事実|じじつ}, {基準|きじゅん}, {調査|ちょうさ} | {話|はなし}, {写真|しゃしん}, {資料|しりょう}, {作品|さくひん}, アイデア |

Where only one sounds right:

- {規則|きそく}に{基|もと}づいて{処分|しょぶん}する (discipline someone under the rules). With をもとに it sounds
  as if the rules were raw material for something new.
- {小説|しょうせつ}をもとにしたドラマ (a drama adapted from a novel). に{基|もと}づいた sounds as if the novel
  were evidence.

## 〜にそって: along, following

〜にそって / 〜にそった + noun has two uses. (Its kanji is outside N2, so it's written in kana.)

1. *Along* something long: a road, a river, a coast, a wall.

   {川|かわ}にそってさくらの{木|き}が{並|なら}んでいる。 — Cherry trees line the river.
   {海岸|かいがん}にそって{道|みち}が{続|つづ}いている。 — The road runs along the coast.

2. *Following* a plan, a policy, a manual or someone's wishes.

   {会社|かいしゃ}の{方針|ほうしん}にそって、{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てた。 — We drew up the plan in line with company policy.
   お{客様|きゃくさま}のご{希望|きぼう}にそったプランをご{提案|ていあん}します。 — We'll suggest a plan in line with your wishes.

> **Review (N3 4): 〜にしたがって.** It also means "following": {指示|しじ}にしたがって{行動|こうどう}する
> (act as instructed). にしたがって is obeying (instructions, rules, a person); にそって is keeping to a
> line (a plan, a policy, a route). Many sentences take either. にしたがって also means "as A
> changes, B": {年|とし}を{取|と}るにしたがって (as you get older); にそって doesn't.

## 〜に{応|おう}じて: according to, in response to

〜に{応|おう}じて / 〜に{応|おう}じた + noun says that something changes to match something else: age,
need, ability, the number of people, the season.

{年齢|ねんれい}に{応|おう}じて、{質問|しつもん}の{内容|ないよう}を{変|か}えた。 — We changed the questions according to age.
{必要|ひつよう}に{応|おう}じて、{資料|しりょう}をお{送|おく}りします。 — We'll send materials as needed.
{能力|のうりょく}に{応|おう}じた{仕事|しごと}を{任|まか}せる。 — We give people work that suits their ability.

The verb {応|おう}じる on its own means "to respond to, accept, take part in": {調査|ちょうさ}に{応|おう}じる
(take part in a survey), {注文|ちゅうもん}に{応|おう}じる (take an order). Lesson 14 adds
に{応|こた}える (respond to hopes and expectations), with the same kanji and a different reading.

## 〜をもって: by means of; as of (to recognize)

〜をもって is very formal. You'll see it on notices and in announcements.

{本日|ほんじつ}をもって、{受付|うけつけ}を{終了|しゅうりょう}いたします。 — As of today, applications are closed.
{結果|けっか}は{書面|しょめん}をもってお{知|し}らせします。 — We will inform you of the results in writing.

## Which one?

| Pattern | Meaning | Typical nouns | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| に{基|もと}づいて | on the basis of (a standard you follow) | law, facts, data, standards | {基準|きじゅん}に{基|もと}づいて{判断|はんだん}する |
| をもとに | using as material | stories, photos, answers, data | {写真|しゃしん}をもとに{地図|ちず}を{作|つく}る |
| にそって | along; in line with | roads, rivers; plans, policy, wishes | {計画|けいかく}にそって{進|すす}める |
| に{応|おう}じて | varying with, as fits | age, need, ability, number | {人数|にんずう}に{応|おう}じて{部屋|へや}を{選|えら}ぶ |
| にしたがって | obeying; as A changes | instructions, rules; changes | {指示|しじ}にしたがう |
| をもって | by means of; as of (formal) | dates, documents | {本日|ほんじつ}をもって{終了|しゅうりょう} |

## Research words

| Topic | Words |
|---|---|
| surveys | {調査|ちょうさ}, {世論調査|よろんちょうさ}, アンケート, {回答者|かいとうしゃ}, {対象者|たいしょうしゃ}, {実態|じったい}, {集計|しゅうけい} |
| samples | {標本|ひょうほん}, サンプル, {母集団|ぼしゅうだん}, {信頼性|しんらいせい}, {誤差|ごさ} |
| measuring | {測定|そくてい}, {測定値|そくていち}, {計測|けいそく}, {測量|そくりょう}, {観測|かんそく}, {予測|よそく}, {数値|すうち} |
| rates and ratios | {確率|かくりつ}, {比率|ひりつ}, {効率|こうりつ}, {能率|のうりつ}, {合格率|ごうかくりつ}, {比例|ひれい}, {倍増|ばいぞう} |
| statistics | {統計|とうけい}, {統計学|とうけいがく}, {平均値|へいきんち}, {指数|しすう}, {指標|しひょう}, {変動|へんどう}, {前年比|ぜんねんひ}, {算出|さんしゅつ}, {下位|かい} |
| causes | {要因|よういん}, {要素|ようそ}, {相関|そうかん}, {因果関係|いんがかんけい}, {現象|げんしょう}, {反応|はんのう} |
| standards | {基準|きじゅん}, {基準値|きじゅんち}, {標準|ひょうじゅん}, {基本|きほん}, {検証|けんしょう}, {検定|けんてい} |
| layers and groups | {層|そう}, {年齢層|ねんれいそう}, {若年層|じゃくねんそう}, {階層|かいそう}, {地層|ちそう}, {高層|こうそう} |

Notes:

- {比率|ひりつ} is a ratio (A to B: {男女|だんじょ}の{比率|ひりつ}); {割合|わりあい} (N3) is a share of a whole
  ({女性|じょせい}の{割合|わりあい}). In practice they overlap.
- {相関|そうかん} (correlation) is not {因果関係|いんがかんけい} (cause and effect). A good report says which
  it has found.
- はかる has several kanji: {測|はか}る for length, depth and size, {計|はか}る for time, {量|はか}る for weight.
  They're one word (N3's はかる, which N3 wrote {量|はか}る), so there's no new vocab item; choose the kanji by what you measure.
- {効率|こうりつ} is efficiency in general (a machine, a method); {能率|のうりつ} is a person's efficiency at
  work.
- {現象|げんしょう} (phenomenon) and {減少|げんしょう} (decrease, N3) sound the same. In a sentence about
  numbers, it's usually {減少|げんしょう}.

### Describing data

| Japanese | English |
|---|---|
| {前年比|ぜんねんひ}で{五|ご}パーセント{増加|ぞうか}した | rose 5% year on year |
| {三割|さんわり}を{超|こ}える | exceed 30% |
| {横|よこ}ばいが{続|つづ}いている | has stayed flat |
| {平均値|へいきんち}を{上回|うわまわ}る / {下回|したまわ}る | above / below the mean |
| {年齢層|ねんれいそう}が{上|あ}がるにつれて{高|たか}くなる | gets higher with each older age group |
| {誤差|ごさ}にすぎない | is no more than measurement error (lesson 20's に{過|す}ぎない) |

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji: bases and elements, measuring and checking, and change.

### Bases, standards and elements

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 基 | base, foundation | キ | もと | 11 | {基本|きほん}, {基準|きじゅん}, {基地|きち}, {基|もと}づく |
| 標 | mark, sign | ヒョウ | — | 15 | {標準|ひょうじゅん}, {標本|ひょうほん}, {目標|もくひょう}, {標識|ひょうしき}, {指標|しひょう}, {標準語|ひょうじゅんご} |
| 素 | element; plain | ソ, ス | — | 10 | {要素|ようそ}, {素材|そざい}, {元素|げんそ}, {質素|しっそ}, {素早|すばや}い, {素直|すなお}, {素人|しろうと} |
| 層 | layer, stratum | ソウ | — | 14 | {層|そう}, {年齢層|ねんれいそう}, {地層|ちそう}, {階層|かいそう}, {高層|こうそう} |

- {目標|もくひょう}, {標準語|ひょうじゅんご} (N4) and {素直|すなお} (N3) are now written with kanji.
- {素人|しろうと} (amateur, layperson) is a special reading of the whole word: it's neither ソ nor ス.
  Its opposite, くろうと (expert), has a first kanji outside N2.
- 素 is ソ in most words and ス in a few everyday ones: {素直|すなお}, {素早|すばや}い.

### Measuring and checking

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 測 | measure | ソク | はか(る) | 12 | {測定|そくてい}, {測量|そくりょう}, {予測|よそく}, {観測|かんそく}, {計測|けいそく}, {測|はか}る |
| 査 | investigate | サ | — | 9 | {調査|ちょうさ}, {検査|けんさ}, {捜査|そうさ} |
| 検 | examine, check | ケン | — | 12 | {検査|けんさ}, {検証|けんしょう}, {検定|けんてい}, {点検|てんけん}, {検察|けんさつ} |
| 統 | unite; govern | トウ | — | 12 | {統計|とうけい}, {統一|とういつ}, {伝統|でんとう}, {伝統的|でんとうてき} |

- {調査|ちょうさ}, {検査|けんさ}, {捜査|そうさ} (a police investigation; its first kanji is lesson 29's) and
  {伝統|でんとう}, {伝統的|でんとうてき} (N3) are now written with kanji.
- 測, 検 and 統 are all 12 strokes. 検 has the tree radical (木) and 険 (danger) has the "hill" one
  (阝) with the same right side: checking wood, guarding against danger.

### Rates, change and response

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 率 | rate, ratio; lead | リツ, ソツ | — | 11 | {確率|かくりつ}, {比率|ひりつ}, {効率|こうりつ}, {合格率|ごうかくりつ}, {率直|そっちょく} |
| 象 | phenomenon; elephant | ショウ, ゾウ | — | 12 | {現象|げんしょう}, {対象|たいしょう}, {印象|いんしょう}, {気象|きしょう}, {象|ぞう} |
| 傾 | lean, tilt | ケイ | かたむ(く), かたむ(ける) | 13 | {傾|かたむ}く, {傾|かたむ}ける, {傾向|けいこう}, {傾|かたむ}き |
| 応 | respond | オウ | こた(える) | 7 | {反応|はんのう}, {対応|たいおう}, {応用|おうよう}, {応答|おうとう}, {適応|てきおう}, {応|おう}じる, {応援|おうえん}, {応募|おうぼ} |

- {対象|たいしょう}, {傾向|けいこう}, {対応|たいおう}, {応援|おうえん}, {応募|おうぼ} (N3 and earlier) and
  {象|ぞう} (elephant, N4) are now written with kanji.
- 率 is リツ in rates ({確率|かくりつ}, {比率|ひりつ}, {合格率|ごうかくりつ}) and ソツ in {率直|そっちょく}
  (frank). Learn ソツ with that word.
- 応 has a second kun'yomi, こた(える), for lesson 14's に{応|こた}える.
- {反応|はんのう} is read はんのう, not はんおう: オウ becomes ノウ after ン here.

Memory notes:

- 基: a basket shape on top, set on earth (土): the base everything stands on.
- 標: a tree (木) and a sign on a post (the right side): a marker.
- 素: a plant growing (the top) over thread (糸, lesson 24): raw, plain thread, the basic element.
- 層: a roof (尸) over a stack of layers: storeys, strata.
- 測: water (氵) beside 則 (rule, lesson 11): measuring water by a rule.
- 査: a tree (木) over a pile of planks: wood checked piece by piece.
- 検: a tree (木) and many people under one roof: checking each one.
- 統: thread (糸) beside a shape that fills up: threads pulled together into one.
- 率: thread being pulled straight between dots and lines: leading, and the rate of the pull.
- 象: the shape of an elephant, trunk at the top, legs below.
- 傾: a person (亻) beside a head that leans over: tilting.
- 応: a roof (广) over 心 (heart): the heart that answers.
- 含: 今 (now) over 口 (mouth): something held in the mouth right now: to contain.

## Dialogue: planning a survey

Yui and Kenta are graduate students. A city has asked their professor's lab to survey how
residents use the public library. (Polite-casual, as between colleagues.)

```dialogue
# In the lab
ゆい: {市|し}から{頼|たの}まれた{図書館|としょかん}の{調査|ちょうさ}、どう{進|すす}める？
= How shall we go about the library survey the city asked for?
けんた: まず、{去年|きょねん}の{貸|か}し{出|だ}しのデータをもとに、{利用者|りようしゃ}の{傾向|けいこう}を{見|み}てみようと{思|おも}う。
= First I thought we'd look at trends among users, using last year's lending data.
ゆい: いいね。それで{気|き}になることが{出|で}てきたら、アンケートで{確|たし}かめる、と。
= Good. Then if anything interesting comes up, we check it with a questionnaire.
けんた: うん。{対象者|たいしょうしゃ}はどうやって{選|えら}ぶ？
= Right. How do we choose who to ask?
ゆい: {図書館|としょかん}に{来|く}る{人|ひと}だけに{聞|き}くと、{来|こ}ない{人|ひと}の{理由|りゆう}が{分|わ}からないでしょう。{住民|じゅうみん}{全体|ぜんたい}から{選|えら}ばないと。
= If we only ask people who come to the library, we won't find out why the others don't come. We need to choose from all residents.
けんた: そうだね。{年齢層|ねんれいそう}に{応|おう}じて{人数|にんずう}を{決|き}めたほうがいいかな。{若年層|じゃくねんそう}は{回答率|かいとうりつ}が{低|ひく}いから。
= True. Should we decide the numbers according to age group? Young people's response rate is low.
ゆい: それは{先生|せんせい}に{相談|そうだん}しよう。{市|し}の{方針|ほうしん}にそって{質問|しつもん}を{作|つく}る{必要|ひつよう}もあるし。
= Let's ask the professor about that. We also need to write the questions in line with the city's policy.
けんた: {質問|しつもん}の{書|か}き{方|かた}で{結果|けっか}が{変|か}わるから、{気|き}を{付|つ}けないとね。
= We'll have to be careful: the wording of the questions changes the results.
ゆい: うん。あと、{報告書|ほうこくしょ}には{数字|すうじ}に{基|もと}づいたことだけを{書|か}こう。{私|わたし}たちの{印象|いんしょう}は{入|い}れないで。
= Yes. And let's only put things in the report that are based on the figures. Not our impressions.
けんた: {了解|りょうかい}。{相関|そうかん}があっても、{因果関係|いんがかんけい}とは{限|かぎ}らないからね。
= Got it. A correlation doesn't necessarily mean cause and effect, after all.
ゆい: さすが{統計|とうけい}の{授業|じゅぎょう}、{真面目|まじめ}に{聞|き}いてたね。
= You really did listen in statistics class, didn't you.
けんた: {一応|いちおう}ね。じゃ、データの{集計|しゅうけい}から{始|はじ}めようか。
```

{回答率|かいとうりつ} = response rate; {了解|りょうかい} = understood, got it (its first kanji is lesson 27's); {一応|いちおう} =
more or less, for what it's worth. Count the basis phrases: をもとに (data as material), に{応|おう}じて
(numbers to match age groups), にそって (following the city's policy), に{基|もと}づいた (only what
the figures support).

## Reading: how an opinion poll works

An explanatory piece (だ/である style).

> {新聞|しんぶん}やテレビは、よく「{世論調査|よろんちょうさ}によると、{賛成|さんせい}は{四割|よんわり}」といった{数字|すうじ}を{伝|つた}える。だが、{調査|ちょうさ}に{答|こた}えるのは{千人|せんにん}から{二千人|にせんにん}{程度|ていど}にすぎない。それでなぜ{国民|こくみん}{全体|ぜんたい}の{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かるのだろうか。
>
> ポイントになるのは、{標本|ひょうほん}の{選|えら}び{方|かた}である。{調査|ちょうさ}を{行|おこな}う{側|がわ}は、{電話|でんわ}{番号|ばんごう}などをもとに、{対象者|たいしょうしゃ}を{偶然|ぐうぜん}に{任|まか}せて{選|えら}ぶ。こうすると、どの{人|ひと}も{同|おな}じ{確率|かくりつ}で{選|えら}ばれるため、{標本|ひょうほん}は{母集団|ぼしゅうだん}、つまり{国民|こくみん}{全体|ぜんたい}をよく{表|あらわ}すようになる。{統計学|とうけいがく}に{基|もと}づいて{計算|けいさん}すると、{千人|せんにん}{程度|ていど}でも{誤差|ごさ}は{数|すう}パーセントに{収|おさ}まる。
>
> もちろん、{結果|けっか}をそのまま{信|しん}じてよいわけではない。まず、{答|こた}えてくれる{人|ひと}にかたよりがあると、{結果|けっか}もずれる。{最近|さいきん}は{若年層|じゃくねんそう}ほど{電話|でんわ}に{出|で}ない{傾向|けいこう}があるため、{多|おお}くの{調査|ちょうさ}では{年齢層|ねんれいそう}に{応|おう}じて{結果|けっか}を{調整|ちょうせい}している。{調査|ちょうさ}を{断|ことわ}る{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えれば、{標本|ひょうほん}の{信頼性|しんらいせい}も{下|さ}がってしまう。
>
> また、{質問|しつもん}の{書|か}き{方|かた}によっても{数字|すうじ}は{変|か}わる。「{税金|ぜいきん}を{上|あ}げてでも{福祉|ふくし}を{手厚|てあつ}くするべきだと{思|おも}いますか」と{聞|き}くか、「{福祉|ふくし}のために{税金|ぜいきん}が{上|あ}がることに{賛成|さんせい}ですか」と{聞|き}くかで、{反応|はんのう}はかなり{違|ちが}うだろう。
>
> {世論調査|よろんちょうさ}の{数字|すうじ}を{見|み}るときは、どんな{人|ひと}を{対象|たいしょう}に、どんな{質問|しつもん}をしたのかを{確|たし}かめたい。{数字|すうじ}そのものより、その{数字|すうじ}がどう{作|つく}られたかが{大切|たいせつ}なのである。{数字|すうじ}だけが{一人歩|ひとりある}きしないよう、{注意|ちゅうい}したい。

{偶然|ぐうぜん}に{任|まか}せる = to leave to chance; {収|おさ}まる = to fall within;
かたより = bias (its kanji is outside N2); {一人歩|ひとりある}き = (of a figure or a word) taking on a life of its own; {手厚|てあつ}くする = to make more generous (its second kanji is lesson 30's); 〜てでも = even if it means…

1. What question does the first paragraph ask?
2. Why can a sample of about a thousand people represent the whole country?
3. Why do many surveys adjust their results by age group?
4. What does the writer advise readers to check?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. How a survey of only one or two thousand people can show the opinion of the whole nation.
2. Because the people are chosen by chance, so everyone has the same probability of being chosen and the sample reflects the population; by statistics, the error stays within a few per cent.
3. Because younger people tend not to answer the phone, so the people who answer are biased.
4. Who was surveyed and what question was asked: how the figure was produced matters more than the figure itself.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Newspapers and TV often report figures such as "according to an opinion poll, 40% are in
favour". But only about one to two thousand people answer the survey. So how can it show what
the whole nation thinks?

What matters is how the sample is chosen. Those running the survey use phone numbers and the like to
choose the people to ask by chance. That way everyone has the same probability of being chosen,
and the sample comes to represent the population, that is, the nation as a whole, well.
Calculated on the basis of statistics, even with about a thousand people the error falls within
a few per cent.

Of course, that doesn't mean you can simply believe the results. First, if the people who agree
to answer are biased, the results will be off too. These days, the younger people are, the more
they tend not to answer the phone, so many surveys adjust their results according to age group. And if more people refuse to take part, the
sample becomes less reliable.

The wording of the question also changes the figures. People's reactions would probably differ
quite a lot depending on whether you ask "Do you think welfare should be improved even if it
means raising taxes?" or "Are you in favour of taxes going up for the sake of welfare?"

When you look at an opinion poll figure, it's worth checking who was surveyed and what was
asked. What matters is not so much the figure itself as how it was produced. We should take care that the figure doesn't take on a life of its own.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{調査|ちょうさ}の{結果|けっか}に{基|もと}づいて{判断|はんだん}します。
= We'll decide on the basis of the survey results.
{実話|じつわ}をもとにした{映画|えいが}です。
= It's a film based on a true story.
{川|かわ}にそって{歩|ある}きましょう。
= Let's walk along the river.
{必要|ひつよう}に{応|おう}じて{連絡|れんらく}します。
= I'll contact you as needed.
{本日|ほんじつ}をもって{閉店|へいてん}いたします。
= We close for good as of today.
```

## Common mistakes

- をもとに with a rule or a standard: "We decided under the rules" is {規則|きそく}に{基|もと}づいて{決|き}めた.
- に{基|もと}づいて with raw material for something new: "a drama adapted from a novel" is
  {小説|しょうせつ}をもとにしたドラマ.
- Writing にそって with its kanji: the kanji is outside N2, so the course writes にそって.
- に{応|おう}じて for a fixed rule that doesn't vary: "according to the law" is {法律|ほうりつ}によると or
  {法律|ほうりつ}に{基|もと}づいて, not に{応|おう}じて, unless something changes with it.
- Reading {反応|はんのう} as はんおう, or {率直|そっちょく} as りっちょく.
- {素人|しろうと} read as そにん: it's a special reading.

## Key points

- 〜に{基|もと}づいて / {基|もと}づく / {基|もと}づいた: on the basis of (facts, law, data, standards);
  formal.
- 〜をもとに(して) / をもとにした: using as material for something new.
- 〜にそって / にそった (kana): along (a road, a river); in line with (a plan, policy, wishes).
- 〜に{応|おう}じて / に{応|おう}じた: varying with, to suit (age, need, ability); {応|おう}じる: to respond
  to, take part in.
- Review: 〜にしたがって (obeying; as A changes). Recognize: 〜をもって (as of; by means of).
- New kanji: 基 標 素 層 測 査 検 統 率 象 傾 応 含; special reading {素人|しろうと}. Write {調査|ちょうさ},
  {検査|けんさ}, {対象|たいしょう}, {傾向|けいこう}, {目標|もくひょう}, {伝統|でんとう}, {対応|たいおう} with kanji
  from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Over and concerning: をめぐって, に関する, にこたえて
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 13 gave the basis of an action. This lesson is about the topic of a discussion and the
response to it: what a debate is about (〜をめぐって), what information is about (〜に{関|かん}して), and
what an action answers (〜に{応|こた}えて). These are the phrases of news reports, meetings and
official statements.

{風力発電|ふうりょくはつでん}の{計画|けいかく}をめぐって、{住民|じゅうみん}の{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれている。 — Residents are divided over the wind-power plan.
{大気|たいき}{汚染|おせん}に{関|かん}するデータが{公開|こうかい}された。 — Data on air pollution has been made public.
{住民|じゅうみん}の{声|こえ}に{応|こた}えて、{市|し}はごみの{回収|かいしゅう}を{週|しゅう}{三回|さんかい}にした。 — In response to residents' views, the city increased rubbish collection to three times a week.

The theme is the environment, energy and resources: fuels and power, pollution and rubbish, ice
and the poles, mining and land, borders. N3 had climate and the basics ({環境|かんきょう}, {汚染|おせん},
{資源|しげん}, {温暖化|おんだんか} are carried, and now take kanji); disasters are lesson 16's.

## 〜をめぐって: over (a disputed issue)

〜をめぐって (before a noun 〜をめぐる) names the issue that people argue, compete or disagree over.
(Its kanji is outside N2, so it's written in kana.) What follows is a word of conflict or debate:
{議論|ぎろん}, {対立|たいりつ}, {争|あらそ}い, {意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれる, {裁判|さいばん}, {問題|もんだい}になる.

{原子力|げんしりょく}{発電所|はつでんしょ}の{再開|さいかい}をめぐって、{議論|ぎろん}が{続|つづ}いている。 — The debate over restarting the nuclear power station continues.
{水|みず}をめぐる{争|あらそ}いは、{昔|むかし}からあった。 — There have always been conflicts over water.
{親|おや}の{遺産|いさん}をめぐって、{兄弟|きょうだい}が{裁判|さいばん}を{起|お}こした。 — The siblings went to court over their parents' estate.

The noun is something several sides want or see differently. For a neutral "about", use について or
に{関|かん}して: a textbook is {環境|かんきょう}について{書|か}かれている; written with をめぐって it would
sound as if the textbook were taking part in a quarrel.

## 〜に{関|かん}して, 〜について: about, concerning

> **Review (N3 12).** 〜に{関|かん}して / 〜に{関|かん}する + noun: about, concerning (formal):
> {環境問題|かんきょうもんだい}に{関|かん}する{本|ほん}, この{件|けん}に{関|かん}してご{質問|しつもん}はありますか.
> 〜について / 〜についての + noun: about (everyday): {燃料|ねんりょう}について{調|しら}べる.

The difference from をめぐって:

| | について | に{関|かん}して | をめぐって |
|---|---|---|---|
| register | everyday | formal | formal, news |
| the noun is | any topic | a topic of information, research, questions | an issue with several sides |
| typical second half | {話|はな}す, {調|しら}べる, {書|か}く | {情報|じょうほう}, {質問|しつもん}, {調査|ちょうさ}, {規則|きそく} | {議論|ぎろん}, {対立|たいりつ}, {争|あらそ}い, {裁判|さいばん} |
| example | ダムについて{話|はな}す | ダムに{関|かん}する{資料|しりょう} | ダムの{建設|けんせつ}をめぐる{対立|たいりつ} |

Many sentences take more than one: {計画|けいかく}について / に{関|かん}して / をめぐって{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれた.
With をめぐって the reader expects a dispute.

## 〜に{応|こた}えて: in response to

〜に{応|こた}えて (before a noun 〜に{応|こた}える, also 〜に{応|こた}えた) says that someone acted to meet a
request, a hope, a need or an expectation.

{住民|じゅうみん}の{要望|ようぼう}に{応|こた}えて、{市|し}はバスの{本数|ほんすう}を{増|ふ}やした。 — In response to residents' requests, the city ran more buses.
ファンの{声|こえ}に{応|こた}えて、{追加|ついか}{公演|こうえん}が{決|き}まった。 — Responding to fans' calls, an extra performance was arranged.
{期待|きたい}に{応|こた}えられるよう、{頑張|がんば}ります。 — I'll do my best to live up to your expectations.
{時代|じだい}のニーズに{応|こた}える{技術|ぎじゅつ} — technology that meets the needs of the age

こたえる is N5's word with a second kanji: {答|こた}える answers a question or a letter;
{応|こた}える responds to hopes, requests and expectations.

{質問|しつもん}に{答|こた}える — answer a question
{期待|きたい}に{応|こた}える — live up to expectations

Don't mix it up with lesson 13's に{応|おう}じて (same kanji, read おう). に{応|おう}じて says that
something varies to match ({年齢|ねんれい}に{応|おう}じて{料金|りょうきん}が{変|か}わる); に{応|こた}えて says that
someone acted because they were asked or expected to.

## Reminder: を{中心|ちゅうしん}に, における

> **Review (N3 12).** 〜を{中心|ちゅうしん}に(して): centred on, mainly ({北海道|ほっかいどう}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に
> {雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}った). 〜において / 〜における + noun: in, at (formal; places, fields, periods):
> {日本|にほん}におけるエネルギー{問題|もんだい} (the energy problem in Japan), {会議|かいぎ}において{決|き}める.

## Which one?

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| をめぐって / をめぐる | over (a dispute) | {国境|こっきょう}をめぐる{対立|たいりつ} |
| に{関|かん}して / に{関|かん}する | about, concerning (formal) | {汚染|おせん}に{関|かん}する{調査|ちょうさ} |
| について / についての | about (everyday) | ごみについての{説明|せつめい} |
| に{応|こた}えて / に{応|こた}える | in response to (requests, hopes) | {要望|ようぼう}に{応|こた}えて{増|ふ}やす |
| に{応|おう}じて (13) | according to (varies with) | {量|りょう}に{応|おう}じて{払|はら}う |
| を{中心|ちゅうしん}に | centred on | {都市|とし}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に |
| における | in (formal) | {世界|せかい}における{日本|にほん}の{役割|やくわり} |

## Environment words

| Topic | Words |

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

In a mountain town of about eight thousand people, residents are split in two over a plan to
generate power with rows of solar panels. Under the plan, about 50 hectares of forest to the
north of the town would be cleared and about 100,000 panels installed. For the town, it would be the biggest development ever.

Supporters argue that making electricity without relying on fossil fuels is necessary to prevent
global warming. The fee the company would pay the town for the land is also hoped to make up for
the town's scarce funds. While construction lasts, there will also be more work for local people.

Opponents, on the other hand, are worried about the effects of cutting down the forest. Without
the trees, earth and sand might wash down in heavy rain. Some also fear that the river that is
the town's water source will be polluted. One resident says, "It's strange to get rid of a forest
for the sake of power generation that's supposed to protect the environment."

In response to these concerns, last month the town began a survey by experts. The results on the
risk of landslides and the effects on water quality are due to be published next spring. The
mayor has said, "I want to decide on the basis of the survey results."

Few people oppose increasing renewable energy. The question is where and how to build it.
Similar debates in many places confront us with the question of how to build a sustainable
society.

</details>
