## Common mistakes

- をめぐって for a neutral topic: "a lecture about the history of energy" is
  エネルギーの{歴史|れきし}についての{講義|こうぎ}. をめぐって needs a dispute.
- {答|こた}える for expectations: {期待|きたい}に{応|こた}える, {要望|ようぼう}に{応|こた}える. {答|こた}える is for
  questions and letters.
- Reading に{応|こた}えて as におうじて: same kanji, different word. If someone acts because they were
  asked, it's こたえて.
- Mixing up the pairs: ×{氷|こおり}を{溶|と}ける. The one with を is {溶|と}かす; {溶|と}ける has が:
  {氷|こおり}が{溶|と}ける.
- {汚|きたな}い for pollution in formal writing: {川|かわ}が{汚|きたな}い is fine in speech; reports say
  {水質|すいしつ}が{悪|わる}い or {汚染|おせん}されている.

## Key points

- 〜をめぐって / 〜をめぐる (kana): over a disputed issue; followed by words of debate and conflict.
- 〜に{関|かん}して / に{関|かん}する: about, concerning (formal, neutral); 〜について: about (everyday).
- 〜に{応|こた}えて / に{応|こた}える: in response to requests, hopes, expectations; compare
  {答|こた}える (answer) and 13's に{応|おう}じて (varies with).
- Review: を{中心|ちゅうしん}に (centred on), における (in, formal).
- New kanji: 環 境 源 燃 油 汚 染 埋 掘 極 氷 凍 溶. Write {環境|かんきょう}, {資源|しげん}, {汚染|おせん},
  {燃|も}える, {石油|せきゆ}, {凍|こお}る, {冷凍|れいとう} with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Reasons in notices: につき, により, ため, とあって
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The last lesson of the module puts its reasons where you meet them every day: on notices. A sign
on a closed door, an announcement at the station, a letter from the ward office all give a
reason, but in a **[[formal register]]** with its own grammar. This lesson teaches the **causal
expressions** of notices (〜につき, 〜により, 〜ため) and **notice style** itself: the short,
fixed phrases that make a notice sound like one.

{改装|かいそう}につき、{一週間|いっしゅうかん}{休業|きゅうぎょう}いたします。 — We are closed for a week for refurbishment.
{強風|きょうふう}により、{運転|うんてん}を{見合|みあ}わせております。 — Services are suspended because of strong winds.
{工事|こうじ}のため、この{通路|つうろ}は{通|とお}れません。 — This passage is closed because of building work.
{連休|れんきゅう}とあって、{館内|かんない}は{家族連|かぞくづ}れでにぎわった。 — It being a long weekend, the building was busy with families.

The theme is public facilities and buildings: closures and repairs, cleaning, smoking areas,
storage, and the districts of a city. The home, furniture and DIY were N3's (lesson 27); moving
offices is lesson 10's. Carried words that now take kanji: {修理|しゅうり}, {整理|せいり}, {掃除|そうじ},
{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}, {床|ゆか}, {畳|たたみ}, {地域|ちいき}.

## 〜につき: owing to; per

〜につき follows a noun and has two common jobs.

1. *Owing to* (notices and announcements only). It gives the reason for a closure, a change or
   a ban, and is the most formal-looking of the notice reasons.

   {改装|かいそう}につき、{一週間|いっしゅうかん}{休業|きゅうぎょう}いたします。 — We are closed for a week for refurbishment.
   {清掃中|せいそうちゅう}につき、{立|た}ち{入|い}りはごえんりょください。 — Cleaning in progress: please do not enter.
   {満席|まんせき}につき、{受付|うけつけ}を{終了|しゅうりょう}しました。 — All seats are taken, so bookings have closed.

   It's rare in conversation: a friend would say {改装中|かいそうちゅう}だから{休|やす}みだって.

2. *Per, for each.* This one is used in speech too.

   {貸|か}し{出|だ}しは{一人|ひとり}につき{十冊|じゅっさつ}までです。 — You can borrow up to ten books per person.
   {会議室|かいぎしつ}の{使用料|しようりょう}は{一時間|いちじかん}につき{五百円|ごひゃくえん}です。 — The meeting room costs 500 yen an hour.

In business letters you may also meet 〜につき meaning "concerning" (この{件|けん}につき), a stiff
form of について. Recognize it; you don't need to use it.

Don't confuse it with lesson 10's 〜につけ (whenever): {何|なに}かにつけて{親|おや}に{電話|でんわ}する (phone one's
parents at every excuse).

## 〜により, 〜による: due to (formal)

> **Review (N3 13).** によって / により / による has several jobs: depending on
> ({人|ひと}によって{違|ちが}う), by (the doer of a passive: {市|し}により{管理|かんり}されている), by means of,
> and *cause*.

As a cause, 〜により (and before a noun 〜による) is the standard formal word for "due to": news,
announcements, official letters. In notices, により is more usual than によって.

{大雨|おおあめ}により、{国道|こくどう}は{通行止|つうこうど}めになっています。 — The national highway is closed due to heavy rain.
{台風|たいふう}による{被害|ひがい}は、{二十|にじゅう}の{市町村|しちょうそん}に{広|ひろ}がった。 — Damage from the typhoon spread to twenty towns and villages.
{機械|きかい}の{故障|こしょう}により、{本日|ほんじつ}は{休館|きゅうかん}いたします。 — Due to a mechanical fault, the building is closed today.

## 〜ため(に): because of (formal)

〜ため(に) is a cause in formal speech and writing: after a noun with の, after the plain form of
verbs and adjectives (な-adjectives with な). As a formal noun it's written in kana.

{工事|こうじ}のため、この{通路|つうろ}は{通|とお}れません。 — This passage is closed because of building work.
{利用者|りようしゃ}が{少|すく}ないため、{日曜日|にちようび}の{開館|かいかん}を{休止|きゅうし}します。 — Because of low use, we are suspending Sunday opening.
{安全|あんぜん}のため、{屋上|おくじょう}は{立|た}ち{入|い}り{禁止|きんし}です。 — For safety's sake, the roof is out of bounds.

ため can also be a purpose ("in order to": {合格|ごうかく}するために{勉強|べんきょう}する). After a noun,
context decides: {安全|あんぜん}のため is "for safety"; {工事|こうじ}のため is "because of the work". In
notices it's nearly always the reason.

## 〜ことから: from the fact that

> **Review (N3 6).** 〜ことから gives the basis for a name or a judgement: {川|かわ}が{多|おお}いことから、
> この{町|まち}は「{水|みず}の{町|まち}」と{呼|よ}ばれている (because there are many rivers, the town is called
> "the town of water"). {窓|まど}が{割|わ}れていたことから、{泥棒|どろぼう}が{入|はい}ったと{分|わ}かった. It's a
> reasoned "because", common in explanations and news.

## 〜とあって: being (a special occasion) (to recognize)

〜とあって follows a noun or a plain form and gives a special circumstance that explains a striking
situation: "it being…, (naturally)…". It's news and written style.

{連休|れんきゅう}とあって、{館内|かんない}は{家族連|かぞくづ}れでにぎわった。 — It being a long weekend, the building was busy with families.
{入場|にゅうじょう}{無料|むりょう}とあって、{朝|あさ}から{長|なが}い{列|れつ}ができた。 — With entry free, a long queue formed from the morning.
{人気|にんき}{作家|さっか}が{来|く}るとあって、{会場|かいじょう}は{満員|まんいん}だった。 — With a popular author coming, the hall was full.

The second half describes what happened or what people did, not the speaker's wish or a request.

## 〜ゆえ(に): because (literary; to recognize)

〜ゆえ(に) is an old written "because", still met in essays, titles and set phrases. Before a noun:
〜ゆえの.

{若|わか}さゆえの{失敗|しっぱい} — a mistake that came from youth
{貧|まず}しさゆえに、{学校|がっこう}に{行|い}けない{子供|こども}もいる。 — Because of poverty, some children can't go to school.

## Which reason?

| Pattern | Register | Where you meet it | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| から / ので | everyday | speech, most writing | {工事|こうじ}だから{閉|し}まっている |
| のため | formal | notices, announcements, writing | {工事|こうじ}のため{休館|きゅうかん} |
| により / による | formal | news, announcements, official letters | {大雪|おおゆき}により{運休|うんきゅう} |
| につき | very formal | written notices only (cause); also "per" | {改装|かいそう}につき{休業|きゅうぎょう} |
| ことから | neutral, explanations | names, conclusions | {形|かたち}が{似|に}ていることから |
| とあって | news, written | special circumstances | {連休|れんきゅう}とあって{混雑|こんざつ} |
| ゆえ(に) | literary | essays, titles | {若|わか}さゆえ |

## Notice style

Notices have a grammar of their own. They're short, polite to the reader, and full of fixed
phrases. Here are the building blocks; the "Notice language" reference sheet puts them together.

| Phrase | What it does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜こと | a rule (plain, firm) | {館内|かんない}では{静|しず}かにすること |
| ごえんりょください | please don't (polite; its kanji is outside N2) | {館内|かんない}での{喫煙|きつえん}はごえんりょください |
| お / ご〜ください | please do | {足元|あしもと}にご{注意|ちゅうい}ください |
| ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください | please note (and accept) | {予告|よこく}なく{変更|へんこう}する{場合|ばあい}があります。ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください |
| 〜{願|ねが}います / お〜{願|ねが}います | we ask you to | お{静|しず}かに{願|ねが}います |
| ご{協力|きょうりょく}をお{願|ねが}いいたします | thank you for your cooperation | {分別|ぶんべつ}にご{協力|きょうりょく}をお{願|ねが}いいたします |
| 〜{禁止|きんし} | banned | {撮影|さつえい}{禁止|きんし}, {立|た}ち{入|い}り{禁止|きんし} |
| 〜{可|か} / 〜{不可|ふか} | allowed / not allowed | {持|も}ち{込|こ}み{可|か}, {再入場|さいにゅうじょう}{不可|ふか} |
| 〜{中|ちゅう} | in progress | {清掃中|せいそうちゅう}, {工事中|こうじちゅう}, {準備中|じゅんびちゅう} |
| 〜{限|かぎ}り | only (lesson 20) | {本日|ほんじつ}{限|かぎ}り |
| 〜にて | = で (formal) | {受付|うけつけ}にてお{申|もう}し{込|こ}みください |
| ただし / なお | however / note also (lesson 28) | ただし、{土日|どにち}は{休|やす}みです |
| noun endings | no verb at all | {本日|ほんじつ}{休館|きゅうかん}, {終日|しゅうじつ}{禁煙|きんえん} |

Three things to notice:

- Notices use the organization's humble forms for what it does (いたします, しております) and
  honorific requests for what the reader does (ご{利用|りよう}ください).
- They prefer kango (Chinese-reading words): {休館|きゅうかん}, {使用|しよう}, {清掃|せいそう}, {喫煙|きつえん}
  rather than {休|やす}み, {使|つか}う, {掃除|そうじ}, タバコを{吸|す}う.
- The firmest rules drop politeness altogether: 〜こと, 〜{禁止|きんし}, 〜{厳禁|げんきん}.

## Facility words

| Topic | Words |
|---|---|
| buildings | {公民館|こうみんかん}, {区役所|くやくしょ}, {館内|かんない}, {場内|じょうない}, {屋上|おくじょう}, {床面積|ゆかめんせき}, {共用|きょうよう} |
| opening and closing | {休館日|きゅうかんび}, {休止|きゅうし}, {再開|さいかい}, {終日|しゅうじつ}, {当面|とうめん}, {見合|みあ}わせる, {通行止|つうこうど}め |
| repairs | {改修|かいしゅう}, {改装|かいそう}, {改築|かいちく}, {建|た}て{替|か}え, {補修|ほしゅう}, {修正|しゅうせい}, {点検|てんけん}, {整備|せいび}, {調整|ちょうせい}, {設置|せっち} |
| cleaning and order | {清掃|せいそう}, {清掃員|せいそういん}, {掃|は}く, {整|ととの}う, {整|ととの}える, {整列|せいれつ}, {清|きよ}い, {清|きよ}らか, {清書|せいしょ} |
| smoking | {喫煙|きつえん}, {喫煙所|きつえんじょ}, {分煙|ぶんえん}, {受動|じゅどう}{喫煙|きつえん}, {喫茶店|きっさてん} |
| storage | {車庫|しゃこ}, {金庫|きんこ}, {書庫|しょこ}, ロッカー |
| parts of buildings | {柱|はしら}, {電柱|でんちゅう}, {板|いた}, {板張|いたば}り, {看板|かんばん}, {床下|ゆかした}, {手|て}すり, {段差|だんさ}, {空調|くうちょう}, {灯|あか}り, {消灯|しょうとう}, {灯油|とうゆ} |
| access | バリアフリー, {多目的|たもくてき}トイレ, エスカレーター, {自動|じどう}ドア, {防犯|ぼうはん}カメラ |
| using | {貸|か}し{出|だ}し, {使用料|しようりょう}, {持|も}ち{込|こ}み, {了承|りょうしょう} |
| areas | {区|く}, {地区|ちく}, {区域|くいき}, {区画|くかく}, {区間|くかん}, {区切|くぎ}る, {区別|くべつ}, {流域|りゅういき}, {全域|ぜんいき} |
| training | {研修|けんしゅう}, {修了|しゅうりょう}, {修行|しゅぎょう}, {床屋|とこや} |

Notes:

- {改修|かいしゅう} repairs and improves a building or road; {改装|かいそう} redoes the interior (shops);
  {改築|かいちく} rebuilds part of it; {建|た}て{替|か}え pulls it down and builds again. {修理|しゅうり} (N4)
  is fixing a thing that's broken.
- {清掃|せいそう} is the formal word for {掃除|そうじ}; notices say {清掃中|せいそうちゅう}, people say
  {掃除|そうじ}してる.
- {修了|しゅうりょう} (completing a course) and {終了|しゅうりょう} (ending, N3) sound the same:
  {研修|けんしゅう}を{修了|しゅうりょう}する, but {受付|うけつけ}を{終了|しゅうりょう}する.
- {区|く} is a ward of a large city (Tokyo has 23); {地区|ちく} is any district; {区域|くいき} is a zone
  marked for a purpose ({禁煙|きんえん}{区域|くいき}).
- The word for "facility", しせつ, has a first kanji outside N2, so it stays in kana: {公共|こうきょう}しせつ.
  So does そうこ (warehouse).

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji: repair and order, cleaning and smoking, the parts of a building, and areas.

### Repair, order and cleaning

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 修 | repair; study | シュウ, シュ | — | 10 | {修理|しゅうり}, {修正|しゅうせい}, {改修|かいしゅう}, {補修|ほしゅう}, {研修|けんしゅう}, {修了|しゅうりょう}, {修行|しゅぎょう} |
| 整 | put in order | セイ | ととの(える), ととの(う) | 16 | {整理|せいり}, {整備|せいび}, {調整|ちょうせい}, {整列|せいれつ}, {整|ととの}える, {整|ととの}う |
| 掃 | sweep | ソウ | は(く) | 11 | {掃除|そうじ}, {掃除機|そうじき}, {清掃|せいそう}, {掃|は}く |
| 清 | pure, clean | セイ | きよ(い), きよ(らか) | 11 | {清掃|せいそう}, {清書|せいしょ}, {清|きよ}い, {清|きよ}らか |

- {修理|しゅうり}, {整理|せいり}, {掃除|そうじ} and {掃除機|そうじき} (N4 and N3) are now written with kanji.
- 修 is シュ in {修行|しゅぎょう} (training as a monk or craftsman), シュウ elsewhere.
- 清 has the water radical (氵) and 青 (blue): clear water. Compare 晴 (sun: fine weather), 静
  (quiet) and 精 (spirit, lesson 18): they share the right side and the sound セイ.

### Smoking and storage

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 喫 | consume (smoke, drink) | キツ | — | 12 | {喫煙|きつえん}, {喫煙所|きつえんじょ}, {受動|じゅどう}{喫煙|きつえん}, {喫茶店|きっさてん} |
| 庫 | storehouse | コ | — | 10 | {車庫|しゃこ}, {金庫|きんこ}, {書庫|しょこ}, {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}, {在庫|ざいこ} |

- {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ} (N5; its middle kanji is lesson 29's) and {在庫|ざいこ} (N3) are now written with kanji.
- 喫 is キッ before さ: {喫茶店|きっさてん}. It appears in few words, all about smoking or drinking.
- 庫 is a vehicle (車) under a roof (广): a garage, then any storehouse.

### Parts of a building

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 柱 | pillar | チュウ | はしら | 9 | {柱|はしら}, {電柱|でんちゅう} |
| 板 | board | ハン, バン | いた | 8 | {板|いた}, {看板|かんばん}, {黒板|こくばん}, {板張|いたば}り |
| 床 | floor; bed | ショウ | ゆか, とこ | 7 | {床|ゆか}, {床下|ゆかした}, {床面積|ゆかめんせき}, {床屋|とこや} |
| 畳 | tatami; fold | ジョウ | たたみ, たた(む) | 12 | {畳|たたみ}, {畳|たた}む, 〜{畳|じょう} ({六畳|ろくじょう}) |
| 灯 | lamp, light | トウ | ひ | 6 | {灯|あか}り, {灯油|とうゆ}, {消灯|しょうとう} |

- {黒板|こくばん}, {床|ゆか}, {畳|たたみ} and {畳|たた}む (N5 and N4) are now written with kanji. Rooms are
  measured in tatami: {六畳|ろくじょう}の{部屋|へや} is a room of six mats (about 10 square metres).
- まないた (chopping board) is usually printed まな{板|いた}: its first part has an off-list kanji.
- 床 is ゆか (floor) on its own, とこ in {床屋|とこや} (barber) and in old words for a bed.
- The official kun'yomi of 灯 is ひ (a light, a lamp). {灯|あか}り is a common spelling that
  suggests a lamp's light, but あかり isn't an official reading of 灯: official and school
  writing uses {明|あ}かり.

### Areas

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 区 | ward, section | ク | — | 4 | {区|く}, {区役所|くやくしょ}, {地区|ちく}, {区別|くべつ}, {区間|くかん}, {区切|くぎ}る |
| 域 | area, region | イキ | — | 11 | {地域|ちいき}, {区域|くいき}, {流域|りゅういき}, {全域|ぜんいき}, {領域|りょういき} |

- {地域|ちいき} (N3) is now written with kanji. {領域|りょういき} (territory, field) is lesson 21's word.
- 区 is the shortest kanji in this lesson (4 strokes): a box open on the right with an ✕ inside.

Memory notes:

- 修: a person (亻) beside a staff and long brushing strokes (彡): tidying, repairing, polishing a
  skill.
- 整: a bundle being tied (束) and a hand striking (攵) over 正 (correct): beating things into the
  right shape.
- 掃: a hand (扌) holding a broom (the right side): to sweep.
- 喫: a mouth (口) beside a carved shape over 大: taking things in by mouth.
- 柱: a tree (木) beside 主 (master, main): the main timber holding the house up.
- 板: a tree (木) beside 反 (turn over): wood sawn flat.
- 床: a tree (木) under a roof (广): wooden flooring under the roof.
- 畳: a field (田) over layers, piled up and folded: mats laid side by side.
- 灯: fire (火) beside a stroke shaped like a nail: a flame on a stand.
- 域: earth (土) beside a shape with a mouth (口) guarded by a halberd: an area of land with a
  border.

```trace
修整掃清喫庫柱板床畳灯区域
```

## Dialogue: booking a room during the works

Reiko wants to book a room at the community centre for her calligraphy group. Kinoshita works at
the reception desk. (Polite speech; Kinoshita uses business keigo.)

```dialogue
# At the community centre reception
れいこ: すみません、{来月|らいげつ}{和室|わしつ}を{予約|よやく}したいんですが。
= Excuse me, I'd like to book the Japanese-style room for next month.
きのした: もうしわけございません。{来月|らいげつ}は{改修|かいしゅう}{工事|こうじ}のため、{二階|にかい}のお{部屋|へや}はご{利用|りよう}いただけないんです。
= I'm very sorry. Because of renovation work next month, the rooms upstairs can't be used.
れいこ: えっ、{全部|ぜんぶ}ですか。
= What, all of them?
きのした: はい。{畳|たたみ}の{入|い}れ{替|か}えと、{空調|くうちょう}の{点検|てんけん}がございまして。{一階|いっかい}の{会議室|かいぎしつ}でしたら、{空|あ}いておりますが。
= Yes. The tatami are being replaced and the air conditioning inspected. If the meeting room downstairs would do, it's free.
れいこ: {書道|しょどう}の{会|かい}なので、{床|ゆか}に{紙|かみ}を{広|ひろ}げたいんですよ。{会議室|かいぎしつ}は{机|つくえ}ですよね。
= It's for a calligraphy group, so we'd like to spread paper on the floor. The meeting room has desks, doesn't it?
きのした: はい。ただ、{机|つくえ}は{動|うご}かせますので、{板張|いたば}りの{床|ゆか}をお{使|つか}いいただくこともできます。
= Yes. But the desks can be moved, so you could use the wooden floor.
れいこ: それならいいかな。{料金|りょうきん}はどのくらいですか。
= That might be fine. How much does it cost?
きのした: {一時間|いちじかん}につき{四百円|よんひゃくえん}です。{区内|くない}の{団体|だんたい}は{半額|はんがく}になります。
= It's 400 yen per hour. Groups based in the ward pay half.
れいこ: うちは{区内|くない}のグループです。じゃあ、{第二|だいに}{土曜日|どようび}の{午後|ごご}をお{願|ねが}いします。
= We're a group in the ward. Then the afternoon of the second Saturday, please.
きのした: かしこまりました。それから、{工事|こうじ}の{期間|きかん}{中|ちゅう}は{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}の{一部|いちぶ}が{使|つか}えませんので、なるべく{電車|でんしゃ}かバスでお{越|こ}しください。
= Certainly. Also, part of the car park is out of use during the works, so please come by train or bus if you can.
れいこ: {分|わ}かりました。あ、{喫煙所|きつえんじょ}はまだ{裏|うら}にありますか。メンバーに{聞|き}かれるので。
= All right. Oh, is the smoking area still at the back? The members will ask.
きのした: もうしわけありません、{工事|こうじ}のため、{当面|とうめん}の{間|あいだ}ご{利用|りよう}いただけません。
= I'm sorry, it's out of use for the time being because of the works.
れいこ: そうですか。{伝|つた}えておきます。ありがとうございました。
= I see. I'll let them know. Thank you.
```

{和室|わしつ} = Japanese-style room; {書道|しょどう} = calligraphy; {区内|くない} = within the ward;
{団体|だんたい} = group (lesson 26's word); お{越|こ}しください = please come (honorific). Kinoshita gives
the reason for the closure with 〜ため, the hourly fee with につき ("per"), and keeps the notice-style
いたします, ございます and ご{利用|りよう}いただけない. The "owing to" につき stays on paper.

## Reading: the library is closing for repairs

A notice from a ward library (です/ます style, as notices are).

> 【{中央|ちゅうおう}{図書館|としょかん}{休館|きゅうかん}のお{知|し}らせ】
>
> {平素|へいそ}より{当館|とうかん}をご{利用|りよう}いただき、ありがとうございます。{当館|とうかん}は{建物|たてもの}の{改修|かいしゅう}{工事|こうじ}につき、{一月|いちがつ}{五日|いつか}から{三月|さんがつ}{三十一日|さんじゅういちにち}まで{休館|きゅうかん}いたします。{工事|こうじ}では、{古|ふる}くなった{空調|くうちょう}{設備|せつび}の{交換|こうかん}、{床|ゆか}の{張|は}り{替|か}え、エレベーターの{整備|せいび}などを{行|おこな}います。{工事|こうじ}{中|ちゅう}は{大|おお}きな{音|おと}が{出|で}ることがございます。{周辺|しゅうへん}の{皆様|みなさま}にはごめいわくをおかけしますが、ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください。
>
> {休館|きゅうかん}{中|ちゅう}は、{駅前|えきまえ}の{分館|ぶんかん}が{通常|つうじょう}どおり{開館|かいかん}しております。また、インターネットでの{本|ほん}の{予約|よやく}は{休館|きゅうかん}{中|ちゅう}も{受|う}け{付|つ}けており、{予約|よやく}した{本|ほん}は{分館|ぶんかん}でお{受|う}け{取|と}りいただけます。ただし、{分館|ぶんかん}は{面積|めんせき}が{小|ちい}さいため、{雑誌|ざっし}の{古|ふる}い{号|ごう}や{大型|おおがた}の{本|ほん}は{置|お}いておりません。ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください。
>
> {休館|きゅうかん}{期間|きかん}{中|ちゅう}の{貸|か}し{出|だ}しは、{一人|ひとり}につき{二十冊|にじゅっさつ}まで、{期間|きかん}は{四週間|よんしゅうかん}とします。お{借|か}りになった{本|ほん}は、{分館|ぶんかん}の{窓口|まどぐち}、または{各|かく}{地区|ちく}の{公民館|こうみんかん}に{置|お}かれたブックポストにお{返|かえ}しください。
>
> なお、{工事|こうじ}の{期間|きかん}{中|ちゅう}は{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}もご{利用|りよう}いただけません。また、{改修|かいしゅう}{後|ご}は{建物|たてもの}の{周|まわ}りも{禁煙|きんえん}となり、{喫煙所|きつえんじょ}はなくなります。{皆様|みなさま}のご{理解|りかい}をお{願|ねが}いいたします。
>
> {工事|こうじ}の{状況|じょうきょう}により、{再開|さいかい}の{日|ひ}が{変|か}わる{場合|ばあい}がございます。{最新|さいしん}の{情報|じょうほう}は{区|く}のホームページでお{知|し}らせいたします。ご{不便|ふべん}をおかけいたしますが、ご{協力|きょうりょく}をお{願|ねが}いいたします。
>
> {緑区|みどりく}{立|りつ}{中央|ちゅうおう}{図書館|としょかん}

{平素|へいそ}より = (we thank you) always (a fixed opening of formal letters; its second kanji is lesson 13's);
{周辺|しゅうへん} = the surrounding area (lesson 27's word);
{張|は}り{替|か}え = replacing (flooring); {分館|ぶんかん} = branch (library); {通常|つうじょう}どおり =
as usual; {号|ごう} = issue (of a magazine); {大型|おおがた} = large-format; ブックポスト = book return box;
〜{立|りつ} = run by (a ward or city); {緑区|みどりく} is a made-up ward.

1. Why is the library closing, and for how long?
2. What will readers not find at the branch library?
3. What are the borrowing rules during the closure?
4. What will change for smokers after the work?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. For renovation of the building (new air-conditioning equipment, new floors, lift maintenance), from 5 January to 31 March; the reopening date may change with the progress of the work.
2. Old issues of magazines and large-format books, because the branch is small.
3. Up to twenty books per person ({一人|ひとり}につき), for four weeks; return them at the branch counter or the book boxes at community centres.
4. The area around the building becomes non-smoking and the smoking area will go.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

[Notice: Central Library closure]

Thank you, as always, for using the library. The library will be closed from 5 January to 31
March for renovation of the building. The work includes replacing the old air-conditioning
equipment, renewing the floors and servicing the lifts. There may be loud noise during the work; we
apologize to our neighbours for the disturbance and ask for their understanding.

During the closure, the branch library in front of the station is open as usual. Online reservations of books are also accepted
during the closure, and reserved books can be collected at the branch. However, as the
branch is small, it doesn't stock back issues of magazines or large-format books. We ask for your
understanding.

During the closure you may borrow up to twenty books per person, for four weeks. Please return
borrowed books at the branch counter or to the book return boxes at the community centres in each
district.

Please note that the car park will also be out of use during the work. In addition, after the
renovation the area around the building will also be non-smoking, and the smoking area will be
removed. We ask for everyone's understanding.

The reopening date may change depending on the progress of the work. The latest information will
be posted on the ward's website. We apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your
cooperation.

Midori Ward Central Library

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{改装|かいそう}につき、{休業|きゅうぎょう}いたします。
= Closed for refurbishment.
お{一人|ひとり}につき{二枚|にまい}までです。
= Two per person.
{強風|きょうふう}により、{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まっています。
= Trains have stopped because of strong winds.
{館内|かんない}での{喫煙|きつえん}はごえんりょください。
= Please refrain from smoking in the building.
ご{不便|ふべん}をおかけいたしますが、ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください。
= We apologize for the inconvenience and ask for your understanding.
```

## Common mistakes

- につき in conversation for a cause: to a friend, {工事中|こうじちゅう}だから{閉|し}まってるよ, not
  {工事中|こうじちゅう}につき. (The "per" につき is fine in speech.)
- Writing ごえんりょください with kanji: its second kanji is outside N2, so this course writes it
  in kana. In print you'll see it with kanji.
- Reading 〜{可|か} and 〜{不可|ふか} the wrong way round: {持|も}ち{込|こ}み{可|か} means you may bring food in.
- とあって for your own wishes: ×{連休|れんきゅう}とあって、{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}きたい. Use だから:
  {連休|れんきゅう}だから{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}きたい. とあって reports what happened.
- {清掃|せいそう} in daily talk: say {掃除|そうじ}する at home. {清掃|せいそう} belongs on signs and in reports.
- Confusing {修了|しゅうりょう} and {終了|しゅうりょう}: you {修了|しゅうりょう}する a course; a meeting, a
  service or an event {終了|しゅうりょう}する.

## Key points

- 〜につき (after a noun): owing to (written notices only); per ({一人|ひとり}につき).
- 〜により / による: due to (formal; news and announcements).
- 〜ため(に): because of (formal); in notices nearly always the reason.
- Review: 〜ことから (the basis for a name or a conclusion). Recognize: 〜とあって (it being…),
  〜ゆえ(に) (literary because).
- Notice style: 〜こと, ごえんりょください, ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください, お〜{願|ねが}います, 〜{禁止|きんし},
  〜{可|か} / 〜{不可|ふか}, 〜{中|ちゅう}, noun endings; kango and humble forms.
- New kanji: 修 整 掃 清 喫 庫 柱 板 床 畳 灯 区 域. Write {修理|しゅうり}, {整理|せいり}, {掃除|そうじ},
  {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}, {黒板|こくばん}, {床|ゆか}, {畳|たたみ}, {地域|ちいき} with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: The lay-judge system
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Since 21 May 2009, ordinary citizens in Japan have helped decide serious criminal trials. They are
called {裁判員|さいばんいん} (lay judges), and the scheme is the {裁判員|さいばんいん}{制度|せいど}. Any adult
with the vote may one day get a letter saying they could be chosen, so it's a topic that turns up
in the news, in conversation and in N2-level reading. This lesson explains how the system works,
what a day in court looks like, and what people think of it, using lesson 11's からには and {以上|いじょう}.

The facts here were checked in November 2026 on the courts' and the Ministry of Justice's
websites. Rules can change, so check the official pages if you need the details.

## What lay judges do

- *Who sits.* In most cases, six lay judges sit with three professional judges
  ({裁判官|さいばんかん}).
- *Which cases.* Serious criminal cases only, such as murder, robbery causing injury or death,
  and setting fire to a house where people live. Civil cases (one person suing another) don't use
  lay judges.
- *Where.* In district courts ({地方裁判所|ちほうさいばんしょ}, the {地裁|ちさい} of the news), the first
  level of trial.
- *What they decide.* Together with the judges, whether the defendant ({被告人|ひこくにん}) is guilty,
  and if so, what the sentence should be.

{裁判員|さいばんいん}は、{裁判官|さいばんかん}と{一緒|いっしょ}に、{被告人|ひこくにん}が{有罪|ゆうざい}かどうかを{決|き}める。{有罪|ゆうざい}の{場合|ばあい}は、どのくらいの{刑|けい}にするかも{決|き}める。
(Lay judges decide with the judges whether the defendant is guilty. If guilty, they also decide
how heavy the sentence should be.) The word for a criminal sentence, けい, has a kanji outside N2;
it's shown here with furigana for recognition only.

## How people are chosen

1. *The candidate list.* Each year, names are drawn by lot ({くじ引|び}き) from the electoral roll
   (せんきょにんめいぼ; its last kanji is outside N2) to make a list of candidates for the next
   year. People on it are told by letter, usually late in the year.
2. *Who can be chosen.* People with the right to vote in national elections ({有権者|ゆうけんしゃ}).
   The age is 18 or over: 18- and 19-year-olds have been chosen since 2023, after a change in the
   law. Some people can't serve, for example members of the Diet and people who work in the
   courts or as lawyers.
3. *A case comes up.* Candidates are drawn again by lot for a particular trial and called to
   the court.
4. *Selection day.* At the court, through a short procedure ({選任|せんにん}{手続|てつづ}き), six lay
   judges (and usually some substitutes) are appointed from those who came.

### Can you say no?

In principle, no. But some reasons for declining ({辞退|じたい}) are accepted, for example:

- being 70 or over;
- being a full-time student;
- serious illness or injury that keeps you from coming to court;
- having to care for a family member.

Work on its own isn't always accepted as a reason, though the court considers each case. Employers
must let staff take the time off, and lay judges are paid a daily allowance and their travel
costs.

## A day in court

| Step | Japanese | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Hearings | {公判|こうはん} | In open court: the prosecution ({検察官|けんさつかん}) and the defence ({弁護人|べんごにん}) present evidence, witnesses speak, the defendant is questioned. Lay judges may ask questions too. |
| Deliberation | {評議|ひょうぎ} | Behind closed doors, judges and lay judges discuss the facts and the sentence. |
| Decision | {評決|ひょうけつ} | A majority decides, but the majority must include at least one professional judge and at least one lay judge. |
| Judgment | {判決|はんけつ} | The presiding judge ({裁判長|さいばんちょう}) reads out the verdict in court. |

According to the courts, in many cases lay judges come to court on about seven days in all;
complicated trials can take much longer.

### The duty of confidentiality

Lay judges have a {守秘義務|しゅひぎむ}: they mustn't reveal what was said in deliberation, who
held which opinion, or how the vote went, and this continues after the trial is over. What
happened in open court, and their own impressions of taking part, are another matter: they may
talk about those.

{評議|ひょうぎ}の{内容|ないよう}は{話|はな}してはいけないが、{公開|こうかい}の{裁判|さいばん}で{見|み}たことは{話|はな}してもよい。
(You mustn't talk about the deliberations, but you may talk about what you saw at the public
hearings.)

## For and against

People still argue about the system. Here are the main points, in the kind of language you'll meet
in opinion columns.

*For*

- {国民|こくみん}の{常識|じょうしき}が{裁判|さいばん}に{生|い}かされる。 — Ordinary people's common sense is put to use in trials.
- {裁判|さいばん}が{分|わ}かりやすくなった。{一般|いっぱん}の{人|ひと}が{参加|さんか}する{以上|いじょう}、{専門|せんもん}{用語|ようご}ばかりでは{進|すす}められないからだ。 — Trials have become easier to follow: since ordinary people take part, they can't be run in jargon alone.
- {裁判|さいばん}への{関心|かんしん}が{高|たか}まる。 — Interest in the courts grows.

*Against*

- {負担|ふたん}が{大|おお}きい。{仕事|しごと}や{家庭|かてい}がある{人|ひと}にとって、{何日|なんにち}も{休|やす}むのは{簡単|かんたん}ではない。 — The burden is heavy: for people with jobs or families, taking days off isn't easy.
- {心|こころ}の{負担|ふたん}もある。{事件|じけん}の{写真|しゃしん}を{見|み}て、{眠|ねむ}れなくなった{人|ひと}もいる。 — There's a mental burden too: some people couldn't sleep after seeing photographs of the crime.
- {守秘義務|しゅひぎむ}が{厳|きび}しいため、{経験|けいけん}を{社会|しゃかい}で{共有|きょうゆう}しにくい。 — Because confidentiality is so strict, it's hard to share the experience with society.

And the kind of sentence a lay judge might say afterwards:

{選|えら}ばれたからには、{責任|せきにん}を{持|も}って{考|かんが}えようと{思|おも}った。 — Once I'd been chosen, I felt I had to think it through responsibly.
{人|ひと}の{人生|じんせい}を{決|き}める{以上|いじょう}、{簡単|かんたん}に{結論|けつろん}を{出|だ}すわけにはいかない。 — Given that we're deciding someone's life, we can't reach a conclusion lightly.

## Dialogue: a letter from the court

Two colleagues, Aya and Shun, at lunch. (Casual speech between colleagues of the same age.)

```dialogue
# A letter from the court
あや: ねえ、{昨日|きのう}{家|いえ}に{裁判所|さいばんしょ}から{手紙|てがみ}が{届|とど}いてたの。
= Hey, a letter from the court arrived at my place yesterday.
しゅん: え、{何|なに}かしたの？
= What, did you do something?
あや: してないよ！{裁判員|さいばんいん}の{候補者|こうほしゃ}になったっていうお{知|し}らせ。
= No! It was to tell me I've been put on the list of lay-judge candidates.
しゅん: ああ、くじ{引|び}きで{選|えら}ばれるやつね。じゃあ、もう{決|き}まりなの？
= Oh, the one where they draw names by lot. So is it decided, then?
あや: ううん、リストに{入|はい}っただけで、{実際|じっさい}に{呼|よ}ばれるかどうかはまだ{分|わ}からないんだって。
= No, I've just been put on the list. Apparently they don't know yet whether I'll actually be called.
しゅん: そうなんだ。{選|えら}ばれたら{仕事|しごと}はどうするの？
= I see. What about work if you're chosen?
あや: {会社|かいしゃ}は{休|やす}ませてくれなきゃいけないらしいよ。{日当|にっとう}も{出|で}るし。
= Apparently the company has to let me have the time off. And there's a daily allowance.
しゅん: でも、{難|むずか}しい{事件|じけん}だったら{大変|たいへん}そう。
= But it sounds tough if it's a difficult case.
あや: うん、ちょっと{怖|こわ}い。でも、{選|えら}ばれたからには、ちゃんとやりたいと{思|おも}う。
= Yeah, it's a bit scary. But if I'm chosen, I want to do it properly.
しゅん: えらいね。{終|お}わったら{話|はなし}を{聞|き}かせてよ。
= Good for you. Tell me all about it when it's over.
あや: {裁判|さいばん}で{見|み}たり{聞|き}いたりしたことならね。{評議|ひょうぎ}のことは{話|はな}しちゃいけないの。{守秘義務|しゅひぎむ}があるから。
= What I see and hear at the trial, sure. I'm not allowed to talk about the deliberations. There's a duty of confidentiality.
しゅん: そっか。{秘密|ひみつ}を{守|まも}る{以上|いじょう}、こっちも{聞|き}かないようにするよ。
= Right. Since you have to keep it secret, I'll make sure I don't ask either.
```

{日当|にっとう} = daily allowance; えらい = good
for you, admirable; {秘密|ひみつ} = secret (lesson 30's kanji).

## Reading: a notice for candidates

A made-up notice of the kind candidates receive. (The court is invented.)

> 【{裁判員|さいばんいん}{候補者|こうほしゃ}の{皆様|みなさま}へ】
>
> あなたは、{来年|らいねん}の{裁判員|さいばんいん}{候補者|こうほしゃ}のリストに{入|はい}りました。これは、{有権者|ゆうけんしゃ}の{中|なか}からくじで{選|えら}ばれたもので、すぐに{裁判所|さいばんしょ}に{来|き}ていただくわけではありません。{事件|じけん}が{決|き}まった{場合|ばあい}は、{改|あらた}めてお{知|し}らせします。
>
> {次|つぎ}に{当|あ}てはまる{方|かた}は、{辞退|じたい}を{申|もう}し{出|で}ることができます。お{送|おく}りした{用紙|ようし}にご{記入|きにゅう}の{上|うえ}、{返送|へんそう}してください。
>
> ・{七十歳|ななじゅっさい}{以上|いじょう}の{方|かた}
> ・{学生|がくせい}の{方|かた}
> ・{重|おも}い{病気|びょうき}やけがで、{裁判所|さいばんしょ}に{来|く}ることが{難|むずか}しい{方|かた}
>
> {候補者|こうほしゃ}のリストに{入|はい}ったことは、ご{家族|かぞく}などに{話|はな}してもかまいません。ただし、インターネットなどで{公|おおやけ}にすることはごえんりょください。
>
> みどり{地方裁判所|ちほうさいばんしょ}

〜に{当|あ}てはまる = to apply to; {用紙|ようし} = form; ご{記入|きにゅう}の{上|うえ} = after filling in
(lesson 7's の{上|うえ}); {返送|へんそう}する = to send back; {公|おおやけ}にする = to make public. The list
form, ・ at the start of a line, is how notices set out conditions.

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

[To lay-judge candidates]

You have been placed on next year's list of lay-judge candidates. You were chosen by lot from among
eligible voters; this does not mean you have to come to the court straight away. If a case is
assigned, you will be notified again.

People to whom any of the following apply may ask to decline. Please fill in the form we sent
and send it back.

- People aged 70 or over
- Students
- People for whom serious illness or injury makes coming to court difficult

You may tell your family and others that you are on the candidate list. However, please do not
make it public on the internet or elsewhere.

Midori District Court

</details>

## Key points

- {裁判員|さいばんいん}{制度|せいど}: since 21 May 2009; usually six citizens and three judges decide
  serious criminal cases in district courts, both guilt and sentence.
- Candidates are drawn by lot from voters aged 18 or over (18 and 19 since 2023); some reasons for
  declining are accepted (70 or over, students, illness, care).
- Steps: {公判|こうはん} → {評議|ひょうぎ} → {評決|ひょうけつ} (a majority with at least one judge and one lay
  judge) → {判決|はんけつ}. Deliberations stay secret ({守秘義務|しゅひぎむ}).
- からには and {以上|いじょう} are natural in opinions about duty: {選|えら}ばれたからには, {人|ひと}を{裁|さば}く{以上|いじょう}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Four-character compounds
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

N3 introduced よじじゅくご (four-character compounds; its third kanji is outside N2, so the word is
in kana) with {一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう} and {十人十色|じゅうにんといろ}. These are set phrases of four kanji,
many from Chinese classics or Buddhist texts, that pack an idea or a judgement into one word. They
turn up in speeches, headlines, essays, school mottos and company slogans, and in conversation,
often with a smile, when someone wants to sound neat or wise.

This lesson takes eight common ones whose kanji are all on the course list. For each: what the
four kanji say, what the whole means, and when people use it.

## How they work in a sentence

Most work as nouns: they take の before a noun, だ / です at the end, and で or に after them.

{弱肉強食|じゃくにくきょうしょく}の{世界|せかい} — a dog-eat-dog world
どの{方法|ほうほう}も{一長一短|いっちょういったん}だ。 — Every method has its pros and cons.
{電光石火|でんこうせっか}の{速|はや}さで — with lightning speed

A few also work as な-adjectives: {公明正大|こうめいせいだい}な{選挙|せんきょ} (a fair, open election),
{公明正大|こうめいせいだい}に{行|おこな}う (do it fairly and openly).

Read them as one word. The reading is usually the on'yomi of each kanji in turn, with the usual
sound changes: {一長一短|いっちょういったん} (いち → いっ), {電光石火|でんこうせっか} (せき → せっ).

## The eight

### {起承転結|きしょうてんけつ}: the four steps of a story

| Kanji | {起|き} | {承|しょう} | {転|てん} | {結|けつ} |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Meaning | rise, begin | receive, carry on | turn | tie up |

The four parts of a well-built story: set it up ({起|き}), develop it ({承|しょう}), bring a twist ({転|てん}), and tie
it up ({結|けつ}). It began as the plan of a four-line Chinese poem; today people use it for stories,
speeches, and especially the four-panel comic strips in newspapers, where each panel is one step.
{起承転結|きしょうてんけつ}がはっきりした{話|はなし} is a story with a clear shape. Lesson 30h2 asks whether
essays should follow it too (teachers disagree).

A tiny example, one sentence a step:

> {起|き}：{朝|あさ}、かさを{持|も}たずに{家|いえ}を{出|で}た。
>
> {承|しょう}：{駅|えき}に{着|つ}く{前|まえ}に、{激|はげ}しい{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}した。
>
> {転|てん}：{困|こま}っていると、{知|し}らない{人|ひと}がかさを{差|さ}し{出|だ}してくれた。
>
> {結|けつ}：それは、{去年|きょねん}{私|わたし}が{電車|でんしゃ}に{忘|わす}れたかさだった。

(Set-up: I left home in the morning without an umbrella. Development: before I reached the station
it began to pour. Twist: as I stood there, a stranger held out an umbrella to me. Ending: it was
the umbrella I'd left on a train the year before.)

### {弱肉強食|じゃくにくきょうしょく}: the strong eat the weak

| {弱|じゃく} | {肉|にく} | {強|きょう} | {食|しょく} |
|---|---|---|---|
| weak | meat | strong | eat |

"The weak are meat; the strong eat." Said of nature, of business and of any harsh competition,
usually with a sigh or as a criticism: {弱肉強食|じゃくにくきょうしょく}の{世界|せかい} (a dog-eat-dog world).

{値下|ねさ}げ{競争|きょうそう}で{小|ちい}さな{店|みせ}が{次々|つぎつぎ}に{消|き}えていく。まさに{弱肉強食|じゃくにくきょうしょく}だ。 — Small shops are vanishing one after another in the price war. It's the law of the jungle.

### {適材適所|てきざいてきしょ}: the right person in the right place

| {適|てき} | {材|ざい} | {適|てき} | {所|しょ} |
|---|---|---|---|
| suitable | material (talent) | suitable | place |

Putting each person where their abilities fit best. Managers, coaches and teachers say it when
they assign roles: {適材適所|てきざいてきしょ}で{人|ひと}を{配置|はいち}する (place people where they fit).

### {大器晩成|たいきばんせい}: great talents mature late

| {大|たい} | {器|き} | {晩|ばん} | {成|せい} |
|---|---|---|---|
| great | vessel | late | complete |

A great vessel takes long to make: people of great ability often succeed late. It's said to
encourage someone who's slow to get going, or about someone who did well later in life. Saying it
about yourself sounds like a joke.

{兄|あに}は{四十歳|よんじゅっさい}を{過|す}ぎてから{作家|さっか}として{有名|ゆうめい}になった。{大器晩成|たいきばんせい}の{人|ひと}だ。 — My brother became famous as a writer after forty. A late bloomer.

### {一長一短|いっちょういったん}: pros and cons

| {一|いっ} | {長|ちょう} | {一|いっ} | {短|たん} |
|---|---|---|---|
| one | long (strength) | one | short (weakness) |

Every choice has a good point and a bad point. It's a balanced, cool word, at home in reports
and discussions: {都会|とかい}と{田舎|いなか}の{生活|せいかつ}には、それぞれ{一長一短|いっちょういったん}がある.
({田舎|いなか} is lesson 26's special reading.)

### {我田引水|がでんいんすい}: bending things to your own advantage

| {我|が} | {田|でん} | {引|いん} | {水|すい} |
|---|---|---|---|
| my own | field | draw | water |

Drawing water into your own rice field (and away from everyone else's): arguing or acting only
for your own benefit. It criticizes someone else's reasoning; you'd hardly say it about yourself.

{自分|じぶん}の{会社|かいしゃ}の{商品|しょうひん}だけをすすめるのは、{我田引水|がでんいんすい}の{意見|いけん}だと{言|い}われても{仕方|しかた}がない。 — Recommending only your own company's products, you can hardly complain if people call it self-serving.

### {電光石火|でんこうせっか}: as quick as lightning

| {電|でん} | {光|こう} | {石|せっ} | {火|か} |
|---|---|---|---|
| electric | light | stone | fire (spark) |

A flash of lightning, a spark struck from a stone: something over in an instant. It praises
speed: {電光石火|でんこうせっか}の{早|はや}わざ (a lightning-fast move), {電光石火|でんこうせっか}の{速|はや}さで{仕事|しごと}を{片付|かたづ}ける.

### {公明正大|こうめいせいだい}: fair and open

| {公|こう} | {明|めい} | {正|せい} | {大|だい} |
|---|---|---|---|
| public | bright | right | great |

With nothing hidden and nothing unfair. It's used of elections, contests, decisions and people:
{公明正大|こうめいせいだい}な{判断|はんだん} (a fair and open judgement), {公明正大|こうめいせいだい}に{選|えら}ぶ.

## Dialogue: choosing roles for the school festival

The class committee is deciding who does what for the school festival. Riku is the class
representative; Mei and Daiki are on the committee. (Casual speech between classmates.)

```dialogue
# Planning the class café
りく: じゃあ、{役割|やくわり}を{決|き}めよう。{料理|りょうり}、{会計|かいけい}、{宣伝|せんでん}、どれから？
= Right, let's decide the jobs. Cooking, money, publicity: which first?
めい: {料理|りょうり}はだいきでしょう。{家|いえ}がパン{屋|や}なんだから。
= Daiki should do the cooking. His family runs a bakery.
だいき: いいけど、{会計|かいけい}はめいがやってよ。{暗算|あんざん}、{電光石火|でんこうせっか}じゃん。
= Fine, but you do the money, Mei. You're lightning-fast at mental arithmetic.
めい: それほどでもないけど…まあ、{適材適所|てきざいてきしょ}ってことね。
= I'm not that fast… but OK, the right person in the right place, I suppose.
りく: {宣伝|せんでん}は{絵|え}がうまい{人|ひと}がいいな。ポスターとチラシ、どっちがいいと{思|おも}う？
= For publicity we want someone who's good at drawing. Posters or flyers, which do you think?
だいき: {一長一短|いっちょういったん}だね。ポスターは{目立|めだ}つけど、チラシは{持|も}って{帰|かえ}ってもらえる。
= Both have pros and cons. Posters stand out, but people can take flyers home.
めい: {両方|りょうほう}{作|つく}ればいいじゃない。
= Why not make both?
りく: {予算|よさん}が{足|た}りないよ。あと、{場所|ばしょ}は{一番|いちばん}いい{教室|きょうしつ}がいいって{言|い}ったら、{先生|せんせい}に{我田引水|がでんいんすい}だって{言|い}われた。
= We haven't got the budget. Oh, and when I said we wanted the best classroom, the teacher said I was only thinking of us.
だいき: そりゃそうだ。{場所|ばしょ}はくじ{引|び}きで{決|き}めるんでしょう？
= Well, fair enough. Isn't the room decided by drawing lots?
りく: うん。{公明正大|こうめいせいだい}に、だって。
= Yeah. "Fair and open," they said.
めい: じゃあ、あとはくじ{運|うん}だね。
= Then it's down to the luck of the draw.
```

{会計|かいけい} = accounts, handling money; {目立|めだ}つ = to stand out; くじ{運|うん} = luck in a draw.

## Key points

- よじじゅくご are four-kanji set phrases that work as nouns (some as な-adjectives); read them as
  one word.
- {起承転結|きしょうてんけつ} (set-up, development, twist, ending), {弱肉強食|じゃくにくきょうしょく} (survival of the
  fittest), {適材適所|てきざいてきしょ} (the right person in the right place), {大器晩成|たいきばんせい} (late bloomer),
  {一長一短|いっちょういったん} (pros and cons), {我田引水|がでんいんすい} (self-serving), {電光石火|でんこうせっか}
  (lightning-fast), {公明正大|こうめいせいだい} (fair and open).
- Several carry a judgement: {我田引水|がでんいんすい} criticizes, {大器晩成|たいきばんせい} encourages,
  {弱肉強食|じゃくにくきょうしょく} usually laments. Use them about others with care.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: It could happen: かねない, おそれがある, 得る
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 4 is about how sure you are and what you feel you must do: "it could happen", "I can't",
"there's no way", "it's best to", "it's only". Grammar books call this area **[[modality]]**: the
part of a sentence that shows the speaker's attitude to what they say (how likely, how necessary,
how desirable it is), as opposed to the plain facts. You already know a good deal of it from N4
and N3: かもしれない, はずだ, に{違|ちが}いない, べきだ, わけにはいかない. N2 adds the patterns that
newspapers, announcements and careful speakers use.

This lesson is about **[[possibility]]**, mostly of something bad:

このままでは、{大|おお}きな{事故|じこ}につながりかねない。 — If things go on like this, it could well lead to a serious accident.
{明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}にかけて、{大雨|おおあめ}になるおそれがあります。 — There's a risk of heavy rain through tomorrow morning.
{大|おお}きな{地震|じしん}は、どこででも{起|お}こり{得|う}る。 — A big earthquake can happen anywhere.

The theme is disasters, extreme weather and safety. N4 and N3 gave you the basic words ({地震|じしん},
{避難|ひなん}, {防災|ぼうさい}) and N5 the weather ({雲|くも}, {曇|くも}り): this lesson's kanji let you
write them, and add the words of rescue, prevention, humidity and dryness.

## It could well happen (and that would be bad): 〜かねない

〜かねない joins the ます stem. It looks negative, but it means "could well, might easily": the
speaker sees a real risk of a bad result and is warning about it.

| Verb | ます stem + かねない |
|---|---|
| {起|お}こる | {起|お}こりかねない |
| なる | なりかねない |
| {起|お}こす | {起|お}こしかねない |
| する | しかねない |
| passive {言|い}われる | {言|い}われかねない |

{寝不足|ねぶそく}のまま{運転|うんてん}すると、{事故|じこ}を{起|お}こしかねない。 — If you drive without enough sleep, you could easily cause an accident.
このまま{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}けば、{川|かわ}があふれかねない。 — If it keeps raining like this, the river could well overflow.
そんな{言|い}い{方|かた}をすると、{誤解|ごかい}されかねないよ。 — Put it like that and you could easily be misunderstood.
{小|ちい}さな{油断|ゆだん}が、{大|おお}きな{災害|さいがい}につながりかねません。 — A small lapse could lead to a major disaster.

Points to remember:

- Only bad results. You can't use it for something you hope for: "she might well pass" is
  {合格|ごうかく}するかもしれない, not ×{合格|ごうかく}しかねない.
- It usually comes with a condition or a cause: このままでは, 〜と, 〜ば, 〜たら, 〜で. The sentence
  says "this situation could lead to that bad result".
- It's a little formal: common in news, business and careful advice, and heard in everyday
  speech when someone gives a warning. Polite: 〜かねません.
- It's written in kana: its kanji isn't on the course list.
- Don't confuse it with 〜かねる (lesson 17), which is a polite "can't": お{答|こた}えしかねます (I'm
  afraid I can't answer that). かねない is "could"; かねる is "can't". The negative of one
  looks like the other, which is exactly why learners mix them up.

### かねない and かもしれない

かもしれない is neutral: good or bad, likely or not. かねない is a warning that something bad
is a real possibility, usually as a consequence.

{明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}かもしれない。 — It might rain tomorrow. (neutral)
{準備|じゅんび}をしないと、{試合|しあい}に{負|ま}けかねない。 — If we don't prepare, we could well lose the match. (a warning)

## There's a risk of: 〜おそれがある

〜おそれがある says that there's a risk of something bad. It's the voice of weather forecasts,
news, product labels and official notices: an assessment, not a personal worry.

| Before おそれがある | Example |
|---|---|
| verb, dictionary form (also ない form) | {雪|ゆき}が{積|つ}もるおそれがある |
| noun + の | {大雨|おおあめ}のおそれがある |

{台風|たいふう}の{影響|えいきょう}で、{明日|あした}は{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まるおそれがあります。 — Because of the typhoon, trains may stop tomorrow.
この{地域|ちいき}では、{土砂|どしゃ}{災害|さいがい}のおそれがあるため、{避難|ひなん}を{呼|よ}びかけている。 — In this area, people are being urged to evacuate because of the risk of landslides.
{海岸|かいがん}から{離|はな}れてください。つなみのおそれがあります。 — Please move away from the coast. There is a risk of a tsunami.

It changes like any noun phrase:

- in front of a noun: 〜おそれのある / おそれがある: {倒|たお}れるおそれのある{木|き} (trees that may fall);
- negative: おそれはない ({健康|けんこう}への{影響|えいきょう}のおそれはありません: there is no risk to health);
- "also a risk": おそれもある.

おそれ is written in kana in this course, like other formal nouns (you'll see {恐|おそ}れ in print). On its
own, おそれ also means "fear", but in this pattern it's always "risk".

### おそれがある and かねない

| | 〜かねない | 〜おそれがある |
|---|---|---|
| joins | ます stem | dictionary form, noun + の |
| sounds like | a person's warning about a consequence | an official or objective assessment |
| typical place | advice, business, editorials | forecasts, news, labels, notices |

{無理|むり}をすると、{体|からだ}をこわしかねないよ。 — Push yourself too hard and you could ruin your health. (a friend's warning; おそれがある would sound like a doctor's report)
この{薬|くすり}は、{眠|ねむ}くなるおそれがあります。 — This medicine may cause drowsiness. (a label; かねない would sound oddly personal)

Both are about bad things. Many sentences can take either; the difference is the voice.

## It can happen, it can't happen: 〜{得|う}る, 〜{得|え}ない

〜{得|う}る (also 〜{得|え}る) joins the ます stem and means "can, is possible". It's about
possibility, not ability: it says something can happen or be done in principle. It's written
style, except for one very common word, あり{得|え}ない.

| Form | Reading | Example |
|---|---|---|
| dictionary form | うる (often) or える | {起|お}こり{得|う}る, {考|かんが}え{得|う}る |
| negative | えない (always) | あり{得|え}ない, {想像|そうぞう}し{得|え}ない |
| past, ます form | えた, えます | あり{得|え}た |

The dictionary form has two readings. うる is the older one and is common in writing
(あり{得|う}る, {起|お}こり{得|う}る); える is common too, especially in speech. Every other form uses
え: ×ありうない doesn't exist.

{地震|じしん}は、いつ、どこで{起|お}こってもおかしくない。だれにでも{起|お}こり{得|う}ることだ。 — An earthquake could happen anywhere at any time. It can happen to anyone.
{考|かんが}え{得|う}るすべての{方法|ほうほう}を{試|ため}した。 — We tried every conceivable method.
{事故|じこ}の{原因|げんいん}としては、{二|ふた}つのことが{考|かんが}え{得|う}る。 — Two possible causes of the accident can be considered.

In conversation, あり{得|え}ない is everywhere: "no way, unbelievable", often with a complaint.

「{財布|さいふ}、{家|いえ}に{忘|わす}れてきちゃった。」「えっ、ありえない！」 — "I've left my wallet at home." "What? Unbelievable!"

Notes:

- Not ability. "She can swim" is {泳|およ}げる, not ×{泳|およ}ぎ{得|う}る. 〜{得|う}る is about
  what is possible (an event, an outcome, an idea), not someone's skill.
- 〜{得|え}ない is formal: {理解|りかい}し{得|え}ない (incomprehensible). Lesson 17's
  〜ざるを{得|え}ない uses the same kanji in a different pattern.
- 得 on its own as a verb, {得|え}る "to get, gain" (formal), is N3's word.

## Review: 〜ないとも{限|かぎ}らない, 〜といけないから

Two patterns from earlier lessons go with possibility.

> 〜ないとも{限|かぎ}らない (lesson 5): "it's not impossible that…", a small risk you don't want to
> rule out. It often justifies a precaution: {停電|ていでん}しないとも{限|かぎ}らないから、{電池|でんち}を
> {買|か}っておこう (there might be a power cut, you never know, so let's buy batteries).
>
> 〜と / 〜てはいけないから (N4): "in case": {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}るといけないから、かさを{持|も}って
> いく (I'll take an umbrella in case it rains). It names the bad thing and the precaution together.

## How likely is it?

From surest to least sure. Speakers don't draw the lines in exactly the same place; this is a
guide.

| Pattern | Strength | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| 〜に{違|ちが}いない (N3) | almost certain | the speaker's conviction |
| 〜はずだ (N4) | expected | reasoning from facts |
| 〜おそれがある | a real risk | objective, official; bad things |
| 〜かねない | a real risk | a warning about a consequence; bad things |
| 〜かもしれない (N4) | maybe | neutral |
| 〜{得|う}る | possible in principle | written; can happen |
| 〜ないとも{限|かぎ}らない | small, but not zero | justifies a precaution |

## Disasters and safety words

| Topic | Words |
|---|---|
| disasters | {災害|さいがい}, {天災|てんさい} / {人災|じんさい}, {災難|さいなん}, {震災|しんさい}, {火災|かさい}, {二次災害|にじさいがい}, {被災|ひさい}, {被災地|ひさいち}, {被害|ひがい} (N3) |
| earthquakes | {地震|じしん}, {震度|しんど}, {震源|しんげん}, {余震|よしん}, ゆれ (its kanji is off the list), {震|ふる}える |
| weather | {気象|きしょう} (lesson 13), {気象庁|きしょうちょう}, {悪天候|あくてんこう}, {空模様|そらもよう}, {雨雲|あまぐも}, {入道雲|にゅうどうぐも}, {突風|とっぷう}, {寒波|かんぱ}, {降水量|こうすいりょう}, {湿度|しつど}, {湿気|しっけ}, {雨季|うき} / {乾季|かんき} |
| wet and dry | {湿|しめ}る, {乾|かわ}く, {乾|かわ}かす |
| storms and sea | {荒|あ}れる, {荒|あら}い, {荒|あ}らす, {荒波|あらなみ} (lesson 3), {沈|しず}む, {沈|しず}める |
| danger | {危機|きき}, リスク, {危|あや}うい, {危|あや}うく, {爆発|ばくはつ}, {爆発的|ばくはつてき}, {火山|かざん} (lesson 3), {土砂|どしゃ} (lesson 3), {熱中症|ねっちゅうしょう} (lesson 2) |
| prevention | {防止|ぼうし}, {防水|ぼうすい}, {防災用品|ぼうさいようひん}, {非常食|ひじょうしょく}, {乾電池|かんでんち}, {備|そな}え, {用心|ようじん}, {油断|ゆだん} (lesson 14), ハザードマップ, {避|さ}ける |
| evacuation | {避難所|ひなんじょ}, {避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}, {非常時|ひじょうじ}, {緊急|きんきゅう} (lesson 4), {断水|だんすい}, {安否|あんぴ} |
| rescue | {救|すく}う, {救助|きゅうじょ}, {救出|きゅうしゅつ}, {救援|きゅうえん}, {支援|しえん}, {援助|えんじょ}, {生存者|せいぞんしゃ}, {救急|きゅうきゅう}, {救急箱|きゅうきゅうばこ} |
| fire service | {消防|しょうぼう}, {消防署|しょうぼうしょ}, {消防車|しょうぼうしゃ}, {消防士|しょうぼうし} (lesson 11), {消火|しょうか}, {消火器|しょうかき} |
| possibility | おそれ, あり{得|え}る, {万一|まんいち}, {恐|おそ}らく, いざ |

Notes:

- {震度|しんど} is the Japanese scale of how strongly the ground shakes at a given place (from 0 to
  7, with 5 and 6 split into {弱|じゃく} and {強|きょう}), announced by {気象庁|きしょうちょう}, the Japan
  Meteorological Agency. It isn't the size of the quake itself (magnitude: マグニチュード), so one
  earthquake has one magnitude but many {震度|しんど} readings.
- {救助|きゅうじょ} is rescuing people from danger; {救援|きゅうえん} and {支援|しえん} are bringing help and
  supplies to an area; {援助|えんじょ} is aid, often money or goods; N3's {応援|おうえん} is cheering on
  or backing someone.
- {万一|まんいち} (also {万|まん}が{一|いち}): "in the unlikely event": {万一|まんいち}のときは、この
  {番号|ばんごう}に{電話|でんわ}してください. いざ is "when it comes to it": いざというとき (when the
  moment comes, in an emergency).
- {危|あや}うく is "nearly (but luckily not)": {危|あや}うく{車|くるま}にひかれるところだった (I was nearly
  hit by a car). Lesson 8 met 〜ところだった.
- {防止|ぼうし} (prevention) sounds the same as {帽子|ぼうし} (hat, N5's ぼうし), and {消火|しょうか}
  (putting out a fire) the same as lesson 5's {消化|しょうか} (digestion). Context tells them apart.
- {湿|しめ}る is a group 1 verb although it ends in -める like a group 2 verb: {湿|しめ}らない,
  {湿|しめ}って, {湿|しめ}ったタオル (a damp towel). It sounds like {閉|し}める (to close), a group 2
  verb.
- {熱中症|ねっちゅうしょう} (heatstroke, lesson 2's word) is in every Japanese summer forecast.

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji: disasters and protection, shaking and blasts, wind and water, and the weather.

### Disasters and protection

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 災 | disaster | サイ | — | 7 | {災害|さいがい}, {火災|かさい}, {震災|しんさい}, {防災|ぼうさい}, {被災|ひさい} |
| 防 | defend, prevent | ボウ | ふせ(ぐ) | 7 | {防|ふせ}ぐ, {防止|ぼうし}, {予防|よぼう}, {防犯|ぼうはん}, {消防|しょうぼう} |
| 避 | avoid | ヒ | さ(ける) | 16 | {避|さ}ける, {避難|ひなん}, {避難所|ひなんじょ} |
| 救 | rescue, save | キュウ | すく(う) | 11 | {救|すく}う, {救助|きゅうじょ}, {救急|きゅうきゅう}, {救急車|きゅうきゅうしゃ} |
| 援 | help, aid | エン | — | 12 | {援助|えんじょ}, {支援|しえん}, {救援|きゅうえん}, {応援|おうえん} |

- Carried words you can now write with kanji: {災害|さいがい}, {防災|ぼうさい}, {避難|ひなん}, {防|ふせ}ぐ,
  {予防|よぼう}, {防犯|ぼうはん}, {救急車|きゅうきゅうしゃ}, {応援|おうえん}.
- 避 is also in {避|さ}ける: "avoid" a person, a road or a topic ({混雑|こんざつ}を{避|さ}ける, avoid the
  crowds).

### Shaking and blasts

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 震 | shake, quake | シン | ふる(える) | 15 | {地震|じしん}, {震度|しんど}, {余震|よしん}, {震|ふる}える |
| 爆 | burst, explode | バク | — | 19 | {爆発|ばくはつ}, {爆発的|ばくはつてき} |

- {地震|じしん} (N4's じしん) now takes kanji.
- {震|ふる}える is to tremble or shiver: {寒|さむ}さで{震|ふる}える, {声|こえ}が{震|ふる}える.
- 爆 has 19 strokes, the most in this lesson.

### Wind and water

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 沈 | sink | チン | しず(む), しず(める) | 7 | {沈|しず}む, {沈|しず}める |
| 荒 | rough, wild | コウ | あ(れる), あ(らす), あら(い) | 9 | {荒|あ}れる, {荒|あら}い, {荒|あ}らす, {荒波|あらなみ} |

- {荒|あ}れる is "to get rough, become stormy": {海|うみ}が{荒|あ}れる, {天気|てんき}が{荒|あ}れる; also
  of skin and of a meeting that turns stormy. {荒|あ}らす is to damage or ruin a place:
  はたけが{動物|どうぶつ}に{荒|あ}らされた (the field was ruined by animals).
- {荒|あら}い is "rough, violent": {波|なみ}が{荒|あら}い, {言葉|ことば}が{荒|あら}い, {息|いき}が{荒|あら}い.
- {沈|しず}む is also used for the sun ({日|ひ}が{沈|しず}む) and for a gloomy mood ({気分|きぶん}が{沈|しず}む).

### The weather

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 雲 | cloud | ウン | くも | 12 | {雲|くも}, {雨雲|あまぐも}, {入道雲|にゅうどうぐも} |
| 曇 | cloudy | ドン | くも(る) | 16 | {曇|くも}る, {曇|くも}り |
| 湿 | damp | シツ | しめ(る) | 12 | {湿度|しつど}, {湿気|しっけ}, {湿|しめ}る |
| 乾 | dry | カン | かわ(く), かわ(かす) | 11 | {乾|かわ}く, {乾|かわ}かす, {乾電池|かんでんち}, {乾杯|かんぱい} |

- Carried words with kanji now: {雲|くも}, {曇|くも}る, {曇|くも}り, {乾杯|かんぱい}.
- In {雨雲|あまぐも} the 雨 is read あま and 雲 becomes ぐも. 曇's on'yomi ドン is rare ({曇天|どんてん}, a
  cloudy sky); learn it by the kun'yomi.
- {乾|かわ}く (dry) has a twin, かわく "be thirsty", written with another kanji that's off the
  list: のどがかわく stays in kana in this course.
- "Dryness" is かんそう, with a second kanji off the list. It sounds the same as N3's
  かんそう (impressions), so the course leaves it out.

Memory notes:

- 災 is a river in flood (the three wavy strokes on top) over fire (火): the two great disasters.
- 防 is a hillside (阝) and a direction (方): putting up a slope in the enemy's way.
- 避 has the walking road (辶): stepping aside, out of the way.
- 救 is "seek" (求, N3) with a hand holding a stick (攵): reaching out to pull someone back.
- 援 is a hand (扌) pulling someone up: help.
- 震 is rain (雨) over a shape that once meant a creature shaking the ground.
- 沈 is water (氵) closing over something: it sinks.
- 荒 is grass (艹) on wasteland where the river (川) has run wild: rough.
- 雲 is rain (雨) over a curl of vapour; 曇 is the sun (日) behind a cloud (雲).
- 湿 is water (氵) beside the sun (日) over the ground: laid out in the sun but still damp.
- 乾 has 十 / 日 / 十 on the left, the sun rising in a gap: dry.

```trace
災防避救援震爆沈荒雲曇湿乾
```

## Dialogue: a typhoon on the way

Misaki and Kōta work in the same office. It's early afternoon and a typhoon is coming. (Casual
speech between colleagues.)

```dialogue
# Leaving early
みさき: ねえ、ニュース{見|み}た？{今夜|こんや}、{台風|たいふう}が{関東|かんとう}に{上陸|じょうりく}するかもしれないって。
= Hey, did you see the news? They say the typhoon might hit the Kantō area tonight.
こうた: うん。{夕方|ゆうがた}から{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まるおそれがあるって、{駅|えき}でも{放送|ほうそう}してた。
= Yeah. They were announcing at the station too that trains may stop from this evening.
みさき: じゃあ、{早|はや}めに{帰|かえ}ったほうがいいね。{遅|おそ}くなると、{帰|かえ}れなくなりかねないし。
= Then we'd better go home early. If we leave it late, we could end up not being able to get home.
こうた: でも、{今日|きょう}{中|じゅう}にこの{資料|しりょう}を{仕上|しあ}げないと…。
= But I've got to finish these documents today…
みさき: {家|いえ}でもできるでしょ？{無理|むり}して{残|のこ}って、{駅|えき}で{何時間|なんじかん}も{待|ま}つことになったら{最悪|さいあく}だよ。
= You can do that at home, can't you? If you push it and stay, and end up waiting at the station for hours, that'd be the worst.
こうた: それもそうか。{部長|ぶちょう}に{言|い}ってくる。
= That's true. I'll go and tell the department head.
こうた: {部長|ぶちょう}も「{今日|きょう}は{全員|ぜんいん}{三時|さんじ}で{帰|かえ}っていい」って。
= The department head says "everyone can go home at three today" too.
みさき: よかった。あ、{家|いえ}に{水|みず}とか{乾電池|かんでんち}ある？{停電|ていでん}だってあり{得|え}るよ。
= Good. Oh, have you got water and batteries at home? A power cut's possible too.
こうた: {水|みず}はあるけど、ライトの{電池|でんち}、{切|き}れてたかも。
= I've got water, but the batteries in my torch might be dead.
みさき: じゃあ{帰|かえ}りにコンビニ{寄|よ}ろう。{前|まえ}の{台風|たいふう}のとき、{夕方|ゆうがた}にはもう{電池|でんち}が{売|う}り{切|き}れてたんだよね。
= Then let's stop at a convenience store on the way home. Last typhoon, the batteries had already sold out by the evening.
こうた: そうなんだ。うちのベランダの{自転車|じてんしゃ}も{中|なか}に{入|い}れなきゃ。
= Really? I'd better bring my bike in from the balcony too.
みさき: そうそう。{風|かぜ}で{飛|と}ばされないとも{限|かぎ}らないからね。
= Right. You never know, the wind could blow it away.
こうた: {大|おお}げさだなあ。…でも、{油断|ゆだん}は{禁物|きんもつ}か。
= You're exaggerating… But I suppose you can't be too careful.
みさき: そういうこと。じゃ、{急|いそ}ごう。
= Exactly. Right, let's hurry.
```

{上陸|じょうりく} (to make landfall) is lesson 3's word; {禁物|きんもつ} (something to avoid) is lesson 11's;
{仕上|しあ}げる = to finish off; {大|おお}げさ = exaggerated; {売|う}り{切|き}れる = to sell out.
Count the possibility patterns: an official risk (おそれがある), a personal warning (かねない),
"possible" (あり{得|え}る) and a small risk that justifies a precaution (ないとも{限|かぎ}らない).

## Reading: preparing at home

A newspaper column on disaster preparedness (だ/である style).

> {日本|にほん}は{地震|じしん}や{台風|たいふう}が{多|おお}い{国|くに}だ。{大|おお}きな{災害|さいがい}は、いつ、どこで{起|お}きてもおかしくない。{災害|さいがい}はだれにでも{起|お}こり{得|う}るのである。それにもかかわらず、{備|そな}えが{十分|じゅうぶん}な{家庭|かてい}は{多|おお}くない。ある{市|し}が{行|おこな}った{調査|ちょうさ}では、{三日分|みっかぶん}の{水|みず}と{非常食|ひじょうしょく}を{用意|ようい}している{家庭|かてい}は、{半数|はんすう}に{満|み}たなかったという。「{必要|ひつよう}だとは{思|おも}うが、つい{後回|あとまわ}しにしてしまう」という{声|こえ}が{多|おお}かった。
>
> {大|おお}きな{地震|じしん}の{後|あと}は、{電気|でんき}や{水道|すいどう}が{止|と}まるおそれがある。{断水|だんすい}が{何日|なんにち}も{続|つづ}けば、{飲|の}み{水|みず}だけでなく、トイレも{使|つか}えなくなる。{店|みせ}のたなからは、{水|みず}や{乾電池|かんでんち}がすぐに{消|き}える。「うちはだいじょうぶ」という{油断|ゆだん}が、{被害|ひがい}を{大|おお}きくしかねないのだ。
>
> では、{何|なに}から{始|はじ}めればいいのか。{専門家|せんもんか}は、{特別|とくべつ}なことをする{必要|ひつよう}はないと{言|い}う。{普段|ふだん}{食|た}べているものを{少|すこ}し{多|おお}めに{買|か}っておき、{古|ふる}いものから{使|つか}って、{使|つか}った{分|ぶん}だけ{買|か}い{足|た}せばいい。これなら{非常食|ひじょうしょく}を{食|た}べずに{捨|す}ててしまうこともない。
>
> また、ハザードマップで{自宅|じたく}の{周|まわ}りの{危険|きけん}を{確|たし}かめ、{避難所|ひなんじょ}までの{道|みち}を{一度|いちど}{家族|かぞく}で{歩|ある}いておくことも{大切|たいせつ}だ。{夜|よる}や{大雨|おおあめ}の{日|ひ}には、いつもの{道|みち}が{使|つか}えないこともあり{得|え}る。
>
> {災害|さいがい}そのものを{防|ふせ}ぐことはできない。しかし、{被害|ひがい}を{小|ちい}さくすることはできる。{防災|ぼうさい}は{特別|とくべつ}な{日|ひ}のためのものではなく、{毎日|まいにち}の{暮|く}らしの{中|なか}で{少|すこ}しずつ{進|すす}めるものなのである。

{満|み}たない = to fall short of; {買|か}い{足|た}す = to buy more to top up; {自宅|じたく} = one's
home; {後回|あとまわ}しにする = to put off; {専門家|せんもんか} (expert) and {普段|ふだん} (usually) are lesson 1's and lesson 12's words.

1. What did one city's survey find?
2. According to the writer, what could make the damage worse?
3. What does the column suggest doing about food, and what is the advantage?
4. Why should a family walk the route to the shelter together?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Fewer than half of households had three days' worth of water and emergency food ready.
2. The complacent feeling that "we'll be fine" (「うちはだいじょうぶ」という{油断|ゆだん}):
   {被害|ひがい}を{大|おお}きくしかねない.
3. Buy a little more of what you usually eat, use the oldest first and buy again what you've used.
   That way the emergency food never goes uneaten and thrown away.
4. Because at night or in heavy rain the usual route may be impossible to use (あり{得|え}る), so
   it's important to know the way.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Japan is a country with many earthquakes and typhoons. A major disaster could happen anywhere at
any time. Disasters can happen to anyone. Even so, not many households are well prepared. In a
survey carried out by one city, fewer than half of households had three days' worth of water and
emergency food ready. Many said, "I know it's necessary, but I keep putting it off."

After a big earthquake, electricity and water may be cut off. If the water stays off for days,
you lose not only drinking water but the use of the toilet too. Water and batteries soon disappear from
the shop shelves. The complacency of "we'll be fine" can easily make the damage worse.

So where should you start? Experts say you don't need to do anything special. Buy a little more
of the food you usually eat, use the oldest first, and buy more to replace what you've used. That
way you won't end up throwing emergency food away uneaten.

It's also important to check the dangers around your home on a hazard map and to walk the route
to the shelter once as a family. At night or on a day of heavy rain, the usual way may not be
usable.

We can't prevent disasters themselves. But we can make the damage smaller. Disaster
preparedness isn't something for a special day; it's something we do little by little in our
everyday lives.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
このままでは、{事故|じこ}につながりかねません。
= If things go on like this, it could well lead to an accident.
{明日|あした}は{大雨|おおあめ}になるおそれがあります。
= There's a risk of heavy rain tomorrow.
そんなこと、ありえないよ。
= That's impossible. / No way.
{地震|じしん}は、どこででも{起|お}こりうる。
= An earthquake can happen anywhere.
{万一|まんいち}のときは、{避難所|ひなんじょ}に{行|い}ってください。
= In an emergency, please go to the shelter.
```

## Common mistakes

- ×{明日|あした}は{晴|は}れかねない for "it might be sunny tomorrow". かねない is only for bad
  results; use かもしれない.
- ×{起|お}こるかねない. かねない joins the ます stem: {起|お}こりかねない.
- Reading かねない as "can't". It means "could (easily)": {失敗|しっぱい}しかねない is "could fail",
  not "can't fail". The polite "can't" is lesson 17's 〜かねます.
- ×{大雨|おおあめ}がおそれがある. After a noun, おそれ takes の: {大雨|おおあめ}のおそれがある.
- ×ありうない, ×ありうません. Only the dictionary form can be read うる; everything else is え:
  あり{得|え}ない, あり{得|え}ます.
- 〜{得|う}る for skill: "I can read kanji" is {漢字|かんじ}が{読|よ}める, not ×{読|よ}み{得|う}る.
- 〜おそれがある for a friend's worry: {風邪|かぜ}をひくおそれがあるよ sounds like a weather
  report. Say {風邪|かぜ}ひいちゃうよ or ひくかもしれないよ.

## Key points

- Modality: the speaker's attitude (how likely, necessary, desirable). This module's topic.
- 〜かねない (ます stem): could well (lead to something bad); a warning about a consequence; kana.
- 〜おそれがある (dictionary form, noun + の): there's a risk of (bad); forecasts, news, labels;
  おそれのある before a noun; kana.
- 〜{得|う}る / 〜{得|え}る (ます stem): can, is possible (not ability); written. Negative and other
  forms always え: あり{得|え}ない (very common in speech: no way).
- 〜ないとも{限|かぎ}らない: a small risk you can't rule out, often with a precaution.
- New kanji: 災 防 避 救 援 震 爆 沈 荒 雲 曇 湿 乾. Write {災害|さいがい}, {防災|ぼうさい},
  {避難|ひなん}, {地震|じしん}, {防|ふせ}ぐ, {予防|よぼう}, {救急車|きゅうきゅうしゃ}, {応援|おうえん},
  {雲|くも}, {曇|くも}り, {乾杯|かんぱい} with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Can't and must: かねる, がたい, ざるを得ない, わけにはいかない
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 16 was about what could happen. This lesson is about what you can't do and what you
must, the language of a company that has to refuse a request, accept a loss or change its plans.

{申|もう}しわけございませんが、{電話|でんわ}ではお{答|こた}えしかねます。 — I'm sorry, but I'm unable to answer that over the phone.
その{話|はなし}はちょっと{信|しん}じがたい。 — That story is a bit hard to believe.
{材料費|ざいりょうひ}が{上|あ}がったので、{値上|ねあ}げせざるを{得|え}ない。 — Material costs have gone up, so we have no choice but to raise prices.
{大事|だいじ}なお{客|きゃく}さんの{頼|たの}みだから、{断|ことわ}るわけにはいかない。 — It's a request from an important customer, so we can't turn it down.

Two terms help here. **[[Obligation]]** is what you must do, whether the pressure comes from rules,
from other people or from the situation; Japanese has many ways to say it, and they differ in
who or what is doing the pushing. A **[[polite refusal]]** says no without saying いいえ: Japanese
business language softens, apologizes and gives a reason, and 〜かねます is one of its main
tools.

The theme is business and management: companies, strategy, competition, profit and loss,
planning, expansion and cooperation. N3 gave you {営業|えいぎょう} and {対策|たいさく} in kana; this
lesson's kanji let you write them.

## I'm unable to (politely): 〜かねる

〜かねる joins the ます stem and conjugates as a group 2 verb (かねます, かねました). It means "find
it impossible to, can't bring yourself to": not lack of ability, but that your position, the
rules or your feelings won't let you.

Its commonest use is a polite refusal by staff, with humble お〜いたす or plain stem + かねます:

その{条件|じょうけん}では、お{引|ひ}き{受|う}けいたしかねます。 — I'm afraid we can't accept on those terms.
{個人|こじん}{情報|じょうほう}については、お{答|こた}えしかねます。 — We're unable to answer questions about personal information.
{当店|とうてん}では、{返品|へんぴん}はお{受|う}けしかねますので、ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください。 — Please note that this shop cannot accept returns.

It also describes someone who can't decide or can't bear something:

どちらの{案|あん}がいいか、{決|き}めかねている。 — I can't make up my mind which plan is better.
{一人|ひとり}で{困|こま}っているこうはいを{見|み}るに{見|み}かねて、{手伝|てつだ}った。 — I couldn't stand by and watch my junior struggling alone, so I helped. (a set phrase: {見|み}るに{見|み}かねて)

Notes:

- Kana, like かねない: its kanji isn't on the list.
- かねる and かねない. 〜かねる is "can't (politely)"; its negative 〜かねない (lesson 16) is
  "could well (happen)". They look like opposites in form but are used in different places:
  かねる for a person's own decision, かねない for a risk.
- お{待|ま}ちかね (the long-awaited…) comes from {待|ま}ちかねる "can hardly wait":
  お{待|ま}ちかねの{新商品|しんしょうひん} (the new product you've all been waiting for).
- Customers don't use 〜かねます about the shop. It's the speaker's own side declining.

## Hard to (believe, accept, forgive): 〜がたい

〜がたい joins the ます stem and works as an い-adjective (がたく, がたかった). It means "hard to",
but for things that are hard to accept, believe or put into words, not hard physically.

| ます stem + がたい | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {信|しん}じがたい | hard to believe |
| {理解|りかい}しがたい | hard to understand (accept) |
| {許|ゆる}しがたい | unforgivable |
| {忘|わす}れがたい | unforgettable |
| {想像|そうぞう}しがたい | hard to imagine |
| {言|い}いがたい | hard to call it… |
| {得|え}がたい | hard to come by, precious |

{社長|しゃちょう}が{急|きゅう}に{辞|や}めるなんて、{信|しん}じがたい{話|はなし}だ。 — It's hard to believe that the president would suddenly quit.
{今回|こんかい}の{企画|きかく}は、うまくいったとは{言|い}いがたい{結果|けっか}に{終|お}わった。 — This project ended with results you could hardly call a success.
{留学|りゅうがく}の{一年|いちねん}は、{私|わたし}にとって{忘|わす}れがたい{経験|けいけん}だ。 — My year abroad is an unforgettable experience for me.

### がたい and にくい

N4's 〜にくい is "hard to" in a practical, physical sense. 〜がたい is mental or moral, and more
written.

この{肉|にく}は{固|かた}くて{食|た}べにくい。 — This meat is tough and hard to eat. (×{食|た}べがたい)
この{字|じ}は{小|ちい}さくて{読|よ}みにくい。 — This writing is small and hard to read.
あんなひどいことを{言|い}うなんて、{許|ゆる}しがたい。 — Saying something so cruel is hard to forgive.

With some verbs both are possible with a change of feel: {理解|りかい}しにくい{説明|せつめい} (an
explanation that's hard to follow) vs {理解|りかい}しがたい{行動|こうどう} (behaviour that's hard to
accept). 〜がたい is in kana in this course.

## Have no choice but to: 〜ざるを{得|え}ない

〜ざるを{得|え}ない is "have no choice but to, can't help but": the situation forces you to do
something you'd rather not. ざる is a classical negative, so it joins the ない form without ない:

| Verb | ない form | 〜ざるを{得|え}ない |
|---|---|---|
| {行|い}く | {行|い}かない | {行|い}かざるを{得|え}ない |
| {認|みと}める | {認|みと}めない | {認|みと}めざるを{得|え}ない |
| する | (しない) | せざるを{得|え}ない |
| {来|く}る | {来|こ}ない | {来|こ}ざるを{得|え}ない |

する is the exception: it's せざるを{得|え}ない, not ×しざるを{得|え}ない (the same せ as in せず).

{売|う}り{上|あ}げが{下|さ}がり{続|つづ}け、{工場|こうじょう}を{一|ひと}つ{閉|と}じざるを{得|え}なくなった。 — With sales falling and falling, we had no choice but to close one of the factories.
{台風|たいふう}が{近|ちか}づいているので、イベントは{中止|ちゅうし}せざるを{得|え}ない。 — A typhoon's coming, so we have to cancel the event.
{最初|さいしょ}は{反対|はんたい}したが、{彼|かれ}の{案|あん}のほうがいいと{認|みと}めざるを{得|え}ない。 — I was against it at first, but I have to admit his plan is better.

The last example shows a second use: "I can't help concluding, I have to admit".

It's formal and fairly written. In everyday speech you'd say 〜しかない or 〜なきゃいけない:
{中止|ちゅうし}するしかないね.

## Can't, have to (it wouldn't be right): 〜わけにはいかない (review)

> N3 lesson 7: 〜わけにはいかない (dictionary form) is "I can't, because it wouldn't be right";
> 〜ないわけにはいかない is "I can't not, so I have to", for social or moral reasons.
> {明日|あした}は{大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}があるから、{休|やす}むわけにはいかない。

### Four ways to say "must"

| Pattern | Where the pressure comes from | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| 〜なければならない (N4) | rules, necessity | neutral |
| 〜しかない (N3) | it's the only option left | spoken, resigned |
| 〜ざるを{得|え}ない | circumstances force you, against your wishes | formal, reluctant |
| 〜ないわけにはいかない | social or moral duty, other people's expectations | "I couldn't not" |

じょうしに{誘|さそ}われたら、{行|い}かないわけにはいかない。 — If your boss invites you, you can't not go. (a social duty)
{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まったので、タクシーで{行|い}かざるを{得|え}なかった。 — The trains stopped, so I had no choice but to take a taxi. (the situation)

Swap them and the sentences become odd: the boss's invitation isn't "circumstances", and
stopped trains aren't a social duty. Many sentences can take both, though, with a change of
emphasis.

ないわけにはいかない and ざるを{得|え}ない are both **[[double negatives]]**: two negatives that
add up to a positive "must" (not doing it is not possible). Lesson 19's ないことには is another.

### To recognize: 〜ずにはすまない

〜ずにはすまない (also 〜ないではすまない) is "it won't end without…", so "you'll have to": a
situation can't be settled unless you do something, usually an apology or a payment.

{大事|だいじ}な{書類|しょるい}をなくしたのだから、{謝|あやま}らずにはすまないだろう。 — You lost an important document, so you'll have to apologize.

You'll mostly read it; you won't be asked to produce it.

## Refusing politely

A polite refusal in business avoids a bare "no". It usually has an apology, a reason and a
softened refusal, sometimes a counter-offer.

| Part | Phrases |
|---|---|
| apology | {申|もう}しわけございません, あいにく (unfortunately), せっかくですが (kind of you, but) |
| reason | 〜ておりまして, {規則|きそく}で{決|き}まっておりまして |
| refusal | 〜かねます, いたしかねます, ご{期待|きたい}にそえず (we couldn't meet your hopes; its last kanji is off the list), {今回|こんかい}は{見送|みおく}らせていただきます (we'll pass this time) |
| softening | 〜のですが…, ちょっと…, {検討|けんとう}させていただきます |
| alternative | {代|か}わりに〜はいかがでしょうか, 〜でしたら{可能|かのう}です |

Note: {検討|けんとう}させていただきます ("we'll consider it") often means a polite no, depending on
tone and context. Don't take it as a promise.

- {市場|しじょう} is the market in economics ({国内|こくない}{市場|しじょう}, the domestic market); read

  circumstances); the adverb やむを{得|え}ず is "reluctantly, having no choice". It's
  ざるを{得|え}ない's cousin.

- 企 is a person (人) standing on tiptoe (止): looking ahead, planning.
- 営 has fire-like strokes over a building with two rooms: a busy house that's kept running.
- 策 is bamboo (竹, lesson 3) over a thorny shape: a plan with sharp points, a measure.
- 案 is a woman at peace (安, N5) over a wooden desk (木): sitting down to think up a plan.
- 討 is words (言) and a hand measuring: weighing things up in discussion.
- 協 is ten (十) beside three forces (力): many people pulling together.
- 益 is water (the top) over a dish (皿, lesson 19): it fills and overflows, a gain.
- 損 is a hand (扌) over a mouth and the shell that once meant money: money slipping out of your hand.
- 展 is a body lying stretched out (the top) over clothes: unfolding.
- 拡 is a hand (扌) and wide (広, N4): widening.
- 競 is two people standing (立 and 兄 twice): side by side, competing.

## Dialogue: asking for a discount

Takahashi sells stationery for a company called Sunlight Bungu. Kimura, a buyer, phones about a
quote. Afterwards Takahashi talks to the section chief, Yamada. (Business keigo, then casual speech
inside the company.)

```dialogue
# A difficult request
たかはし: いつもお{世話|せわ}になっております。サンライト{文具|ぶんぐ}の{高橋|たかはし}でございます。
= Thank you for your continued business. This is Takahashi from Sunlight Bungu.
きむら: ああ、{高橋|たかはし}さん。{先日|せんじつ}のお{見積|みつ}もりなんですが、もう{少|すこ}しなんとかなりませんか。{一割|いちわり}{下|さ}げていただけると{助|たす}かるんですが。
= Ah, hello, Takahashi. About the quote the other day: is there anything more you can do? It would help us a lot if you could take ten per cent off.
たかはし: {申|もう}しわけございません。{材料費|ざいりょうひ}が{上|あ}がっておりまして、{一割|いちわり}のお{値引|ねび}きはいたしかねます。
= I'm very sorry. Our material costs have gone up, so I'm afraid we can't offer a ten per cent discount.
きむら: そうですか…。{他社|たしゃ}さんからも{見積|みつ}もりをいただいているので、このままだとおんしゃにお{願|ねが}いするのは{難|むずか}しいかもしれません。
= I see… We've had quotes from other companies too, so as it stands it may be hard to place the order with you.
たかはし: それは{困|こま}ります…。では、{数量|すうりょう}を{増|ふ}やしていただけるのであれば、{五|ご}パーセントまでは{検討|けんとう}させていただきます。
= That would be a problem for us… Well, if you could increase the quantity, we could consider up to five per cent.
きむら: {五|ご}パーセントですか。{社内|しゃない}で{協議|きょうぎ}して、{明日|あした}までにお{返事|へんじ}します。
= Five per cent. We'll discuss it internally and give you an answer by tomorrow.
たかはし: ありがとうございます。よろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
= Thank you very much. I look forward to hearing from you.
たかはし: {課長|かちょう}、{五|ご}パーセントまでなら、と{言|い}ってしまいました。
= Chief, I went and said we could do up to five per cent.
やまだ: うーん、{利益|りえき}はほとんど{出|で}ないな。でも、あそこは{大事|だいじ}なお{客|きゃく}さんだから、{断|ことわ}るわけにはいかない。
= Hmm, there'll be hardly any profit. But they're an important customer, so we can't turn them down.
たかはし: はい。{他社|たしゃ}に{取|と}られたら、{来年|らいねん}の{取引|とりひき}にも{影響|えいきょう}が{出|で}かねませんし。
= Yes. If another company takes them, it could easily affect next year's business too.
やまだ: そうだな。{今回|こんかい}は{受|う}けざるを{得|え}ないだろう。その{代|か}わり、{次|つぎ}の{企画|きかく}で{取|と}り{返|かえ}そう。
= Right. This time we'll have no choice but to accept. In return, let's make it back on the next project.
たかはし: {分|わ}かりました。{部長|ぶちょう}にはどう{説明|せつめい}しましょうか。
= Understood. How should we explain it to the department head?
やまだ: ぼくから{話|はな}しておくよ。{正直|しょうじき}、{部長|ぶちょう}が{喜|よろこ}ぶとは{言|い}いがたいけどね。
= I'll talk to the department head. Honestly, I can't say it'll go down well.
```

{見積|みつ}もり = a quote, an estimate; {値引|ねび}き = a discount; {他社|たしゃ} = another company;
おんしゃ = your company (polite, in speech; its first kanji is off the list); {数量|すうりょう} =
quantity; {取|と}り{返|かえ}す = to win back. Takahashi's いたしかねます is the polite refusal; his
{検討|けんとう}させていただきます here is a real offer, because he names a figure.

A newspaper feature (だ/である style) about a small manufacturer.
