> {社長|しゃちょう}の{北野|きたの}{健一|けんいち}さんは「{価格|かかく}を{上|あ}げざるを{得|え}なかった。{長年|ながねん}の{取引先|とりひきさき}に{頼|たの}むのは{心苦|こころぐる}しかったが、このままでは{会社|かいしゃ}そのものが{続|つづ}けられなくなりかねない」と{話|はな}す。
>
> しかし、{値上|ねあ}げだけでは{問題|もんだい}は{解決|かいけつ}しない。そこで{北野|きたの}さんは、{若|わか}い{社員|しゃいん}の{提案|ていあん}を{受|う}けて、{自社|じしゃ}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{生|い}かした{新|あたら}しい{事業|じぎょう}を{始|はじ}めた。{精密|せいみつ}な{部品|ぶひん}を{作|つく}る{技術|ぎじゅつ}で、キャンプ{用品|ようひん}を{作|つく}るのだ。{社員|しゃいん}にキャンプ{好|ず}きが{多|おお}かったことがきっかけだった。
>
> 「{最初|さいしょ}は{反対|はんたい}しました。{部品|ぶひん}だけを{作|つく}ってきた{会社|かいしゃ}が、{一般|いっぱん}の{消費者|しょうひしゃ}に{向|む}けた{商品|しょうひん}を{作|つく}るなんて、{正直|しょうじき}{信|しん}じがたかった」。だが、{社員|しゃいん}が{作|つく}った{試作品|しさくひん}を{手|て}に{取|と}って、{考|かんが}えが{変|か}わったという。{商品|しょうひん}はインターネットで{販売|はんばい}され、{今|いま}では{売|う}り{上|あ}げの{一割|いちわり}を{占|し}めるまでになった。
>
> もちろん、{本業|ほんぎょう}の{部品|ぶひん}をやめるわけにはいかない。{社員|しゃいん}の{生活|せいかつ}がかかっているのだ。「{新|あたら}しいことを{試|ため}さないで{会社|かいしゃ}を{守|まも}ることは、もうできない。{今|いま}はそう{考|かんが}えています」。{北野|きたの}さんの{目|め}は、すでに{次|つぎ}の{商品|しょうひん}に{向|む}いている。

{製作所|せいさくしょ} = works (in company names); {心苦|こころぐる}しい = to feel bad (about burdening
someone); {試作品|しさくひん} = a prototype; {本業|ほんぎょう} = main business; {反映|はんえい}させる = to reflect (pass on); {占|し}める (to make up
a share) is lesson 30's word; {一般|いっぱん}, {販売|はんばい}, {消費者|しょうひしゃ} and {価格|かかく} are
lesson 12's.

1. Why did Mr Kitano raise his prices, and how did he feel about it?
2. What new business did the company start, and whose idea was it?
3. What changed Mr Kitano's mind about it?
4. Does the company plan to stop making parts?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Fuel and material costs kept rising and the company made a loss; without raising prices the
   company itself could have gone under ({続|つづ}けられなくなりかねない). He felt bad about asking
   long-standing customers ({心苦|こころぐる}しかった).
2. Camping goods made with its precision-parts technology; it was a young employee's proposal.
3. Holding the prototype that the employees had made.
4. No: {本業|ほんぎょう}の{部品|ぶひん}をやめるわけにはいかない, because the staff's livelihoods depend
   on it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

With fuel and material prices still rising, running a small or medium-sized company is getting
harder. Kitano Works, a company of thirty employees that makes machine parts, ran at a loss last
year for the first time in thirty years. Unlike large companies, it's hard for them to pass rising
costs straight on in their prices.

"We had no choice but to raise our prices," says the president, Kenichi Kitano. "I felt bad
asking customers we've dealt with for years, but at this rate the company itself could easily
end up unable to carry on."

But raising prices alone doesn't solve the problem. So, taking up a proposal from a young
employee, Mr Kitano started a new business that makes use of the company's own technology: it
makes camping goods with the technology it uses for precision parts. It began because many of the
staff were keen campers.

"At first I was against it. A company that had only ever made parts making products for ordinary
consumers? Honestly, it was hard to believe." But when he held the prototype the staff had made,
he says, he changed his mind. The products are sold online, and they now make up ten per cent of
sales.

Of course, the company can't give up its main business, parts. The employees' livelihoods depend
on it. "We can't protect the company any more without trying new things. That's how I see it
now." Mr Kitano is already looking ahead to the next product.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{申|もう}しわけございませんが、お{答|こた}えいたしかねます。
= I'm very sorry, but I'm unable to answer that.
それはちょっと{信|しん}じがたいですね。
= That's a little hard to believe.
{今回|こんかい}は{中止|ちゅうし}せざるを{得|え}ません。
= This time we have no choice but to cancel.
{部長|ぶちょう}の{頼|たの}みだから、{断|ことわ}るわけにはいかない。
= It's the department head's request, so I can't turn it down.
{社内|しゃない}で{検討|けんとう}させていただきます。
= We'll consider it within the company.
```

## Common mistakes

- ×しざるを{得|え}ない. する becomes せ: せざるを{得|え}ない.
- ×{行|い}かないざるを{得|え}ない. ざる replaces ない: {行|い}か + ざるを{得|え}ない.
- 〜かねる for inability: "I can't swim" is {泳|およ}げない, not ×{泳|およ}ぎかねる. かねる is about
  what your position or feelings won't let you do.
- Using 〜かねます about the other person: ×お{客様|きゃくさま}はお{待|ま}ちしかねます. It's your own
  side declining.
- ×{重|おも}くて{持|も}ちがたい. Physical difficulty is 〜にくい: {持|も}ちにくい. がたい is for
  believing, accepting, forgiving, forgetting.
- 〜ざるを{得|え}ない in casual speech with friends: correct, but stiff. Friends say 〜しかない or
  〜なきゃ.
- Taking {検討|けんとう}させていただきます as a yes. It's often a polite no.

## Key points

- Obligation and polite refusal: this lesson's two jobs.
- 〜かねる (ます stem; group 2): can't (politely), unable to; staff refusals お〜いたしかねます;
  {決|き}めかねる, {見|み}るに{見|み}かねて. Not the same as lesson 16's かねない (could well).
- 〜がたい (ます stem; い-adjective): hard to (believe, accept, forgive, forget); 〜にくい for
  practical difficulty.
- 〜ざるを{得|え}ない (ない form without ない; する → せざるを{得|え}ない): have no choice but to;
  also "have to admit"; formal.
- 〜ないわけにはいかない: can't not (social or moral duty). Both are double negatives.
- 〜ずにはすまない (to recognize): you'll have to (to settle things).
- New kanji: 企 営 総 策 案 討 協 益 損 展 拡 及 競. Write {営業|えいぎょう}, {対策|たいさく},
  {政策|せいさく}, {案内|あんない}, {提案|ていあん}, {展示|てんじ}, {競争|きょうそう}, {競技|きょうぎ},
  {損|そん}, {及|およ}び with kanji from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: No way: っこない, まい, ようがない, ものか
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lessons 16 and 17 dealt with risks and duties. This lesson is the strong end of
**[[possibility]]**: "it can't possibly happen", "I won't", "there's no way to", "as if I would!".
Some of these patterns are casual and emotional, some are written and old-fashioned, so the
register matters as much as the meaning.

そんな{難|むずか}しい{問題|もんだい}、{一日|いちにち}で{解|と}けっこないよ。 — There's no way you can solve a problem that hard in a day.
あんなに{寒|さむ}い{所|ところ}には、もう{二度|にど}と{行|い}くまい。 — I'll never go to such a cold place again. (written)
{星|ほし}が{見|み}えないので、{観測|かんそく}のしようがない。 — The stars aren't visible, so there's no way to observe them.
{負|ま}けるもんか。{最後|さいご}まで{頑張|がんば}るぞ。 — No way am I going to lose. I'll keep going to the end.

The theme is science and space: states of matter, pressure and gravity, measuring precisely, the
universe and astronauts. N3 gave you {宇宙|うちゅう} and {星|ほし} in kana; their kanji are here.

## No way it'll happen: 〜っこない

〜っこない joins the ます stem and means "there's no way, it can't possibly": a strong, casual
denial, mostly about whether something can happen or be done. It often follows a potential verb.

| Verb | ます stem + っこない |
|---|---|
| できる | できっこない |
| {分|わ}かる | {分|わ}かりっこない |
| {勝|か}てる (potential of {勝|か}つ) | {勝|か}てっこない |
| {間|ま}に{合|あ}う | {間|ま}に{合|あ}いっこない |
| {見|み}つかる | {見|み}つかりっこない |

{今|いま}から{走|はし}っても、{間|ま}に{合|あ}いっこない。 — Even if we run now, there's no way we'll make it.
こんな{小|ちい}さい{望遠鏡|ぼうえんきょう}で、{土星|どせい}の{輪|わ}なんか{見|み}えっこないよ。 — There's no way you'll see Saturn's rings with a telescope this small.
「{宇宙飛行士|うちゅうひこうし}になりたいんだ。」「なれっこないって{思|おも}ってるでしょ？」 — "I want to be an astronaut." "You think there's no way I can, don't you?"

Points:

- Casual speech only. You'd say it to friends and family; in polite or written Japanese use
  〜はずがない or 〜わけがない (ありません / ない).
- It's about the speaker's view of what's possible, so it's usually about events and abilities,
  not about a fact ("he isn't a doctor" isn't っこない).
- The っこ is unchanging. There's no positive ×できっこある.

## Won't, surely won't: 〜まい

〜まい is a written, rather old-fashioned negative. It has two jobs, like the volitional
it mirrors:

1. Negative will: "I won't, I'm determined not to". Usually the speaker's own resolve.
2. Negative guess: "surely not, probably not", a written ないだろう.

{二度|にど}と{同|おな}じ{失敗|しっぱい}はするまいと{心|こころ}に{決|き}めた。 — I made up my mind never to make the same mistake again. (will)
{空|そら}がこんなに{晴|は}れているから、{雨|あめ}は{降|ふ}るまい。 — With the sky this clear, it surely won't rain. (guess)
この{計算|けいさん}に{間違|まちが}いはあるまい。 — There's surely no mistake in this calculation. (guess)

### How まい joins

| Verb type | Form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| group 1 | dictionary form + まい | {行|い}くまい, {降|ふ}るまい, あるまい |
| group 2 | dictionary form or stem + まい | {食|た}べるまい / {食|た}べまい, {見|み}るまい / {見|み}まい |
| する | するまい / すまい (also しまい) | {二度|にど}とするまい |
| {来|く}る | くるまい / こまい (also きまい) | もう{来|く}るまい |

The group 1 form is fixed; for group 2, する and {来|く}る speakers and dictionaries differ, and
the forms in brackets are less common. If you write one, the dictionary form + まい is the safe
choice. まい isn't one of the app's drill forms.

Two set uses:

- 〜まいと{思|おも}う / 〜まいと{決|き}める: decide not to. {二度|にど}と{遅刻|ちこく}するまいと{思|おも}った.
- 〜のではあるまいか (to recognize): "isn't it perhaps…?", a written のではないだろうか.
  {宇宙|うちゅう}のどこかに{生命|せいめい}があるのではあるまいか (might there not be life somewhere in
  the universe?).

### To recognize: 〜(よ)うが〜まいが

〜(よ)うが〜まいが, "whether or not", is lesson 25's: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ろうが{降|ふ}るまいが
(whether it rains or not).

## There's no way to: 〜ようがない (review)

> N3 lesson 10: ます stem + ようがない, "there's no way to (do it)", because the means are
> missing. With a する noun: {連絡|れんらく}のしようがない (there's no way to get in touch).
> {住所|じゅうしょ}が{分|わ}からないから、{手紙|てがみ}の{出|だ}しようがない。

ようがない is about the lack of a method; っこない is the speaker's judgement that something
can't happen.

{雲|くも}が{厚|あつ}くて、{月|つき}の{観測|かんそく}のしようがない。 — The clouds are so thick there's no way to observe the moon. (no means)
こんな{天気|てんき}じゃ、{月|つき}なんか{見|み}えっこないよ。 — In this weather there's no way you'll see the moon. (judgement)

## Can't be: わけがない, はずがない, っこない (review table)

| Pattern | Register | Typical feel |
|---|---|---|
| 〜はずがない (N4) | neutral | reasoning from facts: it can't be (true) |
| 〜わけがない (N3) | neutral, more emotional | no way; also your own refusal |
| 〜っこない | casual | no way it'll happen or can be done |
| 〜まい | written | surely not; won't |

{彼|かれ}は{今|いま}アメリカにいるから、ここにいるはずがない。 — He's in America now, so he can't be here. (reasoning)
あの{人|ひと}が{約束|やくそく}を{守|まも}るわけがない。 — There's no way that person will keep their promise. (emotional)
{一晩|ひとばん}でレポート{十枚|じゅうまい}なんて、{書|か}けっこないよ。 — Ten pages of report in one night? No way I can write that. (casual)

## As if I would! I'll never…: 〜ものか

〜ものか (casual もんか) is a strong, emotional negative: "as if…!, I'll never…". It follows
the plain form (nouns and な-adjectives with な) and is said with a falling intonation.

{二度|にど}とあんな{店|みせ}に{行|い}くもんか。 — I'll never go to that shop again.
{負|ま}けるものか。{最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}る。 — I'm not going to lose. I'll run to the end.
「{痛|いた}くない？」「{平気|へいき}なもんか。すごく{痛|いた}いよ。」 — "Doesn't it hurt?" "Fine? Not a chance. It really hurts."

It can also be rhetorical: "is it…? (of course not)": こんな{問題|もんだい}、{小学生|しょうがくせい}に{分|わ}かるものか (as if a primary schoolchild could understand a problem like this!).

Notes:

- 〜もんか and 〜ものか are casual and emphatic; 〜ものですか is a softer, rather old-fashioned
  polite version, heard mostly from women. In polite conversation you'd normally say
  {絶対|ぜったい}に〜ません instead.
- Don't confuse it with N3's 〜ものだ (that's how it is / used to) or lesson 12's 〜ものだから.
  Here the か is the key: a question that expects "no".
- {負|ま}けてたまるか is a similar set phrase: "I'm not going to let myself lose".

## Want to but can't: 〜(よ)うにも〜ない

The volitional + にも + the potential of the same verb in the negative: "even if I try to, I
can't".

{連絡|れんらく}しようにも、{電話番号|でんわばんごう}が{分|わ}からない。 — I'd like to get in touch, but I don't know the phone number.
{宇宙|うちゅう}では、{水|みず}をコップに{注|そそ}ごうにも{注|そそ}げない。 — In space, you can't pour water into a cup even if you try.
{雪|ゆき}で{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まって、{帰|かえ}ろうにも{帰|かえ}れなかった。 — The trains stopped because of the snow, so I couldn't get home however much I wanted to.

The second verb is usually the potential of the first ({帰|かえ}ろうにも{帰|かえ}れない), but it can
be another negative that blocks the action (〜ようにも〜がない). It's written and spoken.

## Science and space words

| Topic | Words |
|---|---|
| states of matter | {液体|えきたい}, {気体|きたい}, {固体|こたい}, {液|えき}, {粉|こな}, {粉末|ふんまつ}, {粉雪|こなゆき}, {花粉|かふん} |
| matter and atoms | {原子|げんし}, {分子|ぶんし}, {元素|げんそ} (lesson 13), {水素|すいそ}, {物体|ぶったい}, {物理|ぶつり}, {真空|しんくう}, {純金|じゅんきん}, {単純|たんじゅん} |
| force and pressure | {重力|じゅうりょく}, {無重力|むじゅうりょく}, {引力|いんりょく}, {圧力|あつりょく}, {水圧|すいあつ}, {気圧|きあつ}, {高気圧|こうきあつ} / {低気圧|ていきあつ}, {大気|たいき}, {圧倒的|あっとうてき} |
| measuring | {質量|しつりょう}, {重量|じゅうりょう}, {密度|みつど}, {体積|たいせき}, {角度|かくど}, {直角|ちょっかく}, {三角|さんかく}, {秒|びょう}, {秒速|びょうそく}, {秒針|びょうしん}, {精度|せいど}, {精密|せいみつ}, {誤差|ごさ} (lesson 13) |
| the universe | {天体|てんたい}, {銀河|ぎんが}, {天|あま}の{川|がわ}, {星座|せいざ}, {星空|ほしぞら}, {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}, {満月|まんげつ}, {光年|こうねん}, {無限|むげん}, {月面|げつめん}, {火星|かせい} / {金星|きんせい} / {木星|もくせい} / {土星|どせい} |
| observing | {天文学|てんもんがく}, {天文台|てんもんだい}, {望遠鏡|ぼうえんきょう}, {観測|かんそく} (lesson 13), {探査|たんさ}, {探査機|たんさき} |
| space flight | {宇宙船|うちゅうせん}, {宇宙飛行士|うちゅうひこうし}, {宇宙人|うちゅうじん}, ロケット, {打|う}ち{上|あ}げる, {飛行|ひこう}, {上空|じょうくう} |
| size and extent | {巨大|きょだい}, {巨人|きょじん}, {超|ちょう}〜, {超過|ちょうか}, {密接|みっせつ}, {密閉|みっぺい}, {過密|かみつ} |
| effort | {精神|せいしん}, {精一杯|せいいっぱい}, {二度|にど}と |

Notes:

- {気体|きたい} (gas) sounds the same as {期待|きたい} (hope, N3). In a listening question you'll never
  be asked to choose between them.
- {秒|びょう} counts seconds: {三十秒|さんじゅうびょう}, {秒速|びょうそく}{三十万|さんじゅうまん}キロ (300,000 km
  a second, roughly the speed of light).
- {光年|こうねん} (light year) is a distance, the distance light travels in a year, not a time.
- {超|ちょう}〜 is a prefix "super-, ultra-" ({超高速|ちょうこうそく}, ultra-high-speed) and, in casual
  speech, "really": {超|ちょう}おいしい. Lesson 27 lists it with the other prefixes.
  {超|こ}える is "to exceed (a number or limit)": {気温|きおん}が{三十度|さんじゅうど}を{超|こ}える. It's N3's
  こえる ({越|こ}える, "to cross") written with another kanji, not a new word: use 超 for numbers and
  limits, {越|こ}える for mountains, borders and years.
- {角|かく} / {角|かど} / {角|つの}: 角 has three readings. {角度|かくど} and {三角|さんかく} use カク; N5's
  かど (street corner) is now {角|かど}; つの is a horn.
- {精一杯|せいいっぱい} is "with all one's might": {精一杯|せいいっぱい}{頑張|がんば}ります.
- {圧倒的|あっとうてき} is "overwhelming": {圧倒的|あっとうてき}な{差|さ} (an overwhelming gap).
- {単純|たんじゅん} (simple, simplistic) is a common word that now takes its kanji.

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji: space, matter and pressure, and size and measurement.

### Space

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 宇 | eaves; space | ウ | — | 6 | {宇宙|うちゅう}, {宇宙船|うちゅうせん} |
| 宙 | the sky, mid-air | チュウ | — | 8 | {宇宙|うちゅう}, {宇宙人|うちゅうじん} |
| 星 | star | セイ | ほし | 9 | {星|ほし}, {星座|せいざ}, {火星|かせい}, {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし} |

- Carried words you can now write: {宇宙|うちゅう}, {星|ほし}.
- 星 is ほし alone and in {星空|ほしぞら}, ぼし in {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}, and セイ in the planets
  ({火星|かせい}, {金星|きんせい}) and {星座|せいざ}.

### Matter and pressure

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 液 | liquid | エキ | — | 11 | {液体|えきたい}, {液|えき}, {溶液|ようえき} |
| 粉 | powder, flour | フン | こな | 10 | {粉|こな}, {粉末|ふんまつ}, {花粉|かふん}, {粉雪|こなゆき} |
| 純 | pure | ジュン | — | 10 | {単純|たんじゅん}, {純度|じゅんど}, {純金|じゅんきん} |
| 圧 | pressure | アツ | — | 5 | {圧力|あつりょく}, {気圧|きあつ}, {水圧|すいあつ}, {圧倒的|あっとうてき} |
| 密 | dense, secret | ミツ | — | 11 | {密度|みつど}, {精密|せいみつ}, {密接|みっせつ}, {過密|かみつ} |

- {花粉|かふん} (pollen): {花粉症|かふんしょう} is hay fever (症 is lesson 2's kanji).
- 密 is also in {秘密|ひみつ} (a secret), lesson 30's word now that 秘 comes there.
- Flour is こむぎこ, written in kana here because its middle kanji is off the list.

### Size and measurement

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 巨 | huge | キョ | — | 5 | {巨大|きょだい}, {巨人|きょじん} |
| 超 | exceed, super- | チョウ | こ(える) | 12 | {超|ちょう}, {超過|ちょうか}, {超|こ}える |
| 秒 | second (of time) | ビョウ | — | 9 | {秒|びょう}, {秒速|びょうそく}, {秒針|びょうしん} |
| 角 | angle, corner, horn | カク | かど, つの | 7 | {角度|かくど}, {三角|さんかく}, {直角|ちょっかく}, {角|かど} |
| 精 | refined, spirit | セイ | — | 14 | {精密|せいみつ}, {精度|せいど}, {精神|せいしん}, {精一杯|せいいっぱい} |

- N5's かど (corner) is now {角|かど}.
- 精 is also in {精算|せいさん}: settling up, paying the difference (a fare at the station, expenses
  at work). It sounds like N3's {生産|せいさん} (production).

Memory notes:

- 宇 and 宙 both have the roof (宀): the great roof over everything, space.
- 星 is the sun (日) over 生 (be born, N5): a light born in the sky.
- 液 is water (氵) and 夜 (night, N4): the dew that forms at night, a liquid.
- 粉 is rice (米) divided (分): ground into powder.
- 純 is thread (糸, lesson 24) with a sprout pushing up: plain, unmixed silk.
- 圧 is earth (土) under an overhanging cliff: pressed down.
- 密 is a roof (宀) over 必 (surely) and a mountain (山): packed tight, hidden away.
- 巨 is a big carpenter's square: huge.
- 超 is running (走, N4) and a sword over a mouth (the right-hand part): running past, exceeding.
- 秒 is grain (禾) and few (少): a tiny amount, a second.
- 角 is a horn, drawn from the animal's horn itself.
- 精 is rice (米) and blue (青, N4): polished, refined.


## Dialogue: waiting for meteors

Haruto and his older sister Aoi are on the roof of their block of flats, waiting for a meteor
shower. (Casual speech between siblings.)

```dialogue
# A night on the roof
はると: ねえ、ほんとに{流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}なんか{見|み}えるの？{東京|とうきょう}だよ。
= Hey, will we really see shooting stars? This is Tokyo.
あおい: {明|あか}るい{流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}なら、{町|まち}の{中|なか}でも{見|み}えるって。{一時間|いちじかん}に{何個|なんこ}かは{見|み}られるはずだよ。
= They say you can see the bright ones even in the city. We should see a few an hour.
はると: でも、{雲|くも}が{出|で}てきたよ。これじゃ{見|み}えっこないって。
= But the clouds are coming over. There's no way we'll see anything now.
あおい: {待|ま}ってれば、{晴|は}れるかもしれないでしょ。
= If we wait, it might clear up.
はると: {寒|さむ}いよ…。{帰|かえ}ろうにも、かぎはおねえちゃんが{持|も}ってるし。
= It's cold… And even if I wanted to go back, you've got the key.
あおい: もんく{言|い}わない。ほら、{少|すこ}しずつ{雲|くも}が{切|き}れてきた。
= Stop complaining. Look, the clouds are breaking up a bit.
はると: あ、あれ、{木星|もくせい}？すごく{明|あか}るい。
= Oh, is that Jupiter? It's really bright.
あおい: そう。あそこの{三|みっ}つ{並|なら}んだ{星|ほし}があるのがオリオン{座|ざ}。
= Yes. And the one with three stars in a row over there is Orion.
はると: あっ、{今|いま}の{見|み}た？いっしゅんだったけど！
= Oh, did you see that? It was only for a split second!
あおい: {見|み}た{見|み}た！{一秒|いちびょう}もなかったね。
= I saw it! It wasn't even a second.
はると: {願|ねが}い{事|ごと}、{言|い}うひまなんかないじゃん。
= There's no time to make a wish.
あおい: {次|つぎ}は{言|い}ってみなよ。{三回|さんかい}{言|い}えたらかなうって。
= Try it on the next one. They say if you can say it three times, it comes true.
はると: {三回|さんかい}なんて{無理|むり}だよ。でも、もう{帰|かえ}るもんか。{次|つぎ}のを{見|み}るまで{待|ま}つ。
= Three times? Impossible. But there's no way I'm going home now. I'm waiting till I see the next one.
あおい: さっきまで{帰|かえ}りたいって{言|い}ってたくせに。
= And there you were, wanting to go home a minute ago.
```

いっしゅん = an instant (its second kanji is off the list); もんくを{言|い}う = to complain (its second kanji is off the list);
{願|ねが}い{事|ごと} = a wish; かなう = to come true. はると's もう{帰|かえ}るもんか is his own resolve, and
{見|み}えっこない is his judgement about the clouds.

## Reading: living without gravity

An explanatory article for general readers (だ/である style).

> {国際|こくさい}{宇宙|うちゅう}ステーションは、{地上|ちじょう}から{約|やく}{四百|よんひゃく}キロの{上空|じょうくう}を、{約|やく}{九十分|きゅうじっぷん}で{地球|ちきゅう}を{一周|いっしゅう}している。{中|なか}では{重力|じゅうりょく}をほとんど{感|かん}じないため、{人|ひと}も{物|もの}もふわふわと{浮|う}いてしまう。{窓|まど}の{外|そと}では、{一日|いちにち}に{十六回|じゅうろっかい}も{日|ひ}が{昇|のぼ}っては{沈|しず}んでいく。
>
> {無重力|むじゅうりょく}に{近|ちか}い{環境|かんきょう}では、{地上|ちじょう}の{常識|じょうしき}が{通用|つうよう}しない。{例|たと}えば{液体|えきたい}は、コップに{注|そそ}ごうにも{注|そそ}げない。{水|みず}は{丸|まる}い{玉|たま}になって、{空中|くうちゅう}に{浮|う}かんでしまうのだ。そのため{飲|の}み{物|もの}は、{袋|ふくろ}に{入|い}れてストローで{飲|の}む。{塩|しお}やこしょうのような{粉|こな}も、そのままでは{飛|と}び{散|ち}って{機械|きかい}の{中|なか}に{入|はい}りかねない。{液|えき}に{混|ま}ぜて{使|つか}うのはそのためだ。
>
> {体|からだ}にも{変化|へんか}が{起|お}きる。{重力|じゅうりょく}がないと、{骨|ほね}やきんにくを{使|つか}わなくなるので、{少|すこ}しずつ{弱|よわ}くなっていく。{宇宙飛行士|うちゅうひこうし}が{毎日|まいにち}{二時間|にじかん}ほど{運動|うんどう}するのは、{地球|ちきゅう}に{戻|もど}ったとき{歩|ある}けなくならないようにするためである。
>
> {眠|ねむ}るときにも{工夫|くふう}がいる。{体|からだ}が{流|なが}されないよう、{固定|こてい}した{寝袋|ねぶくろ}に{入|はい}って{眠|ねむ}るのだ。{上|うえ}も{下|した}もない{世界|せかい}なので、{立|た}ったまま{寝|ね}ても{横|よこ}になって{寝|ね}ても、{感覚|かんかく}はまったく{同|おな}じだそうだ。
>
> ある{飛行士|ひこうし}は、{子供|こども}のころ「{宇宙|うちゅう}なんか{行|い}けっこない」と{笑|わら}われたそうだ。しかし、あきらめるものかと{勉強|べんきょう}を{続|つづ}け、{夢|ゆめ}をかなえた。{窓|まど}から{見|み}た{青|あお}い{地球|ちきゅう}の{美|うつく}しさは、{言葉|ことば}では{説明|せつめい}しようがないという。

{国際|こくさい}{宇宙|うちゅう}ステーション = the International Space Station; {通用|つうよう}する = to hold
good, work; {注|そそ}ぐ = to pour; {飛|と}び{散|ち}る = to scatter; {混|ま}ぜる = to mix; {工夫|くふう} = ingenuity, a clever way; {寝袋|ねぶくろ} = a sleeping bag; {一周|いっしゅう}
(going round once) is lesson 27's word. The figures (about 400 km, about 90 minutes, about two
hours of exercise) are the commonly given round numbers.

1. Why does a drink go in a bag with a straw?
2. Why are salt and pepper mixed into a liquid?
3. Why do astronauts exercise every day?
4. What did people say to the astronaut as a child, and what did the astronaut do?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Because liquid can't be poured into a cup: water forms balls and floats in the air.
2. Because powder would scatter and could get into the machines ({入|はい}りかねない).
3. Without gravity, bones and muscles weaken; they exercise so that they can still walk when they
   return to Earth.
4. They laughed and said there was no way the child could go to space ({行|い}けっこない). The child
   was determined not to give up (あきらめるものか), kept studying and made the dream come true.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

The International Space Station circles the Earth about 400 km up, going round once in about 90
minutes. Inside, you feel almost no gravity, so people and things float about. Outside the window, the sun rises and sets as many as sixteen
times a day.

In conditions close to weightlessness, the common sense of life on the ground doesn't work. For
example, you can't pour a liquid into a cup, however hard you try. The water forms a round ball
and floats in the air. So drinks are put in bags and drunk through a straw. Powders such as salt
and pepper would scatter as they are and could get into the machinery. That's why they're used
mixed into a liquid.

The body changes too. Without gravity you stop using your bones and muscles, so they gradually
weaken. Astronauts exercise for about two hours every day so that they won't be unable to walk
when they get back to Earth.

Sleeping takes some ingenuity too. So as not to drift away, they sleep inside a sleeping bag
that's been fixed in place. In a world with no up or down, it apparently feels exactly the same whether
you sleep standing up or lying down.

One astronaut, it's said, was laughed at as a child: "There's no way you'll ever get to space."
But, determined not to give up, the child kept studying and made the dream come true. The beauty
of the blue Earth seen from the window, the astronaut says, is impossible to put into words.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
そんなの、できっこないよ。
= There's no way I can do that.
{二度|にど}と{同|おな}じ{失敗|しっぱい}はするまい。
= I won't make the same mistake twice.
{連絡|れんらく}しようにも、{番号|ばんごう}が{分|わ}からない。
= I'd like to get in touch, but I don't know the number.
{負|ま}けるもんか。
= No way am I going to lose.
{言葉|ことば}では{説明|せつめい}しようがない。
= There's no way to explain it in words.
```

## Common mistakes

- ×できるっこない. っこない joins the ます stem: できっこない, {分|わ}かりっこない.
- っこない in polite or written Japanese. It's casual: in a report or to a customer, say
  〜はずがありません or 〜ことはありえません.
- ×{行|い}きまい. For group 1 verbs まい follows the dictionary form: {行|い}くまい.
- Using まい in conversation for "I won't": it sounds bookish. Say {二度|にど}と{行|い}かない or
  {絶対|ぜったい}{行|い}かない.
- Saying ものか with a rising tone. It's said falling, as an exclamation ("As if I'd go!"); rising,
  {行|い}くものか？ sounds like a real question.
- ×{帰|かえ}ろうにも{帰|かえ}る. The second part must be negative: {帰|かえ}ろうにも{帰|かえ}れない.
- Writing {超|こ}える and {越|こ}える as two words. They're one verb in two spellings: 超 for
  figures and limits, {越|こ}える for places and time.

## Key points

- 〜っこない (ます stem; casual): no way it'll happen or can be done; often after a potential.
- 〜まい (written): won't (resolve) / surely won't (guess); group 1 dictionary form + まい; する
  → するまい / すまい; {来|く}る → くるまい / こまい (forms vary). Not a drill form.
- 〜ようがない (review): no way to (no means).
- はずがない (reasoning), わけがない (emotional), っこない (casual), まい (written).
- 〜ものか / 〜もんか (plain form; な for nouns and な-adjectives): as if…!, I'll never…
- 〜(よ)うにも〜ない: want to, but can't.
- New kanji: 宇 宙 星 液 粉 純 圧 密 巨 超 秒 角 精. Write {宇宙|うちゅう}, {星|ほし}, {角|かど} with kanji
  from now on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Best to, unless, must: にこしたことはない, ないことには, ほかない
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This lesson is about advice and judgement: what's best, what has to happen first, what's left
when there's no other way, and what's too obvious to need saying.

{野菜|やさい}は{毎日|まいにち}{食|た}べるに{越|こ}したことはない。 — Of course, it's best to eat vegetables every day.
{食|た}べてみないことには、{味|あじ}は{分|わ}からない。 — You can't tell what it tastes like until you try it.
{店|みせ}が{閉|し}まっていたので、{家|いえ}にあるもので{作|つく}るほかなかった。 — The shops were shut, so I had no choice but to make something from what we had at home.
{朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}が{大切|たいせつ}なのは、{言|い}うまでもない。 — It goes without saying that breakfast is important.

The theme is food and nutrition: diet, nutrients, flavours and seasoning, dairy and eggs, sweets
and preserved food. N3 had cooking and the kitchen, and earlier courses wrote many of these words in kana
({栄養|えいよう}, {濃|こ}い, {薄|うす}い, {卵|たまご}, {塩|しお}); this lesson's kanji write them.

## It's best to (obviously): 〜に{越|こ}したことはない

〜に{越|こ}したことはない means "nothing beats…, it's best to…". Literally "there's nothing that
goes beyond ({越|こ}す) it". It states something everyone would agree with, often before a "but".

| Before に{越|こ}したことはない | Example |
|---|---|
| verb, dictionary form (or ない form) | {早|はや}く{寝|ね}るに{越|こ}したことはない |
| い-adjective | {安|やす}いに{越|こ}したことはない |
| な-adjective, noun (no だ) | {新鮮|しんせん}に{越|こ}したことはない, {手作|てづく}りに{越|こ}したことはない |

{食品|しょくひん}は{新|あたら}しいに{越|こ}したことはないが、{古|ふる}いものから{使|つか}うことも{大切|たいせつ}だ。 — Of course fresher food is better, but it's also important to use up the older things first.
{塩分|えんぶん}は{少|すく}なめにするに{越|こ}したことはない。 — It's best to keep salt on the low side.
{用心|ようじん}するに{越|こ}したことはない。 — You can't be too careful.

Points:

- It's a general truth, not an order to one person: more "it's best to" than "you should".
  For direct advice, use this lesson's review patterns below (〜ことだ, 〜べきだ).
- Often followed by が or けど and a realistic objection: {手作|てづく}りに{越|こ}したことはないけど、
  {忙|いそが}しい{日|ひ}は{無理|むり}だよね.
- {越|こ}す is in kanji in this pattern (the course rule; 越 is an N3 kanji).

## Unless you…, nothing will happen: 〜ないことには

〜ないことには joins the ない form and says that without the first thing, the second can't
happen. The main clause is negative or means "it's impossible, hard": {分|わ}からない, {始|はじ}まらない,
{決|き}められない, {何|なに}もできない.

{実際|じっさい}に{食|た}べてみないことには、{好|す}きかどうか{分|わ}からない。 — Unless you actually try it, you won't know whether you like it.
{材料|ざいりょう}がそろわないことには、{料理|りょうり}は{始|はじ}められない。 — Until the ingredients are all here, we can't start cooking.
{本人|ほんにん}に{聞|き}いてみないことには、{何|なに}とも{言|い}えない。 — Until we ask the person concerned, I can't say anything.

Like lesson 17's ないわけにはいかない, it's a **[[double negative]]**: "not doing A, B doesn't
happen" means "you must do A first". The difference from 〜なければ: ないことには stresses that
A is a condition you can't skip, and it usually comes with an unwelcome or blocked result.

{運動|うんどう}しなければやせない。 — If you don't exercise, you won't lose weight. (neutral)
{運動|うんどう}しないことには、やせようがない。 — Without exercise, there's just no way to lose weight. (A first, nothing else works)

## There's nothing for it but: 〜ほかない

〜ほかない joins the dictionary form: "there's nothing else to do but…, have no choice but to".
Variants: 〜よりほかない, 〜ほか{仕方|しかた}がない (ほか is written in kana here: it's a formal noun in
this use).

{雨|あめ}で{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}けないので、{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}にあるもので{作|つく}るほかない。 — It's raining and I can't go shopping, so there's nothing for it but to make something from what's in the fridge.
だれも{手伝|てつだ}ってくれないなら、{一人|ひとり}でやるよりほかない。 — If nobody's going to help, I'll just have to do it on my own.

### ほかない, しかない, ざるを{得|え}ない

| Pattern | Register | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| 〜しかない (N3) | spoken and written | the only option left |
| 〜ほかない / よりほかない | a little formal, written | the same, more resigned and serious |
| 〜ざるを{得|え}ない (17) | formal | forced against your wishes |

They overlap a lot: {待|ま}つしかない and {待|ま}つほかない both mean "we can only wait". ほかない
sounds more serious and more written; in a chat with a friend, しかない is the natural choice.

## No need to (it's obvious): 〜までもない

〜までもない joins the dictionary form: "it's not even necessary to…, there's no need to go as
far as…". 〜までもなく is "without needing to…".

{言|い}うまでもないが、{食|た}べすぎは{体|からだ}に{悪|わる}い。 — It goes without saying that overeating is bad for you.
この{程度|ていど}の{熱|ねつ}なら、{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}くまでもない。 — With a fever this mild, there's no need to go to hospital.
{言|い}うまでもなく、{和食|わしょく}の{基本|きほん}はご{飯|はん}とみそしるだ。 — Needless to say, the basis of Japanese food is rice and miso soup.

{言|い}うまでもない and {言|い}うまでもなく are by far the commonest uses; you'll see them in essays as
openers ("needless to say").

## Review: advice with ことだ, べきだ, ものだ

> N3 lesson 9: 〜ことだ (that's what you should do: practical advice to one person:
> {健康|けんこう}のためには、よく{寝|ね}ることだ), 〜べきだ (should, on principle: {食|た}べ{物|もの}をむだに
> するべきではない), 〜ものだ (that's what people normally do: {出|で}された{料理|りょうり}は{残|のこ}さず
> {食|た}べるものだ).

| Pattern | Says | Compare |
|---|---|---|
| 〜に{越|こ}したことはない | it's best to (everyone would agree) | soft; often "but…" |
| 〜ことだ | you should (to one person, practical) | direct advice |
| 〜べきだ | should (principle, duty) | strong; opinions |
| 〜ものだ | that's what one does (social norm) | general |
| 〜ないことには | not without (a condition first) | blocked result |
| 〜ほかない | no choice but | resigned |

## Food and nutrition words

| Topic | Words |
|---|---|
| nutrition | {栄養素|えいようそ}, {栄養価|えいようか}, {栄養不足|えいようぶそく}, {栄養士|えいようし}, {養分|ようぶん}, たんぱく{質|しつ}, ビタミン, {消化|しょうか} (lesson 5), {吸収|きゅうしゅう} |
| eating habits | {食生活|しょくせいかつ}, {主食|しゅしょく}, {主菜|しゅさい}, {副菜|ふくさい}, {間食|かんしょく}, {空腹|くうふく}, {食材|しょくざい}, {原材料|げんざいりょう} (lesson 9) |
| salt | {塩分|えんぶん}, {塩味|しおあじ}, {塩気|しおけ}, {食塩|しょくえん}, {塩水|しおみず}, {塩辛|しおから}い, {減塩|げんえん}, {塩加減|しおかげん} |
| sweet and hot | {甘|あま}み, {甘|あま}さ, {甘口|あまくち}, {甘党|あまとう}, {甘酒|あまざけ}, {甘味料|かんみりょう}, {辛口|からくち}, {辛|から}さ, {辛党|からとう}, {激辛|げきから}, {苦|にが}み, {香辛料|こうしんりょう} |
| strong and mild | {濃厚|のうこう}, {濃度|のうど}, {濃|こ}さ, {薄味|うすあじ}, {薄口|うすくち}, {薄|うす}める, {薄|うす}まる, {薄切|うすぎ}り |
| milk and eggs | {乳|ちち}, {母乳|ぼにゅう}, {乳製品|にゅうせいひん}, {粉|こな}ミルク, {生|なま}クリーム, {生卵|なまたまご}, ゆで{卵|たまご}, {卵焼|たまごや}き, {卵黄|らんおう}, {卵白|らんぱく} |
| sweets | {和菓子|わがし}, {洋菓子|ようがし}, {菓子|かし}パン |
| keeping food | {干物|ひもの}, {乾物|かんぶつ}, {保存食|ほぞんしょく}, {保存料|ほぞんりょう}, {冷凍食品|れいとうしょくひん}, {賞味期限|しょうみきげん}, {消費期限|しょうひきげん} |
| cooking with steam | {蒸気|じょうき}, {蒸発|じょうはつ}, {蒸|む}し{焼|や}き, {茶|ちゃ}わん{蒸|む}し |
| dishes | {大皿|おおざら}, {小皿|こざら}, {取|と}り{皿|ざら}, {一皿|ひとさら} |
| other | {味|あじ}わう, {甘|あま}える, {養|やしな}う, {栄|さか}える (lesson 8), {飲料|いんりょう} |

Notes:

- {甘口|あまくち} / {辛口|からくち}: mild / hot (curry), sweet / dry (sake, wine); {辛口|からくち} is also
  "harsh" of criticism: {辛口|からくち}の{評論|ひょうろん} (lesson 20).
- {甘党|あまとう} is someone with a sweet tooth; {辛党|からとう} is, in the traditional sense, someone
  who prefers alcohol to sweets, though many people now use it for a lover of spicy food.
- {賞味期限|しょうみきげん} is "best before" (quality); {消費期限|しょうひきげん} is "use by" (safety), for food
  that goes off quickly.
- {干物|ひもの} is dried fish; {干|ほ}し{物|もの} is laundry hung out to dry. Same kanji, different words.
- {乳|ちち} is milk (from the breast) and the breast itself: written; everyday milk is

- {甘|あま}える is to depend on someone's kindness, to act like a spoilt child: お{言葉|ことば}に

- みそしる (miso soup) is written in kana here: its last kanji isn't on the list.

## Dialogue: advice from a dietitian

Yūki, an office worker, sees the dietitian, Satō, after a health check. (Polite speech.)

```dialogue
# After the health check
さとう: {健康|けんこう}{診断|しんだん}の{結果|けっか}を{見|み}ると、{血圧|けつあつ}が{少|すこ}し{高|たか}めですね。{普段|ふだん}、お{食事|しょくじ}はどうされていますか。
= Looking at your health check results, your blood pressure is a little high. What do you usually eat?
ゆうき: {昼|ひる}はほとんど{外食|がいしょく}で、ラーメンやカツどんが{多|おお}いです。{夜|よる}はコンビニのお{弁当|べんとう}ですね。
= Lunch is nearly always out, mostly ramen and katsudon. In the evening it's a convenience-store bento.
さとう: そうですか。{外食|がいしょく}は{味|あじ}が{濃|こ}いものが{多|おお}いので、どうしても{塩分|えんぶん}が{多|おお}くなりがちなんです。
= I see. Food when you eat out tends to be strongly flavoured, so you inevitably take in a lot of salt.
ゆうき: やっぱり、{自分|じぶん}で{作|つく}らないとだめですか。
= So I really have to cook for myself?
さとう: もちろん、{自分|じぶん}で{作|つく}るに{越|こ}したことはありません。でも、{無理|むり}をすると{続|つづ}きませんから、まずはできることから{始|はじ}めましょう。
= Of course, cooking for yourself is best. But if you push yourself too hard, you won't keep it up, so let's start with what you can do.
ゆうき: {例|たと}えば、どんなことですか。
= Such as what?
さとう: ラーメンのスープを{全部|ぜんぶ}{飲|の}まないだけでも、ずいぶん{違|ちが}いますよ。それから、{野菜|やさい}を{一皿|ひとさら}{足|た}すこと。
= Just not drinking all the ramen soup makes quite a difference. And add a plate of vegetables.
ゆうき: スープを{残|のこ}すのは、ちょっともったいない{気|き}がしますけど…。
= Leaving the soup feels like a bit of a waste, though…
さとう: お{気持|きも}ちは{分|わ}かります。でも、{数字|すうじ}を{下|さ}げたいなら、がまんするほかありませんね。
= I understand how you feel. But if you want to bring the numbers down, there's nothing for it but to put up with it.
ゆうき: {分|わ}かりました。{薄味|うすあじ}に{慣|な}れるまで、{時間|じかん}がかかりそうだなあ。
= All right. It looks as if it'll take a while to get used to milder food.
さとう: {味覚|みかく}は{二|に}、{三週間|さんしゅうかん}で{慣|な}れると{言|い}われています。やってみないことには{分|わ}かりませんから、まず{一か月|いっかげつ}{試|ため}してみてください。
= They say your sense of taste adjusts in two or three weeks. You won't know until you try, so please give it a month first.
ゆうき: はい。{次|つぎ}の{健康|けんこう}{診断|しんだん}が{楽|たの}しみになるように、{頑張|がんば}ります。
```

{健康|けんこう}{診断|しんだん} = a health check; {血圧|けつあつ} = blood pressure; {外食|がいしょく} = eating
out; もったいない = wasteful, a shame; がまんする = to put up with it (its second kanji is off the
list); {味覚|みかく} = the sense of taste. Notice the three kinds of advice: what's ideal
({作|つく}るに{越|こ}したことはありません), what's unavoidable (がまんするほかありません) and what has
to happen first (やってみないことには{分|わ}かりません).

## Reading: is low salt just a sacrifice?

An opinion column (だ/である style) with a counter-view.

> {和食|わしょく}は{体|からだ}にいいと{言|い}われる。{野菜|やさい}や{魚|さかな}を{多|おお}く{使|つか}い、{油|あぶら}も{少|すく}ないからだ。しかし、{弱点|じゃくてん}もある。しょうゆやみそ、つけもの、{干物|ひもの}など、{塩分|えんぶん}の{多|おお}い{食品|しょくひん}がよく{使|つか}われることだ。{塩分|えんぶん}のとりすぎが{血圧|けつあつ}を{上|あ}げ、{病気|びょうき}の{原因|げんいん}になりかねないことは、{言|い}うまでもない。
>
> そこで{減塩|げんえん}がすすめられるのだが、{薄味|うすあじ}の{料理|りょうり}はおいしくないと{感|かん}じる{人|ひと}も{多|おお}いだろう。{好|す}きなものをがまんしてまで{長生|ながい}きしたくない、という{声|こえ}も{聞|き}く。その{気持|きも}ちはよく{分|わ}かる。{食|た}べることは{生活|せいかつ}の{楽|たの}しみであり、ただがまんするほかないのなら、{長|なが}く{続|つづ}けるのは{難|むずか}しい。
>
> しかし、{減塩|げんえん}はがまんだけではない。だしの{味|あじ}をしっかりきかせたり、レモンの{香|かお}りやしょうがなどの{香辛料|こうしんりょう}を{上手|じょうず}に{使|つか}ったりすれば、{塩|しお}を{減|へ}らしても{物足|ものた}りなさは{感|かん}じにくい。また、{人|ひと}の{味覚|みかく}は{慣|な}れるもので、{数週間|すうしゅうかん}{薄味|うすあじ}を{続|つづ}けると、{前|まえ}の{味|あじ}が{濃|こ}すぎると{感|かん}じるようになるという。{薄味|うすあじ}は、{慣|な}れれば{素材|そざい}の{味|あじ}を{楽|たの}しむ{食|た}べ{方|かた}でもあるのだ。
>
> もちろん、{塩分|えんぶん}は{少|すく}ないに{越|こ}したことはない。だが、{大切|たいせつ}なのは、{一度|いちど}にすべてを{変|か}えようとしないことだ。{実際|じっさい}に{試|ため}してみないことには、{自分|じぶん}に{合|あ}うやり{方|かた}は{見|み}つからない。まずは{一日|いちにち}{一食|いっしょく}から{始|はじ}めてみてはどうだろうか。{無理|むり}をしないことが、{結局|けっきょく}は{一番|いちばん}の{近道|ちかみち}なのである。

{弱点|じゃくてん} = weak point; つけもの = pickles (its first kanji is off the list); すすめる = to
recommend (its kanji in this sense is off the list); {長生|ながい}き = long life; だしの{味|あじ}をきかせる =
to bring out the flavour of the stock; {物足|ものた}りなさ = the feeling that something is missing; {素材|そざい} (ingredients, material) is
lesson 13's word; {近道|ちかみち} = a short cut.

1. What weak point of Japanese food does the writer mention?
2. What objection to low-salt eating does the writer bring up, and how does the writer respond to
   the feeling behind it?
3. What two things make cutting down on salt easier, according to the column?
4. What does the writer suggest as a first step, and why?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Many salty foods are used, such as soy sauce, miso, pickles and dried fish.
2. That low-salt food doesn't taste good, and that people don't want to live longer if it means
   giving up food they love. The writer understands the feeling: if it were nothing but
   sacrifice (がまんするほかない), it would be hard to keep up.
3. Using flavour from stock, lemon and spices so that food doesn't taste lacking, and the fact
   that our sense of taste gets used to milder food in a few weeks.
4. To start with one meal a day, because you shouldn't try to change everything at once, and you
   won't find what works for you until you actually try ({試|ため}してみないことには).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Japanese food is said to be good for you. It uses plenty of vegetables and fish, and not much
oil. But it has a weak point: salty foods such as soy sauce, miso, pickles and dried fish are
used a great deal. It goes without saying that too much salt raises blood pressure and can easily
lead to illness.

So people are advised to cut down on salt, but many probably feel that food with little salt
doesn't taste good. You also hear people say they don't want to live longer if it means giving up
the things they love. I understand that feeling well. Eating is one of the pleasures of life, and
if it were nothing but putting up with things, it would be hard to keep it up for long.

But cutting down on salt isn't only a sacrifice. If you bring out the flavour of the stock and
make good use of lemon and spices such as ginger, you hardly feel that anything is missing even
with less salt. Our sense of taste also adapts: after a few weeks of milder food, they say, the
old flavours start to taste too strong. Once you're used to it, mild food is also a way of
enjoying the taste of the ingredients themselves.

Of course, less salt is better. But the important thing is not to try to change everything at
once. Until you actually try, you won't find the way that suits you. Why not start with one meal
a day? Not pushing yourself is, in the end, the quickest way there.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{早|はや}く{寝|ね}るに{越|こ}したことはない。
= Of course, it's best to go to bed early.
{食|た}べてみないことには、{分|わ}からない。
= You won't know until you try it.
{今日|きょう}は{待|ま}つほかない。
= There's nothing for it but to wait today.
{言|い}うまでもありません。
= It goes without saying.
{甘|あま}いものは{少|すこ}し{減|へ}らします。
= I'll cut down a little on sweet things.
```

## Common mistakes

- ×{安|やす}いのに{越|こ}したことはない, ×{新鮮|しんせん}なに{越|こ}したことはない. Adjectives and nouns
  join directly: {安|やす}いに, {新鮮|しんせん}に{越|こ}したことはない.
- 〜に{越|こ}したことはない as a direct order. It's a general "it's best to"; to tell someone what
  to do, use 〜ことだ or 〜たほうがいい.
- A positive main clause after ないことには: ×{食|た}べてみないことには、おいしい. The result must be
  negative or blocked: …{分|わ}からない, …{何|なに}も{言|い}えない.
- ×{待|ま}ったほかない. ほかない follows the dictionary form: {待|ま}つほかない.
- 〜までもない for something that does need doing. It means the thing is unnecessary because it's
  obvious or too small: {病院|びょういん}に{行|い}くまでもない (no need to go to hospital).
- {干物|ひもの} for laundry. Laundry is {干|ほ}し{物|もの} or {洗濯物|せんたくもの}; {干物|ひもの} is dried fish.

## Key points

- 〜に{越|こ}したことはない (plain form; nouns and な-adjectives directly): it's best to, of course;
  often "…but".
- 〜ないことには〜ない: unless (A first), nothing (B) happens; a double negative.
- 〜ほかない / 〜よりほかない (dictionary form): no choice but; more serious and written than
  しかない.
- 〜までもない / 〜までもなく: no need to; {言|い}うまでもない (needless to say).
- Review: 〜ことだ (practical advice), 〜べきだ (principle), 〜ものだ (norm).
- New kanji: 皿 卵 塩 甘 辛 濃 薄 菓 乳 栄 養 干 蒸. Write {皿|さら}, {卵|たまご}, {塩|しお}, {甘|あま}い,
  {辛|から}い, {濃|こ}い, {薄|うす}い, お{菓子|かし}, {牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}, {栄養|えいよう}, {干|ほ}す, {蒸|む}す,
  {蒸|む}し{暑|あつ}い with kanji from now on.

lessons.title: Only, the best, as long as: に過ぎない, に限る, 限り
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The last core lesson of the module is about limits: saying that something is "only" this much,
that one thing is the best, that something happens "only when" or "as long as". Two verbs do most
of the work: {過|す}ぎる (go beyond) and {限|かぎ}る (limit).

これは{一|ひと}つの{例|れい}に{過|す}ぎない。 — This is no more than one example.
{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は、{家|いえ}で{本|ほん}を{読|よ}むに{限|かぎ}る。 — On a rainy day, there's nothing like staying in and reading.
{急|いそ}いでいるときに{限|かぎ}って、{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れる。 — The train is always late just when I'm in a hurry.
{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}らない{限|かぎ}り、{試合|しあい}は{行|おこな}われます。 — Unless it rains, the match will go ahead.

The theme is publishing and the written word: newspapers and magazines, books, authors and
editors, printing, parts of speech and chapters, and reviews. N3 had the news and reporting
({記者|きしゃ}, {報道|ほうどう}); N5 and N4 had {雑誌|ざっし} and {文章|ぶんしょう} in kana, which this lesson's
kanji now write.

## No more than, merely: 〜に{過|す}ぎない

〜に{過|す}ぎない says that something is only this much and no more, often to play it down. It's
written and formal; in conversation you'd usually say 〜だけだ.

| Before に{過|す}ぎない | Example |
|---|---|
| noun | {一例|いちれい}に{過|す}ぎない |
| verb, plain form | {言|い}ってみたに{過|す}ぎない |
| い-adjective | {少|すく}ないに{過|す}ぎない (rare) |
| な-adjective + である | {偶然|ぐうぜん}であるに{過|す}ぎない |

この{本|ほん}が{売|う}れたのは、{運|うん}がよかったに{過|す}ぎない。 — This book sold well simply because it was lucky.
{新聞|しんぶん}に{出|で}ているのは、{事件|じけん}のほんの{一部|いちぶ}に{過|す}ぎない。 — What's in the paper is only a tiny part of the incident.
{私|わたし}は{一|いち}{読者|どくしゃ}として{感想|かんそう}を{述|の}べたに{過|す}ぎません。 — I was only giving my impressions as an ordinary reader.

It often comes with ただ, {単|たん}なる (mere), {単|たん}に (merely) or わずか (just): {参加者|さんかしゃ}は
わずか{十人|じゅうにん}に{過|す}ぎなかった (there were only ten participants).

{過|す}ぎない is a negative of {過|す}ぎる "go beyond", so literally "it doesn't go beyond…".
Its kanji is N3's.

## There's nothing like: 〜に{限|かぎ}る

〜に{限|かぎ}る means "the best thing is…, nothing beats…": the speaker's own opinion about what
works best in a situation. It follows a noun or a verb's dictionary or ない form.

{疲|つか}れたときは、{早|はや}く{寝|ね}るに{限|かぎ}る。 — When you're tired, the best thing is an early night.
{夏|なつ}は{冷|つめ}たいそばに{限|かぎ}るね。 — In summer, nothing beats cold soba.
{知|し}らない{人|ひと}からのメールは、{開|ひら}かないに{限|かぎ}る。 — Best not to open emails from people you don't know.

### に{限|かぎ}る and に{越|こ}したことはない

Both mean "it's best to", but in different voices.

| | 〜に{限|かぎ}る | 〜に{越|こ}したことはない (19) |
|---|---|---|
| whose view | the speaker's own, from experience | general, everyone would agree |
| typical follow-up | a firm recommendation | often "…but" |
| feel | "take it from me" | "obviously, of course" |

{旅行|りょこう}は{平日|へいじつ}に{限|かぎ}る。どこも{空|す}いているから。 — The only way to travel is on weekdays: everywhere's empty.
{旅費|りょひ}は{安|やす}いに{越|こ}したことはないが、{安全|あんぜん}も{大事|だいじ}だ。 — Of course cheaper travel is better, but safety matters too.

   うちの{子|こ}に{限|かぎ}って、うそをつくはずがない。 — My child, of all children, would never lie.

## Only (in notices): 〜に{限|かぎ}り

〜に{限|かぎ}り is "only, limited to", the language of notices and offers.

{本日|ほんじつ}に{限|かぎ}り、{全品|ぜんぴん}{二割|にわり}{引|び}きです。 — Today only, everything is 20 per cent off.

complains or trusts ("of all"). And 〜に{限|かぎ}らず (not only, lesson 21) is the opposite of
に{限|かぎ}り.

## As long as, unless, as far as: 〜{限|かぎ}り

{限|かぎ}り after a plain form or noun + の / である sets the limit within which something holds.

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜{限|かぎ}り(は) | as long as | {生|い}きている{限|かぎ}り, {私|わたし}が{社長|しゃちょう}である{限|かぎ}り |
| 〜ない{限|かぎ}り | unless | {本人|ほんにん}が{反対|はんたい}しない{限|かぎ}り |
| 〜{限|かぎ}りでは | as far as (I know, I've seen) | {私|わたし}が{知|し}っている{限|かぎ}りでは |
| できる{限|かぎ}り | as much as possible | できる{限|かぎ}り{早|はや}く |

この{雑誌|ざっし}が{読|よ}まれている{限|かぎ}り、{編集部|へんしゅうぶ}はなくならない。 — As long as this magazine is read, the editorial department won't disappear.

{限|かぎ}り also ends lesson 23's うれしい{限|かぎ}りだ (I couldn't be happier).
