questions.stem: {本文|ほんぶん}を{読|よ}む{前|まえ}に、まず＿＿に{目|め}を{通|とお}しておくと{効率|こうりつ}がいい。
questions.explanation: {設問|せつもん} are the questions set on a passage: reading them first is the strategy of the lesson. {食器|しょっき} (dishes), {名札|なふだ} (name tags) and {底辺|ていへん} (base, bottom) make no sense here.

questions.stem: 「この{仕事|しごと}を{明日|あした}までに{終|お}わらせるのは、{到底|とうてい}{無理|むり}だ。」 Which is closest in meaning?
choices: {明日|あした}までに{終|お}わらせるのは、{少|すこ}し{難|むずか}しい。
{明日|あした}までなら、なんとか{終|お}わる。
{明日|あした}までに{終|お}わるかどうか、まだ{分|わ}からない。
{明日|あした}までに{終|お}わらせることは、まったくできない。
questions.explanation: {到底|とうてい} + negative is "not … at all, utterly impossible". It's far stronger than "a little difficult", and leaves no doubt.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {接|せっ}する correctly?
choices: {子供|こども}に{接|せっ}するときは、{目|め}の{高|たか}さを{合|あ}わせるといい。
{駅|えき}で{友|とも}だちと{接|せっ}して、{一緒|いっしょ}に{帰|かえ}った。
{新|あたら}しいパソコンをインターネットに{接|せっ}した。
{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けて、{部屋|へや}に{風|かぜ}を{接|せっ}した。
questions.explanation: 〜に{接|せっ}する is to deal with people ({客|きゃく}に{接|せっ}する, {子供|こども}に{接|せっ}する). Meeting a friend is {会|あ}う, connecting a computer is {接続|せつぞく}する, and letting in air is {風|かぜ}を{入|い}れる.

questions.stem: {駅|えき}の［改札］で{友|とも}だちを{待|ま}った。 How is the bracketed word read?
questions.explanation: {改札|かいさつ} (ticket gate): 札 is サツ in compounds and ふだ on its own ({名札|なふだ}). 改 is カイ, without voicing.

questions.stem: {落|お}とした{財布|さいふ}を{一日中|いちにちじゅう}［さがした］。 Which kanji is right for a lost thing?
questions.explanation: {捜|さが}す is to look for something or someone lost. 捨 is {捨|す}てる (throw away), 拾 {拾|ひろ}う (pick up) and 接 セツ (contact); all share the hand radical.

questions.stem: {停電|ていでん}は{二時間後|にじかんご}に［復旧］した。 How is the bracketed word read?
questions.explanation: {復旧|ふっきゅう}: フク + キュウ, with the small っ (フク shortens before k). ×ふくきゅう keeps the full sound; ふきゅう is {普及|ふきゅう} (spread), a different word.

questions.stem: Listen to the station announcement. What should passengers do?

audio.text: ただいま、つよいかぜのため、うんてんをみあわせております。おいそぎのかたは、ちかてつをごりようください。

choices: Wait on the platform for the next train.
Go home because the station is closing.
Use the subway if they are in a hurry.
questions.explanation: {運転|うんてん}を{見合|みあ}わせております: services are suspended because of strong wind. お{急|いそ}ぎの{方|かた}は、{地下鉄|ちかてつ}をご{利用|りよう}ください: those in a hurry should use the subway. Nothing about the station closing or tomorrow's tickets.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the man do first?

audio.text: おんな：あ、そのしりょう、いんさつするまえに、さんページめのすうじ、なおしてもらえる？　おとこ：わかりました。じゃあ、なおしてから、いんさつします。

choices: Correct a figure on page three.
questions.explanation: なおしてから、いんさつします: he corrects the figure first, then prints. Booking a room and phoning aren't mentioned in this exchange.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.

audio.text: おそれいりますが、こちらにおなまえをおかきいただけますか。

choices: はい、お{書|か}きになります。
いいえ、どういたしまして。
はい、{書|か}いてさしあげます。
questions.explanation: A polite request to write your name: the natural reply is a simple yes. お{書|か}きになります is honorific about yourself, どういたしまして answers thanks, and {書|か}いてさしあげます offers it as a favour, which is odd for your own name.

questions.stem: Build the sentence from a notice.
questions.prompt: Items handed in are kept at the counter for one week.
questions.explanation: {拾得物|しゅうとくぶつ}は、カウンターで{一週間|いっしゅうかん}{保管|ほかん}いたします. {保管|ほかん}いたします is the humble "we keep". The place and the period can swap. {捨|す}てて (throwing away) is the opposite of keeping.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: Before throwing things away, you can look for someone who will use them.
questions.explanation: {捨|す}てる{前|まえ}に{使|つか}ってくれる{人|ひと}を{探|さが}せばいい (Text 4, opinion B). {探|さが}す is looking for someone you want; {拾|ひろ}う (to pick up) makes no sense with a person here.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and answer the question.

{蔵|くら}の{厚|あつ}いかべは、{火|ひ}に{強|つよ}いだけではない。{外|そと}の{暑|あつ}さや{寒|さむ}さが{中|なか}に{伝|つた}わりにくいため、{一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて{温度|おんど}の{変化|へんか}が{小|ちい}さい。そのため、{酒|さけ}やしょうゆを{作|つく}って{保管|ほかん}する{場所|ばしょ}にも{向|む}いていた。{今|いま}でも{酒|さけ}を{造|つく}る{所|ところ}を「{酒蔵|さかぐら}」と{呼|よ}ぶのは、その{名残|なごり}である。

What does その{名残|なごり} refer to?
choices: That storehouses were built to resist fire.
That the temperature outside is very hot or cold.
That soy sauce is now made in factories.
That storehouses were once used for making and keeping sake.
questions.explanation: その points back to the sentence before: storehouses were suited to making and keeping sake and soy sauce. The name {酒蔵|さかぐら} is a trace ({名残|なごり}) of that use. Fire resistance is a separate point, and factories aren't mentioned.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and choose the word for the gap.

{文字|もじ}だけのやり{取|と}りでは、{言葉|ことば}の{意味|いみ}の{一部|いちぶ}しか{伝|つた}わらない。（　）、{読|よ}む{側|がわ}はその{足|た}りない{部分|ぶぶん}を{自分|じぶん}の{不安|ふあん}で{埋|う}めてしまう。
questions.explanation: The second sentence continues the process: only part gets through, and then the reader fills the gap with anxiety. そして links the two steps. もっとも would add a limit, なお unrelated extra information, and すなわち a restatement of the same thing.

questions.stem: このお{弁当|べんとう}は「{要|よう}___」です。{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}に{入|い}れてください。 Type the two-kanji word (in kanji or kana) that means "refrigeration", as on food labels.
questions.explanation: {要|よう}{冷蔵|れいぞう}: "keep refrigerated" on food labels. {冷蔵|れいぞう} is refrigeration; {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ} is the fridge itself.

questions.stem: How many timed parts does the JLPT N2 have, and how long are they?
choices: Three: vocabulary 30 minutes, grammar and reading 70 minutes, listening 40 minutes.
Two: language knowledge and reading 105 minutes, listening 50 minutes.
Two: language knowledge 60 minutes, reading and listening 90 minutes.
questions.explanation: N2 has two timed parts: vocabulary, grammar and reading together (105 minutes), then listening (50 minutes). Three parts with separate vocabulary is N3's structure.

questions.stem: A candidate scores 50 in language knowledge, 45 in reading and 17 in listening: 112 of 180. What is the result?
choices: Fail: listening is below the sectional pass mark of 19.
questions.explanation: You need 90 of 180 overall and at least 19 in each of the three sections. Listening at 17 is below the {基準点|きじゅんてん}, so the result is a fail, whatever the total.

questions.stem: Which task type is NOT part of the N2 listening section?
questions.explanation: Verbal expressions (choosing what to say in a pictured situation) belongs to N3 and below. N2 listening has task-based comprehension, key points, general outline, quick response and integrated comprehension.

questions.stem: You have two minutes left in the first part and three questions unanswered. What is the best thing to do?
choices: Fill in an answer for every question.
Leave them blank to avoid losing points.
Go back and check your vocabulary answers.
questions.explanation: There's no penalty for a wrong answer, so never leave a blank: mark your best guess for every question. Listening can't be started early.

questions.stem: {雨|あめ}___、{試合|しあい}は{予定|よてい}どおり{行|おこな}われた。 (Despite the rain, the match went ahead as planned.)
questions.explanation: 〜にもかかわらず is "despite (a fact)": it rained, and yet. 〜にかかわらず and 〜を{問|と}わず mean "regardless of (any case)" and need a range ({天気|てんき}にかかわらず), and 〜に{限|かぎ}らず is "not only".

questions.stem: {一度|いちど}{約束|やくそく}した___、{最後|さいご}までやるつもりだ。
questions.explanation: 〜からには: "now that (I've promised), I will…", followed by a resolve. 〜ばかりに gives a cause with a regretted result, くせに blames, and とたんに is "the moment that".

questions.stem: こんな{難|むずか}しい{問題|もんだい}、{一日|いちにち}で{解|と}け___よ。 (casual: no way I can solve…)
questions.explanation: 〜っこない (casual) is "no way it'll happen": {解|と}けっこない. かねない is "might (lead to something bad)", ざるを{得|え}ない "have no choice but", and ないことはない "it's not impossible", the opposite.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {占|し}める correctly?
choices: {寒|さむ}いので、{窓|まど}を{占|し}めてください。
ネクタイを{占|し}めて{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}く。
{店|みせ}は{夜|よる}{九時|くじ}に{占|し}める。
{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}が{町|まち}の{人口|じんこう}の{半分|はんぶん}{近|ちか}くを{占|し}めている。
questions.explanation: {占|し}める is to occupy or make up a share: {人口|じんこう}の{半分|はんぶん}{近|ちか}くを{占|し}める. Closing a window or a shop is {閉|し}める, and putting on a tie is ネクタイをしめる (another kanji): same sound, different words.

questions.stem: {冬|ふゆ}は___コートが{欠|か}かせない。
questions.explanation: A coat that keeps you warm is {厚|あつ}い (thick). {浅|あさ}い is shallow, {硬|かた}い hard (of materials), and {奥|おく}の (at the back) doesn't describe a coat.

questions.stem: {自動販売機|じどうはんばいき}に［硬貨］を{入|い}れた。 How is the bracketed word read?
questions.explanation: {硬貨|こうか} (a coin): 硬 is コウ (its kun'yomi かた(い) is for {硬|かた}い) and 貨 is カ, as in {貨物|かもつ}. It sounds like {効果|こうか} (effect).

questions.stem: {猫|ねこ}が［いっぴき］{庭|にわ}に{入|はい}ってきた。 Which is right for the bracketed word?
questions.explanation: {一匹|いっぴき}: 〜{匹|ひき} counts small animals; after いち it becomes いっぴき. 四 (four), 比 (compare) and 引 (pull) look or sound a little alike but aren't counters.

questions.stem: {留学|りゅうがく}して、{聞|き}く{力|ちから}がぐんと［伸］びた。 How is the bracketed kanji read?
questions.explanation: {伸|の}びた: {伸|の}びる, to grow, improve. シン is its on'yomi ({追伸|ついしん}, P.S.); with okurigana びる it's の.

questions.stem: Listen. Why did the woman run out of time?

audio.text: おとこ：どっかい、どうだった？　おんな：さいごのちょうぶん、ぜんぜんじかんたりなかった。じょうほうをさがすもんだいを、さきにやればよかったよ。

choices: She started with the long passage and didn't reach the end.
She spent too long on the vocabulary section.
She arrived late for the test.
She did the tasks in order and the last long passage took too long.
questions.explanation: She ran out of time on the last long passage and regrets not doing the information-retrieval task first (〜ばよかった): she did them in order. Vocabulary and arriving late aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the man advise?

audio.text: さいごのごふんは、みなおしにつかったほうがいいよ。わからないもんだいも、かならずなにかえらんでおいてね。

choices: Skip the questions you don't know.
Use the last five minutes to check and answer every question.
Finish five minutes early and leave.
Spend the last five minutes on the long essay.
questions.explanation: {見直|みなお}しに{使|つか}ったほうがいい: use the last five minutes for checking; and choose something even for questions you don't know (かならずなにかえらんで). That's the opposite of skipping.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.

audio.text: しけん、おつかれさま。けっか、いつわかるんだっけ？

choices: うん、{疲|つか}れたから{帰|かえ}るね。
{一月|いちがつ}の{終|お}わりごろだったと{思|おも}うよ。
{試験|しけん}は{十二月|じゅうにがつ}だよ。
うん、{結果|けっか}はよかったよ。
questions.explanation: The question is when the results come out (いつ{分|わ}かる): around the end of January. The first reply answers only おつかれさま, the third gives the test date, and the fourth claims a result that isn't known yet.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: What matters is building up small efforts.
questions.explanation: {小|ちい}さな{努力|どりょく}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねることが{大切|たいせつ}だ. 〜ことが{大切|たいせつ}だ: "what matters is …". {丸暗記|まるあんき} (rote learning) has no place in the sentence.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: A cat is sleeping at the back of the garden.
questions.explanation: {猫|ねこ}が{一匹|いっぴき}、{庭|にわ}の{奥|おく}で{寝|ね}ている. 〜{匹|ひき} counts animals; 〜{枚|まい} counts flat things. The place phrase can also come first.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and answer the question.

N2に{合格|ごうかく}したとき、{私|わたし}は{気|き}づいた。{新聞|しんぶん}の{社説|しゃせつ}はまだ{辞書|じしょ}なしでは{読|よ}めないし、{会議|かいぎ}ではまだ{半分|はんぶん}しか{話|はなし}についていけない。N2は{終|お}わりではなく、{入|い}り{口|ぐち}だったのだ。それからは、{机|つくえ}の{前|まえ}で{勉強|べんきょう}する{時間|じかん}を{減|へ}らし、{好|す}きな{小説|しょうせつ}を{毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}しずつ{読|よ}むことにした。

What did the writer realize after passing N2?
choices: That N2 was the highest level worth taking.
That there was still a long way to go.
That newspapers are easier than novels.
That studying at a desk is the only way to improve.
questions.explanation: N2は{終|お}わりではなく、{入|い}り{口|ぐち}だった: N2 was an entrance, not the end; the writer still couldn't read editorials without a dictionary or follow meetings. The writer then studied less at a desk, the opposite of the last choice. ({社説|しゃせつ} = an editorial.)

questions.stem:
Read the passage and choose the word for the gap.

{合計|ごうけい}{点|てん}が{九十点|きゅうじゅってん}を{超|こ}えれば、{基本的|きほんてき}には{合格|ごうかく}である。（　）、{一|ひと}つでも{基準点|きじゅんてん}に{届|とど}かない{科目|かもく}があれば、{不合格|ふごうかく}となる。
questions.explanation: The second sentence is an exception to the first: you pass with 90, except when a section is below its minimum. ただし introduces it. したがって would make failing a result of passing, なお adds unrelated information, and つまり restates.

questions.stem: On the JLPT N2, each of the three scoring sections is marked out of 60. What is the overall pass mark out of 180? Type the number.
questions.explanation: The pass mark is 90 of 180, with at least 19 in each section (N3's pass mark is 95).

questions.stem: In part 1, why does Haruto go into the storehouse?
choices: To look for his grandmother's will.
To clear it out before the house is sold.
To find the old doll set for the Doll Festival.
To take photos for a book he is editing.
questions.explanation: His aunt says the house will be let go ({手放|てばな}す) by spring and the storehouse must be cleared before it's sold. The doll box is something he finds; a will and a book are never mentioned.

questions.stem: What is unusual about the letters in the box?
choices: They are addressed to Haruto's grandmother.
They were all sent from Tokyo.
They have no stamps or postmarks and are all dated 3 March.
They are written in Haruto's aunt's handwriting.
questions.explanation: どのふうとうにも{切手|きって}がなく、{消印|けしいん}もない…すべての{日付|ひづけ}が{三月|さんがつ}{三日|みっか}だった: never posted, all dated the same day. They are addressed to {千代|ちよ}, in the grandfather's hand ({筆跡|ひっせき}).

questions.stem: What does Haruto first fear when he sees the name {千代|ちよ}?
choices: That his grandfather had a secret lover.
That the letters belong to a stranger.
That the letters are about money.
questions.explanation: {祖父|そふ}には、{祖母|そぼ}に{言|い}えない{相手|あいて}がいたのではないか: he fears a secret relationship. The first letter, about plum blossom and schoolchildren, makes him doubt it ({恋人|こいびと}への{手紙|てがみ}にしては、みょうな{書|か}き{方|かた}).

questions.stem: What clue does the aunt remember in part 3?
choices: Her father went out alone early every Doll Festival morning, and the doll set was never displayed.
Her mother often spoke of a girl called Chiyo.
A pupil called Chiyo used to visit the house.
Her father kept the storehouse locked on 3 March.
questions.explanation: ひなまつりの{日|ひ}だけは…{朝早|あさはや}く{一人|ひとり}で{出|で}かけていた, and the dolls she thought were hers were never displayed ({一度|いちど}もかざってもらったことがない). Her parents never mentioned Chiyo, and nothing is said of a pupil or a lock.

questions.stem: What does the temple's register show?
choices: Chiyo was a pupil who moved away.
Chiyo was the grandfather's first child, who died aged three on 3 March.
Chiyo was the head priest's mother.
questions.explanation: {三歳|さんさい}で{亡|な}くなっています。{六十五年前|ろくじゅうごねんまえ}の、{三月|さんがつ}{三日|みっか}です…{先生|せんせい}の、{最初|さいしょ}のお{子|こ}さんですよ. The letters were written every year on the anniversary of her death ({命日|めいにち}), which is also the Doll Festival.

questions.stem: Why, according to Haruto's guess, did his grandparents never speak of Chiyo?
choices: The priest asked them not to.
They wanted to keep the sorrow from the child born after her.
questions.explanation: {生|う}まれてくる{子|こ}に{悲|かな}しみを{背負|せお}わせまいと: so as not to make the child who would be born (the aunt) carry the sorrow. 〜まいと is lesson 18's まい ("so as not to").

questions.stem: What is the last letter in the box, and what does it reveal?
choices: A letter from Chiyo's teacher, thanking the family.
A letter from the aunt, written as a child.
A letter from the grandfather to the grandmother.
A letter from the grandmother, showing she had known about the letters all along.
questions.explanation: The round, small hand is the grandmother's: {毎年|まいとし}こっそり{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}いていたこと、お{母|かあ}さんはずっと{知|し}っていましたよ. She pretended not to know ({知|し}らぬふり) because she thought the letters comforted him.

questions.stem: {何十回|なんじゅっかい}もここに{来|き}ている___、よしえはそれがだれのものなのか{考|かんが}えたこともなかった。 Choose the form the story uses.
questions.explanation: 〜にもかかわらず: despite having come dozens of times, she had never wondered. からには ("now that") and ばかりに ("just because, with a bad result") give reasons, and うちに ("while") changes the meaning.

questions.stem: Listen to the aunt. How does she feel?

audio.text: おねえさんがいたなんてね。あってみたかったなあ。けんかもしたかもしれないけど。

choices: Wistful that she never met her sister.
Glad that she had no sister.
questions.explanation: 〜なんて expresses surprise, and {会|あ}ってみたかったなあ a gentle regret: she wishes she had met her sister, imagining even their quarrels. Nothing angry, afraid or glad.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the grandfather do every year?

audio.text: せんせいは、まいとしひなまつりのあさになると、しろいうめのえだをいっぽんもって、はかにきていました。

choices: He visited the school on the morning of the Doll Festival.
He planted a plum tree every spring.
He brought one white plum branch to the grave on Doll Festival morning.
He gave plum branches to his pupils.
questions.explanation: Every year on the morning of ひなまつり he came to the grave (はかにきていました) with one white plum branch. The school, planting and pupils aren't in the sentence.

questions.stem: Why does Haruto smile as he writes his own letter?
choices: He realizes that Chiyo was another aunt of his.
He remembers a joke his grandfather told.
He has finished his work for the publisher.
He thinks his handwriting is better than his grandmother's.
questions.explanation: {自分|じぶん}にもおばがもう{一人|ひとり}いたのだ: Chiyo, his mother's eldest sister, is another aunt he never knew. The other reasons aren't in the text.

questions.stem: What does "{一度|いちど}も{出|だ}されることのない、けれど{確|たし}かに{届|とど}いている{手紙|てがみ}" (the story's last line) suggest?
choices: The letters will finally be posted.
The letters were lost in the post.
Nobody will read the letters again.
The letters are never sent, yet their love reaches the one they're written to.
questions.explanation: The letters are never posted ({出|だ}されることのない), but in another sense they arrive: the feeling reaches Chiyo, and now reaches the family. The family plans to keep writing, so they will be read again.

questions.stem: In an 800-character {小論文|しょうろんぶん}, where should your answer to the question (your claim) first appear?
choices: In the middle of the main body.
questions.explanation: State your position in the じょろん, clearly and once; repeat it in other words in the {結論|けつろん}. A {小論文|しょうろんぶん} isn't a mystery story.

questions.stem: Where does the counter-view belong in the three-part plan?
choices: In the conclusion, as the final word.
In the main body ({本論|ほんろん}), introduced with {確|たし}かに and answered with しかし.
questions.explanation: The counter-view goes in the {本論|ほんろん}: {確|たし}かに〜。しかし〜. Leaving it out looks one-sided; ending on it would change sides.

questions.stem: Why does the lesson suggest the three-part plan rather than {起承転結|きしょうてんけつ} for an argument?
choices: The {転|てん} brings in something unexpected, which suits stories better than arguments (though teachers differ).
{起承転結|きしょうてんけつ} is too short for 800 characters.
{起承転結|きしょうてんけつ} is only used in poetry.
Exam markers forbid {起承転結|きしょうてんけつ}.
questions.explanation: The {転|てん} (turn) introduces a twist, exactly what a story needs and an argument shouldn't do. The lesson hedges: some teachers still recommend it. Nothing forbids it.

questions.stem: Which sentence is in the right style for a {小論文|しょうろんぶん}?
choices: スマートフォンはすごく{便利|べんり}だと{思|おも}います。
スマートフォンはめっちゃ{便利|べんり}じゃん。
スマートフォンは{非常|ひじょう}に{便利|べんり}な{道具|どうぐ}である。
スマートフォンって、{便利|べんり}ですよね。
questions.explanation: The である style with a written intensifier ({非常|ひじょう}に) is right. The others use です / ます or casual speech (すごく, めっちゃ, じゃん, って, よね).

questions.stem: The model essay's conclusion begins 「{以上|いじょう}のように」. What does this phrase do?
choices: It asks the reader a question.
It sums up what has been argued above.
questions.explanation: {以上|いじょう}のように = "as shown above": the standard way to open a conclusion by summing up. New reasons don't belong in a conclusion.

questions.stem: Which is the best use of the last five minutes?
choices: Adding a new argument at the end.
Rewriting the essay in です / ます.
すいこう: rereading, fixing sentence endings and checking the length.
questions.explanation: すいこう (polishing) is rereading and correcting: varying the {文末|ぶんまつ}, fixing mistakes, checking the character count. Switching to です / ます would break the style.

questions.stem: {持|も}たせなければ{問題|もんだい}が{起|お}きない___。 (from the model essay: "It's not as if not giving them one means no problems arise.")
questions.explanation: 〜ば…というものではない rejects a too-simple rule (lesson 28). というものだ would assert it, にほかならない identifies something precisely, and にすぎない ("no more than") doesn't follow {起|お}きない like this.

questions.stem: Listen to the teacher. What does she advise?

audio.text: ぶんまつがぜんぶ、とおもう、だと、じしんがないようにみえます。いろいろなかたちをつかいましょう。

choices: End every sentence with と{思|おも}う to sound polite.
Vary the sentence endings, because all と{思|おも}う looks unsure.
questions.explanation: If every {文末|ぶんまつ} is 〜と{思|おも}う, the writing looks unsure of itself ({自信|じしん}がない); use various forms. Nothing about length or feelings.

questions.stem: Listen. How should the essay be planned?

audio.text: かきはじめるまえに、しゅちょう、りゆうふたつ、はんたいのいけん、けつろんを、よんぎょうでメモしておきましょう。

choices: Note the claim, two reasons, the opposing view and the conclusion in four lines first.
Start writing at once and plan as you go.
Write the conclusion first and stop there.
questions.explanation: Before writing, note in four lines: the claim ({主張|しゅちょう}), two reasons, the opposing view and the conclusion. That's step 3 of "How to write one".

questions.stem:
Read the paragraph from a student's essay and answer the question.

{確|たし}かに、スマートフォンを{使|つか}いすぎると{視力|しりょく}が{落|お}ちるという{心配|しんぱい}はある。しかし、それはスマートフォンそのものの{問題|もんだい}というより、{使|つか}い{方|かた}の{問題|もんだい}である。{夜|よる}は{居間|いま}に{置|お}くといったルールがあれば、{危険|きけん}はかなり{減|へ}らせるはずだ。

What does this paragraph do in the essay?
choices: It states the writer's claim for the first time.
It admits a counter-view and answers it.
It gives an example from the writer's childhood.
questions.explanation: {確|たし}かに introduces the other side (worries about eyesight) and しかし answers it (it's a matter of how phones are used). That's the counter-view part of the {本論|ほんろん}.

questions.stem:
Read the conclusion and choose the word for the gap.

{以上|いじょう}のように、{私|わたし}は{子供|こども}にスマートフォンを{持|も}たせることに{賛成|さんせい}である。（　）、{大切|たいせつ}なのは{持|も}たせることではなく、{持|も}たせた{後|あと}に{大人|おとな}が{関心|かんしん}を{持|も}ち{続|つづ}けることだ。
questions.explanation: The writer keeps the claim but adds a condition that limits it: ただし. なぜなら would give a reason, たとえば an example and その{上|うえ} an extra point in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which word means the main body of an essay?
questions.explanation: {本論|ほんろん} is the main body: reasons, examples and the counter-view. じょろん is the introduction, {結論|けつろん} the conclusion, and {文末|ぶんまつ} the end of a sentence.

glossary.definition: A short word in hiragana that follows a word or a clause and shows its job in the sentence: は (topic), が (subject), を (object), に, で, と, も, か, ね, よ… Particles do much of the work that word order and prepositions do in English.

A particle made of several words that works as one unit, often a particle plus a verb form: について, に{対|たい}して, にもかかわらず, に{際|さい}して. Many belong to writing. This course writes some in kanji ({基|もと}づいて, {限|かぎ}らず) and some in kana (にもかかわらず, をめぐって); the module 1 reference sheet lists them.

Characters taken from Chinese that carry a meaning as well as a sound. Japanese writes most nouns and the stems of verbs and adjectives in kanji and the grammar in kana: {雇用|こよう}, {雇|やと}う. This course writes a word in kanji when all its kanji are on the N5, N4, N3 and N2 lists (1,039 in all).
Small kana printed over kanji to show how they are read: {賃金|ちんぎん}. This course puts furigana on every kanji except the one a question is testing, and you can switch them off.
A kanji reading that comes from the Chinese pronunciation it was borrowed with, used mostly in words of two or more kanji: 雇 is コ in {雇用|こよう}. Kanji tables write on'yomi in katakana.
A kanji reading that is a native Japanese word, often used for a kanji on its own or with okurigana: 雇 read やと in {雇|やと}う, 岩 read いわ. Kanji tables write kun'yomi in hiragana.
The kana written after a kanji to finish a word, usually the part that changes when it conjugates: the う of {雇|やと}う, the しい of {激|はげ}しい. Kanji tables show them in brackets: はげ(しい).

The unit of timing in Japanese, one beat. Each kana is a mora; small ゃ, ゅ, ょ belong to the kana before them; っ, ん and the second half of a long vowel count on their own. {賃金|ちんぎん} has four (ち・ん・ぎ・ん). Pitch accent is counted in morae.

The pattern of high and low pitch on the morae of a word. In standard (Tokyo) Japanese a word is marked by the mora after which the pitch falls, or 0 if it never falls: {賃金|ちんぎん:1}, {雇用|こよう:0}. Some words differ only in accent: {肩|かた:1} (shoulder) and [かた:2] (person, polite).
An adjective that ends in い and conjugates by itself: {激|はげ}しい, {激|はげ}しくない, {激|はげ}しかった, {激|はげ}しくて. It goes straight before a noun: {激|はげ}しい{雨|あめ}.
An adjective that takes な before a noun ({頑固|がんこ}な{人|ひと}) and conjugates with だ / です like a noun: {頑固|がんこ}だ, {頑固|がんこ}ではない. In written style it takes である: {頑固|がんこ}である.
The form a verb or adjective has in a dictionary: {雇|やと}う, {与|あた}える, する, {激|はげ}しい. It is also the plain non-past form used before nouns and many patterns.
The part of a verb before ます: {雇|やと}い ({雇|やと}います), {与|あた}え ({与|あた}えます), し (します). Many patterns attach to it: 〜ながら, 〜つつ, 〜{次第|しだい}, 〜がたい. In writing it can also join two clauses, like the て form.
The verb or adjective form ending in て or で: {雇|やと}って, {与|あた}えて, して, {激|はげ}しくて. It joins clauses ("and", "so") and comes before auxiliary verbs (〜ている, 〜てしまう).
The plain negative: {雇|やと}わない, {与|あた}えない, しない, {来|こ}ない. Patterns such as 〜ないこともない and 〜ないとも{限|かぎ}らない are built on it.
The plain past form, ending in た or だ: {雇|やと}った, {与|あた}えた, した, {激|はげ}しかった. Many patterns use it: 〜たものの, 〜たかと{思|おも}うと.
A written negative that ends in ず: {言|い}わず (without saying), {雇|やと}わず. する becomes せず and {来|く}る becomes {来|こ}ず. It appears in 〜ずに (without doing) and in set phrases; lesson 26 adds the related 〜ぬ.

The forms without です / ます: {雇|やと}う, {雇|やと}わない, {雇|やと}った, {雇|やと}わなかった; {高|たか}い; {静|しず}かだ; {学生|がくせい}だ. They are used in casual speech, in だ / である writing, and inside longer sentences before most patterns, even in polite speech.
The forms with です and ます: {雇|やと}います, {雇|やと}いません, {雇|やと}いました, {高|たか}いです. The everyday polite style between adults who aren't close, and of letters, notices and speeches.

A verb whose stem ends in a consonant, so its last kana changes row through the forms: {雇|やと}う → {雇|やと}わない, {雇|やと}います, {雇|やと}って. Some verbs ending in いる or える belong here and look like group 2: {張|は}り{切|き}る, {限|かぎ}る, {減|へ}る, {走|はし}る.
A verb ending in る after an い- or え-row sound that drops る in every form: {与|あた}える → {与|あた}えない, {与|あた}えます, {与|あた}えて; {離|はな}れる → {離|はな}れない.
The two irregular verbs する and {来|く}る, and the many nouns that become verbs with する: {専念|せんねん}する, {感激|かんげき}する. The potential of a する verb is できる: {専念|せんねん}できる.
The form that says someone can do something: {雇|やと}える (can hire), {与|あた}えられる, できる, {来|こ}られる. It conjugates like a group 2 verb.
The form for "let's" and "I'll": {雇|やと}おう, {与|あた}えよう, しよう, {来|こ}よう. With とする it means "try to"; with と{思|おも}う, "I'm thinking of".
A form that sets a condition, "if": the ば form ({雇|やと}えば, {高|たか}ければ), and also たら, と and なら. Each has its own uses; the ば form is the drill form called "conditional".

The form that makes the subject the one something is done to: {雇|やと}われる (be hired), {認|みと}められる (be recognized). Group 1 moves the last kana to the あ row and adds れる ({雇|やと}う → {雇|やと}われる); group 2 adds られる; される, {来|こ}られる. It also expresses suffering something ({雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}られた) and, in formal writing, respect.
The form for "make or let someone do": {悩|なや}ませる (cause someone to worry), {驚|おどろ}かせる, させる. Group 1 moves the last kana to the あ row and adds せる ({悩|なや}む → {悩|なや}ませる); group 2 adds させる.
A verb that acts on an object marked with を: {離|はな}す (let go of something), {傷|きず}つける (hurt someone). Many come in pairs with an intransitive verb: {離|はな}す / {離|はな}れる.
A verb with no object: something happens or someone moves by itself. {離|はな}れる (move away), {傷|きず}つく (be hurt), {刺|さ}さる (stick in).
A verb that follows another verb's て form and adds a meaning instead of its own: 〜ている, 〜てしまう, 〜ておく, 〜ていく, 〜てくる, 〜てもらう. This course writes them in kana.

A clause or adjective placed before a noun to describe it, in the plain form: {昨日|きのう}{雇|やと}われた{人|ひと} (the person hired yesterday). な-adjectives take な and nouns take の; in writing, である also appears before some formal nouns.
A word that turns a clause into a noun so it can take particles: の and こと. {働|はたら}くのが{好|す}きだ, {話|はな}すことができる.
A noun that has little meaning of its own and is used to build grammar: こと, もの, ところ, わけ, はず, ため, よう. This course writes them in kana. Many N2 patterns are made from them: 〜ものの, 〜というわけではない, 〜ないこともない.

The plain style of articles, essays and reports, with だ or である instead of です / ます and many patterns that are rare in conversation (〜ものの, 〜にもかかわらず, 〜つつ). Careful writers keep one style in a text and don't mix it with です / ます.

The system of polite language: the polite form (です / ます), honorific language that raises the person you talk about, and humble language that lowers yourself or your side. Business, shops and formal letters use all three.
Keigo that raises the person who does the action: いらっしゃる, おっしゃる, お〜になる, 〜られる. You use it for customers, superiors and others you show respect to, never for yourself.
Keigo that lowers yourself or your side to show respect to the other person: {伺|うかが}う, {申|もう}し{上|あ}げる, いたす, お〜する. It is used for your own actions, never for the listener's.

Granting that something is true and then saying something that goes against it: "although", "granted that", "even so". Japanese has many concessive patterns that differ in style and feeling: のに, けれども, 〜ものの, 〜とはいえ, 〜にもかかわらず, 〜ながらも, 〜つつも (lessons 1 and 2).

Setting two things, or two sides of one thing, against each other: "on the other hand", "whereas". 〜{一方|いっぽう}で contrasts two things or sides, 〜{反面|はんめん} the good and bad sides of one thing (lesson 3).

Denying the whole rather than every part: "not all", "not always", "not exactly". {全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かるわけではない (I don't understand all of it), {必|かなら}ずしも〜とは{限|かぎ}らない (not necessarily). Lesson 5 compares how strong each pattern is.

Softening a statement so it is less direct or less absolute: "it's not that…", "I wouldn't say no", "it could happen". Japanese hedges a great deal, in speech and in essays: 〜というわけではない, 〜ないこともない, 〜とも{言|い}える, 〜{気|き}がしないでもない (lesson 5).

A word or pattern that places one event in time against another: before it ({前|まえ}に, に{先立|さきだ}って), at it (とき, に{際|さい}して, にあたって), after it (てから, た{上|うえ}で, {次第|しだい}, た{末|すえ}に), or across a span ({間|あいだ}, {以来|いらい}, にわたって, を{通|つう}じて). At N2 many of them are formal and live in speeches, notices and writing.

The grammatical way of presenting an event as under way, not finished. Everyday Japanese uses 〜ている ({雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っている) or 〜てきている for a gradual change; written Japanese has 〜つつある for a change in progress ({人口|じんこう}が{減|へ}りつつある: the population is in the process of falling). つつある goes with verbs of change, not with ordinary actions.
glossary.topic: つつ and つつある

glossary.definition: Two actions done at the same time by the same person: N4's 〜ながら ({歩|ある}きながら{話|はな}す) and its written partner 〜つつ ({考|かんが}えつつ{歩|ある}く). For two different people at the same time, Japanese uses 〜{間|あいだ}(に) instead.
glossary.topic: つつ and つつある

glossary.definition: The event that sets off a change or a new start: きっかけ. 〜をきっかけに(して) names it ({留学|りゅうがく}をきっかけに{料理|りょうり}を{始|はじ}めた: studying abroad got me into cooking); the formal 〜を{機|き}に presents it as a chance someone chose to take ({退職|たいしょく}を{機|き}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}した).

What a statement, a decision or an action rests on: the fact, rule or data that justifies it. N2 has patterns for several kinds of grounds: a fact that commits you (〜からには, 〜{以上|いじょう}, lesson 11), a standard you follow (〜に{基|もと}づいて), a source you build on (〜をもとに), a plan you keep to (〜にそって) and something you vary with (〜に{応|おう}じて), lesson 13.

A word or pattern that gives the cause or reason for what follows. Everyday Japanese uses から and ので; N3 added ため, おかげで, せいで and ことから; N2 adds causes with a colour (〜ばかりに: a bad result; 〜だけに: all the more; 〜ものだから: an excuse, lesson 12) and the formal causes of notices and news (〜につき, 〜により, 〜ため, 〜とあって, 〜ゆえ, lesson 15).

The fixed written style of signs, notices and announcements: short sentences or bare nouns ({本日|ほんじつ}{休館|きゅうかん}), formal causes (〜につき, 〜のため), humble forms for what the organization does (いたします, ございます), honorific requests for the reader (ご{注意|ちゅうい}ください, ごえんりょください, ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください), rules with 〜こと, and markers such as 〜{禁止|きんし}, 〜{可|か} / 〜{不可|ふか} and 〜{中|ちゅう}. Lesson 15 and the "Notice language" sheet.

The level of language used for official, public and written situations: notices, news, business letters, speeches, reports. It prefers kango ({使用|しよう} for {使|つか}う, {清掃|せいそう} for {掃除|そうじ}), formal patterns (〜により rather than 〜で, 〜{以上|いじょう} rather than 〜んだから) and keigo, and avoids contractions. Many N2 patterns live only in the formal register; lessons say which.

The part of a sentence that shows the speaker's attitude to what is said: how likely, necessary or desirable it is, rather than the bare facts. Japanese marks it mostly at the end of the sentence: かもしれない, はずだ, に{違|ちが}いない (how sure), べきだ, なければならない, ざるを{得|え}ない (how necessary), に{越|こ}したことはない, に{限|かぎ}る (how desirable).

Whether something can happen or be the case, as opposed to whether someone is able to do it (ability, the potential form). Japanese has graded expressions: 〜{得|う}る / 〜{得|え}ない (possible in principle, written), 〜かもしれない (maybe), 〜かねない and 〜おそれがある (a real risk of something bad), 〜っこない and 〜はずがない (no way).

What someone must do. Japanese distinguishes where the pressure comes from: 〜なければならない (neutral necessity), 〜しかない / 〜ほかない (the only option left), 〜ざるを{得|え}ない (forced by circumstances, against one's wishes), 〜ないわけにはいかない (a social or moral duty), 〜ことだ / 〜べきだ (advice and principle).

Two negatives that combine into a positive, usually a strong "must": 〜ないわけにはいかない (can't not, so must), 〜ざるを{得|え}ない (ざる is a classical negative + {得|え}ない), 〜ないことには〜ない (without A, no B), 〜ないこともない (it's not that I don't). In Japanese they are normal grammar, not a mistake.

Saying no without a bare いいえ, as business Japanese does: an apology ({申|もう}しわけございません, あいにく), a reason (〜ておりまして), a softened refusal (〜かねます, お〜いたしかねます, {今回|こんかい}は{見送|みおく}らせていただきます) and often an alternative. {検討|けんとう}させていただきます can itself be a polite no.

How far a statement reaches: whether it covers only one case or more. Japanese widens scope with patterns such as 〜はもとより (not to mention), 〜のみならず (not only), 〜を{問|と}わず and 〜にかかわらず (regardless of) and 〜に{限|かぎ}らず (not just), and narrows it with だけ, のみ and 〜に{限|かぎ}る.

A pattern whose job is to make a statement stronger: "unbearably", "can't help it", "can't fail to". In Japanese, 〜てたまらない, 〜てならない, 〜てしょうがない, 〜ないではいられない / 〜ずにはいられない and 〜ずにはおかない. Most describe the speaker's own feelings or actions.

A sentence or pattern that expresses the speaker's surprise, admiration, joy or regret rather than adding information: "how quickly they grow!", "to my surprise", "I couldn't be happier". Japanese uses 〜ものがある, 〜ことに, 〜{限|かぎ}りだ, どれだけ〜ことか, 〜ものだ and 〜といったらない.

Information the speaker got from someone else rather than knows first-hand. Japanese marks it with endings such as 〜そうだ, 〜らしい, 〜ということだ, 〜とのことだ, 〜とか, 〜という{話|はなし}だ, and in news and writing 〜とみられる and 〜とされる; they differ in how sure and how formal they are.

How something looks or seems, or what it resembles. Japanese has many patterns for it: 〜ようだ, 〜みたい, 〜そうだ (looks as if), 〜らしい, 〜っぽい, 〜かのように (as if, though it isn't so), adjective stem + げ (looking…) and 〜ぶり (the way someone does something).

Words that imitate sounds or paint a state, such as ざあざあ (pouring rain) and ぴかぴか (gleaming). Japanese has very many of them, used as adverbs (often with と), with する, or with の / に / だ. They divide into giongo, which imitate sounds, and gitaigo, which describe states, movements and feelings.
Onomatopoeia that imitate real sounds: ざあざあ (pouring rain), ごろごろ (thunder), ごしごし (scrubbing), ワンワン (a dog barking). Animal and human voices are sometimes put in a group of their own, ぎせいご.
Onomatopoeia for things that make no sound: states (ぴかぴか, つるつる, ふわふわ), manners of movement (ぶらぶら, のんびり) and feelings (わくわく, いらいら, そわそわ). Some writers call the feeling words ぎじょうご.

The negative ending of classical Japanese, ぬ, added to the ない stem like ない: {知|し}らぬ, {行|い}かぬ; する → せぬ, {来|く}る → {来|こ}ぬ. Today it survives mostly before nouns ({知|し}らぬ{間|ま}に, {見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}, {予期|よき}せぬ) and in set phrases and old texts. The polite ません and the dialect 〜ん ({分|わ}からん) come from it. It isn't a drill form.

A form inherited from classical Japanese that modern writing still uses for a formal or old-fashioned effect: ぬ (not), 〜ねば (if not), 〜まい (won't), 〜べく (in order to), であろう, なかろう, ゆえに. Recognize them in essays and editorials; in your own writing use them sparingly.

Making words by joining parts: a prefix ({無|む} + {関心|かんしん} → {無関心|むかんしん}), a suffix ({高齢|こうれい} + {化|か} → {高齢化|こうれいか}) or two words ({中心|ちゅうしん} + {部|ぶ}). It is also a JLPT N2 question type: a word with a gap, and four prefixes or suffixes to choose from.

A part attached to the front of a word to change its meaning: {不|ふ}〜, {無|む}〜, {非|ひ}〜, {未|み}〜 (negatives), {再|さい}〜 (again), {超|ちょう}〜, {反|はん}〜, {副|ふく}〜, {諸|しょ}〜, {各|かく}〜, {旧|きゅう}〜, {総|そう}〜, {高|こう}〜 / {低|てい}〜, {半|はん}〜. Most are kango and attach to kango.

A part attached to the end of a word: 〜{化|か} (‑ization), 〜{性|せい} (‑ness), 〜{的|てき} (makes a な-adjective), 〜{感|かん}, 〜{力|りょく}, 〜{率|りつ}, 〜{界|かい}, 〜{型|がた}, 〜{式|しき}, 〜{層|そう}, 〜{観|かん}, 〜{制|せい}, 〜{面|めん}, 〜{上|じょう}; money words 〜{費|ひ}, 〜{料|りょう}, 〜{代|だい}, 〜{賃|ちん}; people words 〜{家|か}, 〜{者|しゃ}, 〜{員|いん}, 〜{派|は}.
A word built from on'yomi, originally from Chinese or made in Japan on the Chinese model: {状態|じょうたい}, {福祉|ふくし}, {完了|かんりょう}. Kango dominate formal writing and take most kanji prefixes and suffixes.

A native Japanese word, usually read with kun'yomi or written in kana: {山|やま}, {話|はな}す, {高|たか}い, {並|なら}ぶ. Wago join other wago, often with rendaku ({山|やま} + {川|かわ} → {山川|やまがわ}), and rarely take kango suffixes.
A word borrowed from another language, mostly from English, and written in katakana: データ, ケア, システム. Some take kango suffixes: デジタル{化|か}, スピード{感|かん}.

The voicing of the first consonant of the second part of a compound: {型|かた} → {大型|おおがた}, {不足|ふそく} → {人手不足|ひとでぶそく}, {力|ちから} → {底力|そこぢから}. It is common in wago compounds and rare with kango suffixes, and it can't always be predicted.
Said of a combination that has become a word of its own, with a meaning you must learn: {無理|むり} (impossible), {非常|ひじょう} (emergency), {無関心|むかんしん}. Lexicalized words are vocabulary items.

Said of a pattern that speakers still use to make new words freely: 〜{化|か}, 〜{性|せい}, 〜{的|てき}, 〜{感|かん}, {再|さい}〜. A new combination such as デジタル{化|か} is understood at once even if no dictionary lists it.

A word at the start of a sentence that shows how it relates to the one before: contrast (しかし, ところが), result (したがって, そのため), limit (もっとも, ただし), addition (なお, その{上|うえ}), restatement (つまり, すなわち, {要|よう}するに), example ({例|たと}えば). The JLPT's text grammar questions often ask for one.

A こそあど word (この, その, あの, これ, それ, こうした, そうした) used in a text to point back to something already mentioned. In writing, その / それ point back to what was just said, この / これ to what the writer presents as close or important, and こうした sums up several things.
A JLPT question type: a passage with numbered gaps where you choose the conjunction, the reference word or the sentence ending that fits the flow of the whole text, not just the sentence.
A JLPT grammar question type: four pieces to put in order inside a sentence, with one gap marked ★; you choose the piece that goes in the ★ gap. This course's build questions practise the same skill.

A JLPT N2 task type in reading and listening. In reading, two short texts (A and B) on one question are compared: where they agree and differ. In listening, several people discuss options and you say who chooses what.
A JLPT N2 reading task: a long essay (over 1,000 characters) with questions about the writer's main claim and reasoning. The claim is usually in the last paragraph.

A JLPT reading task: a brochure, a set of rules or a price list, and a question with conditions (who, when, how many). Read the question first and look only for the rows that match; watch the notes marked ※.

references.title: Concession and contrast (module 1)
references.body:
Module 1's patterns for "although", "despite", "on the other hand", "even if" and "not exactly",
with their forms, style and limits. "Plain" is the plain form; N is a noun; な-adj. is a
な-adjective stem.

## Although, despite (lessons 1 and 2)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Style | Example | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜ものの | although (B goes against A) | plain; な-adj. + な / である; N + である | written, formal | {応募|おうぼ}したものの、{返事|へんじ}が{来|こ}ない | can't end a sentence; B is usually a fact |
| とはいうものの | that said (sentence opener) | — | written | とはいうものの、{生活|せいかつ}は{楽|らく}にならない | |
| 〜とはいえ | granted that A, still B | plain; N / な-adj. directly or + だ | written, formal | {春|はる}とはいえ、まだ{寒|さむ}い | B may be an opinion or advice |
| 〜からといって | just because A (doesn't mean B) | plain; N / な-adj. + だ | all styles; casual からって | {高|たか}いからといって、いいとは{限|かぎ}らない | ends in わけではない, とは{限|かぎ}らない or a negative |
| 〜といっても (N3) | I say A, but only so much | plain; N directly | all styles | {昇進|しょうしん}したといっても、{主任|しゅにん}だ | scales A down |
| 〜にもかかわらず | despite A | plain; N / な-adj. directly or + である | written, formal, news | {雨|あめ}にもかかわらず、{大勢|おおぜい}{来|き}た | no だ before it; B is a fact, not a request |
| (それ)にもかかわらず | and yet (sentence opener) | — | written | | |
| 〜ながら(も) | although (a state) | N; い-adj.; な-adj.; ます stem of state verbs; 〜ていながら | written, set phrases | {小|ちい}さいながらも{快適|かいてき}だ | with action verbs ながら means "while" |
| 〜つつ(も) | even while (thinking, knowing) | ます stem | written | {悪|わる}いと{知|し}りつつも、やめられない | one subject; verbs of thinking and knowing |
| のに | although (with feeling) | plain; N / な-adj. + な | all styles | {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んだのに{治|なお}らない | can end a sentence; surprise or complaint |
| くせに | although (blaming) | plain; N + の; な-adj. + な | speech, often rude | {自分|じぶん}も{遅|おく}れたくせに | one subject, a person, usually not "I" |
| 〜ものを | if only (regret) | plain, often 〜ばよかったものを | literary | | to recognize |

Set phrases with ながら: {残念|ざんねん}ながら (unfortunately), {勝手|かって}ながら (on notices: "we're
sorry for the inconvenience"), {我|わ}ながら (if I say so myself), {子供|こども}ながらに (even as a child).

## Two sides (lesson 3)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜{反面|はんめん} | while A, on the other hand B (one thing, two sides) | plain; な-adj. + な / である; N + である | {便利|べんり}な{反面|はんめん}、{高|たか}い | not for two different things |
| 〜{一方|いっぽう}(で) | whereas; as well as | as 反面 | {都市|とし}は{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている{一方|いっぽう}で、{村|むら}は{減|へ}っている | two things or two sides; also "doing A and also B" |
| 〜たかと{思|おも}うと / 〜たかと{思|おも}ったら | no sooner had A than B | た form | {晴|は}れたかと{思|おも}うと{雨|あめ}になった | things you observe, not your own actions; B has happened (usually past) |
| 〜かと{思|おも}えば | one moment A, the next B | dictionary / ている | {泣|な}いているかと{思|おも}えば{笑|わら}っている | alternating states |
| 〜どころか | far from A (the opposite) | plain; N / な-adj. directly | {止|や}むどころか、{強|つよ}くなった | |
| A どころか B も〜ない | not even B, let alone A | as above | {海外|かいがい}どころか{近所|きんじょ}にも{行|い}かない | B is the smaller thing |
| 〜どころではない | no time / state for A | N; dictionary form | {忙|いそが}しくて{旅行|りょこう}どころではない | casual どころじゃない |

## Even if (lesson 4)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Style | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜にしても | even if, granted | plain; N / な-adj. directly or + である | all styles | {忙|いそが}しいにしても、{連絡|れんらく}はできる |
| 〜にしろ / 〜にせよ | the same, firmer | as にしても | にせよ most written | {理由|りゆう}が{何|なん}であるにせよ |
| question word + にしても | whatever, wherever | | | {何|なに}をするにしても、{勇気|ゆうき}がいる |
| A にしろ B にしろ / A にせよ B にせよ | whether A or B | | | {行|い}くにしろ{行|い}かないにしろ |
| {何|なに}にしても / いずれにしても / いずれにせよ | anyway, in any case | | | |
| 〜としても / たとえ〜としても | even supposing | plain; N / な-adj. + だ | all styles | たとえ{失敗|しっぱい}したとしても |
| 〜にしては (N3) | for, considering (surprise) | plain; N directly | all styles | {初|はじ}めてにしては{上手|じょうず}だ |
| 〜{割|わり}に (N3) | considering | plain; N + の | all styles | {値段|ねだん}の{割|わり}にいい |
| 〜といえども | even, although | N; plain | very written | {専門家|せんもんか}といえども (to recognize) |

## Not exactly: how strong is it? (lesson 5)

| Pattern | Strength | Example |
|---|---|---|
| plain statement | yes | {好|す}きだ |
| 〜とも{言|い}える | a possible way of putting it | {好|す}きだとも{言|い}える |
| 〜ではない (of the opposite) | yes, without enthusiasm | きらいではない |
| 〜ないこともない / ないことはない / なくもない | a reluctant yes | {好|す}きでないこともない, {分|わ}からなくもない |
| 〜{気|き}がしないでもない | a vague yes (to recognize) | {好|す}きな{気|き}がしないでもない |
| 〜(という)わけではない | denies a guess | きらいというわけではない |
| {必|かなら}ずしも〜とは{限|かぎ}らない | not always, not necessarily | {必|かなら}ずしも{好|す}きとは{限|かぎ}らない |
| 〜とは{言|い}えない | close to no, politely | {好|す}きとは{言|い}えない |
| plain negative | no | {好|す}きではない |

Possibility, strongest first: 〜する → 〜するかもしれない → 〜しないとも{限|かぎ}らない (can't be ruled
out; usually with a precaution) → 〜するとは{限|かぎ}らない (not necessarily) → 〜することはない (no
need, no chance). いちがいに〜とは{言|い}えない: you can't generalize.

Before というわけではない, nouns and な-adjectives take no な: {病気|びょうき}というわけではない,
きらいというわけではない.

## Kana or kanji: N2's compound particles

The course writes these with kanji: {際|さい}して, {先立|さきだ}って, {基|もと}づいて, {応|おう}じて, {限|かぎ}らず,
{限|かぎ}り, を{問|と}わず, {越|こ}したことはない, {過|す}ぎない, {次第|しだい}, {以上|いじょう}, {上|うえ}は, {以来|いらい},
を{通|つう}じて, を{機|き}に, {末|すえ}に, {折|おり}に, {反面|はんめん}, {一方|いっぽう}, ざるを{得|え}ない, {得|え}る / {得|う}る,
{割|わり}に; from N3: {対|たい}して, {関|かん}して, {比|くら}べて, {違|ちが}いない, {込|こ}めて, {通|とお}して, {中心|ちゅうしん}に.

These in kana: にあたって, をめぐって, にそって, にともなって, にわたって, にかかわらず / にもかかわらず,
からには, ばかりに, だけに, どころか, はもとより, のみならず, とはいえ, といえども, にしろ / にせよ,
からといって, かねる / かねない, 〜がたい, 〜つつ, 〜あげく, 〜ものの, 〜ものなら, 〜ことに, 〜をきっかけに,
〜につき, 〜にいたる, 〜をもって, 〜まい, 〜べく, 〜ねば, 〜ぬ; from N3: について, にとって, として,
によって, によると.

Always kana as well: auxiliary verbs after the て form (〜ている, 〜ていく, 〜てくる, 〜てしまう…), formal
nouns (こと, もの, ところ, わけ, はず, ため, よう, おそれ…), and ある, いる, する, なる, できる, いい / よい.

references.title: Hearsay and likeness
references.body:
How did you hear it, and how does it look? The hearsay and likeness patterns of N4, N3 and N2
(lesson 24 adds the N2 ones), ranked roughly from the most definite to the vaguest. "Heard" means
the speaker got it from someone else; "seen" means the speaker judges from what they observe.

## Hearsay: passing on what you heard

| Pattern | Joins to | How heard | How sure | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜とのことだ | plain form | a message, passed on exactly | quite definite | formal (messages, business) | {部長|ぶちょう}は{遅|おく}れるとのことです |
| 〜ということだ | plain form | reported information | definite | neutral, written | {明日|あした}は{休|やす}みということだ |
| 〜そうだ | plain form | heard or read | definite (source not judged) | neutral | {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}るそうだ |
| 〜とされる / 〜とされている | plain form | the accepted view | general opinion | written, news | {肌|はだ}に{優|やさ}しいとされる |
| 〜とみられる | plain form | an official guess | a likely cause or fact | news | {原因|げんいん}は{火|ひ}の{不始末|ふしまつ}とみられる |
| 〜と{言|い}われている | plain form | people say | widely believed | neutral | {体|からだ}にいいと{言|い}われている |
| 〜という{話|はなし}だ / 〜って{話|はなし}だ | plain form | a story going round | fairly sure | spoken | {来月|らいげつ}{閉店|へいてん}するという{話|はなし}だ |
| 〜らしい | plain form (noun directly) | heard, or inferred | probable | neutral | {彼|かれ}は{辞|や}めるらしい |
| 〜んだって / 〜って | plain form (noun + なんだって) | heard | fairly sure | casual (N3) | {明日|あした}{休|やす}みなんだって |
| 〜とか | plain form (noun + だ) | heard, vaguely | vague, soft | conversation, polite too | {結婚|けっこん}するとか |

## Likeness: how it looks or seems

| Pattern | Joins to | Meaning | Seen or heard | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ます stem / adj stem + そうだ | stem | looks as if; looks like it's about to | seen | neutral | {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りそうだ, おいしそう |
| 〜ようだ / 〜みたいだ | plain form (noun + の / noun directly) | seems; is like | seen or reasoned | ようだ neutral, みたい casual | だれもいないようだ |
| 〜らしい | noun + らしい | typical of, like a real… | — | neutral | {学生|がくせい}らしい{服装|ふくそう} |
| 〜っぽい | noun, stem | -ish, -looking | seen | casual (N3) | {子供|こども}っぽい, {安|やす}っぽい |
| 〜かのように / 〜かのようだ | plain form; noun + である | as if (but it isn't) | an appearance only | written, vivid | {何|なに}もなかったかのように |
| adj stem + げ | adjective stem | looking…, with an air of… | seen (others' feelings) | literary | {寂|さび}しげ, {得意|とくい}げ |
| 〜ぶり / 〜っぷり | noun, ます stem | the way someone does it | seen | neutral; っぷり admiring | {仕事|しごと}ぶり, {食|た}べっぷり |


## Points that are easy to mix up

- そうだ after a stem (looks as if: {降|ふ}りそうだ) and after the plain form (I hear: {降|ふ}るそうだ).
- ようだ (it seems, and it may well be so) and かのようだ (it's as if, but it isn't).
- そう and げ: {楽|たの}しそう and {楽|たの}しげ both describe how someone looks; げ is literary and
  can't predict: ×{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りげだ.
- らしい after a sentence (I hear / it seems) and after a noun (typical of): {彼|かれ}は{学生|がくせい}らしい
  (apparently he's a student) / {学生|がくせい}らしい{服装|ふくそう} (clothes typical of a student).
- とか at the end (I hear) and listing とか ({服|ふく}とか{靴|くつ}とか).

references.title: The N2 kanji
references.body:
The 390 kanji this course adds, in the order of the lessons that teach them. With the 102 kanji of
Japanese N5, the 177 of Japanese N4 and the 370 of Japanese N3 (each listed in that course's kanji
reference) they make 1,039. Any lesson in this course may use a kanji from any of the four lists,
and a word is written with kanji when all its kanji are on them.

On'yomi are in katakana; kun'yomi are in hiragana, with the okurigana in brackets: あさ(い) means
the kanji is read あさ in {浅|あさ}い. Only the readings you meet at N2 are given. Stroke counts are
those of the tracing pads.

references.title: Notice language
references.body:
How Japanese notices are built (lesson 15): the reasons they give, the phrases they ask and
forbid with, and the order they usually follow.

## Reasons on notices

| Pattern | Register | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 〜につき | very formal; written notices | {改装|かいそう}につき{休業|きゅうぎょう}いたします | closed for refurbishment |
| 〜により / 〜による | formal; announcements, news | {強風|きょうふう}により{運転|うんてん}を{見合|みあ}わせております | services suspended due to strong winds |
| 〜のため / 〜ため | formal | {工事|こうじ}のため{通行止|つうこうど}め | road closed for works |
| 〜ことから | explanations | {利用者|りようしゃ}が{増|ふ}えたことから、{時間|じかん}を{延長|えんちょう}します | since users have increased, hours are extended |
| 〜とあって (recognize) | news | {連休|れんきゅう}とあって{混雑|こんざつ}した | it being a long weekend, it was crowded |

〜につき also means "per": {一人|ひとり}につき{二枚|にまい}まで (two per person). That use is fine in speech.

## Asking, forbidding and allowing

| Phrase | Strength | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ご〜ください / お〜ください | polite request | {足元|あしもと}にご{注意|ちゅうい}ください |
| ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください | please note and accept | {変更|へんこう}する{場合|ばあい}がございます。ご{了承|りょうしょう}ください |
| ご{協力|きょうりょく}をお{願|ねが}いいたします | thanks in advance | ごみの{分別|ぶんべつ}にご{協力|きょうりょく}をお{願|ねが}いいたします |
| お〜{願|ねが}います / 〜{願|ねが}います | firm but polite | お{静|しず}かに{願|ねが}います |
| ごえんりょください | please don't (polite) | {館内|かんない}での{飲食|いんしょく}はごえんりょください |
| 〜ないでください | please don't (plainer) | ここに{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{止|と}めないでください |
| 〜こと | a rule, firm | {使用後|しようご}は{元|もと}の{場所|ばしょ}に{戻|もど}すこと |
| 〜{禁止|きんし} / 〜{厳禁|げんきん} | banned / strictly banned | {撮影|さつえい}{禁止|きんし}, {火気|かき}{厳禁|げんきん} |
| 〜{可|か} / 〜{不可|ふか} | allowed / not allowed | {持|も}ち{込|こ}み{可|か}, {再入場|さいにゅうじょう}{不可|ふか} |

ごえんりょください is written in kana in this course (its second kanji is outside N2).

## Small words of notices

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜{中|ちゅう} | in progress | {清掃中|せいそうちゅう}, {工事中|こうじちゅう}, {準備中|じゅんびちゅう} |
| 〜{限|かぎ}り | only (lesson 20) | {本日|ほんじつ}{限|かぎ}り |
| 〜にて | = で (formal) | {受付|うけつけ}にてお{申|もう}し{込|こ}みください |
| {本日|ほんじつ} | today (formal) | {本日|ほんじつ}{休館|きゅうかん} |
| {当館|とうかん} / {当店|とうてん} | this building / this shop | {当館|とうかん}は{終日|しゅうじつ}{禁煙|きんえん}です |
| {当面|とうめん}の{間|あいだ} | for the time being | {当面|とうめん}の{間|あいだ}、{休止|きゅうし}いたします |
| ただし | however (a condition) | ただし、{土日|どにち}は{休|やす}みです |
| なお | note also (an extra point) | なお、{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}はございません |
| noun endings | no verb | {本日|ほんじつ}{休館|きゅうかん}, {終日|しゅうじつ}{禁煙|きんえん} |

ただし and なお are taught fully in lesson 28.

## How a notice is usually ordered

1. A title in brackets: 【{休館|きゅうかん}のお{知|し}らせ】.
2. A greeting, for longer notices: {平素|へいそ}よりご{利用|りよう}いただき、ありがとうございます。
3. What happens and why: {改修|かいしゅう}{工事|こうじ}につき、{三月|さんがつ}{末|まつ}まで{休館|きゅうかん}いたします。
4. Details and alternatives: dates, places, fees, conditions (often as a list starting with ・).
5. Provisos: ただし…, なお…
6. An apology and a request: ご{不便|ふべん}をおかけいたしますが、ご{理解|りかい}とご{協力|きょうりょく}をお{願|ねが}いいたします。
7. Who it's from: the organization's name.

The organization uses humble forms for its own actions (いたします, しております, ございます) and
honorific requests for the reader's (ご{利用|りよう}ください, お{越|こ}しください). Notices prefer kango:
{使用|しよう} for {使|つか}う, {清掃|せいそう} for {掃除|そうじ}, {喫煙|きつえん} for タバコを{吸|す}う.

references.title: Possibility, judgement and obligation
references.body:
Module 4 of Japanese N2 (lessons 16–20). Each row gives how the pattern joins, the meaning, an
example and where it lives. "Plain" means the plain form; "stem" is the ます stem. Speakers don't
all draw the lines between near-synonyms in the same place: the notes give the usual, safe choice.

## It could happen (lesson 16)

| Pattern | Joins | Meaning | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜かねない | stem | could well (something bad) | {事故|じこ}につながりかねない | bad results only; a warning; kana |
| 〜おそれがある | dictionary form; noun + の | there's a risk of | {大雨|おおあめ}のおそれがある | forecasts, news, labels; おそれのある + noun |
| 〜{得|う}る / 〜{得|え}る | stem | can, is possible | {起|お}こり{得|う}る | possibility, not ability; written |
| 〜{得|え}ない | stem | can't be, impossible | あり{得|え}ない | other forms always え: ×ありうない |
| 〜ないとも{限|かぎ}らない | ない form | can't rule out | {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}らないとも{限|かぎ}らない | small risk; often with a precaution |

## Can't and must (lesson 17)

| Pattern | Joins | Meaning | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜かねる | stem | unable to (politely) | お{答|こた}えいたしかねます | your own side's refusal; group 2 verb |
| 〜がたい | stem | hard to (accept, believe) | {信|しん}じがたい | feelings and judgements; 〜にくい for physical difficulty |
| 〜ざるを{得|え}ない | ない form without ない; する → せ | have no choice but | {中止|ちゅうし}せざるを{得|え}ない | forced by circumstances; formal |
| 〜わけにはいかない | dictionary form | can't (it wouldn't be right) | {休|やす}むわけにはいかない | N3 review |
| 〜ないわけにはいかない | ない form | can't not, must | {行|い}かないわけにはいかない | social or moral duty |
| 〜ずにはすまない | ず form | will have to (to settle it) | {謝|あやま}らずにはすまない | to recognize |

## No way (lesson 18)

| Pattern | Joins | Meaning | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜っこない | stem (often potential) | no way | {勝|か}てっこない | casual only |
| 〜まい | group 1: dictionary form; group 2: dictionary form or stem; する → するまい / すまい; {来|く}る → くるまい / こまい | won't (will); surely won't (guess) | {二度|にど}と{行|い}くまい, {雨|あめ}は{降|ふ}るまい | written; forms for groups 2 and 3 vary |
| 〜ようがない | stem | there's no way to | {連絡|れんらく}のしようがない | no means; N3 review |
| 〜はずがない | plain | it can't be | ここにいるはずがない | reasoning |
| 〜わけがない | plain | no way | {守|まも}るわけがない | emotional; own refusal |
| 〜ものか / 〜もんか | plain; な-adj and noun + な | as if…! I'll never… | {負|ま}けるもんか | falling tone; casual |
| 〜(よ)うにも〜ない | volitional + にも + negative potential | want to but can't | {帰|かえ}ろうにも{帰|かえ}れない | |

## Best to, unless, must (lesson 19)

| Pattern | Joins | Meaning | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜に{越|こ}したことはない | plain; noun and な-adj directly | it's best to (of course) | {安|やす}いに{越|こ}したことはない | general truth; often "…but" |
| 〜ないことには〜ない | ない form | unless A, no B | {食|た}べてみないことには{分|わ}からない | main clause negative or blocked |
| 〜ほかない / 〜よりほかない | dictionary form | no choice but | {待|ま}つほかない | more serious than しかない |
| 〜までもない / 〜までもなく | dictionary form | no need to | {言|い}うまでもない | "needless to say" |
| 〜ことだ / 〜べきだ / 〜ものだ | plain | you should / should / that's what one does | {休|やす}むことだ | N3 review |

## Only, the best, as long as (lesson 20)

| Pattern | Joins | Meaning | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜に{過|す}ぎない | noun; plain; な-adj + である | no more than | {一例|いちれい}に{過|す}ぎない | written; spoken 〜だけだ |
| 〜に{限|かぎ}る | noun; dictionary or ない form | nothing beats | {寝|ね}るに{限|かぎ}る | the speaker's own recommendation |
| 〜に{限|かぎ}って | noun | always just when; X of all people | {急|いそ}いでいる{日|ひ}に{限|かぎ}って | complaint or trust |
| 〜に{限|かぎ}り | noun | only (limited to) | {本日|ほんじつ}に{限|かぎ}り | notices |
| 〜{限|かぎ}り(は) | plain; noun + の / である | as long as | {生|い}きている{限|かぎ}り | |
| 〜ない{限|かぎ}り | ない form | unless | {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}らない{限|かぎ}り | |
| 〜{限|かぎ}りでは | plain | as far as | {知|し}っている{限|かぎ}りでは | |
| できる{限|かぎ}り | — | as much as possible | できる{限|かぎ}り{早|はや}く | more formal than できるだけ |

## How sure, how necessary

| Strength | Possibility | Necessity |
|---|---|---|
| strongest | に{違|ちが}いない; っこない / はずがない (no) | ざるを{得|え}ない, ないわけにはいかない |
| strong | はずだ; おそれがある / かねない (risk) | なければならない, べきだ |
| middle | かもしれない | ほかない / しかない |
| weak | {得|う}る; ないとも{限|かぎ}らない | に{越|こ}したことはない (it's best) |

references.title: Reasons, grounds and basis
references.body:
The reason and basis patterns of module 3 (lessons 11–14), with how they join, what follows them
and where they're used. Lesson 15's notice reasons (につき, により, ため) are on the "Notice
language" sheet.

## Since it's so (lesson 11)

| Pattern | Joins | Meaning | What follows | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| からには | plain form; noun / な-adj + である | now that, since… so | duty, resolve, advice, firm conclusion | spoken and written | {引|ひ}き{受|う}けたからには、{最後|さいご}までやる |
| {以上|いじょう}(は) | plain form; noun / な-adj + である | since, given that; as long as… not | duty, logical conclusion, "can't" | formal; rules, contracts | {契約|けいやく}した{以上|いじょう}、{守|まも}るべきだ |
| {上|うえ}は | mostly た form | since, now that | resolve, "nothing for it but" | very formal (recognize) | こうなった{上|うえ}は、やるしかない |
| のだから (N3) | plain form; noun / な-adj + な | since (as we both know) | advice, criticism | spoken (んだから) | {大人|おとな}なんだから、{自分|じぶん}で{決|き}めなさい |
| ことだし | plain form | since (one light reason) | suggestion, decision | casual-polite speech | {雨|あめ}もやんだことだし、{出|で}かけよう |

Not to be confused: 〜た{上|うえ}で (after doing, lesson 7), 〜{上|じょう} (in terms of: {法律上|ほうりつじょう},
lesson 7), and {以上|いじょう} after a number (or more) or at the end of a report (that's all).

## Just because, precisely because (lesson 12)

| Pattern | Joins | Result | Feeling | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ばかりに | plain form; な-adj + な / である; noun + である | bad | regret: just this one thing | {一言|ひとこと}{言|い}ったばかりに、{怒|おこ}らせた |
| 〜たいばかりに | たい form | an extreme effort | how far the wish drove someone | {会|あ}いたいばかりに、{毎週|まいしゅう}{遠|とお}くから{通|かよ}った |
| だけに | plain form; な-adj + な; noun (+ である) | as expected, or all the stronger | "naturally, given that" | {期待|きたい}していただけに、がっかりした |
| だけあって | plain form; な-adj + な; noun | good | praise: lives up to it | {高|たか}いだけあって、{品質|ひんしつ}がいい |
| だけのことはある | (sentence end) | good | "it was worth it" | {高|たか}かっただけのことはある |
| ものだから / もので | plain form; noun / な-adj + な | what happened | excuse, explanation | {道|みち}が{混|こ}んでいたもので、{遅|おく}れました |
| おかげで (N3) | plain form; noun + の | good | thanks | {先生|せんせい}のおかげで{合格|ごうかく}した |
| せいで (N3) | plain form; noun + の | bad | blame | {雨|あめ}のせいで{中止|ちゅうし}になった |
| あまり(に) (N3) | plain form; noun + の | extreme | too much feeling | {心配|しんぱい}のあまり{眠|ねむ}れなかった |

## Based on, in line with, according to (lesson 13)

| Pattern | Before a noun | Meaning | Typical nouns | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| に{基|もと}づいて / に{基|もと}づき | に{基|もと}づく, に{基|もと}づいた | on the basis of (a standard you follow) | law, facts, data, standards | {法律|ほうりつ}に{基|もと}づいて{判断|はんだん}する |
| をもとに(して) | をもとにした | using as material for something new | stories, photos, answers | {実話|じつわ}をもとにした{映画|えいが} |
| にそって | にそった | along; in line with | roads, rivers; plans, policy, wishes | {計画|けいかく}にそって{進|すす}める |
| に{応|おう}じて | に{応|おう}じた | varying with, to suit | age, need, ability, number | {年齢|ねんれい}に{応|おう}じて{料金|りょうきん}が{変|か}わる |
| にしたがって (N3) | にしたがった | obeying; as A changes, B | instructions, rules; changes | {指示|しじ}にしたがって{行動|こうどう}する |
| をもって (recognize) | — | by means of; as of | dates, documents | {本日|ほんじつ}をもって{終了|しゅうりょう}する |

Spelling: にそって and をもとに are in kana in this course (the kanji of そう is outside N2; もと has two
kanji in print); に{基|もと}づいて and に{応|おう}じて keep their kanji.

## Over, concerning, in response to (lesson 14)

| Pattern | Before a noun | Meaning | What follows | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| をめぐって | をめぐる | over (a disputed issue) | debate, conflict, competition | {建設|けんせつ}をめぐって{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれる |
| に{関|かん}して (N3) | に{関|かん}する | about, concerning (formal, neutral) | information, questions, research | {汚染|おせん}に{関|かん}する{調査|ちょうさ} |
| について (N3) | についての | about (everyday) | talking, writing, finding out | ごみについて{話|はな}す |
| に{応|こた}えて | に{応|こた}える, に{応|こた}えた | in response to | an action meeting a request or hope | {要望|ようぼう}に{応|こた}えて{本数|ほんすう}を{増|ふ}やす |
| を{中心|ちゅうしん}に (N3) | を{中心|ちゅうしん}とした | centred on | — | {若者|わかもの}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に{人気|にんき}だ |
| において (N3) | における | in, at (formal) | — | {日本|にほん}における{問題|もんだい} |

One kanji, two readings: {応|おう}じる / に{応|おう}じて (respond, vary with) and に{応|こた}える (respond to hopes);
don't confuse に{応|こた}える with {答|こた}える (answer a question), the same こたえる written with another kanji. をめぐって is in kana (its kanji is outside N2).

references.title: Scope and emphasis
references.body:
The patterns of module 5 (lessons 21–25) in one place: widening a statement, feelings too strong
to bear, exclamations, and conditions with an attitude. "Written" means mostly in writing and
formal speech; in casual speech you'd usually choose the everyday pattern in the last column.

## Widening a statement (lesson 21)

| Pattern | Joins to | Meaning | Register | Everyday version |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A はもとより B も | noun (verb + の) | B too, not to mention A | written, formal | はもちろん |
| A のみならず B も | noun; plain form; な-adj / noun + である | not only A but also B | written | だけでなく |
| のみならず、… | start of a sentence | what's more | written | それに |
| A を{問|と}わず | noun with a range of values ({年齢|ねんれい}, {男女|だんじょ}) | regardless of A | written, formal | {関係|かんけい}なく |
| A にかかわらず / にかかわりなく | noun with a range; verb pair (する・しない) | regardless of A | formal | {関係|かんけい}なく |
| A に{限|かぎ}らず | noun | not just A | spoken and written | だけじゃなくて |
| A ばかりか B まで / さえ | noun; plain form | not only A but even B (surprise) | neutral (N3) | — |
| A をはじめ(として) | noun | A and others, with A as the leading example | neutral (N3) | — |

### にかかわらず or にもかかわらず?

| | 〜にかかわらず | 〜にもかかわらず (lesson 2) |
|---|---|---|
| Meaning | regardless of (whatever A is) | despite (A is a fact) |
| A is | a range: weather, age, yes/no | one fact that is true |
| Test | add "whatever it is" / "whether or not" | add "and yet" |
| Example | {雨天|うてん}にかかわらず{行|おこな}います (rain or shine) | {雨|あめ}にもかかわらず{大勢|おおぜい}{来|き}た (despite the rain) |

## Feelings you can't help (lesson 22)

| Pattern | Joins to | About | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜てたまらない | い-adj 〜くて, な-adj 〜で, 〜たくて, feeling verbs | feelings, sensations, wishes: unbearably | neutral | {会|あ}いたくてたまらない |
| 〜てならない | the same; best with {気|き}がする, {思|おも}える | feelings that come by themselves | written | {気|き}がしてならない |
| 〜てしょうがない / 〜てしかたがない | the same | feelings and annoyances | casual (N3) | {眠|ねむ}くてしょうがない |
| 〜ないではいられない | ない form | actions you can't hold back | neutral | {笑|わら}わないではいられない |
| 〜ずにはいられない | ず form (する → せず) | the same | more written (N3) | {笑|わら}わずにはいられない |
| 〜ずにはおかない | ず form, often causative | a thing can't fail to cause a reaction | written (recognize) | {感動|かんどう}させずにはおかない |

The first four describe your own feelings in statements; for someone else add ようだ, らしい or
〜がっている.

## Exclamations (lesson 23)

| Pattern | Joins to | Meaning | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜ものがある | plain form; な-adj + な; 〜べき | there's something (impressive, hard) about it | formal, measured | {心|こころ}を{打|う}つものがある |
| 〜ことに | た form; い-adj; な-adj + な; at the start | to my surprise, sadly, luckily | written, formal | {驚|おどろ}いたことに |
| 〜{限|かぎ}りだ | feeling い-adj; な-adj + な | I couldn't be more… (your own feeling) | formal | うれしい{限|かぎ}りだ |
| どれだけ / なんと 〜ことか | plain form | how…! | neutral (N3) | どれだけ{泣|な}いたことか |
| 〜ものだ | plain form | how things are; used to (feeling) | neutral (N3) | {早|はや}いものだ |
| 〜といったらない | noun, often 〜さ | indescribably | spoken (recognize) | うれしさといったらない |

## Conditions with an attitude (lesson 25)

| Pattern | Joins to | Meaning | Attitude | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜ものなら | potential, dictionary form | if only I could | a wish against the odds; a challenge | {行|い}けるものなら{行|い}きたい |
| 〜(よ)うものなら | volitional | if you so much as… | a warning: a disaster follows | {遅|おく}れようものなら{大変|たいへん}だ |
| 〜ては / 〜ていては | て form | if you (keep) doing that | a complaint: something bad | {寝|ね}てばかりいては{困|こま}る |
| 〜たら〜たで / 〜ば〜で / 〜なら〜で | the same word twice | if it happens, then… | a new problem either way (or: fine) | {晴|は}れたら{晴|は}れたで{暑|あつ}い |
| 〜さえ〜ば | noun + さえ; verb stem + さえすれば | as long as | the one condition needed (N3) | {水|みず}さえあれば |
| 〜(よ)うが〜まいが / 〜(よ)うと | volitional (+ まい) | whether or not, no matter | it makes no difference (written, recognize) | {降|ふ}ろうが{降|ふ}るまいが |

## Kana or kanji

As everywhere in this course: にかかわらず, にもかかわらず, のみならず, はもとより, ものなら in kana;
を{問|と}わず, に{限|かぎ}らず, {限|かぎ}りだ with kanji.

references.title: Time, occasion and process (module 2)
references.body:
Module 2's patterns for occasions, sequences, spans and processes, with their forms, register and
the limits that trip learners up. "Dict." is the dictionary form; N is a noun; "stem" is the ます
stem. Kana or kanji follows the course rule: に{先立|さきだ}って, に{際|さい}して, {次第|しだい}, {以来|いらい},
を{通|つう}じて, を{機|き}に, {末|すえ}に, {折|おり}に in kanji; にあたって, にわたって, にともなって, をきっかけに,
につけ, つつ, あげく in kana.

## Before and on the occasion (lesson 6)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Register and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜に{先立|さきだ}って / に{先立|さきだ}ち / に{先立|さきだ}つ N | before (an important event) | N / dict. + に{先立|さきだ}って | {開会|かいかい}に{先立|さきだ}って{国歌|こっか}を{歌|うた}う | formal; the event must be big enough to prepare for |
| 〜にあたって / にあたり | on the occasion of (a new start) | N / dict. + にあたって | {留学|りゅうがく}するにあたって{準備|じゅんび}する | speeches, greetings; not for accidents or sudden bad events |
| 〜に{際|さい}して / に{際|さい}し | on (a special) occasion | N / dict. + に{際|さい}して | {結婚|けっこん}に{際|さい}して | very formal; overlaps にあたって |
| 〜{際|さい}(は) / 〜の{際|さい}に | when (formal) | N + の / dict. / た + {際|さい} | お{帰|かえ}りの{際|さい}は | notices and staff speech; fine for routine events |
| 〜を{前|まえ}に(して) | with … ahead; in front of | N + を{前|まえ}に | {試験|しけん}を{前|まえ}にして{緊張|きんちょう}する | everyday and formal |
| 〜{折|おり}(に) / {折|おり}には | on the occasion, when | N + の / dict. + {折|おり} | お{越|こ}しの{折|おり}には | letters; recognize |

## As soon as, after, in the end (lesson 7)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Register and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜{次第|しだい} | as soon as | stem / action N + {次第|しだい} | {届|とど}き{次第|しだい}ご{連絡|れんらく}します | formal; B is an intention or request, not a past fact |
| N + {次第|しだい}だ / {次第|しだい}で(は) | depends on | N + {次第|しだい} | {天気|てんき}{次第|しだい}で{中止|ちゅうし}もある | では adds "in some cases" |
| 〜{次第|しだい}です | that's why (formal) | plain form + {次第|しだい}です | ご{連絡|れんらく}した{次第|しだい}です | letters and emails |
| 〜た{上|うえ}で / ご〜の{上|うえ} | after doing A properly, B | た form / N + の + {上|うえ}で | {確認|かくにん}した{上|うえ}で{署名|しょめい}する | A is a needed step; plain sequences take てから |
| N + {上|じょう} | in terms of | N + {上|じょう} | {契約上|けいやくじょう}, {法律上|ほうりつじょう} | written suffix; read じょう |
| 〜た{末|すえ}(に) / N の{末|すえ} | after long effort, finally | た form / N + の + {末|すえ} | {悩|なや}んだ{末|すえ}に{決|き}めた | written; any result |
| 〜たあげく / N のあげく | after all that, (a bad end) | た form / N + の + あげく | {迷|まよ}ったあげく{買|か}わなかった | the result is bad or disappointing |
| 〜てからでないと | not until | て form + からでないと | {読|よ}んでからでないと{署名|しょめい}できない | review (N3 2); second half negative |

## Since and throughout (lesson 8)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Register and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜て{以来|いらい} / N {以来|いらい} | ever since | て form / N + {以来|いらい} | {卒業|そつぎょう}して{以来|いらい}{会|あ}っていない | a continuing state follows; not for the future |
| それ{以来|いらい} | since then | | それ{以来|いらい}、{行|い}っていない | |
| 〜てからというもの | ever since (a striking change) | て form + からというもの | {子供|こども}が{生|う}まれてからというもの… | emotional, written and narrative |
| 〜にわたって / にわたり / にわたる N | over (a whole span) | span of time, space or number + にわたって | {三日間|みっかかん}にわたって, {全国|ぜんこく}にわたる | needs a span, not a point |
| 〜を{通|つう}じて / を{通|とお}して | all through (a period); by way of | N + を{通|つう}じて | {一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて{暖|あたた}かい | review (N3 14) |
| 〜にいたるまで | right down to | N + にいたるまで | {子供|こども}からお{年寄|としよ}りにいたるまで | written; recognize |
| 〜ところだった | nearly (but didn't) | dict. + ところだった | もう{少|すこ}しで{忘|わす}れるところだった | with もう{少|すこ}しで, {危|あや}うく |

## While and in progress (lesson 9)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Register and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜つつ | while (simultaneous action) | stem + つつ | {考|かんが}えつつ{歩|ある}く | written; one subject (two subjects: 〜{間|あいだ}に) |
| 〜つつ(も) | although | stem + つつも | {悪|わる}いと{知|し}りつつ | lesson 2 |
| 〜つつある | in the process of (progressive aspect) | stem + つつある | {人口|じんこう}が{減|へ}りつつある | written, news; verbs of change; speech: 〜てきている |
| 〜にともなって / にともない / にともなう N | along with (a change or event) | N / dict. + の + にともなって | {工業化|こうぎょうか}にともなって | formal; not with people |
| 〜とともに | together with; as | N / dict. + とともに | {家族|かぞく}とともに{暮|く}らす | review (N3 4); the one that works with people |
| 〜につれて | as (gradually) | N / dict. + につれて | {年|とし}をとるにつれて | review (N3 4) |
| 〜{一方|いっぽう}だ | keeps going one way | dict. + {一方|いっぽう}だ | {物価|ぶっか}が{上|あ}がる{一方|いっぽう}だ | review (N3 4); usually bad |
| 〜ばかりだ | only gets (worse) | dict. + ばかりだ | {悪|わる}くなるばかりだ | almost always bad; a complaint |

## Triggers and occasions (lesson 10)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Register and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜をきっかけに / をきっかけとして | with A as the trigger | N / clause + の + をきっかけに | {留学|りゅうがく}をきっかけに{料理|りょうり}を{始|はじ}めた | B is a change or new start; A may be chance |
| 〜がきっかけで | A was what started it | N + がきっかけで | {一冊|いっさつ}の{本|ほん}がきっかけで | spoken and written |
| 〜を{機|き}に / を{機|き}として / を{契機|けいき}に | taking A as the chance | N + を{機|き}に | {退職|たいしょく}を{機|き}に{移住|いじゅう}した | formal; B is a deliberate decision |
| 〜につけ(て) | whenever (a feeling comes) | dict. ({見|み}る, {聞|き}く, {思|おも}う…) + につけ | {写真|しゃしん}を{見|み}るにつけ{思|おも}い{出|だ}す | written; perception + feeling |
| {何|なに}かにつけて | at every opportunity | | {何|なに}かにつけて{電話|でんわ}してくる | set phrase |
| A につけ B につけ | whether A or B | | うれしいにつけ{悲|かな}しいにつけ | recognize |
| 〜たびに | every time | dict. / N + の + たびに | {会|あ}うたびに | review (N3 2); neutral |
| 〜たとたん(に) | the moment | た form + とたん | {鳴|な}ったとたん{忘|わす}れた | review (N3 2); unexpected |
| 〜かけ / 〜かける | half done | stem + かけ(の) | {書|か}きかけの{手紙|てがみ} | review (N3 3) |

## Near-synonyms at a glance

| Pair | Choose the first when… | Choose the second when… |
|---|---|---|
| に{先立|さきだ}って / にあたって | something is done earlier, in time order | you face the moment: an attitude, preparation, greeting |
| にあたって / に{際|さい}して | looking ahead to a new start | pointing at the special moment itself |
| に{際|さい}して / {際|さい}は | a special occasion | a routine "when" in a notice |
| {次第|しだい} / たらすぐ | formal | everyday speech |
| た{上|うえ}で / てから | A is a needed step for B | a plain sequence |
| た{末|すえ}に / たあげく | any result, after real effort | a bad result, with frustration |
| て{以来|いらい} / てからというもの | neutral "ever since" | a striking change, emotionally told |
| にわたって / を{通|つう}じて | an activity fills the span | something holds at every point of the span |
| つつ / ながら | written | everyday |
| つつある / ている | a change under way (written) | any ongoing action or a resulting state |
| にともなって / につれて | a change or event in the world (formal) | a gradual, proportional change (spoken too) |
| {一方|いっぽう}だ / ばかりだ | describing a trend | complaining about a bad trend |
| をきっかけに / を{機|き}に | any trigger, even chance | a chance deliberately taken |
| につけ / たびに | a perception that brings a feeling | any repeated event |

references.title: Word formation: prefixes and suffixes
references.body:
The commonest kanji prefixes and suffixes at N2 (lesson 27). Combinations are fixed by usage:
learn each word with its prefix. The meanings in the second column are tendencies, not laws.

## Negative prefixes

| Prefix | Core meaning | Words |
|---|---|---|
| {不|ふ}〜 (ぶ in a few words) | not (a state or quality) | {不安|ふあん}, {不便|ふべん}, {不可能|ふかのう}, {不規則|ふきそく}, {不安定|ふあんてい}, {不平等|ふびょうどう}, {不足|ふそく}, {不十分|ふじゅうぶん}, {不器用|ぶきよう} |
| {無|む}〜 (ぶ in a few words) | there is no … | {無料|むりょう}, {無理|むり}, {無関心|むかんしん}, {無責任|むせきにん}, {無意識|むいしき}, {無断|むだん}, {無事|ぶじ} |
| {非|ひ}〜 | outside, non‑ | {非常識|ひじょうしき}, {非公開|ひこうかい}, {非公式|ひこうしき}, {非現実的|ひげんじつてき}, {非課税|ひかぜい} |
| {未|み}〜 | not yet | {未成年|みせいねん}, {未経験|みけいけん}, {未完成|みかんせい}, {未定|みてい}, {未知|みち}, {未解決|みかいけつ} |

{未完成|みかんせい} (not yet finished) ≠ {不完全|ふかんぜん} (flawed). {非公開|ひこうかい} (closed to the
public) ≠ {未公開|みこうかい} (not yet made public).

## Other prefixes

| Prefix | Meaning | Words |
|---|---|---|
| {再|さい}〜 | again | {再開|さいかい}, {再利用|さいりよう}, {再確認|さいかくにん} |
| {超|ちょう}〜 | super‑ | {超高層|ちょうこうそう} (casual {超|ちょう}〜 is speech only) |
| {反|はん}〜 | anti‑, counter‑ | {反比例|はんぴれい}, {反社会的|はんしゃかいてき} |
| {副|ふく}〜 | vice‑, secondary | {副社長|ふくしゃちょう}, {副作用|ふくさよう}, {副業|ふくぎょう} |
| {諸|しょ}〜 | various | {諸問題|しょもんだい}, {諸国|しょこく} |
| {各|かく}〜 | each | {各国|かっこく}, {各地|かくち}, {各自|かくじ} |
| {旧|きゅう}〜 / {新|しん}〜 | old / new | {旧型|きゅうがた}, {新型|しんがた} |
| {総|そう}〜 | total | {総額|そうがく}, {総数|そうすう}, {総合|そうごう} |
| {高|こう}〜 / {低|てい}〜 | high‑ / low‑ | {高性能|こうせいのう}, {高収入|こうしゅうにゅう}; {低温|ていおん}, {低所得|ていしょとく} |
| {半|はん}〜 | half | {半年|はんとし}, {半日|はんにち}, {半額|はんがく} |
| {前|ぜん}〜 / {元|もと}〜 | previous / ex‑ | {前社長|ぜんしゃちょう}; {元|もと}{選手|せんしゅ} |

## Suffixes

| Suffix | Meaning | Words |
|---|---|---|
| 〜{化|か} | ‑ization | {高齢化|こうれいか}, {国際化|こくさいか}, {自由化|じゆうか}, デジタル{化|か} |
| 〜{性|せい} | ‑ness, ‑ity | {安全性|あんぜんせい}, {可能性|かのうせい}, {多様性|たようせい} |
| 〜{的|てき} | ‑ic, ‑al (な-adjective) | {社会的|しゃかいてき}, {一時的|いちじてき}, {基本的|きほんてき} |
| 〜{感|かん} | a sense of | {責任感|せきにんかん}, {安心感|あんしんかん}, {達成感|たっせいかん} |
| 〜{力|りょく} | ability | {想像力|そうぞうりょく}, {集中力|しゅうちゅうりょく}, {説得力|せっとくりょく} |
| 〜{率|りつ} | rate | {合格率|ごうかくりつ}, {確率|かくりつ}, {比率|ひりつ} |
| 〜{界|かい} | world, circles | {業界|ぎょうかい}, {政界|せいかい}, {芸能界|げいのうかい} |
| 〜{型|がた} | type, model | {大型|おおがた}, {小型|こがた}, {血液型|けつえきがた} |
| 〜{式|しき} | style; ceremony | {和式|わしき}, {洋式|ようしき}; {卒業式|そつぎょうしき} |
| 〜{層|そう} | group, layer | {年齢層|ねんれいそう}, {若年層|じゃくねんそう} |
| 〜{観|かん} | view of | {価値観|かちかん}, {人生観|じんせいかん} |
| 〜{制|せい} | system | {会員制|かいいんせい}, {予約制|よやくせい}, {税制|ぜいせい} |
| 〜{面|めん} | aspect | {経済面|けいざいめん}, {安全面|あんぜんめん} |
| 〜{上|じょう} | in terms of | {法律上|ほうりつじょう}, {教育上|きょういくじょう} |
| 〜{状|じょう} | letter; form | {招待状|しょうたいじょう}, {液状|えきじょう} |
| 〜{風|ふう} | style, looking like | {和風|わふう}, {学生風|がくせいふう} |
| 〜{部|ぶ} | part, area | {中心部|ちゅうしんぶ}, {下線部|かせんぶ} |

## Money and people

| Suffix | Tendency | Words |
|---|---|---|
| 〜{費|ひ} | expenses of a type | {生活費|せいかつひ}, {交通費|こうつうひ}, {食費|しょくひ} |
| 〜{料|りょう} | a fee for a service or use | {手数料|てすうりょう}, {入場料|にゅうじょうりょう}, {授業料|じゅぎょうりょう} |
| 〜{代|だい} | the price of something (everyday) | {電気代|でんきだい}, {食事代|しょくじだい} |
| 〜{賃|ちん} | transport, rent, work | {運賃|うんちん}, {家賃|やちん}, {賃金|ちんぎん} |
| 〜{家|か} | an art or calling | {専門家|せんもんか}, {作家|さっか}, {政治家|せいじか} |
| 〜{者|しゃ} | a person who | {研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}, {高齢者|こうれいしゃ}, {消費者|しょうひしゃ} |
| 〜{員|いん} | a member | {会社員|かいしゃいん}, {公務員|こうむいん}, {会員|かいいん} |
| 〜{派|は} | a side, a school | {賛成派|さんせいは}, {反対派|はんたいは}, {少数派|しょうすうは} |

## Sound changes

| Change | Examples |
|---|---|
| Rendaku (voicing) | {大型|おおがた}, {人手不足|ひとでぶそく}, {底力|そこぢから} |
| Small っ | {一周|いっしゅう}, {各国|かっこく}, {学校|がっこう}, {復旧|ふっきゅう} |
| h → p after ん / っ | {反比例|はんぴれい}, {一匹|いっぴき} |

references.title: Written style: spoken and written forms
references.body:
Japanese has three styles: polite (です / ます), plain (casual speech, and the だ style of diaries,
blogs, novels and news) and the written である style of reports, essays, editorials and most N2
reading texts. Choose one for a whole text: だ and である can share a text, but です / ます
shouldn't join them. This sheet sets the spoken forms beside the written ones (lessons 26–28;
N3 lesson 26 introduced the である style).

## Sentence endings

| Spoken or plain | Written | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {原因|げんいん}だ | {原因|げんいん}である | it is the cause |
| {原因|げんいん}じゃない | {原因|げんいん}ではない | it isn't the cause |
| {原因|げんいん}だった | {原因|げんいん}であった | it was the cause |
| {原因|げんいん}だろう | {原因|げんいん}であろう | it is probably the cause |
| 〜と{言|い}えるだろう | 〜と{言|い}えよう | one could say that |
| 〜んじゃないかな | 〜のではないだろうか / 〜のではなかろうか | isn't it the case that…? |
| 〜んだ | 〜のだ / 〜のである | (explaining) |
| 〜と{思|おも}う | 〜と{考|かんが}えられる / 〜と{思|おも}われる / 〜とされる | it is thought / regarded as |

## Negatives and "must"

| Spoken or plain | Written | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| {行|い}かない + noun | {行|い}かぬ + noun | ぬ: the classical negative, mostly before nouns ({知|し}らぬ{間|ま}に); する → せぬ |
| {行|い}かないで / {行|い}かなくて、 | {行|い}かず、 | ず joins clauses; する → せず, {来|く}る → {来|こ}ず |
| {行|い}かないだろう / {行|い}かないつもりだ | {行|い}くまい | まい: won't, surely not; する → するまい / すまい |
| {行|い}かなければならない | {行|い}かねばならない | ねば: ない stem + ねば; する → せねば |
| {行|い}かなければ | {行|い}かねば | if (I) don't go |

None of the written negatives is a drill form.

## Joining clauses

| Spoken | Written |
|---|---|
| {降|ふ}って、 | {降|ふ}り、 |
| {増|ふ}えていて、 | {増|ふ}えており、 |
| {高|たか}くて、 | {高|たか}く、 |
| {問題|もんだい}で、 | {問題|もんだい}であり、 |

## Purpose, reason, extent

| Spoken | Written | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 〜ために | 〜べく (recognize) | in order to |
| 〜から / 〜ので | 〜ため / 〜ゆえ(に) | because |
| だから | したがって / それゆえ | therefore |
| 〜まで | 〜にいたるまで | right down to |
| 〜になった | 〜にいたった | came to (a stage, a result) |
| まさに〜だ | 〜にほかならない | is nothing other than |

## Words

| Spoken | Written |
|---|---|
| でも, だけど | しかし, 〜が |
| とても, すごく | {非常|ひじょう}に, {極|きわ}めて |
| もっと | さらに, {一層|いっそう} |
| まだ | {依然|いぜん}として, {未|いま}だ(に) (usually + negative) |
| どんなに | いかに |
| と (A と B) | および, {並|なら}びに |
| または, か | もしくは |
| そして | かつ |
| {最近|さいきん}, {今|いま} | {今日|こんにち} |
| {私|わたし}たち | {我々|われわれ} |
| ちょっと | やや, {少|すこ}し |

vocab.example: ティッシュ
vocab.exampleEn: tissue, paper tissues

vocab.example: ディナー
vocab.exampleEn: dinner (a restaurant meal)

vocab.example: タトゥー
vocab.exampleEn: tattoo

vocab.example: ヒンドゥー
vocab.exampleEn: Hindu

vocab.example: デュエット
vocab.exampleEn: duet

vocab.example: ウィーン
vocab.exampleEn: Vienna

vocab.example: ウェブサイト
vocab.exampleEn: website

vocab.example: ウォーキング
vocab.exampleEn: walking (for exercise)

vocab.example: ヴァイオリン
vocab.exampleEn: violin (usually written バイオリン)

vocab.example: シェフ
vocab.exampleEn: chef

vocab.example: ジェットコースター
vocab.exampleEn: roller coaster

vocab.example: チェス
vocab.exampleEn: chess

vocab.example: モーツァルト
vocab.exampleEn: Mozart

vocab.example: わたしは がくせいです。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm a student.
vocab.note: Often left out when it's clear you're talking about yourself.

vocab.example: ゆきさんは がくせいです。
vocab.exampleEn: Yuki is a student.

vocab.example: せんせいは にほんへ いきます。
vocab.exampleEn: The teacher is going to Japan.
vocab.note: Also a title after a name (たなかせんせい), for teachers, doctors and other respected professionals. Not used for yourself.

vocab.example: がっこうへ いきます。
vocab.exampleEn: I go to school.

vocab.example: にほんへ いきますか。
vocab.exampleEn: Are you going to Japan?

vocab.example: うちへ かえります。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going home.

vocab.example: みずを のみます。
vocab.exampleEn: I drink water.
